        /* Mood-art slideshow, the permanent backdrop for the whole menu — no
           static cover.png any more, this is what's always behind the SNES-style
           panel below, cycling before, during and after loading (main.js's
           startLoadScreen() never stops it; finishLoading() only retires the
           #loadHud percentage readout). Negative z-index paints above #overlay's
           own flat background but below its normal-flow content (the #overlay > *
           rule above would otherwise win this element's z-index too since it's an
           equal-specificity id selector, hence this rule has to come after it in
           source order). */
        #loadScreen {
          position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; overflow: hidden; background: #05070a;
        }
        #loadScreen .slide {
          /* contain, not cover: show the whole image, not a cropped/zoomed slice —
             letterboxing against #loadScreen's own dark fill beats cutting off the
             art. */
          position: absolute; inset: 0; background-size: contain; background-repeat: no-repeat;
          background-position: center; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 1.8s ease;
        }
        #loadScreen .slide.on { opacity: 1; }
        /* Portrait images alone waste most of a widescreen frame as pillarboxing
           either side — group them 3-up instead, each in its own contained pane,
           so the width actually gets used. */
        #loadScreen .slide.group { display: flex; gap: 3px; }
        #loadScreen .slide.group .pane {
          flex: 1; height: 100%; background-size: contain; background-repeat: no-repeat;
          background-position: center;
        }
        /* Retro arcade loading readout: a neon LOADING/percentage row over a
           segmented LED-style bar, with the current boot stage underneath — the
           "what's it doing" text used to stand alone here as plain gray copy. */
        #loadHud {
          position: absolute; left: 6vw; bottom: calc(2vh + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
          width: min(360px, 70vw); font-family: "Arial Black", Arial, sans-serif;
          background: rgba(6, 10, 14, .7);
          border: 3px solid #29d6ff;
          box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #05070a, 0 0 22px rgba(41, 214, 255, .4), inset 0 0 22px rgba(0, 0, 0, .55);
          padding: 12px 16px;
        }
        #loadHudRow {
          display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline;
          letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 6px;
        }
        #loadLabel {
          font-size: 13px; color: #7ff2ff;
          text-shadow: 0 0 4px #29d6ff, 0 0 12px rgba(41, 214, 255, .65);
        }
        #loadPct {
          font-size: 15px; color: #ff5fce;
          text-shadow: 0 0 4px #ff2bb8, 0 0 12px rgba(255, 43, 184, .65);
        }
        #loadBarTrack {
          height: 10px; padding: 2px; border-radius: 2px;
          background: rgba(255, 255, 255, .05);
          border: 1px solid rgba(127, 242, 255, .35);
          box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(41, 214, 255, .2) inset;
        }
        #loadBarFill {
          height: 100%; width: 0%; border-radius: 1px;
          background:
            repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 6px, rgba(5, 7, 10, .55) 6px 8px),
            linear-gradient(90deg, #29d6ff, #ff5fce);
          box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(255, 95, 206, .65), 0 0 14px rgba(41, 214, 255, .45);
          transition: width .5s ease;
        }
        #loadNote {
          display: block; margin-top: 6px;
          font: 12px/1.3 Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .04em; color: #cfeeff; opacity: .7;
        }
        #loadError {
          position: absolute; z-index: 5; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
          display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; gap: 14px;
          width: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px)); max-height: min(82vh, 680px); overflow: auto;
          padding: clamp(20px, 5vw, 34px); text-align: left; color: #f4f1ea;
          background: rgba(10, 13, 20, .97); border: 2px solid #ff5fce; border-radius: 12px;
          box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #05070a, 0 0 28px rgba(255, 43, 184, .35);
          font: 15px/1.5 Arial, sans-serif;
        }
        #loadError[hidden] { display: none; }
        #loadError h2 { color: #ff8fe0; font: 900 clamp(22px, 5vw, 30px)/1.15 Arial, sans-serif; }
        #loadError p { max-width: none; padding: 0; background: none; font: inherit; }
        #loadError ol { padding-left: 22px; }
        #loadError li + li { margin-top: 6px; }
        #loadErrorDetail {
          max-height: 120px; overflow: auto; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 5px;
          background: rgba(0, 0, 0, .45); color: #b9c6d8; font: 12px/1.4 monospace;
          overflow-wrap: anywhere; white-space: pre-wrap;
        }
        #loadError button {
          align-self: flex-start; min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 22px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px;
          background: #ff5fce; color: #160d18; font: 800 16px Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer;
        }
        #loadError button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #fff; outline-offset: 3px; }
      
        /* -------------------------------------------------- main menu (GTA-style) */
        #introPanel {
          position: absolute; inset: 0; align-self: stretch;
          display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; align-items: center;
          gap: clamp(20px, 3.4vh, 38px);
          padding: 6vh 7vw; text-align: center;
        }
        #introPanel[hidden], #characterSelect[hidden], #multiplayerPanel[hidden] { display: none !important; }
        #menuLogo { line-height: 1; }
        .menu-kicker {
          font: 700 clamp(13px, 1.6vw, 18px) Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .5em;
          text-transform: uppercase; color: #7ff2ff;
          text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(41, 214, 255, .7);
        }
        .menu-wordmark {
          font: 900 clamp(54px, 9vw, 120px)/.86 "Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif;
          color: #f4f0e2; letter-spacing: -.01em;
          text-shadow:
            0 4px 0 #101018,
            0 0 10px rgba(41, 214, 255, .75), 0 0 28px rgba(41, 214, 255, .45),
            0 0 40px rgba(255, 43, 184, .35);
        }
        .menu-tagline {
          font: italic 700 clamp(15px, 1.9vw, 24px) Georgia, serif; color: #ff8fe0; margin-top: 4px;
          text-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(255, 43, 184, .5);
        }
      
        /* SNES-style menu box: a chunky double-bordered panel the options sit
           inside, instead of the old full-screen darkening wash — the art stays
           visible everywhere outside the box. */
        .menu-list, .menu-panel {
          display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; gap: clamp(4px, 1.3vh, 13px);
          background: rgba(6, 10, 14, .7);
          border: 3px solid #29d6ff;
          box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #05070a, 0 0 22px rgba(41, 214, 255, .4), inset 0 0 22px rgba(0, 0, 0, .55);
          padding: clamp(18px, 3vh, 30px) clamp(28px, 5vw, 52px);
          min-width: min(360px, 82vw);
        }
        .menu-list[hidden], .menu-panel[hidden] { display: none; }
        .menu-item {
          all: unset; cursor: pointer; pointer-events: auto; box-sizing: border-box;
          font: 700 clamp(19px, 2.5vw, 29px) "Arial Black", Arial, sans-serif;
          color: rgba(244, 240, 226, .72); letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase;
          padding: 1px 26px; text-align: center; position: relative;
          transition: color .12s, transform .12s;
        }
        .menu-item::before {
          content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 50%; width: 16px; height: 4px;
          background: #7ff2ff; box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(41, 214, 255, .8);
          transform: translateY(-50%) scaleX(0); transform-origin: left;
          transition: transform .12s;
        }
        .menu-item:hover, .menu-item:focus-visible, .menu-item.active {
          color: #fff; transform: translateX(6px); outline: none;
          text-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(127, 242, 255, .85);
        }
        .menu-item:hover::before, .menu-item:focus-visible::before, .menu-item.active::before {
          transform: translateY(-50%) scaleX(1);
        }
        .menu-item:disabled { opacity: .35; cursor: default; }
        .menu-item:disabled:hover { transform: none; color: rgba(244, 240, 226, .35); }
        .menu-item:disabled:hover::before { transform: translateY(-50%) scaleX(0); }
        .menu-item.menu-back {
          color: rgba(244, 240, 226, .48); font-size: clamp(14px, 1.7vw, 19px); margin-top: 6px;
        }
      
        .menu-panel { min-width: min(560px, 80vw); }
        .opt-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: clamp(10px, 2vw, 24px); flex-wrap: wrap; }
        .opt-label {
          width: 150px; flex-shrink: 0; font: 700 13px Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .1em;
          text-transform: uppercase; color: #cfe8bf; opacity: .8;
        }
        .opt-choices { display: flex; gap: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
        .opt-choices .menu-item, .opt-toggle {
          font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .06em; padding: 7px 14px;
          border: 1px solid rgba(160, 190, 150, .3); border-radius: 3px;
          color: rgba(244, 240, 226, .65);
        }
        .opt-choices .menu-item::before, .opt-toggle::before { display: none; }
        .opt-choices .menu-item:hover, .opt-toggle:hover { transform: none; border-color: #e8a13a; color: #fff; }
        .opt-choices .menu-item.active {
          color: #16210f; background: #e8a13a; border-color: #e8a13a; transform: none;
        }
        .opt-toggle.off { color: #ff8a7a; border-color: rgba(255, 90, 60, .5); }
        #musicVolume, #mouseSens, #fovSlider { all: revert; width: 200px; accent-color: #e8a13a; pointer-events: auto; cursor: pointer; }
      
        .menu-confirm { font: 700 clamp(18px, 2.2vw, 24px) Arial, sans-serif; color: #f4f0e2; }
        .menu-confirm-sub { font: 13px Arial, sans-serif; color: rgba(244, 240, 226, .6); margin-top: -6px; }
        .menu-row { display: flex; gap: clamp(20px, 3vw, 36px); margin-top: 4px; }
      
        .menu-footer {
          position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: calc(3.4vh + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
          transform: translateX(-50%); text-align: center;
          font: 12px Arial, sans-serif; color: rgba(230, 230, 220, .45); letter-spacing: .02em;
          max-width: 88vw; background: none; padding: 0;
        }
        .menu-footer b { color: rgba(207, 232, 191, .75); }
        @media (max-width: 720px) {
          #introPanel { padding: 5vh 6vw; gap: 16px; }
          .menu-footer { display: none; }
          .opt-label { width: 100%; }
        }
        #characterSelect { width: min(1080px, 96vw); min-height: min(650px, 88vh); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; text-align: left; }
        #multiplayerPanel { width:min(760px,94vw); padding:28px; background:rgba(10,12,10,.9); border:1px solid rgba(220,165,78,.45); box-shadow:0 20px 80px #000b; text-align:left; }
        .mp-code { font-size:clamp(25px,5vw,48px); letter-spacing:.16em; color:#ffd28b; text-align:center; margin:18px 0; }
        .mp-row { display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center; margin:14px 0; }
        .mp-row input { flex:1; min-width:180px; background:#111914; border:1px solid #82633b; color:#ffe9bd; padding:12px; font:inherit; text-transform:uppercase; }
        #mpPlayers { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr); gap:10px; margin:18px 0; }
        .mp-player { padding:13px; min-height:54px; border:1px solid #493b2b; background:#171710; }
        .mp-player.ready { border-color:#72ba62; } .mp-status { color:#b8a88c; font-size:12px; }
        .select-kicker { color: #e8a13a; letter-spacing: .3em; font: 700 12px Arial, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; }
        .select-title { font-size: clamp(30px, 5vw, 64px); line-height: .9; text-shadow: 0 4px 0 #101c10, 0 0 30px rgba(120,200,120,.4); }
        .select-stage { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(220px, 1fr) minmax(300px, 1.3fr); gap: clamp(18px, 5vw, 64px); align-items: center; flex: 1; }
        #characterPortrait { --accent: #d99a3a; min-height: 290px; display: grid; place-items: center; font-size: clamp(130px, 20vw, 260px); color: var(--accent); text-shadow: 0 10px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.4), 0 0 50px var(--accent); background: radial-gradient(circle, color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 26%, transparent), transparent 65%); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--accent); transition: color .25s, background .25s; }
        #characterInfo { background: rgba(4,6,4,.66); border-left: 3px solid var(--accent, #d99a3a); padding: 22px 26px; backdrop-filter: blur(4px); }
        #characterName { font-size: clamp(24px, 4vw, 52px); line-height: .92; text-transform: uppercase; }
        #characterSubtitle { color: #e8a13a; letter-spacing: .14em; font: 700 12px Arial, sans-serif; margin: 8px 0 24px; }
        .ability-label { color: #a6c997; letter-spacing: .18em; font: 700 11px Arial, sans-serif; }
        #characterAbility { font-size: clamp(18px, 2.5vw, 30px); color: #f3d58e; margin: 5px 0 10px; }
        #characterDescription { font: 15px/1.55 Arial, sans-serif; color: #e6e8da; max-width: 580px; }
        #characterCards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr); gap: 8px; }
        #characterCards button { padding: 12px 8px; border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 60%, #777); font-size: 11px; min-height: 48px; }
        #characterCards button.selected { color: #111; background: var(--accent); border-color: #fff1c5; box-shadow: 0 0 20px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent); transform: translateY(-3px); }
        .select-actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 10px; }
        @media (max-width: 700px) { #characterSelect { min-height: 0; } .select-stage { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 8px; } #characterPortrait { min-height: 150px; font-size: 120px; } #characterInfo { padding: 14px; } #characterSubtitle { margin-bottom: 10px; } #characterCards { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } }
        #mute, #radioBtn {
          position: fixed; bottom: 14px; right: 14px; z-index: 15; pointer-events: auto; cursor: pointer;
          background: rgba(6,10,8,.6); border: 1px solid rgba(160,190,150,.25); color: #f2efe6;
          border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 10px; font-size: 15px; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        }
        /* the car radio sits to the left of the music toggle */
        #radioBtn { right: 60px; }
        #mute.off, #radioBtn.off { opacity: .45; text-decoration: line-through; }
        #crosshair { position: fixed; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 28px; height: 28px; margin: -14px;
          background: transparent; border: 2px solid rgba(255,240,200,0.85); border-radius: 50%;
          z-index: 9; pointer-events: none; display: none; box-shadow: 0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.7), inset 0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.7); }
        #crosshair { transition: transform .08s, border-color .08s; }
        #crosshair.hit { border-color: #ff3b30; transform: scale(1.5); }
        #crosshair::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 4px; height: 4px; margin: -2px;
          background: rgba(255,240,200,0.95); border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.8); }
        .flash { animation: fl .4s ease-out; }
        /* damage indicator (main.js updateDamageFx): a red vignette over the canvas — flashes on every point of HP lost, pulses while health is low.
           (.flash above animates the <body> background, which sits BEHIND the canvas, so it never showed.) */
        #dmg { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 12; pointer-events: none; opacity: 0;
          background: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, rgba(120,0,0,0) 38%, rgba(150,10,10,.55) 72%, rgba(200,10,10,.95) 100%); }
        #dmg.hit { animation: dmgHit .75s ease-out; }
        #dmg.low { animation: dmgLow 1.15s ease-in-out infinite; }
        #dmg.hit.low { animation: dmgHit .75s ease-out; }
        @keyframes dmgHit { 0% { opacity: var(--i, .8); } 100% { opacity: 0; } }
        @keyframes dmgLow { 0%, 100% { opacity: calc(var(--low, .3) * .35); } 50% { opacity: calc(var(--low, .3) * .9); } }
        @keyframes fl { from { background: rgba(200,40,30,.4); } to { background: transparent; } }
        /* ---- cutscenes (src/cinema.js) ---- */
        #hud { transition: opacity .4s; }
        body.letterbox #hud, body.letterbox #crosshair { opacity: 0; }
        #cine { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 18; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
        #cine .bar { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; height: 0; background: #000; transition: height .7s ease; }
        #cine .bar.top { top: 0; }
        #cine .bar.bot { bottom: 0; }
        body.letterbox #cine .bar { height: 11vh; }
        #cineBlack { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #000; opacity: 0; transition: opacity var(--fade, 1s) ease; }
        #cineBlack.on { opacity: 1; }
        #cineFlash { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #fff8e8; opacity: 0; }
        #cineFlash.on { animation: cineFlash .45s ease-out; }
        @keyframes cineFlash { from { opacity: .95; } to { opacity: 0; } }
        #cineSub {
          position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: 13vh; transform: translateX(-50%);
          width: min(900px, 90vw); text-align: center; opacity: 0; transition: opacity .18s;
          font: 600 clamp(15px, 1.7vw, 21px)/1.4 Arial, sans-serif; color: #f4f0e2;
          text-shadow: 0 2px 3px #000, 0 0 14px #000;
        }
        #cineSub.on { opacity: 1; }
        #cineSub em { display: block; font-style: normal; font-size: .7em; letter-spacing: .16em; color: #e8a13a; margin-bottom: 3px; }
        #cineSub.action span { font-style: italic; color: #c9d4bf; }
        #cineCard {
          position: absolute; left: 6vw; top: 16vh; opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px);
          transition: opacity .6s, transform .6s; color: #f4f0e2; text-shadow: 0 3px 8px #000;
          font-family: "Arial Black", Arial, sans-serif;
        }
        #cineCard.on { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
        #cineCard.center { left: 50%; top: 38%; text-align: center; transform: translate(-50%, 8px); }
        #cineCard.center.on { transform: translate(-50%, 0); }
        #cineCard small { display: block; font: 700 13px Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .22em; color: #e8a13a; }
        #cineCard b { display: block; font-size: clamp(26px, 4.2vw, 56px); line-height: 1; }
        #cineCard span { display: block; font: 600 15px Arial, sans-serif; opacity: .8; margin-top: 8px; }
        #cineTitle {
          position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
          text-align: center; opacity: 0; letter-spacing: -.02em; color: #f4f0e2;
          font: 900 clamp(44px, 10vw, 140px)/.9 "Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif;
          text-shadow: 0 6px 0 #101c10, 0 0 60px rgba(232,161,58,.45);
        }
        #cineTitle.on { opacity: 1; transition: opacity .5s; }
        #cineTitle.blast { animation: cineBlast 1.1s ease-out forwards; }
        @keyframes cineBlast {
          0% { opacity: 1; filter: brightness(3); transform: scale(1.05); }
          15% { transform: translate(-8px, 5px) scale(1.03); }
          30% { transform: translate(6px, -4px) scale(1.02); }
          100% { opacity: 0; filter: blur(8px); transform: scale(1.15); }
        }
        #cineSkip { position: absolute; right: 16px; bottom: 12px; font: 11px Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .08em;
          text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(230,230,220,.45); opacity: 0; }
        body.letterbox #cineSkip { opacity: 1; }
        .wasted {
          position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 19; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
          font-size: clamp(48px, 12vw, 130px); color: #b8202a; font-style: italic;
          background: rgba(0,0,0,.5); text-shadow: 0 0 40px #000; pointer-events: none;
        }
      </style>
      </head>
      <body>
      <!-- PRIVATE ACCESS GATE — STATIC, same first-paint principle as the 18+ gate below, and painted
           on top of it (higher z-index): this build is not meant to be found by a stranger who guesses
           the URL. Correct password is remembered in localStorage (keyed by the password's own hash, so
           changing GTB_ACCESS_HASH below silently invalidates every remembered device). This is
           client-side obfuscation, not real access control — the hash is sitting right here in the page
           source — but it stops a casual visitor from landing on an R18+ game by accident, which is the
           actual goal (see docs/CONTENT_POLICY_REVIEW.md). -->
      <div id="gtbAccessGate" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="gtbAccessTitle" style="position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:2147483647;background:#06080c;color:#f4f1ea;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:20px;font:16px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;">
        <section style="box-sizing:border-box;width:min(420px,100%);padding:clamp(24px,5vw,40px);background:#151923;border:3px solid #4fd1ff;border-radius:14px;box-shadow:0 18px 70px #000;">
          <h1 id="gtbAccessTitle" style="margin:0 0 12px;color:#8ad4ff;font:900 22px/1.2 system-ui,sans-serif;">PRIVATE ACCESS</h1>
          <p style="margin:0 0 18px;color:#c4c6d0;font-size:14px;">This build is private. Enter the access password to continue.</p>
          <form id="gtbAccessForm">
            <label for="gtbAccessInput" style="display:block;margin:0 0 6px;color:#c4c6d0;font-size:14px;">Access password</label>
            <input id="gtbAccessInput" type="password" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="go" aria-describedby="gtbAccessError" style="display:block;width:100%;box-sizing:border-box;padding:12px 14px;margin:0 0 10px;border-radius:7px;border:1px solid #454554;background:#0d1017;color:#f4f1ea;font-size:16px;">
            <button id="gtbAccessSubmit" type="submit" style="display:block;width:100%;padding:14px 18px;border:0;border-radius:7px;background:#4fd1ff;color:#0a1620;font:800 15px system-ui;cursor:pointer;">ENTER</button>
          </form>
          <p id="gtbAccessError" role="alert" aria-live="polite" hidden style="margin:12px 0 0;color:#ff8a8a;font-size:13px;"></p>
        </section>
      </div>
      <script>
      (function () {
        // sha256("deltron3030%funkyhomo!") — see docs/CONTENT_POLICY_REVIEW.md. Change the password by
        // recomputing this hash (e.g. `printf '%s' 'newpass' | sha256sum` at a shell) and pasting it here.
        var GTB_ACCESS_HASH = "14abfcdeb124aa9a8a18c5674f01a51b55f831caffeacb96da6f77732a39829a";
        var REMEMBER_KEY = "gtb.access.ok";
        var gate = document.getElementById("gtbAccessGate");
        if (!gate) return;
        try {
          if (localStorage.getItem(REMEMBER_KEY) === GTB_ACCESS_HASH) { gate.remove(); return; }
        } catch (e) {}
        var form = document.getElementById("gtbAccessForm");
        var input = document.getElementById("gtbAccessInput");
        var error = document.getElementById("gtbAccessError");
        function sha256Hex(text) {
          return crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(text)).then(function (buf) {
            return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf)).map(function (b) { return b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"); }).join("");
          });
        }
        function showError(message) {
          error.textContent = message;
          error.hidden = false;
          input.setAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
        }
        function tryEnter() {
          error.hidden = true;
          error.textContent = "";
          input.removeAttribute("aria-invalid");
          if (!(window.crypto && window.crypto.subtle && window.TextEncoder)) {
            var message = location.protocol === "file:"
              ? "Password checking isn't available when this page is opened as a file. Start the game with start-game.cmd or npm start, then open http://localhost:8899."
              : "This browser can't securely check the password here. Open the game over HTTPS or on localhost, or try a current browser.";
            showError(message);
            return;
          }
          try {
            sha256Hex(input.value || "").then(function (hex) {
              if (hex === GTB_ACCESS_HASH) {
                try { localStorage.setItem(REMEMBER_KEY, GTB_ACCESS_HASH); } catch (e) {}
                window.removeEventListener("keydown", lock, true);
                window.removeEventListener("keyup", lock, true);
                gate.remove();
                // The age-gate keyboard trap may still be active. Move focus off the
                // removed password form so the next keyboard action reaches its button.
                var ageYes = document.getElementById("gtbAgeYes");
                if (ageYes) ageYes.focus();
              } else {
                showError("That password didn't match. Check it and try again.");
                input.value = "";
                input.focus();
              }
            }).catch(function () {
              showError("Password checking failed in this browser. Open the game over HTTPS or on localhost, or try a current browser.");
            });
          } catch (e) {
            showError("Password checking failed in this browser. Open the game over HTTPS or on localhost, or try a current browser.");
          }
        }
        form.addEventListener("submit", function (e) {
          e.preventDefault();
          tryEnter();
        });
        input.addEventListener("input", function () {
          if (error.hidden) return;
          error.hidden = true;
          error.textContent = "";
          input.removeAttribute("aria-invalid");
        });
        // Swallow all other input (movement keys, menu shortcuts, the age gate below) until this is answered.
        function lock(e) {
          if (e.target === input || e.target === document.getElementById("gtbAccessSubmit")) return;
          e.preventDefault();
          e.stopImmediatePropagation();
        }
        window.addEventListener("keydown", lock, true);
        window.addEventListener("keyup", lock, true);
        input.focus();
      })();
      </script>
      <!-- The 18+ gate is STATIC: it is the first thing painted, before any script or loading screen (src/adultContent.js adopts these buttons and
           swallows keys until one is pressed; the game never runs behind it un-answered). Nothing is remembered: every launch asks again. -->

        var yes = document.getElementById("gtbAgeYes");
        var no = document.getElementById("gtbAgeNo");
        if (!gate || !yes || !no) return;
        yes.addEventListener("click", function () {

- path: tools\build-site.mjs
  content: |
      // Builds ./dist — only what the game serves — so a direct `wrangler pages deploy` can never upload .env, .git/,
      // server/, tools/, docs/, node_modules/ or the local asset archives (zips, unitypackages, bbdoc).
      //   node tools/build-site.mjs            (npm run build:site)
      //   npm run deploy                       (build:site, then wrangler pages deploy dist)
      // Assets are taken from `git ls-files`, so anything gitignored (source archives) stays out by construction.
      import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
      import { cpSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, existsSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
      import path from "node:path";
      import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
      
      const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
      const out = path.join(root, "dist");
      rmSync(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
      mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
      
      const files = execFileSync("git", ["-c", "core.quotepath=off", "ls-files", "-z", "index.html", "src", "data", "assets", "og.png", "og2.png", "og3.png", "cover.png"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" })
        .split("\0").filter(Boolean);
      let n = 0, bytes = 0;
      for (const f of files) {
        const from = path.join(root, f);
        if (!existsSync(from)) continue;
        const to = path.join(out, f);
        mkdirSync(path.dirname(to), { recursive: true });
        cpSync(from, to);
        n++; bytes += statSync(from).size;
      }
      console.log(`dist/: ${n} files, ${(bytes / 1048576).toFixed(0)} MB`);
      
  referencedBy: {}

  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // cemetery.js — OrleaRouge's "city of the dead", and the ghost who keeps it.
      //
      // Built to St. Louis No. 1 in New Orleans rather than to a lawn of headstones:
      // the water table there is a metre down, so nobody is buried *in* the ground.
      // Everything that reads as that cemetery is here —
      //
      //   oven vaults   the perimeter wall IS the cemetery. Stacked rented vaults,
      //                 three tablets high, plastered and whitewashed, closed with
      //                 engraved marble tablets. Called "fours" (ovens) because a
      //                 year and a day in a New Orleans summer is all it takes.

- path: tools\build-site.mjs
  content: |
      // Builds ./dist — only what the game serves — so a direct `wrangler pages deploy` can never upload .env, .git/,
      // server/, tools/, docs/, node_modules/ or the local asset archives (zips, unitypackages, bbdoc).
      //   node tools/build-site.mjs            (npm run build:site)
      //   npm run deploy                       (build:site, then wrangler pages deploy dist)
      // Assets are taken from `git ls-files`, so anything gitignored (source archives) stays out by construction.
      import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
      import { cpSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, existsSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
      import path from "node:path";
      import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
      
      const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
      const out = path.join(root, "dist");
      rmSync(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
      mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
      
      const files = execFileSync("git", ["-c", "core.quotepath=off", "ls-files", "-z", "index.html", "src", "data", "assets", "og.png", "og2.png", "og3.png", "cover.png"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" })
        .split("\0").filter(Boolean);
      let n = 0, bytes = 0;
      for (const f of files) {
        const from = path.join(root, f);
        if (!existsSync(from)) continue;
        const to = path.join(out, f);
        mkdirSync(path.dirname(to), { recursive: true });
        cpSync(from, to);
        n++; bytes += statSync(from).size;
      }
      console.log(`dist/: ${n} files, ${(bytes / 1048576).toFixed(0)} MB`);

      					}

      				container.add( points );
      
      			}
      
      		}
      
      		return container;
      
      	}

      	Color,
      	DefaultLoadingManager,
      	FileLoader,

      	TextureLoader,
      	Vector2,
      	SRGBColorSpace

      /**
       * Loads a Wavefront .mtl file specifying materials

      	constructor( manager ) {
      
      		super( manager );
      
      	}

      	 *
      	 * @param {String} url - URL to the MTL file.
      	 * @param {Function} [onLoad] - Callback invoked with the loaded object.
      	 * @param {Function} [onProgress] - Callback for download progress.
      	 * @param {Function} [onError] - Callback for download errors.

      	 * @see setPath setResourcePath
      	 *
      	 * @note In order for relative texture references to resolve correctly
      	 * you must call setResourcePath() explicitly prior to load.
      	 */
      	load( url, onLoad, onProgress, onError ) {
      
      		const scope = this;
      
      		const path = ( this.path === '' ) ? LoaderUtils.extractUrlBase( url ) : this.path;
      
      		const loader = new FileLoader( this.manager );
      		loader.setPath( this.path );
      		loader.setRequestHeader( this.requestHeader );
      		loader.setWithCredentials( this.withCredentials );

      			try {
      
      				onLoad( scope.parse( text, path ) );
      
      			} catch ( e ) {
      
      				if ( onError ) {
      
      					onError( e );
      
      				} else {
      
      					console.error( e );
      
      				}
      
      				scope.manager.itemError( url );
      
      			}
      
      		}, onProgress, onError );
      
      	}
      
      	setMaterialOptions( value ) {
      
      		this.materialOptions = value;
      		return this;
      
      	}
      
      	/**
      	 * Parses a MTL file.
      	 *
      	 * @param {String} text - Content of MTL file
      	 * @return {MaterialCreator}
      	 *
      	 * @see setPath setResourcePath

      	 * @note In order for relative texture references to resolve correctly
      	 * you must call setResourcePath() explicitly prior to parse.

      		let info = {};
      		const delimiter_pattern = /\s+/;
      		const materialsInfo = {};
      
      		for ( let i = 0; i < lines.length; i ++ ) {
      
      			let line = lines[ i ];
      			line = line.trim();
      
      			if ( line.length === 0 || line.charAt( 0 ) === '#' ) {
      
      				// Blank line or comment ignore
      				continue;

      			key = key.toLowerCase();

      			if ( key === 'newmtl' ) {
      
      				// New material
      
      				info = { name: value };
      				materialsInfo[ value ] = info;
      
      			} else {

      					info[ key ] = [ parseFloat( ss[ 0 ] ), parseFloat( ss[ 1 ] ), parseFloat( ss[ 2 ] ) ];
      
      				} else {
      
      					info[ key ] = value;
      
      				}
      
      			}
      
      		}

      		materialCreator.setCrossOrigin( this.crossOrigin );

- path: tools\build-site.mjs
  content: |
      // Builds ./dist — only what the game serves — so a direct `wrangler pages deploy` can never upload .env, .git/,
      // server/, tools/, docs/, node_modules/ or the local asset archives (zips, unitypackages, bbdoc).
      //   node tools/build-site.mjs            (npm run build:site)
      //   npm run deploy                       (build:site, then wrangler pages deploy dist)
      // Assets are taken from `git ls-files`, so anything gitignored (source archives) stays out by construction.
      import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
      import { cpSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, existsSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
      import path from "node:path";
      import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
      
      const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
      const out = path.join(root, "dist");
      rmSync(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
      mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
      
      const files = execFileSync("git", ["-c", "core.quotepath=off", "ls-files", "-z", "index.html", "src", "data", "assets", "og.png", "og2.png", "og3.png", "cover.png"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" })
        .split("\0").filter(Boolean);
      files.push(
        "assets/vendor/three/examples/jsm/loaders/OBJLoader.js",
        "assets/vendor/three/examples/jsm/loaders/MTLLoader.js"
      );
      let n = 0, bytes = 0;
      for (const f of files) {
        const from = path.join(root, f);
        if (!existsSync(from)) continue;
        const to = path.join(out, f);
        mkdirSync(path.dirname(to), { recursive: true });
        cpSync(from, to);
        n++; bytes += statSync(from).size;
      }
      console.log(`dist/: ${n} files, ${(bytes / 1048576).toFixed(0)} MB`);
      
  referencedBy: {}

          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4

              with: { node-version: 22 }
            - name: Syntax-check every module
              run: |
                for f in src/*.js server/*.js serve.mjs tools/*.mjs; do node --experimental-detect-module --check "$f" || exit 1; done
            - name: Unit tests (pure node, no browser)
              run: |

            - name: The deployable site builds without secrets or archives

                node tools/build-site.mjs
                test ! -e dist/.env && test ! -e dist/server && test ! -e dist/.git

- **CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pushes to `main` and pull requests. It checks syntax, runs tests, and builds `dist/` to verify excluded paths. It contains no deployment step.
- **Direct Wrangler deploy:** `npm run deploy` builds `dist/` and runs `wrangler pages deploy dist`. Repo notes say this uses the *local* Cloudflare login and targets a separate, stale Pages project—not the live site. I did not run it.
- **Build output:** `wrangler.jsonc` still declares `pages_build_output_dir: "."`, but the documented live deployment uses Cloudflare’s Git connection. The recent `build-site.mjs` update makes the two loader files land in local `dist/`; it does not change how the Git-connected Pages build selects files.

**Bottom line:** the loader modules are now included in the local `dist/` build, but this repo’s docs point to a Git-connected deployment path that serves the repository root. The modules are new files and must be included in the deployed commit for their URLs to work on the live site. They are present locally, but currently untracked; don’t expect them in a Git-triggered deploy until they’re committed. No deployment was made.

- path: src\zombies.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // zombies.js — zombie archetypes as DATA (TASK-078). Not wired into anything.
      //
      // TASK-077 (main.js / npc.js) shipped exactly one zombie: ENEMY_TYPES.zombie
      // (hp 5, speed 2.1, aggro 30, melee 1.7, dmg 9, atkGap 0.8) with its own
      // branch in npc.js's decide() — hunts the closer of the player or any living
      // non-zombie NPC within `aggro`, never calms down, shambles toward
      // recentViolence (gunfire/kills) when idle. This module layers archetypes on
      // that base as stat multipliers plus a small set of behavior FLAGS. Nothing
      // here imports game state, THREE, or any module — it is a plain table plus
      // pure helpers, so wiring it (Claude, per protocol §1 rule 5) touches only
      // ENEMY_TYPES in main.js and ~4 lines in npc.js's zombie branch.
      //
      // Per the human's TASK-077 decision these are reskins/data only: every
      // archetype renders as the same randomZombie() Hoodrat-rig reskin. See
      // "Visual differentiation" below for what that means.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      /**
       * The TASK-077 base zombie, mirrored here as the reference archetype's source.
       * Single source of truth stays `ENEMY_TYPES.zombie` in main.js until
       * integration — if that entry changes, change this mirror to match.
       */
      export const BASE_ZOMBIE = Object.freeze({
        label: "Zombie",
        hp: 5, speed: 2.1, aggro: 30, melee: 1.7, dmg: 9, atkGap: 0.8,
      });
      
      /**
       * Behavior flags. All are DOCUMENTED, NOT WIRED — see Integration notes.
       *
       *   noiseResponse  multiplier on `aggro` limiting how far away an event
       *                  (gunshot, kill, fight — npc.js's recentViolence events)
       *                  will pull this zombie when it has no target. 1 = base
       *                  behaviour (any event it could already "see" pulls it);
       *                  <1 = ignores distant noise (the Brute lumbers, it doesn't
       *                  charge across the parish toward every gunshot); >1 = even
       *                  more of a moth to the flame.
       *   screamOnHostile  { r } — the FIRST time this zombie successfully goes
       *                  hostile (npc.js becomeHostile returns true), it calls the
       *                  npc system's exported noise(x, z, r) with r far larger than
       *                  ordinary violence events (15–22), pulling every idle zombie
       *                  in earshot toward it. once-per-life, not per-target: a
       *                  Screamer that loses its target and finds a new one does NOT
       *                  scream again (e.screamed, cleared on spawn only).
       */
      export const ZOMBIE_ARCHETYPES = Object.freeze({
        // The baseline that already exists (TASK-077). Kept as an explicit entry so
        // spawn tables can always name it, and so the other entries read as deltas.
        shambler: {
          label: "Shambler",
          stats: { hp: 1.0, speed: 1.0, aggro: 1.0, melee: 1.0, dmg: 1.0, atkGap: 1.0 },
          flags: { noiseResponse: 1.0 },
          weight: 55,
        },//  Skinny, fast, always looking. Hits like a grabby child but arrives first
        // and forces the player to keep moving. Speed 4.0 ≈ a Hoodrat (4.7) — faster
        // than the player's comfortable walk, outrun by a sprint or any car.
        runner: {
          label: "Runner",
          stats: { hp: 0.6, speed: 1.9, aggro: 1.4, melee: 1.0, dmg: 0.7, atkGap: 0.8 },
          flags: { noiseResponse: 1.5 },
          look: { h: 0.93, skin: 0xc9d4b8, cloth: 0x7a3a30 },                 // gaunt, bone-pale, in bloodied red
          weight: 20,
        },
      
        // The wall that walks. Near-sighted (aggro 24) and deaf to distant gunfire
        // (noiseResponse 0.35 — it does NOT come running across the map because you
        // shot something two blocks over; it lumbers in a straight line and punishes
        // whoever stands in it). Reach 2.1 and dmg 16 one-shot an unarmored careless
        // player who lets it close; atkGap 1.2 keeps the swing slow and dodgeable.
        brute: {
          label: "Brute",
          stats: { hp: 3.0, speed: 0.55, aggro: 0.8, melee: 1.25, dmg: 1.8, atkGap: 1.5 },
          flags: { noiseResponse: 0.35 },
          look: { h: 1.4, skin: 0xa8906e, cloth: 0x5a1a1a },                  // a head and a half taller than anyone: bloated, sallow, in maroon rags (dark greens vanish at night)
          weight: 12,
        },
      
        // The interesting one. Weak (dmg 3), not fast, notices a little late — and
        // the moment it DOES go hostile it screams (flag above), dragging every
        // idle zombie within ~55 m onto its position. Kill it before it finishes
        // closing, or fight the crowd it called. The scream's audio hook belongs to
        // TASK-081's ambience work; this flag is only the gameplay pull.
        screamer: {
          label: "Screamer",
          stats: { hp: 0.8, speed: 1.1, aggro: 0.9, melee: 1.0, dmg: 0.3, atkGap: 1.0 },
          flags: { noiseResponse: 1.2, screamOnHostile: { r: 55 } },
          look: { h: 1.0, skin: 0xe8e2c8, cloth: 0xe0b020 },                  // hazard-yellow: you see the one that is about to scream
          weight: 8,
        },
      
        // Crawler is deliberately ABSENT — the open design question TASK-078 was
        // asked to write up rather than answer. Full tradeoffs in the task's Notes
        // (TODO.md); recommendation: option (c), skip it this wave. If it ever
        // lands as option (a), it plugs in here as a plain entry like the rest:
        //
        // crawler: {
        //   label: "Crawler",
        //   stats: { hp: 0.6, speed: 0.7, aggro: 0.7, melee: 0.9, dmg: 1.2, atkGap: 1.1 },
        //   flags: { noiseResponse: 1.0, lowProfile: true },
        //   weight: 5,
        // },
        //
        // `lowProfile` is only meaningful once anything reads enemy height — today
        // nothing does (hit detection is 2D x/z distance; npc.js melee range is
        // planar), so a crawler would play as a slow Shambler, not a low one.
      });
      
      /**
       * Resolve an archetype into concrete ENEMY_TYPES-shaped stats, multiplying the

- path: src\npc.js
  content: |
            if (options.length) base = e.home = options[(Math.random() * options.length) | 0];
          }
          // `wanderR` comes from the spawn zone (spawnzones.js WANDER): city blocks
          // keep trips short, out in the parish they stretch out, and market day
          // crowds keep to the stalls
          const a = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
          const r = Math.random() * (base.r || 10) * (e.wanderR || 1) * (e.marketSaturday ? 0.5 : 1);
          e.goal.set(base.x + Math.cos(a) * r, 0, base.z + Math.sin(a) * r);
        }
      
        // Gunfire and fights: the crowd that isn't a fighter runs for its life (human request, 2026-09-26).
        // Hoodrats, rednecks, thugs and klansmen hold their ground (and fight or flee by temperament); zombies and
        // hogs have their own logic; the story's cast is scripted. Everyone else — the tourists, suits,
        // escorts, dockworkers, mechanics, hobos, the Frenchmen Street regulars — hears a shot from far
        // off and bolts, flat out and for a good while, directly away from it.
        const STANDS_GROUND = new Set(["hoodrat", "redneck", "thug", "klansman", "zombie", "hog", "mally", "bubba"]);
        // Only feral hogs attack on sight. Hoodrats and rednecks are back to civilians until provoked (human request 2026-09-27: "shouldn't attack
        // the player unless they are attacked first") — hitting one, or shooting near them, is what turns them hostile; they are armed when it does (main.js spawnEnemy).
        const AMBUSHERS = new Set(["hog"]);
        const PANIC_HEARING = 1.8;            // x the event's own radius: a pistol carries ~47 m, a shotgun ~72 m
        function panicEvent(p) {
          for (let i = events.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const ev = events[i];
            if (now - ev.t > 4) break;
            const r = ev.r * PANIC_HEARING;
            if ((ev.x - p.x) ** 2 + (ev.z - p.z) ** 2 < r * r) return ev;
          }
          return null;
        }
      
        function recentViolence(p) {
          for (let i = events.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const ev = events[i];
            if (now - ev.t > 4) break;
            if ((ev.x - p.x) ** 2 + (ev.z - p.z) ** 2 < ev.r * ev.r) return ev;
          }
          return null;
        }
      
        /**
         * `force` skips the crowd cap. That cap exists so an ambient street brawl
         * cannot eat the frame budget, and ambient fights should keep respecting it —
         * but a SCRIPTED fight has a fixed, known cast, and an ally who silently
         * refuses to join in because six other people are already swinging is a bug
         * the player reads as "Mally just stood there". klan.js uses it for Bubba and
         * Mally; nothing ambient should.
         */
        function becomeHostile(e, rivalTarget = null, force = false) {
          if (e.state === "hostile") {
            if (rivalTarget && (!e.rivalTarget || e.rivalTarget.dead)) e.rivalTarget = rivalTarget;
            return true;
          }
          if (!force && budgeted(e) && hostiles >= maxHostile()) return false;
          e.rivalTarget = rivalTarget || null;
          setState(e, "hostile", 0);
          e.calm = 0;
          return true;
        }

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Zombie-mode ambience (TASK-081). Occasional distant groans — not a moan bed:
      // real silence between them, more often and louder the more zombies are close.
      //
      // Recorded SFX (2026-09-27, human-supplied): assets/audio/zombie/ holds the
      // crowd voices — groan0/groan1/moan0/utter0 — picked at random per groan, and
      // scream0 is the Screamer's wail (playZombieScream). These replaced the old
      // synthesised groans/wail entirely (2026-09-27, human: "the old zombie sounds
      // must be gone") — there is no synth fallback any more. A file that fails to
      // load (404, offline) is simply silent for that voice; the game does not break.
      //
      // `trim` normalises the voices to each other (measured with
      // tools/qa/zombie_audio_audit.mjs, 2026-09-27): raw peaks were groan0 0.28,
      // groan1 0.88, moan0 0.13, utter0 0.48, scream0 0.13 — untrimmed, the random
      // picker would swing groan loudness ~5x between picks. Ambient groans are
      // levelled to a 0.175 peak at full crowd (well under the ~0.32 pistol crack);
      // the Screamer is boosted to ~0.42 point-blank — the loudest voice in the
      // mode, ~1.5x a pistol shot, because it is the jump-scare. Re-run the audit
      // before changing any trim.
      //
      // Everything here is safe to call at any time: before initAudio(), before a
      // user gesture, with the context suspended, or after stop. It never throws.
      //
      //   start: on entering zombie mode / at nightfall   startZombieAmbience(...)
      //   stop:  at dawn / leaving the mode               stopZombieAmbience()
      //   the Screamer's wail: playZombieScream(x, z)     (npc.js env.onScream)
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      const ZOMBIE_SFX = [
        { path: "assets/audio/zombie/groan0.mp3", trim: 0.62 },
        { path: "assets/audio/zombie/groan1.mp3", trim: 0.2 },
        { path: "assets/audio/zombie/moan0.mp3", trim: 1.4 },
        { path: "assets/audio/zombie/utter0.mp3", trim: 0.3 },
      ];
      const ZOMBIE_SCREAM_SFX = { path: "assets/audio/zombie/scream0.mp3", trim: 3.3 };
      const GROAN_MIN_GAP = 4, GROAN_MAX_GAP = 22;     // seconds, at 1 zombie ... a crowd
      const HEARD_FULL_COUNT = 12;                     // this many nearby = the busiest it gets
      let zAmb = null;                                 // { getPlayerPos, getCount, timer }
      
      function audioCtx() {
        return listener && listener.context && listener.context.state === 'running' ? listener.context : null;
      }
      
      // one recorded voice, panned, optionally pitch-shifted — the only zombie
      // voices since the synth was retired; a file that fails to load stays silent
      function playRecorded(ctx, file, volume, pan, rate) {
        return loadSound(file).then((buf) => {
          if (!buf || !audioCtx()) return;
          const src = ctx.createBufferSource(), g = ctx.createGain();
          src.buffer = buf;
          if (rate) src.playbackRate.value = rate;
          g.gain.value = volume;
          src.connect(g);
          let tail = g;
          if (ctx.createStereoPanner) {
            const p = ctx.createStereoPanner(); p.pan.value = pan;
            g.connect(p); tail = p;
          }
          tail.connect(listener.getInput());
          src.start();
        }).catch(() => { /* a missing file must never take the game down */ });
      }
      
      function playGroan(volume) {
        const ctx = audioCtx();
        if (!ctx || !ZOMBIE_SFX.length) return;
        // the clamp matters: Math.random() can return exactly 1, and an unclamped
        // index throws (silently swallowed by scheduleGroan) — the groan would vanish
        const voice = ZOMBIE_SFX[Math.min(ZOMBIE_SFX.length - 1, (Math.random() * ZOMBIE_SFX.length) | 0)];
        playRecorded(ctx, voice.path, volume * voice.trim, Math.random() * 1.6 - 0.8);
      }
      
      /** The Screamer's wail at (x, z): louder than a groan, fading with distance. */
      export function playZombieScream(x, z) {
        try {
          const ctx = audioCtx();
          if (!ctx || !zAmb || !ZOMBIE_SCREAM_SFX) return;
          const p = zAmb.getPlayerPos();
          const d = Math.hypot(p.x - x, p.z - z);
          if (d > 130) return;
          playRecorded(ctx, ZOMBIE_SCREAM_SFX.path, ZOMBIE_SCREAM_SFX.trim * (1 - d / 130),
            Math.max(-0.9, Math.min(0.9, (x - p.x) / 60)), 0.85 + Math.random() * 0.3);
        } catch (e) { /* audio must never take the game down */ }
      }
      
      function scheduleGroan() {
        if (!zAmb) return;
        let gap = 3;                       // nobody near: just check back
        try {
          const n = zAmb.getCount();
          if (n > 0) {
            const crowd = Math.min(1, n / HEARD_FULL_COUNT);
            playGroan(0.35 + 0.65 * crowd);
            gap = GROAN_MAX_GAP - (GROAN_MAX_GAP - GROAN_MIN_GAP) * crowd;
            gap *= 0.6 + Math.random() * 0.8;    // vary the cadence, but keep the documented quiet gap bound
            gap = Math.max(GROAN_MIN_GAP, Math.min(GROAN_MAX_GAP, gap));
          }
        } catch (e) { /* keep the loop alive */ }
        zAmb.timer = setTimeout(scheduleGroan, gap * 1000);
      }

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // gunAudio.js — recorded gunshot samples for cinema.sfx() (2026-09-27).
      //
      // The planarian BGM recordings are multi-shot session files, so single shots
      // were sliced out with ffmpeg (silence-detected boundaries) into
      // assets/audio/gun/: a0/a1/b0/b1 are pistol-calibre single shots, shotgun0 is
      // the one clean 12-gauge boom, tec90/tec91 are two rapid-fire pops.
      //
      // `play(kind, volume)` is called by cinema.js's sfx() for the gun kinds BEFORE
      // its synthesised voices; when the samples are loaded it returns true and the
      // synth for that shot is skipped. Until prewarm() finishes (or if a file 404s)
      // it returns false and the existing synth shot plays — so a missing file degrades
      // to the old sound instead of silence, unlike the zombie SFX where the human
      // ordered the synth retired outright.
      //
      // `trim` levels the slices to each other (ffmpeg astats peaks, 2026-09-27):
      // a0 -9.7 dB, a1 -7.5, b0 -5.8, b1 -7.8, shotgun0 -0.6 (near full scale),
      // tec90/tec91 -4.3. Pistol shots land ~0.3 peak; the shotgun ~0.55 (a boom
      // should be the loudest thing on the range); the Tec-9 lands lighter per shot
      // because its 0.13 s cooldown stacks fast.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      const GUN_SFX = {
        pistolShot: [
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/a0.wav", trim: 0.98 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/a1.wav", trim: 0.75 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/b0.wav", trim: 0.62 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/b1.wav", trim: 0.78 },
        ],
        // the deer rifle reuses the pistol pool for now: the loudest, darkest slices
        // lead so it reads as a heavier round until a dedicated sample exists
        rifleShot: [
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/b0.wav", trim: 0.8 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/b1.wav", trim: 0.95 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/a0.wav", trim: 1.0 },
        ],
        shotgun: [
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/shotgun0.wav", trim: 0.55 },
        ],
        tec9Shot: [
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/tec90.wav", trim: 0.45 },
          { path: "assets/audio/gun/tec91.wav", trim: 0.45 },
        ],
      };

      const pending = new Map();      // path -> in-flight load promise (dedupes parallel fetches)

      let prewarmed = false;
      
      function load(ctx_, path) {
        if (decoded.has(path)) return Promise.resolve(decoded.get(path));
        if (pending.has(path)) return pending.get(path);
        const p = fetch(path)

          .then((bytes) => ctx_.decodeAudioData(bytes))
          .then((buf) => { decoded.set(path, buf); pending.delete(path); return buf; })
          .catch(() => { pending.delete(path); return null; });   // missing file: the synth fallback handles it

        return p;
      }

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // weapons_3d.js — what the player is actually holding.
      //
      // WHAT WAS WRONG. The old version was a "view model": one shared pivot parked
      // near the player's shoulder (`playerPos.y + 1.1`), aimed with `lookAt`, and a
      // per-weapon hardcoded position like `activeWeapon.position.set(0.3, -0.2, 0.2)`.
      // That is a weapon placed NEXT TO a character, not held by one — it does not
      // know where the hands are, it is not a child of anything that animates, and the
      // offsets that make it look reasonable in one pose are wrong in every other.
      // That is why the bat floated beside the player and the shotgun read as
      // detached.
      //
      // WHAT REPLACES IT. Three ideas, and every weapon in the game inherits all three:
      //
      //   1. PARENTING. Every weapon is a child of the character's HAND SOCKET —
      //      `characters.js` builds one per arm at the middle of the fist. Position
      //      comes from the hand, always: the weapon cannot float, drift, or fail to
      //      follow the body through a walk, a turn, a dance clip or a melee swing,
      //      because it is inside the arm that is doing all of that. Nothing here
      //      knows or cares where the camera or the player's world position is.
      //
      //   2. A SOLVED ORIENTATION. A wrist's frame tumbles through every clip, so a gun
      //      rigidly bolted to one would point wherever the wrist happened to be. The
      //      grip node's LOCAL rotation is solved from a desired WORLD orientation each
      //      frame instead:
      //
      //          gripLocal = handWorld⁻¹ · desiredWorld · modelOffset
      //
      //      `desiredWorld` puts the weapon's +Z (its barrel axis) along the aim
      //      direction — or, for melee, leaves the weapon rigidly in the fist, which
      //      is what a bat is. So: position from the hand, orientation from the aim.
      //
      //   3. A GRIP ORIGIN. Every model below is built GRIP-AT-ORIGIN: the point the
      //      hand closes around is (0,0,0) and the barrel runs down +Z. Rotating the
      //      weapon about its own origin is therefore rotating it about the grip, so
      //      recoil kicks the muzzle while the grip stays put in the hand, and nothing
      //      ever pivots around the middle of an image.
      //
      // The muzzle is a real node at the weapon's `muzzleOffset`, so tracers, flashes
      // and shell effects can start at the end of the barrel instead of at the
      // player's navel.
      //
      // Gameplay stays in weapons.js (damage, clip, cooldown, fireMode); everything
      // about how a weapon SITS lives here. Both tables are keyed by the same id, and
      // the one field they must agree on is `hold`.
      //
      // PER-WEAPON CONFIG (the data model the task asked for, in this codebase's idiom):
      //
      //   type            melee | pistol | smg | shotgun | rifle
      //   hold            which arm pose the character uses: pistol | long | melee
      //   orient          "aim"  — barrel solved onto the aim direction (firearms)
      //                   "hand" — rigid in the fist (melee: a bat does not track a camera)
      //   twoHanded       the support hand is solved onto `foregrip` (characters.js IK)
      //   handOffset      where the grip sits inside the fist, in hand-socket space
      //   gripOffset      where the hand's grip is in MODEL space (baked into the build
      //                   so it is normally zero, but it is real per-weapon data)
      //   rotationOffset  model alignment inside the grip node
      //   scale           model scale
      //   muzzleOffset    the muzzle, in model space
      //   foregrip        the support hand's target, in grip-node space
      //   recoil          { pitch, yaw, kick, time } — a rotation about the grip
      //   layer           renderOrder, for anything that has to draw over the body
      //

      // front of the grip, or behind it, per pixel, is the depth buffer — the correct
      // answer for free, and the reason parenting alone settles what used to be a
      // sprite layering problem. `layer` is the hook for parts that must ignore depth:
      // today every weapon material is opaque and a firearm sits at 1 and a bat at 2
      // (in front of the character's merged meshes at 0), so it is a tiebreaker rather
      // than a fix-up. Nothing here reaches for a screen-space offset, because there is
      // no screen-space position to get wrong.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      import * as THREE from "three";
      import { GLTFLoader } from "three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js";
      import { SRGBColorSpace } from "three";
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- materials
      function std(name, color, extra = {}) {
        const m = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ name, color, roughness: 0.6, ...extra });

        wood: std("weapon wood", 0x6b4526, { roughness: 0.74 }),
        woodDark: std("weapon wood dark", 0x472c15, { roughness: 0.82 }),
        steel: std("weapon steel", 0x33383f, { roughness: 0.4, metalness: 0.75 }),
        black: std("weapon black", 0x15171b, { roughness: 0.52, metalness: 0.4 }),
        grip: std("weapon grip", 0x1b1d22, { roughness: 0.9 }),
        brass: std("weapon brass", 0xb99a4c, { roughness: 0.34, metalness: 0.85 }),
      };

      const _geo = new Map();

        const k = `b${w}|${h}|${d}`;

      };
      const cyl = (rt, rb, h, seg = 8) => {
        const k = `c${rt}|${rb}|${h}|${seg}`;

        const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat);
        m.position.set(x, y, z);
        if (rx || ry || rz) m.rotation.set(rx, ry, rz);

        m.frustumCulled = false;
        m.userData.noBatch = true;

        return m;
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the models
      // Every builder returns a Group whose ORIGIN IS THE GRIP POINT and whose +Z is
      // the muzzle direction. Nothing else in the file has to know a weapon's size.
      
      function makeBat() {
        const g = new THREE.Group();

        // below the origin is what the palm actually catches on, and it is what makes
        // the hand read as closed around the handle rather than floating at the end.
        part(g, box(0.05, 0.05, 0.045), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, -0.035);
        const shaft = cyl(0.046, 0.021, 0.78, 8);
        shaft.translate(0, 0.39, 0);
        shaft.rotateX(Math.PI / 2);

        part(g, cyl(0.048, 0.048, 0.02, 8), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, 0.72, Math.PI / 2, 0, 0);
        return g;
      }
      
      function makePistol() {
        const g = new THREE.Group();
        part(g, box(0.042, 0.052, 0.17), MAT.steel, 0, 0.036, 0.075);      // slide / barrel
        part(g, box(0.038, 0.026, 0.15), MAT.black, 0, 0.002, 0.065);      // frame
        part(g, box(0.036, 0.028, 0.03), MAT.black, 0, 0.03, -0.012);      // rear sight block
        const grip = part(g, box(0.036, 0.115, 0.048), MAT.grip, 0, -0.052, -0.028);
        grip.rotation.x = -0.3;                                            // angled back into the palm
        part(g, box(0.026, 0.05, 0.012), MAT.steel, 0, -0.03, 0.026);      // trigger
        return g;
      }
      
      function makeTec9() {
        const g = new THREE.Group();
        part(g, box(0.045, 0.055, 0.28), MAT.black, 0, 0.04, 0.13);        // long receiver
        part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.1), MAT.steel, 0, 0.042, 0.3);           // barrel shroud
        part(g, box(0.032, 0.14, 0.05), MAT.black, 0, -0.06, 0.09);        // magazine
        part(g, box(0.03, 0.05, 0.04), MAT.grip, 0, -0.02, 0.2);           // foregrip
        const grip = part(g, box(0.034, 0.1, 0.045), MAT.grip, 0, -0.048, -0.02);
        grip.rotation.x = -0.28;
        return g;
      }
      
      function makeSawnoff() {
        const g = new THREE.Group();
        part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.36), MAT.steel, -0.019, 0.052, 0.16);    // left barrel
        part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.36), MAT.steel, 0.019, 0.052, 0.16);     // right barrel
        part(g, box(0.062, 0.04, 0.1), MAT.wood, 0, 0.042, -0.02);         // breech
        part(g, box(0.05, 0.036, 0.16), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0.03, 0.13);      // forend

      function makeDeerRifle() {

        part(g, box(0.034, 0.034, 0.62), MAT.steel, 0, 0.045, 0.28);       // long barrel
        part(g, box(0.05, 0.05, 0.2), MAT.wood, 0, 0.03, -0.02);           // receiver / stock wrist
        part(g, box(0.046, 0.075, 0.26), MAT.wood, 0, 0.005, -0.24);       // stock
        part(g, box(0.03, 0.06, 0.09), MAT.wood, 0, 0.012, 0.16);          // forend
        part(g, box(0.012, 0.026, 0.012), MAT.black, 0, 0.068, 0.03);      // rear sight

      const BUILDERS = {
        bat: { build: makeBat },
        pistol: { build: makePistol },
        tec9: { build: makeTec9 },
        sawnoff: { build: makeSawnoff },
        deerRifle: { build: makeDeerRifle },

      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ the GLB
      // The gangster-rifle glTF still stands in for the deer rifle when it loads
      // (assets/models/weapons/gangster_rifle). Its raw bounding box is ~0.70 × 3.79 ×
      // 14.33 units, so it has to be measured rather than guessed at — the old
      // hardcoded `scale 0.05` was luck, not a fit — and, because the file does not
      // come with a grip marker, it is then shifted so that the point a hand would
      // hold (about a third of the way back from the muzzle) lands on the origin, the
      // same place the procedural models put their grip.
      // Authored GLB stand-ins for the procedural builds below. `gripAt` is where
      // along the model's long axis (0 = tail, 1 = muzzle) the hand actually closes —
      // measured, not guessed, the same way the deer rifle's was — so the model lands
      // grip-at-origin like every procedural build does.
      // mac10/shotgun are new (Styloo pack, 2026-09-27): the tec-9 and sawn-off had
      // no authored model before this and stay on the procedural build until a real
      // browser look confirms `rotY`/`gripAt`. deerRifle keeps its own long-approved
      // gangster_rifle look untouched.
      const GLB_SKINS = {
        deerRifle: { url: "assets/models/weapons/gangster_rifle/scene.gltf", length: 0.95, gripAt: 0.34, rotY: Math.PI },
        tec9: { url: "assets/models/weapons/styloo/mac10.glb", length: 0.5, gripAt: 0.4, rotY: Math.PI },
        sawnoff: { url: "assets/models/weapons/styloo/shotgun.glb", length: 0.85, gripAt: 0.32, rotY: Math.PI },

      function loadGlbSkins() {

        // fetch-based GLTFLoader cannot resolve it. Keep the procedural weapon there;

        if (typeof document === "undefined" || !document.baseURI) return;

      /**

       * carries, because it is the one the character rig has to agree on.

          // the camera (see `meleeAim` below): cocked back over the shoulder at rest,
          // swept down and through on the strike. It is deliberately NOT aimed at the
          // crosshair — a bat is not a sighting device — and NOT left rigid in the
          // wrist either, because the wrist tumbles through every walk and dance clip
          // and a bat bolted to it would wave around on its own. rotationOffset is
          // identity: the model's +z IS the bat, so the solved direction is the bat.
          type: "melee", hold: "melee", orient: "melee", twoHanded: false,
          handOffset: [0, 0.005, 0.01], gripOffset: [0, 0, 0], rotationOffset: [0, 0, 0],
          scale: 1, muzzleOffset: [0, 0, 0.78], foregrip: null,
          recoil: { pitch: 0.5, yaw: 0.1, kick: 0.03, time: 0.3 }, layer: 2,
        },
        pistol: {
          type: "pistol", hold: "pistol", orient: "aim", twoHanded: false,
          handOffset: [0, 0.0, 0.0], gripOffset: [0, 0, 0], rotationOffset: [0, 0, 0],
          scale: 1, muzzleOffset: [0, 0.036, 0.17], foregrip: null,
          recoil: { pitch: 0.34, yaw: 0.08, kick: 0.035, time: 0.2 }, layer: 1,
        },
        tec9: {
          type: "smg", hold: "long", orient: "aim", twoHanded: true,
          handOffset: [0, 0.0, -0.02], gripOffset: [0, 0, 0], rotationOffset: [0, 0, 0],
          // foregrip is the FOREGRIP/forend modelled in the build above, measured from
          // the grip — and it is also the one distance the support arm has to be able
          // to reach across to, so it is kept near the weapon's actual forend rather
          // than slid forward for looks. weapon_hold_test.mjs measures that reach.
          scale: 1, muzzleOffset: [0, 0.042, 0.35], foregrip: [0, -0.02, 0.20],
          recoil: { pitch: 0.22, yaw: 0.14, kick: 0.03, time: 0.12 }, layer: 1,
        },
        sawnoff: {
          type: "shotgun", hold: "long", orient: "aim", twoHanded: true,
          handOffset: [0, 0.0, -0.03], gripOffset: [0, 0, 0], rotationOffset: [0, 0, 0],
          scale: 1, muzzleOffset: [0, 0.052, 0.35], foregrip: [0, 0.02, 0.16],
          recoil: { pitch: 0.6, yaw: 0.1, kick: 0.075, time: 0.4 }, layer: 1,
        },
        deerRifle: {
          type: "rifle", hold: "long", orient: "aim", twoHanded: true,
          handOffset: [0, 0.0, -0.03], gripOffset: [0, 0, 0], rotationOffset: [0, 0, 0],
          scale: 1, muzzleOffset: [0, 0.045, 0.6], foregrip: [0, 0.012, 0.16],
          recoil: { pitch: 0.5, yaw: 0.08, kick: 0.06, time: 0.5 }, layer: 1,
        },
      });
      
      const FALLBACK = "pistol";
      const rigFor = (id) => WEAPON_RIGS[id] || WEAPON_RIGS[FALLBACK];
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------ the melee arc
      // Where a bat points, through the swing. Measured in the BODY's vertical plane
      // as an elevation off horizontal-forward: positive is up. ~125° is up and behind
      // the shoulder (cocked); the strike carries it down to ~+20°, level and forward,
      // which is the point in a swing that actually connects.
      //
      // This lives here rather than in characters.js because it is the WEAPON's angle,
      // the same as a gun's barrel direction — the arm only decides where the fist is.
      // The two are animated to the same clock (`attack`), so they read as one swing.
      const MELEE_REST = 2.44;      // rad, ~140°: laid back over the shoulder
      const MELEE_SWEEP = 1.92;     // rad, ~110° of arc, down to ~30° above horizontal
      // The bat also leans OUT of the body's sagittal plane, on the side the gun hand
      // is on. Without it the bat is coplanar with the spine, and a 0.78 m handle
      // resting on a shoulder passes through the head on its way back. (Every
      // character in the game is right-handed: `side` +1 is the support arm and the
      // weapon hangs off the −x shoulder — see characters.js.)

      const _goal = new THREE.Vector3(), _tmp = new THREE.Vector3();
      const WORLD_UP = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
      
      const rig = {
        scene: null,
        actor: null,
        hand: null,
        grip: null,          // child of the hand: position = handOffset, orientation = solved
        recoil: null,        // recoil / reload: rotates about the GRIP, never about the model centre
        model: null,         // the current weapon model, grip at its origin
        muzzle: null,        // Object3D at muzzleOffset, for effect origins
        id: null,
        def: null,
        anim: { type: "idle", time: 0, duration: 0 },

      /**

       * belongs in the scene graph at boot. Keeping the signature means main.js's
       * existing call site does not have to change, and keeping weapons OUT of the

       * boot, and a mesh it cannot see is a mesh it cannot merge into a batch.

      export function initWeapons3D(scene) {
        rig.scene = scene || rig.scene;
        if (!_glbSkinsLoading) { _glbSkinsLoading = true; loadGlbSkins(); }
      }

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // fpsview.js — the first-person view model: the gun in your hands (zombie mode).
      //
      // The third-person weapon is welded to the character's hand (weapons_3d.js), and in first
      // person the character is hidden, so the gun would go with it. This holds a second copy of the
      // weapon's model in front of the camera instead: lower right, barrel forward, drawn on top of
      // the world. It kicks back and pitches up when you fire, dips for a reload, bobs as you walk,
      // and a bat swings across the screen.
      //
      //   const view = createFpsView({ scene, camera });
      //   view.update({ dt, active, weaponId, holstered, moving, sprinting })   // after the camera has moved
      //   view.fire(melee)  /  view.reload(seconds)
      //   view.muzzle(out)  -> the barrel's world position (tracers and flashes start here), or null
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      import * as THREE from "three";
      import { createViewmodel } from "./weapons_3d.js";
      
      // where each weapon rests, in camera space (+x right, +y up, -z forward), and its resting pitch
      const POSE = {
        pistol:    { p: [0.17, -0.17, -0.5], pitch: 0.02 },
        tec9:      { p: [0.18, -0.18, -0.54], pitch: 0.02 },
        sawnoff:   { p: [0.19, -0.2, -0.56], pitch: 0.02 },
        deerRifle: { p: [0.19, -0.21, -0.6], pitch: 0.02 },
        bat:       { p: [0.26, -0.22, -0.55], pitch: -0.55 },
      };
      
      export function createFpsView({ scene, camera }) {
        const holder = new THREE.Group();          // world-space, re-posed from the camera every frame
        holder.visible = false;
        holder.name = "fpsView";
        scene.add(holder);
        let ads = 0;
        let id = null, vm = null, kick = 0, kickMax = 0.1, swing = 0, dip = 0, dipDur = 1, bob = 0;
        const q = new THREE.Quaternion(), turn = new THREE.Quaternion().setFromAxisAngle(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), Math.PI);
        const off = new THREE.Vector3(), pitchQ = new THREE.Quaternion(), rollQ = new THREE.Quaternion();
        const X = new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0), Z = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 1);
      
        function select(weaponId) {
          if (id === weaponId && vm) return;
          if (vm) holder.remove(vm.model);
          id = weaponId;
          vm = createViewmodel(weaponId);
          holder.add(vm.model);
          kickMax = vm.def.recoil.kick * 2.2 + 0.03;
        }
      
        return {
          update({ dt, active, weaponId, holstered = false, moving = false, sprinting = false, aiming = false }) {
            if (!active || holstered) { holder.visible = false; return; }
            select(weaponId);
            holder.visible = true;
            kick = Math.max(0, kick - dt / Math.max(0.08, vm.def.recoil.time));
            swing = Math.max(0, swing - dt / 0.42);
            dip = Math.max(0, dip - dt);
            bob += dt * (moving ? (sprinting ? 12 : 8) : 2);
            const amp = moving ? (sprinting ? 0.016 : 0.010) : 0.002;
            const pose = POSE[weaponId] || POSE.pistol;
            const melee = vm.def.type === "melee";
            ads += ((aiming && !melee ? 1 : 0) - ads) * (1 - Math.exp(-14 * dt));
      
            // camera-space offset: rest pose + walk bob + recoil (pushed back toward the eye)
            const bobK = 1 - ads * 0.85;                       // down the sights it barely sways
            off.set(pose.p[0] * (1 - ads * 0.92) + Math.sin(bob * 0.5) * amp * bobK, pose.p[1] + (-0.105 - pose.p[1]) * ads + Math.abs(Math.sin(bob * 0.5)) * amp * 1.4 * bobK, pose.p[2] + (-0.42 - pose.p[2]) * ads);
            off.z += kick * kickMax;
            off.y -= kick * kickMax * 0.25;
            let pitch = pose.pitch + kick * vm.def.recoil.pitch * 0.5;
            let roll = 0;
            if (dip > 0) {                                   // reload: the gun drops out of frame and comes back
              const t = 1 - dip / dipDur, k = Math.sin(Math.min(1, t) * Math.PI);
              off.y -= 0.22 * k; pitch += 0.5 * k;
            }
            if (melee && swing > 0) {                        // the bat: cocked, then across and down
              const t = 1 - swing, wind = Math.min(1, t / 0.28), strike = t < 0.28 ? 0 : (t - 0.28) / 0.72;
              pitch = pose.pitch - 0.5 * Math.sin(wind * Math.PI) + 1.4 * Math.sin(strike * Math.PI);
              roll = -0.9 * Math.sin(strike * Math.PI);
              off.x -= 0.34 * Math.sin(strike * Math.PI);
            }
            if (sprinting && moving && !melee) { pitch += 0.12; off.y -= 0.03; }   // low-ready while running
      
            // into world space: camera orientation, barrel turned to -z, then the pitch and roll
            camera.updateMatrixWorld(true);
            holder.position.copy(off).applyMatrix4(camera.matrixWorld);
            q.copy(camera.quaternion).multiply(turn);
            pitchQ.setFromAxisAngle(X, -pitch);
            rollQ.setFromAxisAngle(Z, roll);
            holder.quaternion.copy(q).multiply(pitchQ).multiply(rollQ);
            holder.updateMatrixWorld(true);
          },
          fire(melee, recoilMul = 1) { if (melee) swing = 1; else kick = 1 * recoilMul; },
          reload(seconds) { dipDur = Math.max(0.3, seconds || 1); dip = dipDur; },
          /** The barrel's world position, or null when nothing is showing. */
          muzzle(out) {
            if (!holder.visible || !vm) return null;
            vm.muzzle.updateWorldMatrix(true, false);
            return out.setFromMatrixPosition(vm.muzzle.matrixWorld);
          },
          get visible() { return holder.visible; },
        };
      }

        function noiseBuffer(a, seconds, shape) {
          const len = Math.floor(a.sampleRate * seconds);
          const buf = a.createBuffer(1, len, a.sampleRate);
          const d = buf.getChannelData(0);
          for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) d[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * shape(i / len);
          return buf;

        function sfx(kind, volume = 1) {
          if (muted() || skipping) return;
          const a = audio();
          if (!a) return;
          const t = a.currentTime;
          // Recorded gunshots (assets/audio/gun/, 2026-09-27) take the shot when they
          // are loaded; until prewarm finishes, or if a file is missing, the
          // synthesised voice below still fires — a missing sample degrades to the

          if (kind === "shotgun" || kind === "pistolShot" || kind === "tec9Shot" || kind === "rifleShot") {
            prewarmGunAudio(a);

          const out = a.createGain();

          out.connect(a.destination);

            const src = a.createBufferSource();
            src.buffer = noiseBuffer(a, 0.35, (p) => Math.pow(1 - p, 6));
            const lp = a.createBiquadFilter();
            lp.type = "lowpass";
            lp.frequency.setValueAtTime(900, t);
            lp.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(200, t + 0.8);
            const peq = a.createBiquadFilter();
            peq.type = "peaking";
            peq.frequency.value = 140; // far shots lose the bass thump
            peq.Q.value = 0.8;
            peq.gain.value = 0;
            out.gain.value *= 0.35;
            src.connect(lp).connect(peq).connect(out);
            src.start(t);
          } else if (kind === "static") {
            const src = a.createBufferSource();
            src.buffer = noiseBuffer(a, 0.4, () => 0.5);
            const bp = a.createBiquadFilter();

            out.gain.value *= 0.4;
            src.connect(bp).connect(out);

          } else if (kind === "siren") {
            const o = a.createOscillator();
            o.type = "sawtooth";
            for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
              o.frequency.setValueAtTime(620, t + i * 0.4);
              o.frequency.linearRampToValueAtTime(980, t + i * 0.4 + 0.2);

                g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.15, t + r * 0.55 + 0.38);
