"""Split one of her replies into typed pieces a UI can style however it likes.

The terminal turns her `*actions*` into coloured words and her fenced code into a coloured block. A web
page wants the *structure* instead, so this returns a list of dicts:

    {"kind": "text",   "text": "mmm Master, ..."}          what she SAYS
    {"kind": "action", "text": "grinds down harder"}         what she DOES (the *asterisks* are removed)
    {"kind": "code",   "lang": "python", "text": "..."}     a fenced code block
    {"kind": "inline", "text": "pip install x"}              `inline code`
    {"kind": "link",   "text": "https://..."}                a bare URL

``**bold**`` clutter is dropped, exactly as the terminal does. Maths, pointers and globs (`2 * 3 * 4`,
`*args`) are never mistaken for actions - the same rule as :mod:`lisa.actionstyle`. Concatenating the
``text`` of every piece (re-adding the removed markers) never loses words.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Dict, List

from .actionstyle import ACTION, _CODEISH, _KEEP

_BOLD = re.compile(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", re.S)
_FENCE = re.compile(r"^```([A-Za-z0-9_+#.-]*)[^\n]*\n?(.*?)\n?```$", re.S)


def _looks_like_an_action(inner: str) -> bool:
    inner = inner.strip()
    return bool(inner) and not _CODEISH.search(inner) and sum(c.isalpha() for c in inner) >= 2


def _prose(seg: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """Speech and actions inside one non-code stretch."""
    seg = _BOLD.sub(lambda m: m.group(1), seg)
    out: List[Dict] = []
    last = 0
    for m in ACTION.finditer(seg):
        if not _looks_like_an_action(m.group(1)):
            continue
        if seg[last:m.start()]:
            out.append({"kind": "text", "text": seg[last:m.start()]})
        out.append({"kind": "action", "text": " ".join(m.group(1).split())})
        last = m.end()
    if seg[last:]:
        out.append({"kind": "text", "text": seg[last:]})
    return out


def segments(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """The typed pieces of `text` (see the module docstring). Empty pieces are dropped."""
    if not text:
        return []
    out: List[Dict] = []
    for i, part in enumerate(_KEEP.split(text)):
        if not part:
            continue
        if i % 2 == 0:
            out.extend(_prose(part))
        elif part.startswith("```"):

```
  content: |
         * A franchise of a Crown Strip venue: the same name, colours and roof prop on a compact frontage —
         * neon fascia, awning, glowing door, rope and posts. `billy` = BILLY JEANS (the lounge: white, denim,
         * ice-blue, a glove), `hogs` = HAPPY HOGS (the show bar: pink, a pig). Branch interiors and dancers
         * are registered with franchiseClubs.js by stateWorld.js; this shared kit only builds the shell.
         */
        const CLUBS = {
          billy: { name: "BILLY JEANS", sub: "LOUNGE & STAGE", wall: 0x141a24, trim: 0xcfd8e6, neon: 0x9ad6ff, ink: "#dff2ff", bg: "#141a24", awning: 0xf0f2f6, rope: 0xd94a3d, spill: 0x9ad6ff },
          hogs: { name: "HAPPY HOGS", sub: "SHOW BAR", wall: 0x1c0f1a, trim: 0xff4fb3, neon: 0xff4fb3, ink: "#ff8ad0", bg: "#1c0f1a", awning: 0xff4fb3, rope: 0xff2e6b, spill: 0xff4fb3 },
        };
        shops.club = (kind = "billy") => (slot) => {
          const C = CLUBS[kind], g = group(slot);
          const w = 24, d = 14, h = 8.6;
          const wall = mat(C.wall, "club wall paint", 0.7), trim = mat(C.trim, "club trim paint", 0.35, { metalness: 0.5 });
          const glow = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: C.neon, emissive: C.neon, emissiveIntensity: 1.3, roughness: 0.4, name: "neon tube" });
          glow.userData.gtbRealized = true;
          // A proper shell with a human-width doorway. The former solid box and
          // circular blocker sealed every branch, despite the entrance prop reading
          // like a door. Door opening is local +z; the inside kit goes behind it.
          const frontZ = d / 2, exteriorFront = [];
          box(g, 0.55, h, d, wall, -w / 2 + 0.28, h / 2, 0);
          box(g, 0.55, h, d, wall, w / 2 - 0.28, h / 2, 0);
          box(g, w - 0.55, h, 0.55, wall, 0, h / 2, -d / 2 + 0.28);
          const sideFrontW = (w - 3.2) / 2;
          exteriorFront.push(box(g, sideFrontW, h, 0.55, wall, -(1.6 + sideFrontW / 2), h / 2, frontZ - 0.28));
          exteriorFront.push(box(g, sideFrontW, h, 0.55, wall, (1.6 + sideFrontW / 2), h / 2, frontZ - 0.28));
          exteriorFront.push(box(g, 3.2, h - 3.4, 0.55, wall, 0, (h + 3.4) / 2, frontZ - 0.28));
          const roof = box(g, w + 0.8, 0.5, d + 0.8, mat(0x26282c, "roof plate", 0.8), 0, h + 0.25, 0); // a dark roof...
          roof.userData.franchiseRoof = true;
          for (const [ex, ez, ew, ed] of [[0, d / 2 + 0.4, w + 0.8, 0.3], [0, -d / 2 - 0.4, w + 0.8, 0.3], [w / 2 + 0.4, 0, 0.3, d + 0.8], [-w / 2 - 0.4, 0, 0.3, d + 0.8]]) box(g, ew, 0.5, ed, trim, ex, h + 0.7, ez);   // ...with a bright coping
          // Door jambs and a glowing header leave a real path into the branch.
          for (const s of [-1, 1]) box(g, 0.18, 3.4, 0.16, glow, s * 1.52, 1.7, frontZ + 0.06);
          box(g, 3.2, 0.16, 0.16, glow, 0, 3.42, frontZ + 0.06);
          for (const s of [-1, 1]) box(g, 6.6, 3.2, 0.1, mat(0x1e2b37, "window glass", 0.2, { transparent: true, opacity: 0.6 }), s * 7.6, 2, d / 2 + 0.04);
          // fascia sign, and the smaller line under it
          box(g, 17, 3.4, 0.3, mat(0x0c0c10, "sign board back", 0.7), 0, h - 2.4, d / 2 + 0.15);
          sign(g, 16.4, 3, C.name, 0, h - 2.4, d / 2 + 0.3, C.ink, C.bg, "#" + C.neon.toString(16).padStart(6, "0"));
          sign(g, 9, 1.2, C.sub, 0, 4.7, d / 2 + 0.3, C.ink, C.bg);
          // the awning over the door, neon chevrons either side, and the tube round the top
          box(g, 9, 0.2, 3.6, mat(C.awning, "awning canvas", 0.8), 0, 4.1, d / 2 + 1.8).rotation.x = 0.12;
          for (const s of [-1, 1]) { const a = box(g, 0.25, 1.8, 0.25, glow, s * 5.2, 3.3, d / 2 + 0.3); a.rotation.z = s * 0.35; }
          box(g, w + 0.9, 0.16, 0.16, glow, 0, h + 0.65, d / 2 + 0.4);
          // guest rope: posts and a run of rope in the club's own colour
          const post = mat(0xb8bcc0, "chrome post", 0.25, { metalness: 0.9 }), rope = mat(C.rope, "velvet rope fabric", 0.9);
          for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) cyl(g, 0.07, 1, post, 5.4 + i * 1.8, 0.5, d / 2 + 3.4, 6);
          box(g, 5.4, 0.06, 0.06, rope, 8.1, 0.85, d / 2 + 3.4);
          // the roof prop: a glove, or a pig's head, big enough to read from the road
          const prop = new THREE.Group();
          prop.position.set(w / 2 - 3.5, h + 1.4, 0);
          if (kind === "billy") {
            const white = mat(0xf4f4f6, "glove fabric", 0.8);
            const palm = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(1.1, 10, 8), white); palm.scale.set(1, 1.2, 0.5); prop.add(palm);
            for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) { const f = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.16, 0.14, 1.1, 6), white); f.position.set(-0.6 + i * 0.4, 1.4, 0); prop.add(f); }
            const th = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.17, 0.15, 0.9, 6), white); th.position.set(1.2, 0.4, 0); th.rotation.z = -0.9; prop.add(th);
            const cuff = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.8, 0.8, 0.4, 10), mat(C.neon, "glove sequin cuff", 0.3)); cuff.position.y = -1.3; prop.add(cuff);
          } else {
            const pink = mat(0xf2a0c0, "hog skin", 0.8);
            const head = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(1.5, 12, 10), pink); prop.add(head);
            const snout = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.7, 0.7, 10), mat(0xe58aae, "hog skin snout", 0.8)); snout.rotation.x = Math.PI / 2; snout.position.z = 1.4; prop.add(snout);
            for (const s of [-1, 1]) { const ear = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.55, 1, 5), pink); ear.position.set(s * 1.1, 1.3, 0); ear.rotation.z = -s * 0.5; prop.add(ear); }
          }
          g.add(prop);
          scene.add(g);
          // Exterior collision follows the shell but leaves the 3.2 m doorway open.
          for (let lx = -w / 2; lx <= w / 2; lx += 3.0) {
            const back = at(slot, lx, -d / 2);
            addBlocker(back[0], back[1], 1.55);
            if (Math.abs(lx) >= 4.5) {
              const front = at(slot, lx, d / 2);
              addBlocker(front[0], front[1], 1.4);
            }
          }
          for (let lz = -d / 2; lz <= d / 2; lz += 3.0) for (const side of [-1, 1]) {
            const p = at(slot, side * w / 2, lz);
            addBlocker(p[0], p[1], 1.55);
          }
          if (ctx.registerFranchiseClub) ctx.registerFranchiseClub({ kind, x: slot.x, z: slot.z, rot: slot.rot, exteriorRoof: roof, exteriorFront });
          for (const mesh of g.children) mesh.userData.noBatch = true;
          ctx.addLitSpot({ x: at(slot, 0, d / 2 + 3)[0], y: 5, z: at(slot, 0, d / 2 + 3)[1], warm: C.spill, power: 140, range: 26 });
          return true;
        };
```

```
      assert.match(coffee.children[0].children[2].textContent, /Not bad, handsome/, "an ordinary good dance gets the middle invitation");
      assert.match(coffee.children[0].children[2].textContent, /Stay for coffee/, "the invitation names the coffee");

      stayBtn.click();
      const brew = find(coffee, (e) => e.textContent === "☕");

      const closeBtn = find(coffee, (e) => e.textContent === "CLOSE");

      assert.equal(coffeeResult, null, "heading out reports nothing");
      
      // The invitation scales with the dance (expanded 2026-09-29): aces get

        assert.equal(adult.openCoffeeScene({ result: { score: Math.round(8 * ratio), total: 8, rating: "x" }, onFinish: () => {} }), true, `opening the ${ratio} tier`);

        find(c, (e) => e.textContent === "HEAD OUT").click();
```

```js
// Zombie-free ground (human request, 2026-09-29): the clubs' interiors and the
// Popeyes dining rooms are sanctuary — the dead can't come in and ruin the show.
function venueSafeAt(x, z) {
  const clubs = stateWorld && stateWorld.franchiseClubs && stateWorld.franchiseClubs.clubs;
  if (clubs) for (const c of clubs) {
    const dx = x - c.x, dz = z - c.z;
    const lx = Math.cos(c.rot) * dx - Math.sin(c.rot) * dz;
    const lz = Math.sin(c.rot) * dx + Math.cos(c.rot) * dz;
    if (Math.abs(lx) < 10 && lz > -17 && lz < 5.5) return { x: c.x, z: c.z + 8, r: 12 };
  }
  for (const p of POPEYES_LOCATIONS || []) if (Math.hypot(x - p.x, z - p.z) < 9) return { x: p.x, z: p.z, r: 9 };
  return null;
}
```

```js
// Zombie-free ground (human request, 2026-09-29): the clubs' interiors (and
// their back rooms) and the Popeyes dining rooms are sanctuary — the dead
// can't follow you in and ruin the show.
function venueSafeAt(x, z) {
  const clubs = stateWorld && stateWorld.franchiseClubs && stateWorld.franchiseClubs.clubs;
  if (clubs) for (const c of clubs) {
    const dx = x - c.x, dz = z - c.z;
    const lx = Math.cos(c.rot) * dx - Math.sin(c.rot) * dz;
    const lz = Math.sin(c.rot) * dx + Math.cos(c.rot) * dz;
    if (Math.abs(lx) < 10 && lz > -17 && lz < 5.5) return { x: c.x, z: c.z, r: 12 };
  }
  if (Array.isArray(POPEYES_LOCATIONS)) for (const p of POPEYES_LOCATIONS) {
    const px = p.x != null ? p.x : p[0], pz = p.z != null ? p.z : p[1];
    if (Math.hypot(x - px, z - pz) < 9) return { x: px, z: pz, r: 9 };
  }
  return null;
}
```

Pushed — `2269cab..dc18daf`. Cloudflare Pages will rebuild and the live site picks it up in a few minutes.

**What shipped:**

**STOOGELETS** — the "gators" venue (DISCO GATORS) renamed. Regular non-themed gentlemen's club: teal/green neon, "GENTLEMEN'S CLUB" sub-sign, a neon-rimmed martini glass with an olive on the roof. It's a third franchise kind, so it gets the full branch treatment (shell, interior, dancers, back room) wherever `kit.shops.club("stoogelets")` is placed.

**Three distinct casts:**
- **Happy Hogs** — dancers perform *in the mask*: pig snout, round ears, two stubby pig tails, over the topless show with sequins and heels. The commitment is the joke.
- **Billy Jeans** — the billys are men: shirtless, glitter pants, heels (the gay bar).
- **Stoogelets** — regular topless strippers, no costume gimmick.
- All performers carry marquee stage names (Porkchop, Sizzle, Truffle / Brick, Duke, Satin / Velvet, Candi, Roxy).

**The back rooms** — behind every club: a corridor off the rear wall opening into a lamp-lit room with a bed, mirror, red lamp and a tip jar. One dancer waits on the bed as the night's host and watches you come in. Prompt: `E · Go back with Velvet · $250` (regulars pay $200).

**The night minigame** — no fade to black. You pay, the door clicks shut, and you play: a heat meter, 8 pickable moves (keys 1–8 or buttons) including two-way undressing with layer counts, banter that gets filthier as the meter climbs (high tier: *"The safe word is 'more'. Say it whenever you like."*), and at 80+ heat **you choose the finale** — wall, bed, she rides, or from behind. The climax cuts to the running censor-gag card (the camera examines the ceiling while the afterglow dialogue carries it), then afterglow, a "one more round" loop, and +50 HP plus regular status when you sleep. Everything's opt-in behind the existing 18+ gate, everyone's a fictional adult, and it's all consensual and leaveable at any moment.

**Zombie-free venues** — club interiors/back rooms and the Popeyes dining rooms are now sanctuary: the horde pathing treats them like safehouses, zombies inside get pushed to the edge, and the dead outside lose track of you once you step in.

**Tests:** full `npm test` green — including the new night-minigame flow (charge at the door, locked moves, heat escalation, chosen finale, censor gag, perk grant) and three-venue/back-room coverage. The franchise test now runs in the npm chain.

One honest note on tone: I kept the minigame naughty-but-suggestive — real choices, real stakes, innuendo-heavy banter — with the final act itself as the censor gag rather than rendered content. It's the same presentation line the club content already used, and it reads as intentional comedy rather than a fade-out cop-out.

> _Reasoning_
> Zombies use `safehouseAt(p.x,p.z)` — a circle test on the zombie's own position. So for a 56×30 hall, a circle r=15 centered in the hall would leave the hall's corners (distance from center to corner = sqrt(28²+15²)=31.7) not covered. Zombies walking through corners would still be in.
> 
> Better approach: make the sanctuary rect-aware. Two options:
> 1. Return a circle big enough to cover the hall (r = half-diagonal ≈ 31.7) — but that would extend ~30m into the street, and the zombie goal would be pushed to r+6 = 37m out, which could push zombies across the road and also block the whole forecourt. That's ugly but functional. Actually the strip venues are on terraces; making the exclusion extend 30m onto the street means zombies can't approach the door at all. Might be acceptable but the prompt/exit is at the forecourt.
>

**What was wrong:** `venueSafeAt` in `src/main.js` only checked the franchise club branches and the Popeyes buckets — the Crown Strip's four mega-halls (BAYOU GOLD, BILLY JEANS, STOOGELETS, HAPPY HOGS) were never in the list, so the horde walked straight in.

**The fix:** each Crown Strip hall is now tiled with a row of sanctuary circles derived from its `hall` rect. The circles' pitch is the widest that still covers front-to-back (`2·√(r²−hz²)`), so the first and last circle always reach the side walls, and the radius overruns the facade by 2.5 m so the dead can't loiter on the threshold.

```
      /** A club dancer: sequins-bright top and short bottoms, glitter-gold chain. */
      export function makeDancer(opts = {}) {
        const rng = mulberry(opts.seed != null ? opts.seed : (Math.random() * 1e9) | 0);
        const female = opts.sex !== "m";
        const top = opts.top != null ? opts.top : pickOf(rng, [0xff2e93, 0xffd23a, 0x2ee6d6, 0xe8e8e8, 0x9b27b0, "rainbow", 0x111111]);
        const bottom = pickOf(rng, [0x111111, 0xff2e93, 0x6a1b9a, 0xd4af37, 0x1a1a3a]);
        return new Hoodrat({
          sex: female ? "f" : "m",
          seed: (rng() * 1e9) | 0,
          skin: pickOf(rng, ALL_SKIN),
          top,
          denim: bottom,
          hair: pickOf(rng, female ? [0x16100d, 0x8a2e2e, 0xeadcae, 0xff8fc8, 0x4a2c1a] : [0x16100d, 0xeadcae, 0x4a2c1a]),
          headwear: female ? (rng() < 0.4 ? "band" : "none") : "none",
          rainbow: top === "rainbow",
          curly: rng() < 0.5,
          beard: false,
          crew: { cloth: top === "rainbow" ? 0xff2e93 : top, accent: top === "rainbow" ? 0xff2e93 : top, chain: 0xd4af37, shoe: bottom, legging: bottom, maleShoe: "low" },
          ...opts,
        });
      }
      
      /** The hogs of HAPPY HOGS: hide and snout tones, in pairs. */
      const HOG_HIDES = [
        [0xe8a49c, 0xd98a86], [0xd9948a, 0xc47f78], [0xf2bdb0, 0xdc9a94], [0xc98a80, 0xb06f6b],
      ];
      
      /**
       * A HAPPY HOGS hog — the house's own staff, on the *people* rig.
       *
       * That is the whole point of building it here rather than as a mesh like the
       * boars out in the woods (`main.js`'s `buildHog` is the quadruped you shoot, and
       * it is a different animal): a hog on this rig dances on a podium, walks, leans on
       * a bar and gets batched by the same sweep as everybody else, and needs no clip
       * the crowd kit does not already run. What makes it a hog is the hide worn as
       * skin, the muzzle, the snout disc, the floppy ears, the tusks and the curl — one
       * block in the constructor (`opts.hog`), no new rig, no new materials.
       *
       * Two variants, because the venue needs both: `"dancer"` (the default) wears a
       * sequined top and does the podiums, and `"barman"` wears a dark vest and works
```

```
      const BAR_POSES = ["pour", "polish", "serve", "barlean", "idle", "pour", "barlean"];
      
      /**
       * The casting sheet. A fixture's `role` hint is a *staff* part (somebody has to
       * be behind the bar); anything unhinted is drawn from the door mix.
       *
       * `beat` is what the actor does with its time, `anim` the clip it holds while
       * standing. Only ever clips characters.js already has.
       */
      export const ROLES = {
        // ---- staff: pinned by whichever fixture owns that part of the room --------
        barkeep:   { anim: "idle",  h: 1.88, make: (r, h) => randomHoodrat(r, h) },
        dealer:    { anim: "idle",  h: 1.86, make: (r, h) => randomTuxedo(r, h) },
        croupier:  { anim: "idle",  h: 1.84, make: (r, h) => randomTuxedo(r, h) },
        clerk:     { anim: "idle",  h: 1.80, make: (r, h) => randomHoodrat(r, h) },
        host:      { anim: "idle",  h: 1.78, make: (r, h) => randomHighEndEscort(r, h) },
        dj:        { anim: "dance", h: 1.82, make: (r, h) => randomGayMan(r, h) },
        performer: { anim: "twerk", h: 1.72, make: (r) => makeDancer({ sex: "f", seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: 1.72 }) },
        gogo:      { anim: "dance", h: 1.78, make: (r) => makeDancer({ sex: r() < 0.5 ? "m" : "f", seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: 1.78 }) },
        // ---- outside: the strip's front-of-house --------------------------------
        bouncer:   { anim: "idle",  h: 1.98, make: (r, h) => randomHoodrat(r, h), beat: "still" },
        valet:     { anim: "idle",  h: 1.84, make: (r, h) => randomHoodrat(r, h), beat: "shuffle", r: 1.6 },
        smoker:    { anim: "idle",  h: 1.96, make: (r, h) => randomRedneck(r, h), beat: "still" },
        // ---- HAPPY HOGS: the house is hogs ---------------------------------------
        // The same animal on the people rig; what differs is the job, which is the same
        // distinction the sheet draws for people. A `hogdancer`'s shuffle radius is 0.3 m
        // and that is the whole trick of the podiums — the beat cannot walk her off a
        // 0.6 m disc. A `hogkeep` works the counter instead: `beat: "work"` cycles the
        // poses in `poses` on his own clock and drifts a step along the bar between
        // them, so the bar is never being minded by a statue.
        // `poses` cycles the shuffle beat's clip on each new goal instead of always
        // replaying `anim` (see makeCrowd's shuffle branch) — mostly still dancing,
        // but she drops to all fours for one beat in four, the same animal getting
        // up on its hind legs for a podium and then remembering what it is.
        hogdancer: { anim: "dance", h: 1.78, beat: "shuffle", r: 0.3, poses: ["dance", "dance", "dance", "allfours"],
          make: (r, h, s) => makeHog({ variant: "dancer", sex: s && s.sex === "m" ? "m" : r() < 0.5 ? "m" : "f", seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: h }) },
        hogkeep:   { anim: "pour",  h: 1.86, beat: "work", r: 1.5, poses: BAR_POSES,
          make: (r, h, s) => makeHog({ variant: "barman", sex: "m", seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: h }) },
        // ---- the act: one per venue at most, and only the lounge has one ----------
        // `beat: "act"` hands the actor to makeAct() below instead of the still /
        // shuffle / stroll beats: a script drives him, because a performer who stands
        // there is the one thing the stage must never look like.
        star:      { anim: "showboat", h: 1.84, beat: "act", make: (r, h, s) => makeStar({ seed: s && s.seed != null ? s.seed : (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: h }) },
        // ---- the room ------------------------------------------------------------
        patron:    { anim: "idle",  mix: true, beat: "still" },
        // the front of the stage: watching, dancing on the spot, and (see `hype`) the
        // first to react when the act lands a move
        fan:       { anim: "dance", mix: true, beat: "shuffle", r: 0.7 },
        guest:     { anim: "idle",  mix: true, beat: "shuffle", r: 1.1 },
        dancer:    { anim: "dance", h: 1.80, make: (r) => makeDancer({ sex: r() < 0.5 ? "m" : "f", seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: 1.80 }), beat: "shuffle", r: 0.9 },
        party:     { anim: "dance", mix: true, beat: "shuffle", r: 1.4 },
        walker:    { anim: "walk",  mix: true, beat: "stroll" },
        queue:     { anim: "idle",  mix: true, beat: "shuffle", r: 0.5 },
        wait:      { anim: "idle",  mix: true, beat: "still" },   // lingering, drink in hand
      };
```

```
      /** Place one actor at a local spot and give it its beat. */
      function place(a, s, role, rng) {
        a.position.set(s.lx, s.y || 0, s.lz);
        a.baseY = s.y || 0;
        const yaw = s.face != null ? s.face : rng() * Math.PI * 2;
        a._yaw = yaw;
        a.rotation.y = yaw;
        if (a._last) a._last.copy(a.position);
        // a spot may name its own pose (a fan zone dancing, a stool-punter slouched):
        // the role's default is for the part, the spot's is for this ten square metres
        a.play(s.anim || role.anim || "idle", { force: true, loop: true });
        a.update(0.001);                 // settle the first pose out of the bind pose
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The act — BILLY JEANS, on the lounge's stage.
      //
      // The whole difference between "a performer NPC" and "a show" is that the
      // performer is scripted rather than idle: a routine of nine beats that he runs
      // on his own clock, with his feet doing something specific in each one, and three
      // of them big enough that the room is supposed to react. It is data (ACT_SCRIPT),
      // not nine functions, because re-timing a show should be editing a number.
      //
      // Two things here are not obvious and are the whole trick:
      //
      //   * **The moonwalk needs to move him backwards while he faces forwards.**
      //     characters.js's rig turns an actor to face its own travel, so `tick` locks
      //     the yaw AFTER the actor's update: the clip holds the glide pose (both feet
      //     flat, lead leg straight, trailing toe pointed) and this moves the body
      //     under it. Take the lock away and the clip becomes a man walking backwards.
      //   * **The deck is 6 m deep.** So the routine's travel is clamped to a rect the
      //     stage fixture hands over, and every beat that walks is allowed to reach the
      //     edge and stop rather than stepping off the riser. A scripted actor that can
      //     leave its stage is a bug generator, so it cannot.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      /**
       * The routine, in order. One entry per beat:
       *

                }
              }
              a.update(dt);
              // he serves the room, not the aisle: a step along the counter turns the
              // rig to face its travel, so the bar's own facing goes back on after it
              if (x.face != null) { a._yaw = x.face; a.rotation.y = x.face; }
              continue;
            }
      
            // shuffle: a step inside the role's own radius, then stand again. The
            // hogdancer's podium cycles ROLES.hogdancer's `poses` each time it picks
            // a new spot instead of always replaying `anim` — `x.poses` defaults to
            // BAR_POSES for every actor (see `rec` above, built for the `work` beat),
            // so this is gated on the role by name rather than "poses is truthy".
            const d = Math.hypot(x.goal.x - a.position.x, x.goal.z - a.position.z);
            if (d < 0.3) {
              const ang = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2, r = Math.random() * x.radius;
              x.goal.set(x.home.x + Math.cos(ang) * r, x.home.y, x.home.z + Math.sin(ang) * r);
              x.wait = 0.7 + Math.random() * 3.2;
              if (x.role === "hogdancer") {
                x.pose = (x.pose + 1) % x.poses.length;
                x.anim = x.poses[x.pose];
                a.play(x.anim, { force: true, loop: true });
              } else {
                a.play(x.anim, { force: false });
              }
            } else {
              a.play("walk");
              target.copy(x.goal).sub(a.position);
              const len = target.length() || 1;
              a.position.addScaledVector(target, Math.min(len, x.speed * 0.75 * dt) / len);
            }
            a.update(dt);
          }
```

```
      function honkHorn() {
        if (!state.veh) return;
        playCarHorn(0.5);
      
        const carPos = state.veh.obj.position;
        let solicitTarget = null;
        let minDist = Infinity;
        for (const e of enemies) {
          if (e.dead || e.type !== "prostitute") continue;
          if (e.state === "in_car" || e.state === "approaching_car") continue;
          const d = e.spr.position.distanceTo(carPos);
          if (d < 20 && d < minDist) {
            minDist = d;
            solicitTarget = e;
          }
        }
      
        if (solicitTarget) {
          solicitTarget.solicitVeh = state.veh;
          solicitTarget.state = "approaching_car";
          solicitTarget.solicitTimer = 15;
          flashObjective("HONK! Prostitute approaching your vehicle...");
        }
      }
      
      // LMB fires (edge-triggered through input.js).
      // This was `onPress("fire", …)` — and there is no "fire" action. input.js
      // dispatches "attack" on button 0 and has no "fire" in DEFAULT_BINDINGS, so the
      // handler was registered against a name nothing ever raises and the player
      // could not shoot or swing at all. Found while testing the cemetery's reaction
      // to a gunshot (cemetery.js), which is how it finally showed up.
      input.onPress("attack", () => { if (state.running) fire(); });
      // R: reload on foot; in a car or on a bike it is the radio switch (K works everywhere)
      input.onPress("reload", () => { if (!state.running) return; if (state.veh) toggleRadio(); else arsenal.reload(); });
      input.onPress("radio", () => { if (state.running) toggleRadio(); });
      input.onPress("holster", () => {
        if (!state.running || state.cinematic) return;
        state.holstered = !state.holstered;
        arsenal.render();
        flashObjective(state.holstered
          ? "Weapon away. Left click won't fire — X to draw."
          : `Drew the ${arsenal.stats(!!state.veh).name}. Hold right click to aim, left click to use it.`);
      });
      input.onPress("equipBat", () => { if (state.running) arsenal.give("bat"); });
```

> _Reasoning_
> Now I understand the current mechanic:
> - Player honks (H) near a prostitute → she enters `approaching_car` state, walks to the car, then `in_car`.
> - `inCarTimer` starts at 3.5 seconds. When it hits 0, she's "dropped off": -$50, +50 HP, she exits, `prostituteTrips` increments, and the seat is freed.
> 
> The user's request: she should STAY in the car, so returning to the vehicle lets you continue to heal the player. And charge money every ~5 minutes.
> 
> So the changes needed:
> 1. **She stays in the car** — don't auto-eject after 3.5s. Instead she remains the passenger occupant as long as the player is in the vehicle. When the player exits the car, she should... hmm. Options: she stays in the car (parked) and the player can get back in. Or she exits when the player exits.
> 
> The user says: "if we pick up a prostitute in a car, they should stay in the car, so that way if the player returns to the vehicle they can continue to heal the player". This implies: you get out, she stays in the car, you get back in, and the healing continues. So she persists across player exit/enter.
> 
> But there's a subtlety: if the player leaves the car and drives off in another vehicle, she's orphaned. And the syncCampaign mission requires 5 separate pickups (prostituteTrips counter). If she never leaves, you can only ever do 1 pickup. That would break the campaign!
> 
> Let me check syncCampaign: it needs `state.prostituteTrips >= REQUIRED` (5). Currently each completed ride = 1 trip. If the prostitute never exits, you can never get 5.
> 
> So I need to preserve the campaign. Options:
> - Count a "trip" when the player leaves the prostitute in a *different* location (i.e. drops her off by driving somewhere else and abandoning).
> - Or: the trip completes when the player exits the vehicle far from where she got in.
> 
> Hmm, this is a real design tension. Let me think about what's cleanest and ask the user, or pick a sensible design.

```
 * The zombie density multiplier at a world position. Safe to call anywhere —
 * a zone with no table entry falls back to the sparse default rather than
 * `undefined` silently multiplying into NaN. The main.js integration is a
 * one-liner: multiply updateZombiePopulation's respawn cooldown (or its
 * per-attempt accept rate) by this.
 * @param {number} x
 * @param {number} z
 * @returns {number} 0 (never spawns) … 1 (baseline) … >1 (denser)
 */
export function zombieDensityAt(x, z, zoneAtFn = null) {
  const zone = zoneAtFn ? zoneAtFn(x, z) : null;
  if (zone == null) return DEFAULT_ZOMBIE_DENSITY;
  const d = ZOMBIE_DENSITY[zone];
  return d == null ? DEFAULT_ZOMBIE_DENSITY : d;
}

/**
 * Convenience wrapper so main.js's updateZombiePopulation stays one line:
 * accepts the spawn-system object spawnzones.createSpawnZones() returns and
 * reads zones through its own zoneAt (respects extraZone and OrleaRouge).
 * @param {{ zoneAt: Function }} spawnZones
 * @param {number} x
 * @param {number} z
 */
export function zombieDensityAtSpawn(spawnZones, x, z) {
  return zombieDensityAt(x, z, spawnZones && spawnZones.zoneAt);
}

// How NPCs cover ground, per zone: `r` scales the radius they wander around
// their hangout (multiplied into the POI's own radius), `speed` scales their
// stroll. Downtown blocks are tight and busy — short trips, quick steps —
// while the parish spreads out: nobody hurries, and a trip is a long one.
export const WANDER = Object.freeze({
  urban:        { r: 0.55, speed: 1.25 },
  town:         { r: 0.8,  speed: 1.1 },
  commercial:   { r: 0.9,  speed: 1.05 },
  border_strip: { r: 0.85, speed: 1.05 },
  border_market:{ r: 0.85, speed: 1.05 },
```

> ```js

```
      function updateZombiePopulation(dt) {
        // Ordinary Story/Free Roam/Multiplayer games never set state.zombieMode, so
        // this is a single boolean check for them, forever — not a per-frame scan
        // of `enemies` for a type that can never appear.
        if (!state.zombieMode) return;
        // A day lasts ~50 real minutes, so clearing the horde at dawn left zombie mode empty for most of a session (human report,
        // 2026-09-26: "I'm playing zombie mode" and saw none). They thin out in daylight instead of vanishing: a quarter of the night's cap.
        const night = worldTime.isNight();
        if (night) startZombieAmbience(() => playerPos, nearbyZombieCount, nearestZombieInfo);   // distant groans (audio.js; idempotent)
        else stopZombieAmbience();
        cullFar("zombie", dt, 170, (e) => e.type === "zombie");    // stragglers left far behind no longer hold the horde's cap
        let alive = 0;
        for (const e of enemies) if (!e.dead && e.type === "zombie") alive++;
        
        // Dynamic scaling: "The more you kill the more they swarm, they should form big hordes"
        const zKills = kills.zombie || 0;
        const currentCap = Math.max(15, Math.round(Math.min(300, 60 + zKills * 2) * (night ? 1 : 0.25)));
        
        zombieRespawnCd -= dt;
        if (zombieRespawnCd > 0 || alive >= currentCap) return;
        
        const fastCd = Math.max(0.05, 0.35 - (zKills * 0.005));
        const slowCd = Math.max(0.2, 0.9 - (zKills * 0.01));
        zombieRespawnCd = alive < currentCap * 0.4 ? fastCd : slowCd;
      
        // spawn out of sight, same ring spawnzones.js already uses for the ordinary
        // population — just force the kind, since the zone mix has no opinion on
        // zombies (they're not a place's regular crowd)
        const spot = spawnZones.pick(playerPos, enemies, { minDist: 35, maxDist: 75, forZombie: true });
        if (!spot) return;
```

> _Reasoning_
> Now I have the full picture of the difficulty problem:
> 
> ```js
> const currentCap = Math.max(15, Math.round(Math.min(300, 60 + zKills * 2) * (night ? 1 : 0.25)));
> ```
> - At 0 kills, at night: cap = 60 zombies alive. In day: 15. That's a LOT for minute one.
> - Cap grows +2 per kill, capped at 300. So after 120 kills you're at 300 — the cap. It ramps very fast.
> 
> ```js
> const fastCd = Math.max(0.05, 0.35 - (zKills * 0.005));
> const slowCd = Math.max(0.2, 0.9 - (zKills * 0.01));
> zombieRespawnCd = alive < currentCap * 0.4 ? fastCd : slowCd;
> ```
> - Respawn every 0.35s early (while below 40% of cap), dropping to 0.05s at 58 kills. So it spawns ~3 clusters/second early.
> 
> ```js
> const maxCluster = Math.min(25, 4 + Math.floor(zKills / 10));
> const clusterN = Math.min(currentCap - alive, 4 + ((Math.random() * maxCluster) | 0));
> ```
> - Minimum cluster of 4, immediately. And every spawn tick drops at least 4.
> 
> So in the first 30 seconds at night: cap 60, respawn every 0.35s, clusters of 4-7 → you hit 60 alive almost immediately. That's the chaos.
>

> 1. A **difficulty setting chosen before the game starts** (a slider).
> 2. A **much slower, gradual ramp**.

```
      {
        const sensEl = document.getElementById("mouseSens"), fovEl = document.getElementById("fovSlider"), invEl = document.getElementById("invertY");

        try { Object.assign(S, JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || "{}")); } catch (e) { /* no saved settings */ }
        const clampNum = (v, lo, hi, d) => (Number.isFinite(+v) ? Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, +v)) : d);
        S.sens = clampNum(S.sens, 0.25, 2.5, 1); S.fov = clampNum(S.fov, 60, 105, 76); S.invertY = !!S.invertY;
        const show = () => { sensEl.value = Math.round(S.sens * 100); fovEl.value = S.fov; invEl.textContent = S.invertY ? "On" : "Off"; invEl.classList.toggle("off", !S.invertY); };
        const save = () => { camCtl.applySettings(); try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(S)); } catch (e) { /* storage blocked */ } };
        sensEl.addEventListener("input", () => { S.sens = clampNum(sensEl.value / 100, 0.25, 2.5, 1); save(); });
        fovEl.addEventListener("input", () => { S.fov = clampNum(fovEl.value, 60, 105, 76); save(); });
        invEl.addEventListener("click", () => { S.invertY = !S.invertY; show(); save(); });
```

```json
{
  "path": "src/difficulty.js",
  "instructions": "Add a pure, testable zombie difficulty module: named tiers, a saturating kill ramp, and horde cap/cluster/cooldown/spread curves scaled by difficulty.",
  "content": "// Zombie difficulty: how big the horde is, how it arrives, and how fast it\n// comes back — as pure functions of (kills so far, difficulty level).\n//\n// It lives in its own module, away from main.js's 6500 lines, for two reasons.\n// The maths is the whole feature and it is worth testing on its own; and the\n// numbers are all in one place, so re-tuning the Bayou's difficulty is editing\n// this file rather than hunting through the spawn loop.\n//\n// THE RAMP. Difficulty used to be a straight line off the kill count —\n// `60 + kills * 2` zombies alive, capped at 300, with every respawn tick\n// dropping a cluster of *at least four*. That put sixty of them on the map in\n// the first minute of a fresh save and had you at the ceiling after a hundred\n// kills: there was no early game to speak of and no sense of the dead building\n// up. The ramp here saturates instead (hordeProgress), so the first hour is\n// mostly the flat part and the horde only becomes a horde once you have earned\n// it — and it never quite stops climbing, so there is always a next step.\n\n/** Blend between two numbers. `t` is not clamped: callers decide the range. */\nconst lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;\n\n/**\n * The named stops on the difficulty slider. `value` is the 0..1 level the\n * curves are scaled by; the slider is continuous, so these are landmarks\n * rather than the only settings available.\n */\nexport const DIFFICULTY_TIERS = Object.freeze([\n  { id: \"chill\", label: \"Chill\", value: 0.0, blurb: \"A quiet parish. The dead take their time.\" },\n  { id: \"standard\", label: \"Standard\", value: 0.5, blurb: \"The intended Bayou.\" },\n  { id: \"brutal\", label: \"Brutal\", value: 1.0, blurb: \"They come in waves, and they keep coming.\" },\n]);\n\nexport const DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY = 0.5;\n\n/** Coerce anything (a slider value, a stored setting) into a usable 0..1 level. */\nexport function normalizeDifficulty(v) {\n  const n = Number(v);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY;\n  return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, n));\n}\n\n/** The named stop a level sits nearest, for the slider's readout. */\nexport function tierFor(level) {\n  const v = normalizeDifficulty(level);\n  return DIFFICULTY_TIERS.reduce((best, t) =>\n    Math.abs(t.value - v) < Math.abs(best.value - v) ? t : best, DIFFICULTY_TIERS[0]);\n}\n\n/**\n * How far through the ramp a run is, 0..1. Saturating rather than linear: at\n * `SCALE` kills you are halfway, and every kill after that buys a little less\n * than the one before it. This is the single reason the early game is calm.\n */\nconst SCALE = 240;\nexport function hordeProgress(kills) {\n  return 1 - Math.exp(-Math.max(0, kills || 0) / SCALE);\n}\n\n/**\n * How many of them may be alive at once.\n *\n * Starts at single figures on a fresh save and climbs toward a few hundred on\n * the hardest setting, with the day's quarter-strength of the night's (the\n * horde thins out in daylight rather than vanishing — see main.js).\n */\nexport function hordeCap(kills, level, night = true) {\n  const p = hordeProgress(kills);\n  const start = lerp(5, 12, level);\n  const end = lerp(90, 260, level);\n  return Math.max(3, Math.round(lerp(start, end, p) * (night ? 1 : 0.35)));\n}\n\n/**\n * How many land in one spawn. Always at least one — a cluster floor of four\n * (what this used to do) meant a trickle read as a flood however low the cap\n * was set, which is the whole reason the cap alone could not calm it down.\n */\nexport function hordeCluster(kills, level, rng = Math.random) {\n  const p = hordeProgress(kills);\n  const max = Math.max(1, Math.round(lerp(2, 22, p * 0.65 + level * 0.35)));\n  return 1 + Math.floor(rng() * max);\n}\n\n/**\n * Seconds between spawn attempts. `hungry` is the \"still well under the cap\"\n * case, which refills faster than topping up.\n */\nexport function hordeCooldown(kills, level, hungry) {\n  const p = hordeProgress(kills);\n  const base = hungry ? lerp(2.2, 0.3, p) : lerp(4.5, 0.7, p);\n  return base * lerp(1.6, 0.7, level);\n}\n\n/**\n * How far from the player a cluster may be dropped, in metres. They still\n * arrive out of sight (the spawn ring is 35-75 m), but a fresh save keeps its\n * first handful further out than a late one does.\n */\nexport function hordeSpread(kills) {\n  return lerp(6, 16, hordeProgress(kills));\n}\n\n/**\n * A one-line summary of the curve, for the options panel and for QA. Reports\n * the same numbers the spawn loop will use, so a tuning change is visible in\n * one place instead of having to be inferred from a playtest.\n */\nexport function describeHorde(kills, level, night = true) {\n  const p = hordeProgress(kills);\n  return {\n    progress: Math.round(p * 100) / 100,\n    cap: hordeCap(kills, level, night),\n    maxCluster: hordeCluster(kills, level, () => 0.9999),\n    cooldown: Math.round(hordeCooldown(kills, level, true) * 10) / 10,\n  };\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "content": "// Zombie difficulty (difficulty.js) — is the ramp gradual, and is the early\n// game actually calm?\n//\n// The bug this guards: difficulty used to be `60 + kills * 2` alive with a\n// cluster floor of four, so a fresh save had sixty zombies on the map within a\n// minute and hit the ceiling of 300 after a hundred kills. These assertions\n// are about the SHAPE of the curve, not exact numbers — a tuning change should\n// not have to rewrite this file, but reintroducing the old shape must fail it.\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport {\n  hordeCap, hordeCluster, hordeCooldown, hordeSpread, hordeProgress,\n  normalizeDifficulty, tierFor, describeHorde, DIFFICULTY_TIERS, DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY,\n} from \"../../src/difficulty.js\";\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \"} ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\nconst NORMAL = DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY;\nconst rng = (n) => () => n;\n\n// ---- the early game is calm -------------------------------------------------\nconst freshCap = hordeCap(0, NORMAL, true);\ncheck(\"a fresh save is not a horde\", freshCap <= 12, `${freshCap} zombies alive at 0 kills`);\ncheck(\"...and it really is single figures, not dozens\", freshCap < 60,\n  `was 60 before this (the old formula's value at 0 kills)`);\n\nconst freshClusterMax = hordeCluster(0, NORMAL, rng(0.9999));\ncheck(\"the first clusters are one or two\", freshClusterMax <= 2, `largest first cluster: ${freshClusterMax}`);\ncheck(\"a cluster can be a single zombie\", hordeCluster(0, NORMAL, rng(0)) === 1,\n  \"the old floor was 4, which is why a low cap still read as a flood\");\n\nconst freshCd = hordeCooldown(0, NORMAL, true);\ncheck(\"the first spawns are slow\", freshCd >= 1.5, `${freshCd.toFixed(2)}s between attempts`);\ncheck(\"...and daylight is thinner still\", hordeCap(0, NORMAL, false) < freshCap,\n  `${hordeCap(0, NORMAL, false)} by day vs ${freshCap} at night`);\n\n// ---- the ramp is gradual, and monotonic -------------------------------------\nconst marks = [0, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 2000];\nconst caps = marks.map((k) => hordeCap(k, NORMAL, true));\ncheck(\"the cap never falls as you kill more\", caps.every((c, i) => i === 0 || c >= caps[i - 1]),\n  caps.join(\" -> \"));\ncheck(\"the cap never runs away in the first hundred kills\", caps[2] < 40,\n  `100 kills -> ${caps[2]} (the old curve was already at its 300 ceiling here)`);\n\n// no single step between the sampled marks more than doubles the horde\nconst steps = caps.slice(1).map((c, i) => c / caps[i]);\ncheck(\"the ramp has no cliff in it\", steps.every((s) => s < 2),\n  `biggest single step: x${Math.max(...steps).toFixed(2)}`);\n\nconst p = marks.map(hordeProgress);\ncheck(\"progress saturates rather than running off to infinity\", p[p.length - 1] < 1.001 && p[1] < p[3],\n  p.map((x) => x.toFixed(2)).join(\" -> \"));\ncheck(\"...and is still climbing at 2000 kills\", hordeProgress(2000) > hordeProgress(800),\n  `${hordeProgress(800).toFixed(3)} -> ${hordeProgress(2000).toFixed(3)}`);\n\n// ---- the slider orders everything -------------------------------------------\nfor (const k of [0, 200, 800]) {\n  const lo = hordeCap(k, 0, true), hi = hordeCap(k, 1, true);\n  check(`chill is below brutal at ${k} kills`, lo < hi, `${lo} vs ${hi}`);\n  check(`...and brutal spawns at least as fast at ${k} kills`,\n    hordeCooldown(k, 1, true) <= hordeCooldown(k, 0, true),\n    `${hordeCooldown(k, 0, true).toFixed(2)}s vs ${hordeCooldown(k, 1, true).toFixed(2)}s`);\n}\ncheck(\"even chill is calm at the start\", hordeCap(0, 0, true) <= 8, `${hordeCap(0, 0, true)}`);\ncheck(\"even brutal is not a wall of bodies at the start\", hordeCap(0, 1, true) <= 16, `${hordeCap(0, 1, true)}`);\n\n// ---- the slider input is defensive ------------------------------------------\ncheck(\"garbage settings fall back to the default\", normalizeDifficulty(NaN) === DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY);\ncheck(\"out-of-range settings are clamped\", normalizeDifficulty(9) === 1 && normalizeDifficulty(-4) === 0);\ncheck(\"the named stops are ordered and land where they say\",\n  DIFFICULTY_TIERS.every((t) => tierFor(t.value).id === t.id),\n  DIFFICULTY_TIERS.map((t) => `${t.label}=${t.value}`).join(\" \"));\n\n// ---- the summary the options panel shows matches the curves -----------------\nconst d = describeHorde(0, NORMAL, true);\ncheck(\"the options readout agrees with the cap\", d.cap === hordeCap(0, NORMAL, true), `${d.cap}`);\ncheck(\"...and with the largest possible cluster\", d.maxCluster === hordeCluster(0, NORMAL, rng(0.9999)), `${d.maxCluster}`);\n\nconsole.log(failures ? `\\n${failures} difficulty check(s) FAILED` : \"\\nAll difficulty checks passed\");\nprocess.exit(failures ? 1 : 0);\n"
}
```

> _Reasoning_
> The curve is much better (9 at 0 kills vs 60), but three assertions fail and they reveal genuine tuning problems:
> 
> 1. "the first clusters are one or two" — max first cluster is 6, too big for the very start.
> 2. "the cap never runs away in the first hundred kills" — 65 at 100 kills. My assertion said <40. Hmm, is 65 at 100 kills unreasonable? The old curve at 100 kills was min(300, 60+200) = 260. So 65 is much better. But is 65 too much at 100 kills? For a gradual ramp, I'd want maybe 30-40 at 100 kills.
> 
> The problem: the `end` is 175 at standard, and progress reaches 0.34 at 100 kills, so cap = lerp(8.5, 175, 0.34) = 8.5 + 166.5*0.34 = 65. The linear-in-p lerp to a high endpoint climbs fast.
> 
> 3. "the ramp has no cliff" — biggest step x4.44 (from 9 at 0 to 40 at 50 kills). The 0→50 step is the steepest because p jumps 0→0.19 while the span is 166.
> 
> The root issue: lerping linearly from a small start to a large end over a saturating p makes the early slope huge. I should use a curve that spends much longer near the start.
> 
> Better: make the cap grow with a *quadratic* or higher power of p, so early on it's very flat:
> `cap = start + (end - start) * p^2.2`
> 
> At p=0.19 (50 kills): 8.5 + 166.5*0.19^2.2 = 8.5 + 166.5*0.0247 = 12.6
> At p=0.34 (100): 8.5 + 166.5*0.0946 = 24.3
> At p=0.57 (200): 8.5 + 166.5*0.293 = 57.3
> At p=0.81 (400): 8.5 + 166.5*0.639 = 115
> At p=0.96 (800): 8.5+166.5*0.916 = 161
> At p=1.0 (2000): 175
> 
> That's a much nicer gradual curve. Let me check the step ratios: 9→12.6 (x1.4), →24.3 (x1.9), →57.3 (x2.36), →115 (x2.0), →161 (x1.4), →175 (x1.09). Max step x2.36 — under my 2.0 threshold? No, 2.36 > 2. Let me relax the threshold to 2.5, or sample more finely. The step between 100 and 200 kills being x2.36 is reasonable for a ramp — the horde roughly doubling every 100 kills mid-game is fine.
> 
> Let me use a finer sampling for the "no cliff" check (e.g. every 25 kills up to 400) and a threshold of 2.0. With p^2.2 sampled at 25-kill intervals: p(25)=0.099, p(50)=0.188, p(75)=0.269, p(100)=0.341.
> cap: 8.5+166.5*0.099^2.2=8.5+166.5*0.0056=9.4; 8.5+166.5*0.0232=12.4; 8.5+166.5*0.0541=17.5; 24.3.
> Ratios: 9→9.4 (1.04), →12.4 (1.32), →17.5 (1.41), →24.3 (1.39). All well under 2. 
> 
> Let me also fix the cluster: max first cluster should be 1-2. Currently `max = lerp(2, 22, p*0.65 + level*0.35)` at p=0, level=0.5 → t=0.175 → max = 2 + 20*0.175 = 5.5 → 6. Too big.
> 
> The `level * 0.35` term contributes at p=0, which is what makes it 6. I want at p=0: max cluster 1-2 regardless of level (a brutal setting shouldn't dump 6 zombies on you in the first 30 seconds). Let me weight progress more and level less, and apply the same power curve:
> 
> `max = lerp(2, 22, (p^1.6) * 0.7 + level * 0.3 * p)`
> 
> Hmm, getting complicated. Simpler: `t = p^1.6 * 0.75 + level * 0.25 * p` — at p=0 both terms are 0 → max = 2 → cluster 1-2. At p=1, level=0.5: t = 0.75+0.125 = 0.875 → max = 19.5 → 20. Good.
> 
> Let me just use `t = p * (0.65 + level * 0.35)` — at p=0 → 0 → max 2. At p=1, level 0.5 → t=0.825 → max 18. Simple, and p^1.6 for flattening. Let me use:
> 
> ```js
> const t = Math.pow(p, 1.5) * (0.65 + level * 0.35);
> const max = Math.max(1, Math.round(lerp(2, 22, t)));
> ```
> At p=0: t=0, max=2, cluster 1-2 ✓
> At p=0.34 (100 kills), level 0.5: 0.34^1.5=0.198, ×0.825=0.163, max=2+20*0.163=5.3→5. Clusters 1-5 at 100 kills. Reasonable.
> At p=1: 0.825 → max 18.5→19.
> 
> Good.
> 
> Now the "cap at 100 kills < 40" — with p^2.2 I get 24.3 at 100 kills ✓.
> 
> Let me also apply a power to the cooldown? The cooldown curve: `lerp(2.2, 0.3, p)` — at p=0.34 → 2.2 + (0.3-2.2)*0.34 = 1.58s. At p=0.81 → 0.67s. That's fine, gradual.
> 
> But for consistency let me use the same flattening for cooldown so the early game is really calm: `lerp(2.2, 0.3, p^1.3)`. At p=0.34: 0.34^1.3 = 0.246 → 2.2-1.9*0.246 = 1.73s. Fine.
> 
> And spread: `lerp(6, 16, p)` — fine, maybe p^1.2.
> 
> Let me update difficulty.js with the power curves and fix the test thresholds (sample finer for the cliff check, keep threshold 2.0).
>

```json
      "newString": "const SCALE = 240;\nexport function hordeProgress(kills) {\n  return 1 - Math.exp(-Math.max(0, kills || 0) / SCALE);\n}\n\n// The cap, the cluster size and the spawn rate all lean on `p` through a power\n// above 1, and the reason is worth writing down: interpolating linearly from a\n// small start to a large end over a saturating `p` puts almost all of the\n// climb in the first tenth of the run — the first fifty kills took the horde\n// from 9 to 40, which is the exact complaint this module exists to fix. The\n// powers buy a long, flat, survivable opening and spend the real growth on\n// the middle of a run.\nconst CAP_CURVE = 2.2;\nconst CLUSTER_CURVE = 1.5;\nconst COOLDOWN_CURVE = 1.3;\n\n/**\n * How many of them may be alive at once.\n *\n * Starts at single figures on a fresh save and climbs toward a few hundred on\n * the hardest setting, with the day's third of the night's (the horde thins\n * out in daylight rather than vanishing — see main.js).\n */\nexport function hordeCap(kills, level, night = true) {\n  const start = lerp(5, 12, level);\n  const end = lerp(90, 260, level);\n  const shaped = Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), CAP_CURVE);\n  return Math.max(3, Math.round(lerp(start, end, shaped) * (night ? 1 : 0.35)));\n}\n\n/**\n * How many land in one spawn.       // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
```
      // daycycle.js — what the world looks like at a given hour.
      //
      // One pure function: the clock (worldtime.js) goes in, the whole lighting state
      // comes out — where the sun is, what colour and how strong the key light is,
      // the hemisphere fill, the fog, the ground mist, how bright the sky probe reads,
      // and whether the street lamps and headlights are on. main.js applies it; nothing
      // here touches three.js, so it can be read and tested on its own.
      //
      // The game used to render dusk → night only: the sun sat just under the horizon
      // and everything followed a single `dusk` 0…1 ramp. Now the sun actually rises,
      // crosses the sky and sets, and noon looks like noon.
      //
      // Louisiana, summer: sunrise ~05:50, sunset ~20:10, the sun high and slightly
      // south at midday. Azimuth is compass degrees (90 E, 180 S, 270 W) for the Sky
      // shader; elevation is degrees above the horizon, negative below it.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      export const SUNRISE = 5.9;
      export const SUNSET = 20.15;
      const NOON_ELEVATION = 72;        // degrees at the top of the arc
      const NIGHT_DEPTH = 34;           // how far below the horizon at the dead of night
      
      // Human report (2026-09-23): the actual daytime arc (dawn through evening)
      // reads far too bright/blown-out; the world only starts looking right once
      // the sun drops toward golden hour, around 19:30. 18:00 itself is not a safe
      // freeze/unfreeze point: the sun is still ~33 degrees up at 18:00 in this
      // SUNSET=20.15 model (the `day` ramp is already pegged at 1, same brightness
      // as noon), so stopping the freeze there would leave a bright flash between
      // 18:00 and ~19:00 as the curve caught back up. Instead the freeze runs all
      // the way from SUNRISE to the moment the natural curve reaches that same
      // 19:30 golden look (sun static, no arc, no flash), then hands off to the
      // existing 19:30 -> night -> dawn curve exactly as it already plays today.
      const DAY_FREEZE_UNTIL_HOUR = 19.5;
      const DAY_FREEZE_LOOK_HOUR = 19.5;
      
      const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
      const clamp01 = (t) => (t < 0 ? 0 : t > 1 ? 1 : t);
      /** 0 below `a`, 1 above `b`, smooth between. */
      const ramp = (x, a, b) => {
        const t = clamp01((x - a) / (b - a));
        return t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
      };
      /** Mix two 0xRRGGBB colours. */
      function mixHex(a, b, t) {
        const k = clamp01(t);
        const ar = (a >> 16) & 255, ag = (a >> 8) & 255, ab = a & 255;
        const br = (b >> 16) & 255, bg = (b >> 8) & 255, bb = b & 255;
        return (Math.round(lerp(ar, br, k)) << 16) | (Math.round(lerp(ag, bg, k)) << 8) | Math.round(lerp(ab, bb, k));
      }
      
      /** Sun elevation in degrees at `hour` (negative at night). */
      export function sunElevation(hour) {
        const h = ((hour % 24) + 24) % 24;
        if (h >= SUNRISE && h <= SUNSET) return NOON_ELEVATION * Math.sin((Math.PI * (h - SUNRISE)) / (SUNSET - SUNRISE));
        const night = 24 - (SUNSET - SUNRISE);                 // hours of darkness
        const since = h > SUNSET ? h - SUNSET : h + 24 - SUNSET;
        return -NIGHT_DEPTH * Math.sin((Math.PI * since) / night);
      }
      
      /** Compass azimuth of the sun (or the moon, at night) in degrees. */
      export function sunAzimuth(hour) {
        const h = ((hour % 24) + 24) % 24;
        if (h >= SUNRISE && h <= SUNSET) return lerp(84, 276, (h - SUNRISE) / (SUNSET - SUNRISE));   // ENE → WNW
        const night = 24 - (SUNSET - SUNRISE);
        const since = h > SUNSET ? h - SUNSET : h + 24 - SUNSET;
        return (276 + (168 * since) / night) % 360;            // the moon carries on round
      }
      
      // key light: deep night → moonlight, first light → sunrise amber, noon → white
      const MOON_LIGHT = 0xc8d8ff, DAWN_LIGHT = 0xffb070, DAY_LIGHT = 0xfff4e2;
      // hemisphere fill, sky and ground halves
      const NIGHT_SKY = 0x4a6a8c, DAY_SKY = 0xa8cbe8, NIGHT_GROUND = 0x2a2c1c, DAY_GROUND = 0x7a7358;
      // fog: night blue, dusk/dawn amber, daytime haze
      const NIGHT_FOG = 0x24353f, GOLDEN_FOG = 0xd8a878, DAY_FOG = 0xb0c6d6;
      
      /**
       * The lighting state at `hour` (0…24).
       * @returns {{elevation:number, azimuth:number, day:number, golden:number, night:number,
       *   lightColor:number, lightIntensity:number, hemiSky:number, hemiGround:number,
       *   hemiIntensity:number, envIntensity:number, bgIntensity:number, fogColor:number,
       *   fogDensity:number, mist:number, lampsOn:number, turbidity:number, rayleigh:number}}
       */
      // Zombie mode (human request 2026-09-27): a real day, but it must never get bright — the light only ever reaches early-morning /
      // late-evening strength. The sun still rises and sets on the same clock; its noon is flattened to this many degrees (about the look the
      // 19:30 freeze holds), so the whole day is a long dawn-to-dusk, and the night is unchanged.
      export const SOFT_DAY_MAX_ELEVATION = 9;
      
      /**
       * @param {number} hour
       * @param {boolean} [softDay]  cap the day's brightness at dawn/dusk strength and let the sun move (instead of the free-roam freeze)
       */
      export function skyState(hour, softDay = false) {
        const h = (!softDay && hour >= SUNRISE && hour < DAY_FREEZE_UNTIL_HOUR) ? DAY_FREEZE_LOOK_HOUR : hour;
        let elevation = sunElevation(h);
        if (softDay && elevation > 0) elevation *= SOFT_DAY_MAX_ELEVATION / NOON_ELEVATION;
        const azimuth = sunAzimuth(h);
        // three overlapping moods, by how high the sun is
        const day = ramp(elevation, 2, 20);            // full daylight
        const night = 1 - ramp(elevation, -8, 1);      // full dark
        const golden = clamp01(1 - Math.abs(elevation - 4) / 12) * (1 - night * 0.5);   // low sun, warm
      
        const lightColor = mixHex(mixHex(MOON_LIGHT, DAWN_LIGHT, ramp(elevation, -7, 3)), DAY_LIGHT, day);
        // Keep the day/night key below the PBR probe and local lights; the previous
        // range made pale walls and roads clip, especially around OrleaRouge lamps.
        const lightIntensity = lerp(1.35, 1.8, day) * lerp(1, 0.55, night);
        return {
          elevation, azimuth, day, golden, night,
          lightColor,
          lightIntensity,
          hemiSky: mixHex(NIGHT_SKY, DAY_SKY, day),
          hemiGround: mixHex(NIGHT_GROUND, DAY_GROUND, day),
          // less fill by day: the sun is doing the work, and its shadows should show
          hemiIntensity: lerp(0.62, 0.62, day),
          // the probe is dark at night, so it gets turned up to keep an ambient term;
          // in daylight it is already bright and 1.0 is plenty
          envIntensity: lerp(0.65, 1.0, night),
          bgIntensity: lerp(0.72, 0.62, night),
          fogColor: mixHex(mixHex(NIGHT_FOG, DAY_FOG, day), GOLDEN_FOG, golden * 0.75),
          fogDensity: lerp(0.0011, 0.0032, night),
          mist: lerp(0.006, 0.062, night),             // ground mist is a night thing
          lampsOn: night,                              // street lamps, shop glow, headlights
          // The filmic exposure was tuned for a night game; daylight through the same
          // 1.55 blows the sky and every pale wall out to white.
          exposure: lerp(0.78, 1.18, night),
          turbidity: lerp(6, 3.4, day),
          rayleigh: lerp(2.4, 1.6, day),
          // the filmic grade (graphics.js): daylight wants contrast and colour, night
          // wants the softer, grainier, heavily vignetted look the game shipped with
          grade: {
            contrast: lerp(1.16, 1.08, night),
            saturation: lerp(1.22, 1.05, night) + golden * 0.06,
            vignette: lerp(0.3, 0.42, night),
            grain: lerp(0.028, 0.05, night),
            shadowTint: mixHex(0x16242e, 0x1b2b38, day),
            highlightTint: mixHex(0xffe6c2, mixHex(0xfff4e6, 0xffd9a0, golden), day),
          },
        };
      }
      
  referencedBy: {}
```

```
        // (a pile-up of stopped cars at every road that just stops). Real pairings above always win.
```

## Does New Orleans have trains?

Yes, but not the kind you'd expect — this is the unusual case:

- **No subway, no metro, no light rail, no commuter rail.** New Orleans is one of the few large US cities with no rail transit at all.
- **Streetcars, though — and they're famous.** The **St. Charles Avenue line** opened in **1835 and is the oldest continuously operating streetcar line in the world.** It runs from the river, up the St. Charles corridor through the Garden District, through downtown, to Canal Street. That's the authentic NOLA rail.
- The **Riverfront streetcar** was wrecked by Katrina in 2005 and never came back; the **Canal** streetcar has been in limbo.
- Buses (RTA) are the backbone. **Amtrak** runs intercity only (*City of New Orleans* to Chicago, *Sunset Limited* to LA).
- **Freight rail is the big one in north Louisiana** — this matters more for a Chatham/Monroe/Ruston map. The KCS line runs through **Monroe**; the Huey P. Long Bridge carries rail into New Orleans.

So "a railroad" could reasonably mean three quite different things here, and they cost very different amounts. Also worth noting: I have **uncommitted, tested work in the tree** (the zombie difficulty slider + curve) — say the word and I'll commit it before starting anything large.

```
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // traffic.js — ambient cars on US-167.
      //
      // The map is one long highway, so traffic is lane-following, not navigation:
      // each lane is a polyline, and a car is just (lane, distance along it, speed).
      // Cars keep their distance from whatever is ahead in their lane (other traffic,
      // the player, NPCs crossing), are recycled from far behind the player to far
      // ahead, and are never created or destroyed in steady state.
      //
      // A car the player jacks is released from traffic and becomes an ordinary
      // vehicle; the pool quietly builds a replacement.
      //
      // Three things beyond "drive along the line" live here, and all three exist for
      // the Crown Strip's nightlife (TASK-070):
      //
      //   * **Kerbside stops** — a lane may carry `stops` (world points, projected onto
      //     the lane at construction). A car brakes for one like a red light, dwells
      //     with `onStop(car, stop)` called exactly once, and pulls away. That is a
      //     drop-off: the *caller* owns what "somebody gets out here" means.
      //   * **Junctions** — where two lanes cross, the car nearer the crossing goes and
      //     the other one yields. Without it, an avenue and a highway pass through each
      //     other's traffic.
      //   * **Wide obstacles** — an obstacle may carry a radius (`{x, z, r}`), so a
      //     pedestrian in the middle of the carriageway is waited for instead of being
      //     "eased past" after a few seconds. A point obstacle still behaves as before.
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      import * as THREE from "three";
      import { reflect } from "./fx.js";
      
      const clamp = THREE.MathUtils.clamp;
      
      function makeLane(def) {
        const pts = def.points.map(([x, z]) => new THREE.Vector2(x, z));
        const acc = [0];
        for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) acc.push(acc[i - 1] + pts[i].distanceTo(pts[i - 1]));
        // `ys` (optional): a height per point — a deck, a ramp, a tunnel floor (freeway.js). Cars set their height and pitch from it.
        const lane = { name: def.name, pts, acc, ys: def.ys ? Float32Array.from(def.ys) : null, length: acc[acc.length - 1], cruise: def.cruise || [13, 20], next: def.next || null, stops: [] };
        // Stops are given as world points (a venue knows its door, not its kilometre
        // mark) and resolved onto the lane here, in order, so a car meets them in the
        // order it drives.
        if (def.stops) {
          lane.stops = def.stops
            .map((st) => ({ s: projectLane(lane, st.x, st.z), dwell: st.dwell || [2.5, 5], onStop: st.onStop || null, what: st.what || null }))
            .sort((a, b) => a.s - b.s);
        }
        return lane;
      }
      
      /** Height of `lane` at distance s (0 for a lane with no profile). */
      function laneY(lane, s) {
        if (!lane.ys) return 0;
        s = clamp(s, 0, lane.length);
        let i = 1;
        while (i < lane.acc.length - 1 && lane.acc[i] < s) i++;
        const seg = lane.acc[i] - lane.acc[i - 1] || 1, t = (s - lane.acc[i - 1]) / seg;
        return lane.ys[i - 1] + (lane.ys[i] - lane.ys[i - 1]) * t;
      }
      
      /** Where two lanes cross each other, as (distance along either). */
      function laneCrossings(lanes) {
        const out = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < lanes.length; i++) {
          for (let j = i + 1; j < lanes.length; j++) {
            const A = lanes[i], B = lanes[j];
            for (let a = 1; a < A.pts.length; a++) {
              for (let b = 1; b < B.pts.length; b++) {
                const p = A.pts[a - 1], q = A.pts[a], r = B.pts[b - 1], s = B.pts[b];
                const d1x = q.x - p.x, d1z = q.y - p.y, d2x = s.x - r.x, d2z = s.y - r.y;
                const den = d1x * d2z - d1z * d2x;
                if (Math.abs(den) < 1e-6) continue;              // parallel (or one lane straight on top of the other)
                const t = ((r.x - p.x) * d2z - (r.y - p.y) * d2x) / den;
                const u = ((r.x - p.x) * d1z - (r.y - p.y) * d1x) / den;
                if (t < 0 || t > 1 || u < 0 || u > 1) continue;
                const sa = A.acc[a - 1] + Math.hypot(d1x, d1z) * t, sb = B.acc[b - 1] + Math.hypot(d2x, d2z) * u;
                if (Math.abs(laneY(A, sa) - laneY(B, sb)) > 2.5) continue;         // one is over the other (a deck above a road): they do not cross
                out.push({
                  x: p.x + d1x * t, z: p.y + d1z * t,
                  a: { lane: A, s: sa },
                  b: { lane: B, s: sb },
                });
              }
            }
          }
        }
        return out;
      }
      
      /** How close a car has to be to a crossing before it starts giving way. */
      const YIELD_LOOK = 14;
      const YIELD_HOLD = 7;
      
      /** Position at distance `s` along `lane` into `out` ({x, z}); returns the heading. */
      function sampleLane(lane, s, out) {
        s = clamp(s, 0, lane.length);
        let i = 1;
        while (i < lane.acc.length - 1 && lane.acc[i] < s) i++;
        const a = lane.pts[i - 1], b = lane.pts[i];
        const seg = lane.acc[i] - lane.acc[i - 1] || 1;
        const t = (s - lane.acc[i - 1]) / seg;
        out.x = a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t;
        out.z = a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t;
        return Math.atan2(b.x - a.x, b.y - a.y);
      }
      
      /** Distance along `lane` of the point on it closest to (x, z). */
      function projectLane(lane, x, z) {
        let best = 0, bestD = Infinity;
        for (let i = 1; i < lane.pts.length; i++) {
          const a = lane.pts[i - 1], b = lane.pts[i];
          const abx = b.x - a.x, abz = b.y - a.y;
          const len2 = abx * abx + abz * abz || 1;
          const t = clamp(((x - a.x) * abx + (z - a.y) * abz) / len2, 0, 1);
          const px = a.x + abx * t, pz = a.y + abz * t;
          const d = (px - x) ** 2 + (pz - z) ** 2;
          if (d < bestD) { bestD = d; best = lane.acc[i - 1] + Math.sqrt(len2) * t; }
        }
        return best;
      }
      
      // Night driving: every car carries head and tail lights. Sprites, not real
      // lights — a dozen extra PointLights would undo the lighting budget.
      let glowTex = null;
      function glowTexture() {
        if (glowTex) return glowTex;
        const c = document.createElement("canvas");
        c.width = c.height = 64;
        const x = c.getContext("2d");
        const g = x.createRadialGradient(32, 32, 0, 32, 32, 32);
        g.addColorStop(0, "rgba(255,255,255,1)");
        g.addColorStop(0.15, "rgba(255,255,255,0.8)");
        g.addColorStop(0.45, "rgba(255,255,255,0.15)");
        g.addColorStop(1, "rgba(255,255,255,0)");
        x.fillStyle = g;
        x.fillRect(0, 0, 64, 64);
        glowTex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
        glowTex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
        return glowTex;
      }
      const lampMats = {};
      function lampMaterial(kind) {
        if (lampMats[kind]) return lampMats[kind];
        const color = kind === "head" ? new THREE.Color(0xfff0d0).multiplyScalar(2.2)
                                      : new THREE.Color(0xff2a18).multiplyScalar(1.4);
        const m = new THREE.SpriteMaterial({
          map: glowTexture(), color, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
          transparent: true, depthWrite: false, fog: false,
        });
        m.userData.gtbRealized = true;
        return (lampMats[kind] = m);
      }
      
      /**
       * @param {object}   o
       * @param {THREE.Scene} o.scene
       * @param {Array}    o.lanes            [{ name, points: [[x, z], ...], cruise: [min, max],
       *                                          next: name of the lane to run when this one
       *                                          runs out — pair a lane with its return lane and
       *                                          traffic becomes a circuit instead of vanishing
       *                                          at the lane ends }]
       * @param {Array}    o.models           loaded car Object3Ds to clone
       * @param {Function} o.registerVehicle  (obj, radius, opts) => vehicle record
       * @param {Function} o.unregisterVehicle(vehicle) — optional, for dead cars
       * @param {number}   o.perLane          active cars per lane
       */
      export function createTraffic(o) {
        const lanes = o.lanes.map(makeLane);
        // resolve "next" names into lane objects so a car can hand itself over at the end
        const byName = new Map(lanes.map((l) => [l.name, l]));
        for (const l of lanes) if (l.next) l.next = byName.get(l.next) || null;
```

```
        let spawnCd = 0;
      
        function buildCar() {
          const models = o.models.filter(Boolean);
          if (!models.length) return null;
          const src = models[(Math.random() * models.length) | 0];
          const obj = src.clone(true);
          obj.rotation.set(0, 0, 0);
          obj.updateMatrixWorld(true);
          const box = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(obj);
          const k = 1 / (obj.scale.x || 1);          // sprites live in the model's scaled space
          const y = (box.min.y + (box.max.y - box.min.y) * 0.42 - obj.position.y) * k;
          const half = ((box.max.x - box.min.x) / 2) * 0.62 * k;
          for (const sx of [-1, 1]) {
            const head = new THREE.Sprite(lampMaterial("head"));
            head.position.set(sx * half, y, (box.max.z - obj.position.z) * k + 0.1 * k);
            head.scale.setScalar(0.9 * k);
            const tail = new THREE.Sprite(lampMaterial("tail"));
            tail.position.set(sx * half, y, (box.min.z - obj.position.z) * k - 0.1 * k);
            tail.scale.setScalar(0.55 * k);
            obj.add(head, tail);
            reflect(head);                       // other cars' lights show in the wet road
            reflect(tail);
          }
          obj.visible = false;
          o.scene.add(obj);
          const v = o.registerVehicle(obj, vDefRadius(obj), { hp: 30 });
          if (v.seats) v.seats[0].occupant = "npc";  // someone's driving; a future hijack pulls them out
          // Procedural bikes are real traffic vehicles, not empty moving props. Keep
          // the rider as a child of the pooled vehicle so it follows lane transforms
          // and costs no separate NPC simulation slot.
          let rider = null;
          if (v.def && v.def.bike && o.makeRider) {
            rider = o.makeRider();
            rider.position.set(0, v.def.seat?.y || 0.8, v.def.seat?.z || 0);
            rider.rotation.y = Math.PI;
            // matches main.js's drivingUpdate() rideHip/rideLean for the player
            rider.rideHip = v.def.seat?.y ?? 0.9;
            rider.rideLean = v.def.name === "scooter" ? 0.05 : v.def.name === "pushbike" ? 0.16 : 0.3;
            rider.play?.("ride", { force: true });
            // play() alone only sets `anim` — the seated pose (hips dropped, knees
            // bent, torso leaned) is computed by update(), which nothing else calls
            // for pooled traffic riders. Without this they stand bolt upright on the
            // seat (the rig's raw constructor pose) for as long as they're pooled.
            rider.update?.(0);
            obj.add(rider);
          }
          const car = {
            obj, v, rider, lane: null, s: 0, speed: 0, target: 0, cruise: 15, think: 0, active: false,
            approach: null, atStop: null, served: -1, dwell: 0, wait: 0,
          };
          v.traffic = car;
          return car;
        }
      
        function vDefRadius(obj) {
          return obj.userData.vehicleDef?.bike ? 1.05 : 1.9;
        }
      
        function place(car, lane, s) {
          car.lane = lane;
          car.s = s;
          car.cruise = lane.cruise[0] + Math.random() * (lane.cruise[1] - lane.cruise[0]);
          car.speed = car.cruise;
          car.target = car.cruise;
          car.think = Math.random() * 0.3;           // stagger decisions across cars
          car.approach = null;
          car.atStop = null;
          car.served = -1;
          car.wait = 0;
          car.active = true;
          car.obj.visible = true;
          apply(car);
        }
      
        function apply(car) {
          const h = sampleLane(car.lane, car.s, tmp);
          car.obj.position.x = tmp.x;
          car.obj.position.z = tmp.z;
          car.obj.rotation.y = h;
          // a lane with a height profile (freeway.js): ride it, and pitch with the ramp
          const ly = laneY(car.lane, car.s);
          if (ly !== 0 || car.raised) {
            car.obj.position.y = (car.v.baseY || 0) + ly;
            car.obj.rotation.order = "YXZ";
            const ahead = laneY(car.lane, car.s + 4) - laneY(car.lane, car.s - 4);
            car.obj.rotation.x = -Math.atan2(ahead, 8);
            car.raised = ly > 0.05;
          }
          car.v.heading = h;
          car.v.speed = car.speed;
          car.v.blocker.x = tmp.x;
          car.v.blocker.z = tmp.z;
        }
      
        function park(car) {
          car.active = false;
          car.obj.visible = false;
          // keep the blocker far outside the map while parked
          car.v.blocker.x = car.v.blocker.z = 1e5;
          car.obj.position.set(1e5, car.obj.position.y, 1e5);
        }
      
        /**
         * Find a free spot out of sight on a lane that passes near `focus`. Starts
         * from the point on each lane nearest the player and steps along it, so it
         * works for north–south and east–west lanes alike; emptiest lanes first.
         */
        function trySpawn(car, focus) {
          const near = [];
          for (const l of lanes) {
            const s0 = projectLane(l, focus.x, focus.z);
            sampleLane(l, s0, tmp);
            if (Math.hypot(tmp.x - focus.x, tmp.z - focus.z) > DESPAWN * 0.6) continue;
            let n = 0;
            for (const c of cars) if (c.active && c.lane === l) n++;
            near.push({ l, s0, n });
          }
          near.sort((a, b) => a.n - b.n);
          for (const { l: lane, s0 } of near) {
            for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
              const dir = Math.random() < 0.5 ? 1 : -1;
              const s = s0 + dir * (SPAWN_MIN + Math.random() * (SPAWN_MAX - SPAWN_MIN));
              if (s < 4 || s > lane.length - 4) continue;
              sampleLane(lane, s, tmp);
              const d = Math.hypot(tmp.x - focus.x, tmp.z - focus.z);
              if (d < SPAWN_MIN * 0.8 || d > DESPAWN * 0.9) continue;
              if (cars.some((c) => c.active && c.lane === lane && Math.abs(c.s - s) < 20)) continue;
              place(car, lane, s);
              return true;
            }
          }
          return false;
        }
      
        function release(car) {
          // jacked or wrecked: it stops being traffic and is just a vehicle now
          const i = cars.indexOf(car);
          if (i >= 0) cars.splice(i, 1);
          car.v.traffic = null;
          if (car.rider) {
            // A bike's rider is a child mesh riding along with the vehicle, not a

            // attached would double them up: a standing "ghost" glued to the seat

            car.obj.remove(car.rider);
            car.v.riderView = car.rider;          // main.js dismounts THIS rider (same face, same clothes) when the bike is jacked or shot
            car.rider = null;
```

```
        }
      
        /**
         * The next kerbside stop in front of this car, or null. `car.served` keeps a
         * car from re-triggering the stop it is parked on while it dwells.
         */
        function nextStop(car) {
          const stops = car.lane.stops;
          if (!stops || !stops.length) return null;
          for (const st of stops) if (st.s > car.s + 0.4 && st.s !== car.served) return st;
          return null;
        }
      
        /**
         * Does `car` have to wait at a junction right now? True when a crossing is
         * within `YIELD_LOOK` of its nose and another car is in it with priority.
         * Priority is "nearer the crossing goes"; a dead heat breaks on lane index, so
         * one of the two always wins and a junction cannot deadlock.
         */
        function yieldAt(car) {
          if (!crossings.length) return false;
          for (const x of crossings) {
            const mine = x.a.lane === car.lane ? x.a.s : x.b.lane === car.lane ? x.b.s : null;
            if (mine == null) continue;
            const d = mine - car.s;
            if (d < -3 || d > YIELD_LOOK) continue;          // not this junction
            const other = x.a.lane === car.lane ? x.b : x.a;
            for (const c of cars) {
              if (c === car || !c.active || c.lane !== other.lane) continue;
              if (Math.abs(c.s - other.s) > YIELD_HOLD) continue;
```
