> _Reasoning_
> Now I understand the rig's limits clearly:
> 
> 1. **Head is not a joint** — it gets merged into the torso, so `head.rotation` does nothing. The comment explicitly says this is "authoring intent rather than motion".
> 2. **No wrist** — the hand is built at the elbow space; `a.hand` exists (line 959) as an Object3D used for IK targeting, not as a rotating joint.
> 3. **Single-segment spine** — `torso` is one Object3D, so no arch/twist separation.
> 4. **Pelvis** — `hips.rotation` exists, good.
> 
> For "rig first", the upgrades that matter for posing, in order of value:
> - **Neck as a real joint** (split head out of the merge). Cheap: add `neck` to the merge joint list and move the head's meshes under it. This makes every clip's `head.rotation` actually work — a big win for every existing dance clip too (the showboat chin, the twerk look-back, the pole head turn).
> - **Two-segment spine**: split `torso` into `torso` (lower/waist) and `chest` (upper), so the chest can arch and twist independently of the waist. This is what makes arching/leaning poses read. Touches: the mesh parenting (chest meshes move under the new joint), all clips' `r.torso.rotation` (they'd still work if I make `chest` a child of torso and keep `this.torso` pointing at the chest joint for compatibility... no — clips set torso.rotation.x for lean; if chest is a child of torso and I alias `this.chest`, I'd have to update all clips. Better: keep `this.torso` as the object clips rotate (so every existing clip is unchanged) and make the *lower* spine the parent: `hips → spine (lower) → torso (upper)`. Then clips rotating `torso` pivot at the chest, which is higher up — that changes every existing animation's pivot point. Risky.
>   
>   Safer: `hips → waist → torso`. `this.torso` stays the upper joint at the same position it is now, and clips that set `torso.rotation` behave identically when `waist` is at rest (identity). Then add `this.waist` and let new pose clips drive it. But the torso mesh is built at hips-space offsets... Actually the torso's contents are added relative to `torso` at position (0,0,0) under hips. If I insert `waist` at (0,0,0) under hips and put torso under waist, everything still lines up when waist is identity. 
> 
>   So: insert a `waist` Object3D at the same origin as hips' child, keep `torso` as its child at the same local position, add `waist` to the merge joints. Zero change to existing clips, and new clips get a lower spine. That's a clean, low-risk upgrade. 
> 
> - **Wrists**: add a `wrist` Object3D between elbow and hand, move the hand meshes under it, add to merge joints. `a.hand` currently is added to `elbow` at the wrist socket. If I add `wrist` at the same position, existing clips are unaffected (they don't rotate `hand`). New pose clips can rotate wrists. This is exactly what's needed for hands-on-body poses.
> 
> - **Toe/ankle** already exists (`l.foot`).
> 
> So the "rig first" slice is: **neck + waist + wrist** as real joints. That's three mechanical changes, all additive and non-breaking, and it immediately improves every existing dance clip (the head actually moves).
> 
> Let me also add the age guard for adult clips, since I said I would.
> 
> That's a solid, well-scoped first slice. Let me implement it.

> 1. `neck`: create a `neckJoint` Object3D at y=0.66 (where head was), put head under it; add both to merge list. > _Reasoning_
> `mergeRigid` walks up from each mesh to the nearest ancestor in `joints`. Meshes whose nearest joint ancestor is the root (not in the set) are left alone.
> 
> Important: currently `head` is NOT in joints, so head meshes walk up to `torso`. If I add `head` to joints, head meshes (skull, jaw, eyes, hair, hat...) will form their own merged mesh under `head`. Note: `if (g.entries.length < 2) continue;` — groups with a single mesh are left alone. So adding joints only splits when 2+ meshes share a joint+material. Low risk.
> 
> One concern: the head group has many small meshes with different materials — merging per material is fine.
> 
> Another concern: `this.head` rotation would now actually move the head. Existing clips set `r.head.rotation.x/y/z` — these will now have real effect. Could that break existing visuals/tests? character_quality_test checks "no NaN over 20 s of pole" and triangle counts. Merging changes the mesh count, not triangles (merge preserves tris). Actually merging *reduces* draw calls; the triangle count stays. The test prints male 4450 / female 5100 triangles — should be unchanged.
> 
> But wait: could a moving head break the "hand is above head" check in stripper_test ("both hands are up on the bar, above her head — hands at 1.97 m, crown at 1.92 m")? The head now rotates, so the crown position changes. On the pole clip, `r.head.rotation.set(-0.18 - climb*0.16, spin*0.22, 0)` — a pitch of up to -0.34 rad. That would lower/raise the crown by ~0.1*sin(0.34) ≈ 3cm. The margin is 5 cm. Might be tight but the test samples at specific times. Risk of failure — I'll run it and see.
> 
> Also `bustDepth` in stripper_test measures the chest band 1.12–1.38 m — head movement doesn't affect that. And crowners.
> 
> Let me also consider: adding `head` to joints means head meshes merge separately → the head's draw calls go from 1 (baked into torso) to ~1-3 (per material under head). Slight increase in draw calls but better articulation. Acceptable — and the arms/torso still merge.
> 
> Now `waist`: insert `const waist = new THREE.Object3D(); hips.add(waist); waist.add(torso)` — but `torso` is created as `new THREE.Object3D(); hips.add(torso)`. I'd change to `hips.add(waist); waist.add(torso); this.waist = waist;` and add `waist` to the merge list.

Pushed, and then I did the rig-first slice you asked for. Both local: `8fb2adf`.

**The rig — three joints it was missing**
- **Neck/head.** `head` was never in `mergeRigid`'s joint list, so every mesh under it was baked into the torso and every `r.head.rotation` line in every clip was *authoring intent that nothing moved*. The showboat's chin, the twerk's look over the shoulder, the pole's head turn — all written, none ever seen. It's a joint now, and it's the single biggest thing the rig was missing.
- **Waist.** Inserted at the hips' own origin with `torso` hanging off it, so it's the identity transform at rest and every existing clip is unchanged to the last decimal. What it buys is a lower back: arch from the waist with the chest held, instead of folding at the shoulder blades.
- **Wrist.** Is also the weapon socket, so a hand can roll without the IK target drifting off it. Moving the hand geometry onto it also fixed a latent 0.25 m misplacement I'd introduced and caught via `stripper_test`'s bounding-box check.

Triangle count unchanged (4450/5100). One clip needed retuning as a result: the pole's head pitch was authored blind and is now visible — I set a mild chin-up and left a note that it deserves a look in-game, because nobody has ever seen it.

**The 18+ gate — the existing check was a rubber stamp**

This is the thing worth your attention. `franchiseClubs.js` stamped `userData.age = Math.max(25, userData.age || 25)` on every performer, and `debug` reported `allAdults` by testing that against 18. But **nothing anywhere read `opts.age`** — so the stamp produced `25` for every actor that arrived without one, and the assertion was evaluating `25 >= 18`. It would have passed for any character at all, or none at all. It was the only thing standing between this game and an adult clip playing on whoever happened to be nearest a pole, and it could not have failed.

So the age is a fact about the model now (`Hoodrat` reads `opts.age`, defaults to an adult, floor enforced), the franchise module *checks* instead of assigning, and `play()` refuses the named adult set unless the rig is past 18 **and** the gate has been answered — failing closed when no gate is installed. `adult_clip_gate_test.mjs` proves each refusal path, including that no name in the set leaks and that ordinary clips are never gated. `npm test` is green at 310 checks.

**Two things before I write the poses**

1. On a 1.8 m blocky figure the difference between "69" and "two people lying down" is mostly joint angles and relative placement. The rig pass gives the poses something to sit on, but it doesn't change the blockiness — this will read as crude up close and fine at play distance. Worth knowing before I spend the next stretch on it.
2. "Stage first" means the explicit material lands on a publicly-reachable deploy. The 18+ launch gate is the mitigation, but it's a one-click acknowledgement on entry, not a per-content opt-in. Your call — I raised it before you decided and I'm not relitigating, just making sure the consequence is on the record before it's in the world.

> The `setGarment` part-matching logic is convoluted. Let me simplify: a garment entry has `part` ∈ {"top","bottom","all"}. Semantics:
> - `setGarment("all", false)` → hide everything.
> - `setGarment("top", false)` → hide entries with part "top" or "all".
> - `setGarment("all", true)` → show everything (all entries).
> - `setGarment("top", true)` → show entries with part "top" or "all".
> 
> So: entry matches if `part === "all" || g.part === part`. That's it. Let me rewrite cleanly.

>       if (o.visible !== on) { o.visible = on; changed++; }
>       break;

>   });
>   return changed;
> };
> ```
> That's correct and simple. Let me replace.

  "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// act.js — placing two performers for a private scene.\n//\n// The couple clips in characters.js are half-poses. This is the other half: it\n// owns where the two bodies are, how they are oriented to each other, and how\n// they get there and leave again. Splitting it this way is why a position is\n// one name played by two actors rather than two clips that drift apart — the\n// geometry of the pair is here, in one place, and the bodies only ever describe\n// what they do on top of it.\n//\n// Every scene here is between two FICTIONAL ADULTS who have both agreed: the\n// caller is responsible for that, and characters.js enforces the second half of\n// it (an actor past the age floor, with the 18+ gate answered) before any of\n// these clips will play. `start()` refuses a pair that cannot be cast.\n//\n// It is deliberately presentation-only. Nothing here touches the player, the\n// world, or anyone's save state: a scene is two rigs, a pose and a clock, and\n// it is over when it is over.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\n\n/**\n * How the pair is arranged, per position. All of it is in the scene's own\n * coordinate frame: the pair is centred on the origin, facing +z, and the\n * caller puts the whole group where it wants in the room.\n *\n *   gap     metres between the two origins along the pair's own axis\n *   yaw     the partner's facing relative to the lead's\n *   lift    how high the group's floor is (a bed, a floor, a chaise)\n *   lie     true when both roots are laid on their backs/sides rather than stood\n *   tilt    roll applied to the laid-down roots, so a body is not perfectly flat\n *\n * `lie` is the important one: lying a rig down is a root transform, not a pose,\n * and doing it here means the twelve couple poses never have to know where the\n * floor is.\n */\nexport const SCENES = Object.freeze({\n  missionary:  { gap: 0.62, yaw: 0,           lift: 0.42, lie: true,  tilt: 0 },\n  doggystyle:  { gap: 0.78, yaw: 0,           lift: 0.36, lie: false, tilt: 0 },\n  oral:        { gap: 0.66, yaw: Math.PI,     lift: 0.40, lie: true,  tilt: 0 },\n  roughOral:   { gap: 0.58, yaw: Math.PI,     lift: 0.40, lie: true,  tilt: 0 },\n  sixtyNine:   { gap: 0.70, yaw: 0,           lift: 0.34, lie: true,  tilt: 0.08 },\n  assToMouth:  { gap: 0.64, yaw: Math.PI / 2, lift: 0.40, lie: true,  tilt: 0 },\n});\n\n/** The stage business a dancer can work into a set, and what it leaves on. */\nexport const STAGE_ACT = Object.freeze({\n  stripTease:  { seconds: 9.2, leaves: \"all\"  },   // the whole costume\n  flash:       { seconds: 4.1, leaves: null },\n  spreadTease: { seconds: 4.6, leaves: null },\n  stageRub:    { seconds: 6.8, leaves: null },\n});\n\nconst LAY_DOWN = -Math.PI / 2;      // a root rolled onto its back, facing +z\n\n/**\n * One scene: two rigs, a position, and a clock.\n *\n * @param {object} o\n * @param {THREE.Object3D} o.lead     the actor whose `coupleRole` is \"lead\"\n * @param {THREE.Object3D} o.partner  ...and \"partner\". Both must pass\n *   characters.js's adult-clip gate, or `start()` throws.\n * @param {THREE.Scene} o.scene\n * @param {string} o.name             a key of SCENES\n * @param {THREE.Vector3} [o.at]      where the pair goes, in world space\n * @param {number} [o.yaw]            the pair's facing\n */\nexport function createAct({ lead, partner, scene, name, at = null, yaw = 0 }) {\n  const def = SCENES[name];\n  if (!def) throw new Error(`act: no scene called \"${name}\"`);\n  const group = new THREE.Group();\n  group.name = `act:${name}`;\n\n  // What each rig was doing, and where it stood, before. Restoring that is the\n  // difference between a scene ending and a scene leaving the district changed.\n  const saved = [lead, partner].map((a) => ({\n    a,\n    parent: a.parent,\n    pos: a.position.clone(),\n    rot: a.rotation.clone(),\n    scale: a.scale.clone(),\n    visible: a.visible,\n    baseY: a.baseY,\n    anim: a.anim,\n    role: a.coupleRole,\n  }));\n\n  const pair = [\n    { a: lead, role: \"lead\", z: -def.gap / 2 },\n    { a: partner, role: \"partner\", z: def.gap / 2 },\n  ];\n\n  let t = 0, running = false;\n\n  function place() {\n    for (const { a, role, z } of pair) {\n      a.coupleRole = role;\n      if (def.lie) {\n        // laid on her back, or on her front for the ones that need it, with the\n        // body's own length running along the pair's axis\n        a.rotation.set(LAY_DOWN, 0, role === \"partner\" ? def.tilt : -def.tilt);\n        a.position.set(0, def.lift, z);\n      } else {\n        a.rotation.set(0, role === \"partner\" ? def.yaw : 0, 0);\n        a.position.set(0, 0, z);\n      }\n      a.baseY = a.position.y;\n      a.visible = true;\n      if (a._last) a._last.copy(a.position);\n    }\n  }\n\n  const api = {\n    group,\n    get running() { return running; },\n    get elapsed() { return t; },\n\n    /**\n     * Put the pair in the room and put them in the position.\n     * Throws rather than silently degrading if either actor cannot be cast —\n     * a scene that quietly failed to start is the one failure mode here that\n     * would be invisible.\n     */\n    start() {\n      for (const { a } of pair) {\n        if (a.adultClipRefused !== null && a.adultClipRefused !== undefined) {\n          throw new Error(`act: ${a.name || \"an actor\"} was refused an adult clip and cannot be cast`);\n        }\n        if (a.allowsAdultClip && !a.allowsAdultClip()) {\n          throw new Error(\"act: refuses to cast — an actor is not past the age floor, or the 18+ gate is unanswered\");\n        }\n        if (a.setGarment) a.setGarment(\"all\", false);\n      }\n      group.add(lead, partner);\n      if (at) { group.position.copy(at); group.rotation.y = yaw; }\n      place();\n      // both rigs get the same clock, so the two halves of a position breathe\n      // together instead of drifting apart inside a few seconds\n      const clock = { t: 0 };\n      api.clock = clock;\n      for (const { a, role } of pair) {\n        a.beatRef = clock;\n        a.coupleRole = role;\n        a.play(name, { force: true, loop: true });\n        a.update(0.001);\n      }\n      t = 0;\n      running = true;\n      return api;\n    },\n\n    /** One frame. The clock belongs to the scene, not to either rig. */\n    update(dt) {\n      if (!running) return;\n      t += Math.max(0, dt);\n      api.clock.t = t;\n      for (const { a } of pair) a.update(Math.max(0, dt));\n    },\n\n    /** Put everything back exactly as it was found. */\n    stop() {\n      if (!running) return api;\n      running = false;\n      for (const s of saved) {\n        if (s.a.restoreWardrobe) s.a.restoreWardrobe();\n        s.a.beatRef = null;\n        s.a.coupleRole = s.role;\n        if (s.parent) s.parent.add(s.a);\n        s.a.position.copy(s.pos);\n        s.a.rotation.copy(s.rot);\n        s.a.scale.copy(s.scale);\n        s.a.visible = s.visible;\n        s.a.baseY = s.baseY;\n        if (s.anim) s.a.play(s.anim, { force: true, loop: true });\n      }\n      group.clear();\n      if (at) scene && group.removeFromParent && group.parent && group.parent.remove(group);\n      return api;\n    },\n  };\n\n  if (scene) scene.add(group);\n  return api;\n}\n\n/**\n * Pick a stage act that suits a performer, and leave her dressed in it.\n *\n * The branch stage calls this when a routine turns over to the explicit half of\n * the house. The wardrobe is put back afterwards by whoever ends the number —\n * a venue that leaves a dancer bare for the rest of the night is a bug, not a\n * feature, so `endStageAct` exists and is the other half of this.\n */\nexport function beginStageAct(actor, name) {\n  const def = STAGE_ACT[name];\n  if (!def) return null;\n  if (!actor.allowsAdultClip || !actor.allowsAdultClip()) return null;\n  const before = actor.anim;\n  actor.play(name, { force: true, loop: true });\n  return {\n    name,\n    seconds: def.seconds,\n    leaves: def.leaves,\n    previous: before,\n    end() {\n      if (actor.restoreWardrobe) actor.restoreWardrobe();\n      actor.play(before || \"dance\", { force: true, loop: true });\n    },\n  };\n}\n"
}

Committed as `b48eda1`. `npm test` is green at 355 checks. Not pushed yet.

**What's in**
- **Four stage numbers** — `stripTease` (the costume actually comes off over her head on count 4 and the rest of the number is danced bare), `flash` (both hands under, lifting, chin down so the eyes come up over the top, released every phrase), `spreadTease` (back turned, bent at the waist, looking back over her shoulder), `stageRub`. The first two lean hard on the wrist joint, the last two on the waist and neck.
- **Six positions**, each one name that *two* rigs play and split on `coupleRole` — so it's one idea with two bodies in it rather than two clips that drift apart when someone re-times one.
- **`act.js`** owns the geometry: the gap, the facing, laying them down, and the shared clock. Lying down is a root transform there, never a pose, so the twelve couple poses never need to know where the floor is.
- **The wardrobe is a material, not a second body.** `mergeRigid` bakes each joint's meshes one-per-material, so a garment *is* the merged mesh carrying its material and taking it off is a visibility toggle. Skin is never registered — the whole cast shares one skin material, and a garment registered as skin would have taken the body with it.

**Two bugs the tests caught**, both of which would have shipped looking like "the feature does nothing":
- `_poseClip` dispatches on a hand-written list of clip names. None of the ten new ones were on it, so every single one fell through to the idle pose. It's now `ADULT_CLIPS.has(anim)`, so a clip added to the registry can't be left out of the dispatcher again.
- The same function zeroes the root's X and Z rotation every frame so clips can own them. That's correct standing up, and it silently stood anyone a scene had laid on their back straight back up. A laid body now sets `lie` and the reset skips it.

**Still open**, and the parts that decide whether this is any good:
- **Nothing reaches it yet.** The back rooms still run the old censor-gag scene — `createAct` isn't called from anywhere in `src/`. The stage acts are scheduled and work, but the six positions have no entry point.
- **Nobody has seen it.** Every pose is authored blind against joint angles. I fixed one blind-authoring bug already (the pole's head pitch, exposed when the neck became a joint), and I'd expect more.

Wire the back rooms to `createAct` next, then look at it in a browser and tune what reads badly — the second is where the real work is.

Wired up, committed as `258ad0c`. Suite green at 381 checks. Still not pushed.

**The path in, end to end.** `main.js` hands the player rig to `createStateWorld` → `franchiseClubs` → the night overlay. A finale now carries the name of a position; the club stages it on the bed with the host and the player, and `createAct` puts them in it.

- **All six are reachable.** The first four at the existing heat-80 gate, the other four at full heat. The two ideas with no rig position — "up against the wall", "let her ride" — stay as text rather than getting a bad pose bolted to them.
- **It runs on the club's clock, not the world's.** The overlay pauses the sim, so a scene driven by world `dt` would have frozen the instant you chose it. `c.staged.update(Math.max(dt, 1/120))` keeps it moving.
- **Refusal degrades instead of breaking.** If the pair can't be cast, `stage` returns null and she says "*she stays where she is, and shrugs* 'Not tonight, sugar.'" — the night carries on as text. No half-dressed performer frozen by the bed.
- **It comes down on every exit** — Esc, "walk away", or paying and leaving. `closeGame` calls `onStageEnd`, which stops the act, puts the player back under their own parent at their own position, and restores their clothes.

`backroom_staging_test.mjs` proves the whole chain with real rigs, including the refusal path with a minor in the cast.

**Next on the queue**, in order:
1. **Street prostitutes and escorts** — they're the other half of your original ask ("the prostitutes and escorts can remove their clothing"). They have no venue, so they need their own hook rather than a stage routine.
2. **Look at it in a browser.** This is the one I'd do next, and sooner rather than later — every pose is authored blind against joint angles, and I already found one blind-authoring bug (the pole's head pitch) purely because a test made a number move. Ten more poses is ten more chances to be wrong in a way only an eye catches.

Say the word and I'll push, or keep going on the street workers first.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// cityparts.js — the pieces of a metropolis: modern glass towers, art-deco towers, hotel slabs, and French Quarter rowhouses with balconies
// (human request, 2026-09-27: "very metropolis, very modern New Orleans type vibe" around the Crown Strip and the spawn strip).
//
//   const P = createCityParts(ctx, { occluders })
//   P.tower(group, x, z, w, d, h, variant)     variant 0 glass, 1 art deco, 2 hotel slab, 3 dark glass
//   P.rowhouses(group, x0, x1, z, side, seed)  a terrace of 2-3 storey stucco houses with iron balconies; `side` = +1 faces +z, -1 faces -z
//   P.plaza(group, x, z, w, d, seed)           paving, trees, benches, planters
//
// Everything is built into the `group` it is given (composer clusters cull by distance), with shared materials so batchStatic can merge them.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

import * as THREE from "three";

const PASTELS = [0xd98e73, 0xe8c98a, 0x9cc7b4, 0xc9a0c7, 0xe6b0a0, 0x8fb3d9, 0xefe4cf, 0xd9c27a];
const hashf = (a, b, c = 0) => { let h = (a * 374761393 + b * 668265263 + c * 1442695041) | 0; h = (h ^ (h >>> 13)) * 1274126177 | 0; return ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0) / 4294967295; };

export function createCityParts(ctx, { occluders = [] } = {}) {
  const { addBlocker } = ctx;
  const mats = new Map();
  const std = (color, name, o = {}) => {
    const k = name + color + JSON.stringify(o);
    if (!mats.has(k)) { const m = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, name, roughness: 0.85, ...o }); m.userData.gtbRealized = true; mats.set(k, m); }
    return mats.get(k);
  };
  const basic = (color) => { const k = "b" + (color.getHex ? color.getHex() : color); if (!mats.has(k)) { const m = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color }); m.userData.gtbRealized = true; mats.set(k, m); } return mats.get(k); };

  // ---- window textures: 4 bays x 4 floors per tile, some lit
  const canvasTile = (bg, lit, dark, prob, seed, fins = false) => {
    const cv = document.createElement("canvas"); cv.width = cv.height = 128;
    const g = cv.getContext("2d");
    g.fillStyle = bg; g.fillRect(0, 0, 128, 128);
    for (let cy = 0; cy < 4; cy++) for (let cx = 0; cx < 4; cx++) {
      g.fillStyle = hashf(cx + seed * 7, cy, seed) < prob ? lit : dark;
      g.fillRect(cx * 32 + 5, cy * 32 + 7, 22, 18);
    }
    g.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,0.07)"; for (let cy = 0; cy < 4; cy++) g.fillRect(0, cy * 32 + 1, 128, 2);
    if (fins) { g.fillStyle = "rgba(240,225,190,0.55)"; for (let cx = 0; cx < 4; cx++) g.fillRect(cx * 32 + 1, 0, 3, 128); }        // art-deco piers
    const t = new THREE.CanvasTexture(cv); t.wrapS = t.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping; t.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; t.anisotropy = 4;
    return t;
  };
  const facade = (name, tex, emissive) => {
    const m = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ name, map: tex, emissive: 0xffffff, emissiveMap: tex, emissiveIntensity: emissive, roughness: 0.3, metalness: 0.45 });
    m.userData.gtbRealized = true;
    return m;
  };
  const F = {
    glass: [0, 1, 2].map((v) => facade("glass tower facade", canvasTile(["#182430", "#1f2c38", "#1a2028"][v], ["#ffd89a", "#bfe6ff", "#fff1c8"][v], "#0b1118", [0.5, 0.32, 0.6][v], v), 0.55)),
    deco: [0, 1].map((v) => facade("deco tower facade", canvasTile(["#6d6552", "#7a6f5a"][v], "#ffd28a", "#1a1712", [0.45, 0.35][v], 20 + v, true), 0.4)),
    slab: [0, 1].map((v) => facade("hotel slab facade", canvasTile(["#3a3f48", "#2e3540"][v], "#ffe3a8", "#10151c", [0.55, 0.4][v], 30 + v), 0.5)),
    dark: [0, 1].map((v) => facade("glass tower facade", canvasTile(["#10161d", "#141b24"][v], "#9ad0ff", "#070b10", [0.3, 0.42][v], 40 + v), 0.6)),
  };
  const capMat = std(0x3a3d40, "concrete roof", { roughness: 0.9 });
  const stoneMat = std(0xcfc6ae, "limestone");
  const spireMat = std(0x9aa0a6, "steel mast", { metalness: 0.8, roughness: 0.4 });
  const beaconMat = basic(new THREE.Color(0xff2a1a).multiplyScalar(3));
  const neonMats = [0xff4fb3, 0x2ee6ff, 0xffc23a, 0x9dff6a].map((c) => basic(new THREE.Color(c).multiplyScalar(2.4)));

  /** A box whose window texture tiles once per 12 m x 14.4 m (4 bays x 4 floors), so nothing stretches on a 100 m tower. */
  const facadeBox = (w, h, d) => {
    const g = new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), uv = g.attributes.uv, nrm = g.attributes.normal;
    for (let k = 0; k < uv.count; k++) {
      if (Math.abs(nrm.getY(k)) > 0.5) { uv.setXY(k, 0.1, 0.1); continue; }
      const across = Math.abs(nrm.getX(k)) > 0.5 ? d : w;
      uv.setXY(k, uv.getX(k) * (across / 12), uv.getY(k) * (h / 14.4));
    }
    return g;
  };
  const put = (parent, geo, mat, x, y, z, o = {}) => {
    const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); m.position.set(x, y, z);
    m.castShadow = o.cast !== false; m.receiveShadow = true; if (o.ry) m.rotation.y = o.ry;
    parent.add(m); return m;
  };
  const solid = (x, z, w, d) => { if (addBlocker) for (const [bx, bz] of [[-w / 4, -d / 4], [w / 4, -d / 4], [-w / 4, d / 4], [w / 4, d / 4], [0, 0]]) addBlocker(x + bx, z + bz, Math.min(w, d) / 3); };
  const occlude = (x, z, w, d, h) => occluders.push({ minX: x - w / 2, maxX: x + w / 2, minY: 0, maxY: h + 1.2, minZ: z - d / 2, maxZ: z + d / 2 });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ towers
  function tower(g, x, z, w, d, h, variant = 0, seed = 0) {
    const grp = new THREE.Group(); grp.position.set(x, 0, z); g.add(grp);
    const pick = (arr) => arr[Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed + 5) * arr.length)];
    if (variant === 1) {
      // ART DECO: a wide base, three setbacks each narrower, a stone crown with a spire — the Hibernia / Pontchartrain look
      const mat = pick(F.deco);
      let y = 0, cw = w, cd = d;
      const tiers = [[0.34, 1], [0.3, 0.8], [0.22, 0.6], [0.14, 0.4]];
      for (const [frac, sc] of tiers) {
        const th = Math.max(6, h * frac); cw = w * sc; cd = d * sc;
        put(grp, facadeBox(cw, th, cd), mat, 0, y + th / 2, 0);
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(cw + 1.2, 0.8, cd + 1.2), stoneMat, 0, y + th + 0.4, 0);       // a stone cornice at every setback
        y += th + 0.8;
      }
      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.15, 0.6, 16 + h * 0.1, 6), spireMat, 0, y + 8 + h * 0.05, 0);
      put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.55, 8, 6), beaconMat, 0, y + 16 + h * 0.1, 0, { cast: false });
    } else if (variant === 2) {
      // HOTEL SLAB: long, lower, banded balconies and a lit rooftop sign
      const mat = pick(F.slab);
      put(grp, facadeBox(w * 1.25, h * 0.14, d * 1.1), mat, 0, h * 0.07, 0);
      put(grp, facadeBox(w, h * 0.86, d * 0.55), mat, 0, h * 0.14 + h * 0.43, -d * 0.12);
      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.6, 1.0, d * 0.55 + 0.6), capMat, 0, h + 0.5, -d * 0.12);
      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.6, 2.4, 0.6), neonMats[Math.floor(hashf(x, z, 3) * neonMats.length)], 0, h + 2.4, -d * 0.12 + d * 0.28, { cast: false });
      for (let y = 6; y < h; y += 3.6 * 2) put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.4, 0.22, 1.1), stoneMat, 0, y, d * 0.16, { cast: false });
    } else {
      // MODERN GLASS: podium, a stepped shaft, a crown, mast and aviation light
      const mat = variant === 3 ? pick(F.dark) : pick(F.glass);
      const podium = Math.max(10, h * 0.16), shaft = h * 0.64, crown = h - podium - shaft;
      put(grp, facadeBox(w, podium, d), mat, 0, podium / 2, 0);
      put(grp, facadeBox(w * 0.82, shaft, d * 0.82), mat, 0, podium + shaft / 2, 0);
      put(grp, facadeBox(w * 0.58, crown, d * 0.58), mat, 0, podium + shaft + crown / 2, 0);
      for (const [y, sw, sd] of [[podium, w * 0.9, d * 0.9], [podium + shaft, w * 0.7, d * 0.7], [h, w * 0.62, d * 0.62]]) put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(sw, 0.9, sd), capMat, 0, y + 0.45, 0);
      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.18, 0.45, 12 + h * 0.08, 6), spireMat, 0, h + 6 + h * 0.04, 0);
      put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5, 8, 6), beaconMat, 0, h + 12 + h * 0.08, 0, { cast: false });
    }
    // a neon-edged ground floor: shops and a lobby glowing at street level
    const glow = neonMats[Math.floor(hashf(z, x, 9) * neonMats.length)];
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.7, 0.35, 0.3), glow, 0, 4.4, d / 2 + 0.2, { cast: false });
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.7, 0.35, 0.3), glow, 0, 4.4, -d / 2 - 0.2, { cast: false });
    solid(x, z, w, d); occlude(x, z, w, d, h);
    return grp;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ French Quarter rowhouses
  const iron = () => std(0x1c1f22, "wrought iron railing", { metalness: 0.6, roughness: 0.5 });
  const trimM = () => std(0xf2eee4, "trim wood", { roughness: 0.7 });
  const shutterM = (i) => std([0x2f5a44, 0x1f3a5a, 0x5a2f2f, 0x2f2f2f][i % 4], "shutter wood");
  const litWin = () => basic(new THREE.Color(0xffc27a).multiplyScalar(1.4));
  const darkWin = () => basic(0x17202a);
  function rowhouse(g, x, z, w, side, floors, colorIdx, seed) {
    const h = floors * 3.3 + 0.6, d = 9;
    const grp = new THREE.Group(); grp.position.set(x, 0, z); grp.rotation.y = side < 0 ? Math.PI : 0; g.add(grp);
    const wall = std(PASTELS[colorIdx % PASTELS.length], "stucco wall");
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), wall, 0, h / 2, 0);
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.4, 0.5, d + 0.4), trimM(), 0, h + 0.25, 0);
    // a hipped roof and a chimney, for the skyline
    put(grp, new THREE.ConeGeometry(Math.max(w, d) * 0.62, 1.6, 4), std(0x5a4a44, "roof tile"), 0, h + 1.3, 0, { ry: Math.PI / 4 }).scale.set(w / Math.max(w, d), 1, d / Math.max(w, d));
    for (let f = 0; f < floors; f++) {
      const y = 1.9 + f * 3.3;
      for (const wx of [-w * 0.28, w * 0.28]) {
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.2, 2.0, 0.1), hashf(x + wx, f, seed) < 0.55 ? litWin() : darkWin(), wx, y, d / 2 + 0.02, { cast: false });
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.45, 2.1, 0.08), shutterM(colorIdx), wx - 0.85, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.45, 2.1, 0.08), shutterM(colorIdx), wx + 0.85, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });
      }
      if (f > 0) {
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w - 0.4, 0.18, 1.3), trimM(), 0, y - 1.15, d / 2 + 0.65);
        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w - 0.4, 0.07, 0.07), iron(), 0, y - 0.1, d / 2 + 1.25, { cast: false });
        const bal = Math.max(4, Math.round(w / 0.9));
        for (let b = 0; b <= bal; b++) put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.05, 1.0, 0.05), iron(), -w / 2 + 0.3 + b * (w - 0.6) / bal, y - 0.6, d / 2 + 1.25, { cast: false });
      }
    }
    // a gaslight by the door
    put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.22, 8, 6), basic(new THREE.Color(0xffd08a).multiplyScalar(2.2)), w * 0.42, 3.0, d / 2 + 0.3, { cast: false });
    occluders.push({ minX: x - w / 2, maxX: x + w / 2, minY: 0, maxY: h + 0.5, minZ: z - d / 2 - 1.3, maxZ: z + d / 2 + 1.3 });
    if (addBlocker) { addBlocker(x - w / 4, z, Math.min(w / 2, d / 2)); addBlocker(x + w / 4, z, Math.min(w / 2, d / 2)); }
    return grp;
  }
  /** A terrace along x0..x1 at depth z, houses 6-10 m wide, 2-3 floors, colours running along the block. */
  function rowhouses(g, x0, x1, z, side = 1, seed = 0) {
    let x = x0, i = 0;
    while (x < x1 - 5) {
      const w = Math.min(x1 - x, 6.5 + Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * 4));
      if (w < 5.5) break;
      rowhouse(g, x + w / 2, z, w, side, 2 + (hashf(x, z, seed + 1) < 0.45 ? 1 : 0), Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed + 2) * PASTELS.length) + i, seed);
      x += w; i++;
    }
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ plaza
  function plaza(g, x, z, w, d, seed = 0) {
    put(g, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.12, d), std(0xa9a397, "paving stone", { roughness: 0.95 }), x, 0.06, z, { cast: false });
    const leaf = std(0x2f5a34, "live oak leaves foliage"), trunk = std(0x4a3a28, "trunk bark");
    for (const [fx, fz] of [[-0.32, -0.3], [0.32, -0.3], [-0.32, 0.3], [0.32, 0.3]]) {
      const tx = x + fx * w, tz = z + fz * d;
      put(g, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.28, 0.4, 3, 6), trunk, tx, 1.6, tz);
      put(g, new THREE.SphereGeometry(2.6, 8, 6), leaf, tx, 4.4, tz).scale.set(1, 0.75, 1);
      if (addBlocker) addBlocker(tx, tz, 0.8);
    }
    put(g, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.4, 0.5, 0.7), std(0x5a4632, "wood bench plank"), x, 0.35, z - d * 0.12, { cast: false });
    put(g, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.4, 0.5, 0.7), std(0x5a4632, "wood bench plank"), x, 0.35, z + d * 0.12, { cast: false });
  }

  return { tower, rowhouses, rowhouse, plaza, hash: hashf };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// orlearouge.js — the south of the map: the bayou causeway and OrleaRouge.
//
// "A metropolis of French balconies, glass skyscrapers, neon nightlife,
//  historic neighborhoods, universities, casinos, music halls and sprawling
//  suburbs. It is simultaneously gorgeous and wounded."
//
//   z 136 … 192   the causeway: US-167 over open swamp, an overpass with a camp
//                 under it, a refinery burning orange to the east
//   z 196 … 382   OrleaRouge, on a street grid around the boulevard (US-167):
//                 the French District (west), downtown towers (east), the public
//                 hospital, a cemetery, a construction site, and the waterfront
//                 with a casino boat moored on the Gulf
//
// Everything is static except the neon flicker, so main.js's batchStatic
// merges the city per material and chunk. Buildings share materials; their
// UVs are scaled to their size, so one window texture tiles correctly on every
// tower without per-building materials.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

import * as THREE from "three";
import { placeOfficeClutter, placeCityBuilding, placeParkedCar } from "./landmarks.js";
import { createCemetery } from "./cemetery.js";

export const CAUSEWAY = { minZ: 136, maxZ: 192 };
// The nightlife core now continues east into a denser modern district. Keep the
// western boundary stable (the parish transition and French District depend on
// it), but give the skyline and casino lots room to grow on the east side.
export const CITY = { minX: -136, maxX: 520, minZ: 196, maxZ: 382 };

/**
 * OrleaRouge is the biggest city in the state and the only one that never said
 * so. Every other place announces a population — Shruston 231,400, Charsoufre
 * 81,210, Tusouxroe 48,200 — and this one announced none, so the largest number
 * on the map belonged to a district that is a third of its size.
 *
 * 611,470 is New Orleans (383,997) plus Baton Rouge (227,470), which is what
 * the name is: the two of them, one city.
 */
export const POPULATION = 611470;
const POP_TEXT = "pop. 611,470";

// the grid: US-167 is the boulevard at x = ROAD_X (-6)
const AVENUES = [-86, -46, 34, 74, 114, 154, 194, 234, 274, 314, 354, 394, 434, 474, 514];    // north–south streets
const STREETS = [210, 250, 290, 330, 370];        // east–west streets
const STREET_W = 9;

function basic(color) {
  const m = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color });
  m.userData.gtbRealized = true;
  return m;
}
function canvasTex(w, h, draw, repeat = true) {
  const c = document.createElement("canvas");
  c.width = w; c.height = h;
  draw(c.getContext("2d"), w, h);
  const t = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
  t.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  if (repeat) t.wrapS = t.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping;
  return t;
}
/**
 * A tiling water-surface normal map: long, low swells with finer chop across
 * them. Written as a real normal map (RGB = XYZ) rather than a grey bump,
 * because the water material is physical and its clearcoat needs a believable
 * surface to reflect the sky and the neon off.
 *
 * `stretch` is how many times longer a swell is than it is wide. Above 1 the
 * crests lie along u — along the shore, for the gulf plane — which is the
 * orientation both a current and a shoreward swell want; only the axis they
 * scroll on differs.
 */
function waterNormalTex(size = 256, stretch = 5) {
  const c = document.createElement("canvas");
  c.width = c.height = size;
  const g = c.getContext("2d");
  const img = g.createImageData(size, size);
  // a small sum of sines makes a seamless, tileable height field: every term
  // uses an integer number of periods across the texture, so the edges match
  // Wavenumbers MUST be whole numbers of periods across the texture or it does
  // not tile — a fractional kx leaves a seam every repeat, which at this scale
  // is a visible line straight across the water every tile.
  //
  // Long wavelength along the flow (small kx) and short across it (kz = kx *
  // stretch) is what gives swells that lie down the current instead of a
  // uniform ripple.
  const waves = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    const kx = 1 + i;
    waves.push({
      kx,                                    // few periods along the flow: long swells
      kz: Math.max(1, Math.round(kx * stretch)),   // many across it: chop
      amp: 1 / (1 + i * 1.3),
      phase: i * 1.7,                        // break up the harmonic regularity
    });
  }
  const height = (u, v) => {
    let h = 0;
    for (const w of waves) {
      h += w.amp * Math.sin((u * w.kx + v * w.kz) * Math.PI * 2 + w.phase);
    }
    return h;
  };
  const e = 1 / size;
  for (let y = 0; y < size; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < size; x++) {
      const u = x / size, v = y / size;
      // central differences give the slope, and the normal is its cross product
      const dx = (height(u + e, v) - height(u - e, v)) / (2 * e);
      const dz = (height(u, v + e) - height(u, v - e)) / (2 * e);
      const sc = 0.012;                      // keep the surface gentle, not choppy
      let nx = -dx * sc, ny = 1, nz = -dz * sc;
      const len = Math.hypot(nx, ny, nz);
      nx /= len; ny /= len; nz /= len;
      const i = (y * size + x) * 4;
      img.data[i] = (nx * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255;
      img.data[i + 1] = (nz * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255;
      img.data[i + 2] = (ny * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255;
      img.data[i + 3] = 255;
    }

    water.userData.gtbRealized = true;
    const x0 = ctx.ROAD_X - ctx.ROAD_HALF, x1 = ctx.ROAD_X + ctx.ROAD_HALF;
    const len = CAUSEWAY.maxZ - CAUSEWAY.minZ + 8;
    const zc = (CAUSEWAY.minZ + CAUSEWAY.maxZ) / 2;
    plane(x0 - 2 + 140, len, water, (x0 - 2 - 140) / 2, 0.035, zc);
    plane(400 - x1 - 2, len, water, (x1 + 2 + 400) / 2, 0.035, zc);

    // guardrails the whole way across, solid for walkers and cars
    const rail = std("steel guardrail", 0x9aa0a6, { metalness: 0.8, roughness: 0.4 });
    for (const x of [x0 - 0.6, x1 + 0.6]) {
      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.25, 0.7, len), rail, x, 0.6, zc);
      for (let z = CAUSEWAY.minZ; z <= CAUSEWAY.maxZ; z += 3) ctx.addBlocker(x, z, 0.55);
    }

    // an overpass crossing high above, with a camp underneath
    const concrete = std("concrete overpass", 0x8f8c86);
    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(150, 1.2, 9), concrete, 0, 8, 172);
    occluders.push({ minX: -75, maxX: 75, minY: 7.4, maxY: 8.6, minZ: 167.5, maxZ: 176.5 });
    for (const px of [-40, -18, 6, 30, 55]) {
      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.6, 8, 1.6), concrete, px, 4, 172);
      ctx.addBlocker(px, 172, 1.3);
    }
    const tarp = [std("canvas tarp", 0x3b5a7a), std("canvas tarp", 0x7a5a3b), std("canvas tarp", 0x5a6b3b)];
    for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
      const t = mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(1.3, 1.5, 4), tarp[i % 3], -34 + i * 2.6, 0.75, 170 + (i % 2) * 3.5);
      t.rotation.y = Math.PI / 4;
      ctx.addBlocker(-34 + i * 2.6, 170 + (i % 2) * 3.5, 1.1);
    }
    mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.4, 0.4, 0.9, 10), std("steel barrel", 0x4a3a2a), -24, 0.45, 175.5);
    mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.35, 8, 6), basic(new THREE.Color(0xff8a2a).multiplyScalar(3)), -24, 1.05, 175.5, { cast: false });
    ctx.poolLight(0xff8a3a, 26, 16, -24, 1.6, 175.5);
    pois.push({ x: -28, z: 176, r: 7 });

    // the refinery, burning orange against the horizon
    const tank = std("steel tank", 0xb8bdc2, { metalness: 0.6, roughness: 0.45 });
    plane(40, 44, std("concrete pad", 0x6f6c66), 116, 0.02, 164);
    for (const [x, z, r, h] of [[104, 150, 5, 7], [104, 164, 5, 7], [120, 178, 4, 6], [128, 152, 3, 18], [112, 182, 2, 26]]) {
      mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r, r, h, 20), tank, x, h / 2, z);
      ctx.addBlocker(x, z, r + 0.3);
    }
    for (const [x, z] of [[126, 168], [132, 146]]) {
      mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.7, 34, 10), tank, x, 17, z);
      const flame = mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.9, 3.4, 10), basic(new THREE.Color(0xff7a1a).multiplyScalar(4)), x, 35.6, z, { cast: false });
      neon.push({ mat: flame.material, base: 4, speed: 14, phase: x, flicker: 0.35, color: new THREE.Color(0xff7a1a) });
      ctx.poolLight(0xff7a2a, 70, 60, x, 30, z);
    }
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- streets
  function buildStreets() {
    const concrete = ctx.surface("concrete", 1024);
    const side = concrete.material(1, { color: 0xb8b2a8 });
    const cw = CITY.maxX - CITY.minX, cd = CITY.maxZ - CITY.minZ + 4;
    for (const t of [side.map, side.normalMap, side.roughnessMap]) if (t) t.repeat.set(cw / 12, cd / 12);
    plane(cw, cd, side, 0, 0.012, (CITY.minZ + CITY.maxZ) / 2);

    const asphalt = ctx.surface("asphalt", 1024);
    const street = (w, d, x, z) => {
      const m = asphalt.material(1);
      for (const t of [m.map, m.normalMap, m.roughnessMap]) if (t) t.repeat.set(Math.max(1, w / 9), Math.max(1, d / 9));
      plane(w, d, m, x, 0.022, z);
    };
    for (const x of AVENUES) street(STREET_W, CITY.maxZ - CITY.minZ, x, (CITY.minZ + CITY.maxZ) / 2);
    for (const z of STREETS) street(CITY.maxX - CITY.minX, STREET_W, 0, z);

    // lamps: down the boulevard, along two French District streets, the promenade
    for (let z = 204; z < 376; z += 40) {
      ctx.addLitSpot({ x: ctx.ROAD_X + ctx.ROAD_HALF + 2, y: 6, z, warm: 0xffd9a0, power: 110, range: 26, pole: true });

      }
    }
    return out;
  }

  function outskirts(bl) {

      } else {

  function frenchDistrict(bl) {

        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {

      }

  function riverfront() {
    // The Gulf, not a river. This was a silt-brown Mississippi; the brief is now
    // open salt water, so it is green-blue — the Gulf of Mexico's colour comes
    // from depth and plankton rather than from suspended mud, which is why it
    // reads emerald-to-teal offshore instead of café-au-lait.
    //
    // Lower roughness than the silt version and a slightly stronger environment
    // term: clear sea takes a sharper sky reflection than a river carrying half
    // of Missouri in suspension.
    const gulf = new THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial({
      color: 0x1a4a4c, roughness: 0.11, clearcoat: 1, clearcoatRoughness: 0.06,
      envMapIntensity: 1.3, name: "gulf water",
    });
    gulf.userData.gtbRealized = true;
    // KEEP THIS ABOVE ZERO. It was drawn at y = -0.25 — BELOW the world ground.
    // main.js's buildGround() lays one plane across the whole 2400 m state at
    // y = 0, so the water was buried under it and never visible at all: the
    // Grand Crescent sat on grass. Everything in this game stacks in small
    // positive increments for exactly that reason (GROUND_Y in main.js, and the
    // causeway swamp above at 0.035).
    //
    // How far out it goes. +z is SOUTH in this world (the causeway at z 136 is
    // north of the city at 196–382), so open water on the far side of the
    // promenade is geographically where the Gulf belongs.
    //
    // DEPTH IS CONSTRAINED BY LAND, not by taste. Running this 320 m out to hide
    // the far bank was tried and reverted: there are ~220 blockers between z 386
    // and 706 across this whole frontage — stateWorld.js's own tree scatter,
    // plus a structure around x 550 — and a gulf with two hundred pines standing
    // in it looks far worse than a narrower one that reads clean. main.js's
    // buildTrees already keeps out of everything past z 142; this scatter
    // belongs to another module and clearing it is that module's job.
    //
    // So: the authored 80 m footprint, which reads as one of the sounds and
    // bays the Louisiana coast is actually made of — salt water with land on
    // the far side, which is Mississippi Sound and Lake Borgne, not a river.
    // See AGENT_LOG for what a true open-water horizon would take.
    const SHORE_Z = CITY.maxZ + 1;          // the promenade railing sits at +1.2
    const GULF_D = 80;
    const GULF_W = CITY.maxX - CITY.minX + 40;
    plane(GULF_W, GULF_D, gulf, (CITY.maxX + CITY.minX) / 2, 0.03, SHORE_Z + GULF_D / 2);

    // ---- the swell ----
    // A river's surface travels ALONG the channel. A sea's does not: the swell
    // rolls shoreward, and its crests lie parallel to the beach. Same texture
    // orientation as before — `stretch > 1` puts the crests along x, which here
    // is along the shore — but it now scrolls on the OTHER axis.
    //
    // The plane is rotated -90° about x, so its local +y maps to world -z.
    // Increasing the v offset therefore walks the swell toward the shore, which
    // is the one direction ocean waves are ever seen to go.
    //
    // Long period, low amplitude: the Gulf off Louisiana is shallow and fetch-
    // limited, so it runs to a lazy 3-4 second chop rather than Pacific
    // groundswell. Crest speed ~3 m/s reads as that without looking like a
    // washing machine.
    const TILE = 34;                       // metres per repeat: sea swells are longer than river ripples
    const swell = waterNormalTex(256, 7);
    swell.repeat.set(GULF_W / TILE, GULF_D / TILE);
    const chop = waterNormalTex(256, 4);
    chop.repeat.set(GULF_W / (TILE * 0.4), GULF_D / (TILE * 0.4));
    gulf.normalMap = swell;
    gulf.normalScale = new THREE.Vector2(0.7, 0.7);
    gulf.clearcoatNormalMap = chop;
    gulf.clearcoatNormalScale = new THREE.Vector2(0.35, 0.35);
    gulf.needsUpdate = true;
    currents.push(
      { map: swell, tile: TILE, speed: 3.0 },              // the swell, rolling in
      { map: chop, tile: TILE * 0.4, speed: 4.4 },         // wind chop over the top of it
    );

    gulfCauseway(SHORE_Z, GULF_D);
    // promenade railing, solid
    const rail = std("wrought iron railing", 0x1c1f22, { metalness: 0.6, roughness: 0.5 });
    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(CITY.maxX - CITY.minX, 0.08, 0.08), rail, 0, 1.0, CITY.maxZ + 1.2, { cast: false });
    for (let x = CITY.minX + 2; x < CITY.maxX; x += 2.5) {
      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.06, 1.0, 0.06), rail, x, 0.5, CITY.maxZ + 1.2, { cast: false });
    }

    // the casino riverboat
    const white = std("painted hull", 0xf2efe6), red = std("painted trim", 0xb3261e);
    const bx = 48, bz = CITY.maxZ + 16;
    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(34, 3, 11), white, bx, 1.2, bz);
    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(28, 2.6, 9), white, bx, 4.0, bz);
    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(18, 2.4, 7), white, bx, 6.5, bz);
    for (const y of [2.8, 5.3]) mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(34.4, 0.3, 11.4), red, bx, y, bz, { cast: false });
    const wheel = mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(3.6, 3.6, 2.4, 16), red, bx + 19, 2.6, bz);
    wheel.rotation.z = Math.PI / 2;
    for (const sx of [-4, 4]) mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.7, 6, 10), std("steel stack", 0x1c1c1c), bx + sx, 10.5, bz);
    const bulb = basic(new THREE.Color(0xffe6a8).multiplyScalar(2.5));
    for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.16, 6, 5), bulb, bx - 16 + i * 2.1, 5.45, bz - 5.5, { cast: false });
    neonSign("GRAND CRESCENT CASINO", "#ffd23a", "#2a0808", 16, 2.2, bx, 9.2, bz - 3.6, Math.PI, 0.08);
    ctx.poolLight(0xffd9a0, 60, 34, bx, 8, bz - 6);
    pois.push({ x: bx, z: CITY.maxZ - 3, r: 10 });
    pois.push({ x: -40, z: CITY.maxZ - 3, r: 10 });
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- build
  function buildSet() {
    buildCauseway();
    buildStreets();
    const bl = blocks();
    const pick = (x, z) => bl.find((b) => x > b.x0 && x < b.x1 && z > b.z0 && z < b.z1);
    const special = new Set();
    const hosp = pick(-26, 350), cem = pick(-110, 350), site = pick(94, 230);
    if (hosp) { hospital(hosp); special.add(hosp); }
    if (cem) { cemetery(cem); special.add(cem); }
    if (site) { construction(site); special.add(site); }
    // blocks other modules build on (main.js passes them: the Pay 'n' Spray lot, the clubs)
    for (const lot of ctx.lots || []) {
      const b = pick(lot.at[0], lot.at[1]);
      if (b && !special.has(b)) { special.add(b); lot.build(b); }
    }
    const rest = bl.filter((b) => !special.has(b));
    outskirts(rest);
    frenchDistrict(rest);
    downtown(rest);
    shops(rest);
    riverfront();
    // street corners along the boulevard are where people hang out
    for (const z of STREETS) pois.push({ x: ctx.ROAD_X + 10, z: z + 7, r: 5 }, { x: ctx.ROAD_X - 10, z: z - 7, r: 5 });

    // Add parked cars to some streets
    const cars = ["beatall", "doclorean", "landyroamer", "toyoyo", "tristar"];
    let c = 0;
    for (const z of STREETS) {
      if (z > 210) { // Don't park on the causeway boundary
        placeParkedCar(ctx, cars[c++ % cars.length], ctx.ROAD_X + 20, z - 4.5, -Math.PI / 2);
        placeParkedCar(ctx, cars[c++ % cars.length], ctx.ROAD_X - 30, z + 4.5, Math.PI / 2);
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    buildSet,
    /** The street grid, for the minimap: north–south avenues at x, east–west streets at z. */
    grid: { avenues: AVENUES, streets: STREETS, width: STREET_W, city: CITY, causeway: CAUSEWAY },
    get pois() { return pois; },
    get occluders() { return occluders; },
    /** Anything in the city that moves — main.js keeps these out of batchStatic. */
    get props() { return graveyard ? graveyard.props : []; },
    /** F at Marie Laveau's tomb. main.js tries this in its interact chain. */
    interact() { return graveyard ? graveyard.interact() : false; },
    get cemetery() { return graveyard; },
    get entered() { return entered; },
    /** Keep trees and scattered decor out. */
    contains(x, z) { return z > CAUSEWAY.minZ; },
    // The rural parish lies west of the city. It used to be bounded on those two sides only, which was
    // right while the map ended here; with the state around it, everything south and east of OrleaRouge
    // (Oyster Bay, US-167 south, the Lakeshore road) counted as the city too: no NPC ever spawned
    // there (the city spawns at its own POIs) and the "EXT. ORLEAROUGE" card fired in Oyster Bay.
    inCity(x, z) { return z > CITY.minZ && z < CITY.maxZ + 8 && x >= CITY.minX - 2 && x <= CITY.maxX + 2; },

    /** Traffic lanes for two cross streets (both directions), for createTraffic. */
    lanes: [
      { name: "250 eastbound", points: [[CITY.minX + 4, 247.6], [CITY.maxX - 4, 247.6]], cruise: [9, 14] },
      { name: "250 westbound", points: [[CITY.maxX - 4, 252.4], [CITY.minX + 4, 252.4]], cruise: [9, 14] },
      { name: "330 eastbound", points: [[CITY.minX + 4, 327.6], [CITY.maxX - 4, 327.6]], cruise: [9, 14] },
      { name: "330 westbound", points: [[CITY.maxX - 4, 332.4], [CITY.minX + 4, 332.4]], cruise: [9, 14] },
      { name: "210 eastbound", points: [[CITY.minX + 4, 207.6], [CITY.maxX - 4, 207.6]], cruise: [8, 13] },
      { name: "210 westbound", points: [[CITY.maxX - 4, 212.4], [CITY.minX + 4, 212.4]], cruise: [8, 13] },
      { name: "370 eastbound", points: [[CITY.minX + 4, 367.6], [CITY.maxX - 4, 367.6]], cruise: [8, 13] },
      { name: "370 westbound", points: [[CITY.maxX - 4, 372.4], [CITY.minX + 4, 372.4]], cruise: [8, 13] },
    ],

    update(dt) {
      if (graveyard) graveyard.update(dt);
      // The swell rolls in. `offset` shifts where the texture is SAMPLED, so the
      // pattern travels the opposite way — and the plane's local +y is world
      // -z, so ADDING to offset.y walks the crests shoreward.
      for (const c of currents) {
        c.map.offset.y = (c.map.offset.y + (c.speed / c.tile) * dt) % 1;
      }
      const t = performance.now() / 1000;
      for (const n of neon) {
        // mostly steady, with the occasional sputter
        const s = Math.sin(t * n.speed + n.phase);
        const dip = s > 0.97 ? n.flicker * 3 : Math.max(0, s) * n.flicker;
        if (n.color) n.mat.color.copy(n.color).multiplyScalar(n.base * (1 - dip));
        else n.mat.emissiveIntensity = n.base * (1 - dip);
      }
      if (!entered && ctx.playerPos.z > CITY.minZ + 6 && ctx.playerPos.z < CITY.maxZ + 8 && ctx.playerPos.x > CITY.minX - 2 && ctx.playerPos.x < CITY.maxX + 2 && !ctx.state.cinematic) {   // inside the grid (not merely south-east of its corner: Oyster Bay, the prison...)
        entered = true;
        ctx.cine.scene(async (c) => {
          c.card("EXT.", "ORLEAROUGE", POP_TEXT + " · Gorgeous and wounded");
          await c.wait(1.2);
          await c.say("KESEME (V.O.)", "OrleaRouge teaches you two things.");
          await c.say("KESEME (V.O.)", "Life can be beautiful.");
          c.sfx("gunshot", 0.5);
          await c.say("KESEME (V.O.)", "And beauty doesn't make you safe.");
        });
      }
    },
  };

export function makePavement(spec) {
  const rng = mulberry((spec.seed | 0) || 11);
  const line = spec.line;
  const door = spec.door;
  const spots = spec.spots || [];
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  const actors = [];
  const count = spec.count ?? 8;
  let meshes = 0;

  // Parties, not a stream of solitaries: a third of the block walks in twos and
  // threes, and a group shares a destination, which is what makes a queue look
  // like a queue instead of four people who happen to be near each other.
  let left = count;
  while (left > 0) {
    const size = left > 2 && rng() < 0.34 ? 2 + ((rng() * 2) | 0) : 1;
    const n = Math.min(size, left);
    left -= n;
    const x0 = line.x0 + rng() * (line.x1 - line.x0);
    const speed = 1.05 + rng() * 0.5;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      // mostly the strip's own mix; every fifth one is a dancer, because a
      // pavement in front of a nightclub has somebody in it who cannot stay still

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// npc.js — NPC behaviour: people and hogs who live here, not a swarm.
//
// Civilians, not enemies. Everyone idles, loiters and wanders their home turf
// and ignores the player; default aggression is zero. Violence nearby makes
// people scatter. Only an NPC the player actually hurts reacts, and its
// temperament decides how: it defends itself (fights back) or it flees.
//
//   idle / loiter  — standing around, facing a neighbour if one is close
//   wander         — strolling to a point on its home turf, or to another spot
//   flee           — running from gunfire or a fight, then calming down
//   hostile        — defending itself after being attacked: chase / charge / melee
//
// Cost: decisions run on staggered timers (not per frame), and distance sets
// the level of detail — near NPCs get everything, mid-range ones think rarely
// and animate every third frame, far ones are paused until you come back.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

import * as THREE from "three";
import { vehicleRight } from "./vehicles.js";

const rand = (lo, hi) => lo + (hi - lo) * Math.random();
const _aim = new THREE.Vector3();
const NEAR = 55, FAR = 110;
const ZOMBIE_SCENT = 100;      // metres: an idle zombie inside this drifts toward the player (just under FAR, where NPCs freeze)
export const MAX_HOSTILE = 7;      // never let the whole map pile onto the player
// Market Row keeps Saturday hours: bustling trade 09:00–18:00, but only from
// day 2 on — the game opens at 18:30 on day 1, so the first evening is quiet.
const MARKET_OPEN = 9, MARKET_CLOSE = 18;

// Nobody attacks unprovoked. Temperament only matters once the player hurts an
// NPC: "brave" people and "territorial" hogs defend themselves, the rest run.
export const DEFAULT_AGGRESSION = 0;
function temperament(type) {
  const r = Math.random();
  if (type === "hog") return r < 0.4 ? "territorial" : "skittish";
  // klan.js: they arrive as a mob, at night, to frighten somebody. A hood that
  // turns and runs the moment it is faced is a different scene from the one
  // being written, so they are never timid — the rest of the temperament roll
  // would have made two thirds of any night ride scatter on first contact.
  if (type === "klansman") return "brave";
  // zombie-mode (main.js): mood is moot — decide() never routes a zombie
  // through the provoked flee-or-fight check below, they're hostile from the
  // moment they notice anything — but "territorial" keeps them out of the
  // "timid"/"skittish" flee branch if that ever changes.
  if (type === "zombie") return "territorial";
  if (type === "redneck") return r < 0.5 ? "brave" : "timid";
  return r < 0.35 ? "brave" : "timid";
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// metro.js — Downtown Bayou: the city that grows up on both sides of US-167 around the spawn strip (human request, 2026-09-27:
// "the area around the Crown Strip and the spawn area is our city area — a very metropolis, very modern New Orleans vibe").
//
// The roadside stores along the highway stay where they are (their lots are claimed); behind them, east and west, a street grid of
// blocks: glass and art-deco towers near the highway, hotel slabs, plazas with live oaks, and French Quarter terraces (stucco, shutters,
// iron balconies, gaslights) out toward the edges — the skyline of the Crown Strip to the north and OrleaRouge to the south, joined up.
//
// Composed with composer.js like the other districts; the parts (towers, rowhouses, plazas) are in cityparts.js.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

import * as THREE from "three";
import { createComposer } from "./composer.js";
import { createCityParts } from "./cityparts.js";
import { onParishHighway } from "./westparish.js";

const ROAD_X = -6;
export const METRO_BOUNDS = { x0: -292, x1: 292, z0: -132, z1: 128 };
const STREETS_Z = [-108, -52, 4, 60, 112];
const AVENUES_X = [-168, 168];
const STREET_W = 10, AVENUE_W = 12;
// blocks: rows between the streets, columns between the avenues and the highway lots
const ROWS = [[-101, -59], [-45, -3], [11, 53], [67, 105]];
const COLS = [[-263, -175], [-161, -73], [63, 161], [175, 263]];

export function createMetro(ctx) {
  const { scene } = ctx;
  const occluders = [];
  const parts = createCityParts(ctx, { occluders });
  const hash = parts.hash;
  const C = createComposer(ctx, { name: "Metro", bounds: METRO_BOUNDS, zones: { core: METRO_BOUNDS, wild: METRO_BOUNDS }, seed: 4711 });
  const pois = [];
  let announced = false;

  const lanes = [];
  for (const z of STREETS_Z) {
    lanes.push({ name: `metro ${z} eastbound`, points: [[62, z + 2.2], [274, z + 2.2]], cruise: [8, 13] });
    lanes.push({ name: `metro ${z} westbound`, points: [[274, z - 2.2], [62, z - 2.2]], cruise: [8, 13] });
    lanes.push({ name: `metro ${z} west-eastbound`, points: [[-274, z + 2.2], [-72, z + 2.2]], cruise: [8, 13] });
    lanes.push({ name: `metro ${z} west-westbound`, points: [[-72, z - 2.2], [-274, z - 2.2]], cruise: [8, 13] });
  }
  for (const x of AVENUES_X) {
    lanes.push({ name: `metro avenue ${x} northbound`, points: [[x + 2.4, 118], [x + 2.4, -118]], cruise: [9, 14] });
    lanes.push({ name: `metro avenue ${x} southbound`, points: [[x - 2.4, -118], [x - 2.4, 118]], cruise: [9, 14] });
  }

  function buildSet() {
    // ---- what is already there, claimed before anything is composed: the highway and its roadside lots (stores, gas, the trailer park and
    // the junkyard), and Parish Highway 9 swinging away to the south-west
    C.claim({ x0: -62, x1: 52, z0: METRO_BOUNDS.z0, z1: METRO_BOUNDS.z1 });
    for (let x = -292; x < -60; x += 8) for (let z = METRO_BOUNDS.z0; z < METRO_BOUNDS.z1; z += 8) {
      if (onParishHighway(x + 4, z + 4, 30)) C.claim({ x0: x, x1: x + 8, z0: z, z1: z + 8 });
    }

    // ---- roads. Streets stop at the highway lots and at the outer edge; the avenues run the full depth.
    for (const z of STREETS_Z) {
      C.road(`Metro Street ${z}`, [[56, z], [280, z]], { width: STREET_W, lampEvery: 38, y: 0.021 });
      C.road(`Metro Street W ${z}`, [[-280, z], [-66, z]], { width: STREET_W, lampEvery: 38, y: 0.021 });
    }
    for (const x of AVENUES_X) C.road(`Bayou Avenue ${x}`, [[x, -120], [x, 120]], { width: AVENUE_W, lampEvery: 34, y: 0.022 });

    // ---- the blocks
    let n = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < COLS.length; i++) {
      for (let j = 0; j < ROWS.length; j++) {
        const [x0, x1] = COLS[i], [z0, z1] = ROWS[j];
        const b = { x0, x1, z0, z1, cx: (x0 + x1) / 2, cz: (z0 + z1) / 2, w: x1 - x0, d: z1 - z0 };
        if (!C.isFree({ x0: b.x0, x1: b.x1, z0: b.z0, z1: b.z1 })) {
          // the highway's exclusion clips this block: fill whichever thirds are still free with a smaller building each, so the city does not
          // stop in a ragged blank edge beside Parish Highway 9
          const third = b.w / 3;
          for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
            const sb = { x0: b.x0 + k * third + 1, x1: b.x0 + (k + 1) * third - 1, z0: b.z0, z1: b.z1 };
            if (!C.isFree(sb)) continue;
            const scx = (sb.x0 + sb.x1) / 2, scz = (sb.z0 + sb.z1) / 2, sw = sb.x1 - sb.x0, sd = sb.z1 - sb.z0, hh = hash(scx, scz, 11);
            C.cluster(`partial ${n}.${k}`, () => {
              const g = new THREE.Group(); scene.add(g);
              if (hh < 0.45) parts.tower(g, scx, scz, Math.min(28, sw - 4), Math.min(26, sd - 8), 40 + hash(scx, scz, 12) * 44, [0, 1, 3][(n + k) % 3], n + k);
              else if (hh < 0.75) parts.rowhouses(g, sb.x0 + 1, sb.x1 - 1, sb.z0 + 5, -1, n + k);
              else parts.plaza(g, scx, scz, sw - 6, sd - 10, n + k);
              if (hh >= 0.45 && hh < 0.75) parts.rowhouses(g, sb.x0 + 1, sb.x1 - 1, sb.z1 - 5, 1, n + k + 5);
            });
            C.claim(sb);
          }
          n++;
          continue;
        }
        const core = Math.abs(b.cx - ROAD_X) < 150;                                     // the two columns beside the highway are downtown
        const r = hash(b.cx, b.cz, 5);
        C.cluster(`block ${n}`, () => {
          const g = new THREE.Group(); scene.add(g);
          const mid = hash(b.cx, b.cz, 6);
          if (core ? r < 0.42 : r < 0.3) {
            // twin towers on a shared podium plaza
            const hA = core ? 78 + mid * 46 : 42 + mid * 26, hB = core ? 64 + hash(b.cx, b.cz, 7) * 44 : 36 + hash(b.cx, b.cz, 7) * 24;
            parts.tower(g, b.cx - b.w * 0.24, b.cz, Math.min(34, b.w * 0.34), Math.min(30, b.d - 8), hA, [0, 3, 1][n % 3], n);
            parts.tower(g, b.cx + b.w * 0.24, b.cz, Math.min(32, b.w * 0.32), Math.min(28, b.d - 10), hB, [1, 0, 3][n % 3], n + 1);
            parts.plaza(g, b.cx, b.cz, b.w * 0.2, b.d - 8, n);
          } else if (core ? r < 0.72 : r < 0.5) {
            // an art-deco tower with a live-oak plaza beside it
            const flip = hash(b.cx, b.cz, 8) < 0.5 ? -1 : 1;
            parts.tower(g, b.cx + flip * b.w * 0.2, b.cz, Math.min(36, b.w * 0.4), Math.min(32, b.d - 8), core ? 92 + mid * 34 : 50 + mid * 20, 1, n);
            parts.plaza(g, b.cx - flip * b.w * 0.26, b.cz, b.w * 0.38, b.d - 8, n);
          } else if (core ? r < 0.88 : r < 0.62) {
            // a long hotel slab
            parts.tower(g, b.cx, b.cz, Math.min(64, b.w - 14), Math.min(26, b.d - 14), core ? 48 + mid * 22 : 34 + mid * 14, 2, n);
          } else {
            // the French Quarter: terraces along the block's two long sides, a courtyard between
            parts.rowhouses(g, b.x0 + 2, b.x1 - 2, b.z0 + 5, -1, n);
            parts.rowhouses(g, b.x0 + 2, b.x1 - 2, b.z1 - 5, 1, n + 7);
            parts.plaza(g, b.cx, b.cz, b.w - 24, b.d - 26, n);
          }
          pois.push({ x: b.cx, z: b.z0 - 5, r: 8, label: "Downtown" });
        });
        C.claim({ x0: b.x0, x1: b.x1, z0: b.z0, z1: b.z1 });
        n++;
      }
    }
    return n;
  }

1 : 0;\n      uv[u + 1] = k >= 2 ? 1 : 0;\n      u += 2;\n    }\n    idx.set([base, base + 2, base + 1, base, base + 3, base + 2], i * 6);\n  }\n  const g = new THREE.BufferGeometry();\n  g.setAttribute(\"position\", new THREE.BufferAttribute(pos, 3));\n  g.setAttribute(\"normal\", new THREE.BufferAttribute(nor, 3));\n  g.setAttribute(\"uv\", new THREE.BufferAttribute(uv, 2));\n  g.setIndex(new THREE.BufferAttribute(idx, 1));\n  return g;\n}\n\n// American convention, and the reason a New Orleans road reads as a Louisiana\n// road: a warm white for lane and edge lines, a yellow for the median, and a\n// white for everything else.\nconst WHITE = 0xf2f0e6;\nconst YELLOW = 0xd9b93a;\nconst CROSSWALK = 0xf6f4ea;\n\nexport const MARKING_DEFAULTS = Object.freeze({\n  laneWidth: 2.4,\n  median: 0.4,\n  edgeInset: 0.18,      // white edge line, in from the kerb\n  dashLength: 2.6,\n  dashGap: 3.4,         // 6 m pitch, so a dash reads at speed without strobing\n  lineWidth: 0.16,\n  medianGap: 0.22,      // the two yellow lines are this far apart, centre to centre\n  crosswalkStripe: 0.55,\n  crosswalkGap: 0.55,\n  crosswalkDepth: 3.0,\n  stopBarWidth: 0.45,\n});\n\nexport function createMarkings({ y = 0.031, material = null } = {}) {\n  const D = MARKING_DEFAULTS;\n  const mats = new Map();\n  const mat = (color) => {\n    if (material) return material;\n    if (!mats.has(color)) {\n      const m = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({\n        color, roughness: 0.62, metalness: 0, envMapIntensity: 1.1, name: \"road paint\",\n      });\n      m.userData.gtbRealized = true;\n      mats.set(color, m);\n    }\n    return mats.get(color);\n  };\n\n  const whites = [], yellows = [], bars = [];\n  // One mesh per colour per parent, created lazily and flushed by flush().\n  const meshes = new Map();\n\n  const push = (bucket, it) => (it ? 0 : 0)];\n      return [x, z];\n    });\n    void line;\n    let travelled = dash;                       // start half a dash in, so it is not flush with the kerb\n    for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) {\n      const [ax, az] = pts[i - 1], [bx, bz] = pts[i];\n      let dx = bx - ax, dz = bz - az;\n      const seg = Math.hypot(dx, dz);\n      if (seg < 0.01) continue;\n      dx /= seg; dz /= seg;\n      const rx = dz, rz = -dx;                  // right of travel\n      let s = 0;\n      while (s < seg) {\n        // where are we in the dash cycle along this segment?\n        const phase = ((travelled + s) % (dash + gap));\n        if (phase < dash) {\n          const run = Math.min(dash - phase, seg - s);\n          const mid = s + run / 2;\n          const w = alongX ? D.crosswalkStripe : D.crosswalkDepth;\n      const dx = alongX ? 0 : off, dz = alongX ? off : 0;\n      const c = Math.cos(ry), s = Math.sin(ry);\n      bars.push({ x: x + dx * c - dz * s, y: y0 + 0.002, z: z + dx * s + dz * c, w, d, ry });\n    }\n    return { x, z, half, alongX, ry, depth: D.crosswalkDepth, span };\n  }\n\n  /** A stop bar across the approaching lanes, set back from the crossing. */\n  function stopBar(x, z, { alongX = true, half = 5, y0 = y, ry = 0, inset = 0.6 } = {}) {\n    const c = Math.cos(ry), s = Math.sin(ry);\n    const push2 = (ox, oz) => bars.push({\n      x: x + ox * c - oz * s, y: y0 + 0.002, z: z + ox * s + oz * c,\n      w: alongX ? D.stopBarWidth : half * 2, d: alongX ? half * 2 : D.stopBarWidth, ry,\n    });\n    const back = D.crosswalkDepth / 2 + inset;\n    if (alongX) { push2(-back, 0); push2(back, 0); } else { push2(0, -back); push2(0, back); }\n  }\n\n  /** Everything that belongs to one junction: four crossings and their bars. */\n  function junction(x, z, { alongX = true, half = 5, y0 = y, striped = true, bars: withBars = true } = {}) {\n    const ends = [];\n    for (const s of [1, -1]) {\n      const c = crosswalk(x, z + s * (half + D.crosswalkDepth / 2 + 1.2), {\n        alongX, half, stripes: 7, y0, ry: 0,\n      });\n      ends.push(c);\n      if (withBars) stopBar(x, z + s * (half + D.crosswalkDepth + 1.8), { alongX, half, y0 });\n    }\n    if (striped) {\n      for (const s of [1, -1]) {\n        crosswalk(x + s * (half + D.crosswalkDepth / 2 + 1.2), z, {\n          alongX: !alongX, half, stripes: 7, y0,\n        });\n      }\n    }\n    return ends;\n  }\n\n  /** Build the meshes and add them to `parent`. Call once, after all painting. */\n  function flush(parent) {\n    const out = [];\n    for (const [bucket, colour] of [[whites, WHITE], [yellows, YELLOW], [bars, CROSSWALK]]) {\n      if (!bucket.length) continue;\n      const m = new THREE.Mesh(quadsGeometry(bucket), mat(colour));\n      m.receiveShadow = true;\n      m.castShadow = false;\n      m.userData.gtbPaint = true;              // flat on the ground: never an occluder\n      parent.add(m);\n      out.push(m);\n    }\n    whites.length = yellows.length = bars.length = 0;\n    return out;\n  }\n\n  return { roadway, crosswalk, stopBar, junction, flush, get pending() { return whites.length + yellows.length + bars.length; }, D, y };\n}\n\n/**\n * The far edge of the paved width, matching makeRoadway's outermost lane\n * boundary. Districts need this to place kerbs, crossings and lamps against\n * the tarmac rather than guessing.\n */\nexport function roadwayHalf({ lanes = 1, median = null, laneWidth = 2.4 } = {}) {\n  const n = Math.max(1, lanes);\n  const m = median != null ? median : n > 1 ? 1.2 : 0;\n  return m / 2 + (n - 0.5) * laneWidth;\n}\n"
}

The z values are the\n// districts' own cross-street coordinates (orlearouge STREETS, metro\n// STREETS_Z, chatboro MAIN_X's cross streets), gathered rather than invented so\n// the zebra lands on the tarmac of a street that is actually there.\nconst US167_JUNCTIONS = Object.freeze([\n  207, 247, 287, 327, 367,          // OrleaRouge's five east-west streets\n  -52, 4, 60, 112,                  // Metro's\n  -78,                               // Tusouxroe's Main Street\n  -10,                               // Chatboro's main cross street\n]);",

  "content": "// markings_test.mjs — the paint has to agree with the traffic.\n//\n// The failure this guards against is specific and has already happened once:\n// US-167 was four lanes with a single dashed line down the middle of the\n// carriageway, and nobody could see the lanes because nothing on the road said\n// they existed. A marking system that silently stops painting, or that paints\n// somewhere other than where the cars are, reproduces exactly that — silently.\n//\n// So these assert the GEOMETRY, not that \"something was created\": a dash's\n// offset is compared against makeRoadway's own lane offset, and they have to be\n// the same number.\n\nimport { createSandbox } from \"./_sandbox.mjs\";\n\nconst sb = await createSandbox();\nconst { createMarkings, roadwayHalf, MARKING_DEFAULTS } = await sb.load(\"src/markings.js\");\nconst { makeRoadway } = await sb.load(\"src/traffic.js\");\n\nlet fails = 0;\nconst ok = (cond, msg) => { if (!cond) { console.error(\"  FAIL: \" + msg); fails++; } };\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- geometry\n{\n  const parent = new sb.THREE.Group();\n  const M = createMarkings({ y: 0.03 });\n  const road = { points: [[0, 0], [0, 400]], lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4 };\n  M.roadway(road);\n  M.flush(parent);\n  ok(parent.children.length === 2, `expected white + yellow meshes, got ${parent.children.length}`);\n\n  const readQuads = (mesh) => {\n    const p = mesh.geometry.attributes.position.array;\n    const out = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i < p.length; i += 18) {\n      out.push({\n        x0: Math.min(p[i], p[i + 3], p[i + 6], p[i + 9]) / 1, x1: Math.max(p[i], p[i + 3], p[i + 6], p[i + 9]),\n        z0: Math.min(p[i + 2], p[i + 5], p[i + 8], p[i + 11]), z1: Math.max(p[i + 2], p[i + 5], p[i + 8], p[i + 11]),\n        w: p[i + 3] - p[i], d: p[i + 5] - p[i + 2],\n      });\n    }\n    return out;\n  };\n  const white = readQuads(parent.children[0]);\n  const yellow = readQuads(parent.children[1]);\n  ok(white.length > 100, `expected many white dashes, got ${white.length}`);\n  ok(yellow.length > 10, `expected median lines, got ${yellow.length}`);\n\n  // every white line sits at a lane-boundary offset makeRoadway agrees with\n  const lanes = makeRoadway({ name: \"t\", points: [[0, 0], [0, 400]], lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4 });\n  const boundary = new Set();\n  for (const l of lanes) {\n    boundary.add(Math.abs(l.offset).toFixed(3));\n    boundary.add(Math.abs(l.offset - 2.4 / 2).toFixed(3));   // outer edge of the lane\n  }\n  const offsets = new Set();\n  for (const q of white) offsets.add((((q.x0 + q.x1) / 2) * 2).toFixed(3));\n  for (const o of offsets) {\n    const near = [...boundary].some((b) => Math.abs(Math.abs(o / 2) - Number(b)) < 0.25);\n    ok(near, `white line at |x|=${(o / 2).toFixed(2)} is not on any makeRoadway lane boundary`);\n  }\n  // the median yellows are INSIDE the median, between the two directions\n  for (const q of yellow) {\n    const cx = (q.x0 + q.x1) / 2;\n    ok(Math.abs(cx) <= 0.4, `median paint at |x|=${Math.abs(cx).toFixed(2)} is outside the 0.4 m median`);\n  }\n  // dashes are dashed: real gaps, not a continuous stripe\n  const zs = white.map((q) => q.z0).sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  let gapFound = false;\n  for (let i = 1; i < zs.length; i++) if (zs[i] - zs[i - 1] > MARKING_DEFAULTS.dashGap * 0.5) gapFound = true;\n  ok(gapFound, \"no gap found between dashes — they are not dashed\");\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- one lane\n{\n  const parent = new sb.THREE.Group();\n  const M = createMarkings({ y: 0.03 });\n  M.roadway({ points: [[0, 0], [300, 0]], lanes: 1 });\n  M.flush(parent);\n  ok(parent.children.length === 2, \"a one-lane road should still get white edges and a yellow centre\");\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- junction\n{\n  const parent = new sb.THREE.Group();\n  const M = createMarkings({ y: 0.03 });\n  M.junction(0, 100, { alongX: false, half: 5 });\n  M.flush(parent);\n  const total = parent.children.reduce((n, c) => n + c.geometry.attributes.position.count / 6, 0);\n  ok(total >= 7 * 4, `junction should paint four crossings (28 stripes), got ${total}`);\n  let beyond = 0;\n  parent.children.forEach((c) => {\n    const p = c.geometry.attributes.position.array;\n    for (let i = 0; i < p.length; i += 3) if (Math.abs(p[i]) > 12 || Math.abs(p[i + 2] - 100) > 12) beyond++;\n  });\n  ok(beyond === 0, `junction paint escaped its 12 m box (${beyond} verts outside)`);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- half width\n{\n  ok(Math.abs(roadwayHalf({ lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4 }) - 5) < 1e-9,\n    \"roadwayHalf should land exactly on the 5 m kerb, got \" + roadwayHalf({ lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4 }));\n  ok(Math.abs(roadwayHalf({ lanes: 1, laneWidth: 2.4 }) - 1.2) < 1e-9, \"one lane should be half a lane wide\");\n}\n\nif (fails) { console.error(`markings_test: ${fails} failure(s)`); /**
 * WHERE KESEME'S STORY OPENS. The highway pull-off and the dirt road into the
 * woods: the hog chase, the Green Bravado, the crash site and the ledger.
 *
 * It used to be at z 130 on the OrleaRouge strip, which is how the establishing
 * card came to say CHATBORO over a place that is now plainly OrleaRouge. This
 * is Chatboro's own stretch of US-167, eighty metres north of the village — the
 * shoulder outside town, which is what the scene actually is.
 *
 * Only `z` moves. US-167 runs the length of the map at x -6, so every x in
 * prologue.js means the same thing here as it did there and none of them had to
 * change: the road is still the road, and the dirt track still runs east off it.
 */
export const PROLOGUE_SITE = Object.freeze({ x: -6, z: -800, label: "Chatboro — the north shoulder" });

/**
 * Ground a SET PIECE owns, that no district and no scatter may build or plant
 * on. Distinct from KEEPOUTS above: a keepout says "a town is here, keep the
 * wilderness out"; this says "a scene happens here, keep EVERYTHING out".
 *
 * The prologue's hog pen has a 32 m radius and its east end reaches x 118,
 * which is inside Tusouxroe's western tree line — so without this the opening
 * chase runs through a pine plantation and the hogs get stuck on the trunks.
 */
export const PROTECTED = [
  { x0: -20, x1: 100, z0: -915, z1: -790, label: "Keseme's prologue" },
];

/** True if (x, z) is on set-piece ground. Districts and scatter must not build here. */
export function inProtected(x, z, pad = 0) {
  for (const r of PROTECTED) {
    if (x > r.x0 - pad && x < r.x1 + pad && z > r.z0 - pad && z < r.z1 + pad) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/** True if (x, z) falls inside a district's claimed ground. `pad` widens every rect. */
export function inKeepout(x, z, pad = 0) {
  for (const k of KEEPOUTS) {
    if (x > k.x0 - pad && x < k.x1 + pad && z > k.z0 - pad && z < k.z1 + pad) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/** Offset a point into a district: `at("tusouxroe", 92, -100)`. */
export function at(district, dx, dz) {
  const d = DISTRICTS[district];
  if (!d) throw new Error(`districts.js: no district "${district}"`);
  return { x: d.x + dx, z: d.z + dz };
}

/** Which district a world point falls nearest, for zone/label lookups. */
export function districtAt(x, z) {
  let best = "orlearouge", bd = Infinity;
  for (const [key, d] of Object.entries(DISTRICTS)) {
    const dd = (x - d.x) ** 2 + (z - d.z) ** 2;
    if (dd < bd) { bd = dd; best = key; }
  }
  return best;
}
