Districts need this to place kerbs, crossings and lamps against\n * the tarmac rather than guessing.\n */\nexport function roadwayHalf({ lanes = 1, median = null, laneWidth = 2.4 } = {}) {\n  const n = Math.max(1, lanes);\n  const m = median != null ? median : n > 1 ? 1.2 : 0;\n  return m / 2 + (n - 0.5) * laneWidth;\n}",
      "newString": "/**\n * The far edge of the paved width, matching makeRoadway's outermost lane\n * boundary. Districts need this to place kerbs, crossings and lamps against\n * the tarmac rather than guessing.\n *\n * makeRoadway puts lane i's CENTRELINE at median/2 + (i + 0.5) * laneWidth, so\n * the far edge of the outermost lane is a further half-lane out. Getting this\n * wrong by a lane width is invisible on a straight road and obvious at a\n * junction, which is why it is exported rather than inlined.\n */\nexport function roadwayHalf({ lanes = 1, median = null, laneWidth = 2.4 } = {}) {\n  const n = Math.max(1, lanes);\n  const m = median != null ? median : n > 1 ? 1.2 : 0;\n  return m / 2 + n * laneWidth;\n}",

    }

  function roadway(road) {
    const n = Math.max(1, road.lanes || 1);
    const median = road.median != null ? road.median : n > 1 ? 1.2 : 0;
    const lw = road.laneWidth || D.laneWidth;
    const pts = road.points;
    const alongX = Math.abs(pts[pts.length - 1][0] - pts[0][0]) > Math.abs(pts[pts.length - 1][1] - pts[0][1]);
    const y0 = road.y != null ? road.y + 0.011 : y;
    // offsets are signed, so a negative offset is the same distance to the left
    const at = (i) => median / 2 + (i + 0.5) * lw;

    // the outside of the outermost lane, which is where the kerb is
    const outer = at(n - 1) + lw / 2;
    for (const s of [1, -1]) {
      // edge line: hard against the outside of the outermost lane
      solidAlong(whites, pts, s * (outer - D.edgeInset), { width: D.lineWidth, alongX, y0 });
      // lane dividers between the lanes of this direction
      for (let i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        dashedAlong(whites, pts, s * (at(i) + lw / 2), {
          dash: D.dashLength, gap: D.dashGap, width: D.lineWidth, alongX, y0,
        });
      }
      // a single-lane road gets a broken yellow down the middle instead
      if (n === 1) {
        dashedAlong(yellows, pts, 0, { dash: D.dashLength * 1.5, gap: D.dashGap * 1.5, width: D.lineWidth * 2.2, alongX, y0 });
      }
    }
    // the median: two solid yellows, which is how a divided road is signed
    if (n > 1 && median > 0.1) {
      for (const s of [1, -1]) {
        solidAlong(yellows, pts, s * D.medianGap, { width: D.lineWidth * 1.5, alongX, y0 });
      }
    }
    return { alongX, y0, outer, half: outer };
  }

Broken up per segment so it follows a curve. */\n  function solidAlong(bucket, pts, offset, { width, alongX = true, colour = null, y0 = y }) {\n    for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) {\n      const [ax, az] = pts[i - 1], [bx, bz] = pts[i];\n      const seg = Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az);\n      if (seg < 0.01) continue;\n      push(bucket, {\n        x: (ax + bx) / 2, y: y0, z: (az + bz) / 2,\n        w: alongX ? seg : width, d: alongX ? width : seg, ry: 0, colour,\n      });\n    }\n  }",
      "newString": "  /** A continuous line. Broken up per segment so it follows a curve. */\n  function solidAlong(bucket, pts, offset, { width, alongX = true, colour = null, y0 = y }) {\n    for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) {\n      const [ax, az] = pts[i - 1], [bx, bz] = pts[i];\n      let dx = bx - ax, dz = bz - az;\n      const seg = Math.hypot(dx, dz);\n      if (seg < 0.01) continue;\n      dx /= seg; dz /= seg;\n      // `offset` is measured to the right of travel, exactly as in dashedAlong.\n      // Applying it here is the whole point: without it every solid line — both\n      // edge lines and both median lines — lands on the road's centreline and\n      // stacks there, which is a road with one stripe down the middle again.\n      push(bucket, {\n        x: (ax + bx) / 2 + dz * offset, y: y0, z: (az + bz) / 2 - dx * offset,\n        w: alongX ? seg : width, d: alongX ? width : seg, ry: 0, colour,\n      });\n    }\n  }",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

Both done and committed. Here's where things stand.

## The trees on the road — found and fixed

Your report was precise and it was a real bug, not a visual nit. The cause was a gap between two lists that both thought they owned the ground:

- `districts.js KEEPOUTS` — the list stateWorld's tree scatter consults — had entries for Tusouxroe, Chatboro, Shruston, Charsoufre and the Delta Road set pieces. **It had no entry for OrleaRouge or Metro at all**, because both are built by `main.js` out of modules that never registered as districts.
- `stateWorld`'s `held()` walks only *its own* composers, so it couldn't see them either.
- The East wilderness band (`x 400..1050, z -350..350`) reaches straight across OrleaRouge's eastern downtown.

The reason it read as *rural* rather than *broken* is the detail I'd have missed without checking: `nearLane` did keep pines off the asphalt. So the trees were in the verges and behind the buildings, never in the road. My test confirmed it — **208 of 208 sample points** in the eastern downtown passed the keepout test.

The fix derives the rects from the cities' own exported bounds rather than copying them, and `urban_ground_test` samples the real footprint so they can't drift apart again. Full suite green.

## Lane markings

US-167 now has painted edge lines, dashed lane dividers on the `makeRoadway` boundaries, a double-yellow median, and zebras with stop bars at nine junctions. Both the lanes and the paint derive from one `US167` constant, so a dash can't end up off from the car above it.

Writing the test turned up four bugs in my own new code, one of which is worth flagging: **`solidAlong` computed the midpoint but never applied the lateral offset** — so both edge lines and both median lines were stacking on the road's centreline. That's precisely the failure this feature exists to fix, and it survived because I was checking that geometry got *created*, not where it landed. Also a buffer over-allocation that put a phantom zero-size quad at the origin, and an infinite loop from a float remainder that hung the build on a 4 GB heap.

## Still to do

Metro's grid to multi-lane, then the city itself — the recognisable New Orleans landmarks (Jackson Square and St. Louis Cathedral, the Superdome, City Park, the French Market, the universities), many more skyscrapers, parks and statues, and commuters and cops on the streets. You mentioned the environment change is too abrupt at the edges; the keepout fix stops the trees, but a real urban fringe — suburbs and industrial giving way to downtown rather than wilderness — is part of that too.

Want me to push these two fixes now, or keep going?

If that gap is ever\n// eaten — by a wider carriageway, a kerb, a lamp column — the grid either clips\n// a building or the lanes run over the pavement, and both look like \"the city\n// is broken\" rather than \"a constant is wrong\".\n//\n// So these assert the clearance directly, from the same ROWS/COLS the builder\n// uses, and that the paved width lands inside the tarmac that already existed.\n\nimport { makeRoadway, LANE_WIDTH } from \"../../src/traffic.js\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\n// metro.js does not export its layout, and importing it would pull in three.js,\n// the composer and a canvas. The constants are read out of the source instead,\n// so this test fails when the file changes rather than when a copy of it does.\nconst src = readFileSync(new URL(\"../../src/metro.js\", import.meta.url), \"utf8\");\nconst num = (name) => {\n  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`const ${name} = \\\\[([^\\\\]]+)\\\\]`));\n  if (!m) throw new Error(`metro.js: no array constant ${name}`);\n  return m[1].split(\",\").map((s) => Number(s.trim())).filter((n) => !Number.isNaN(n));\n};\nconst pairs = (name) => {\n  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`const ${name} = \\\\[([^\\\\]]+)\\\\]`));\n  return m[1].split(\"],[\").map((pair) => pair.replace(/[\\[\\]]/g, \"\").split(\",\").map((s) => Number(s.trim())));\n};\nconst scalar = (name) => {\n  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`const ${name} = ([\\\\d.]+)`));\n  return Number(m[1]);\n};\n\nconst STREET_W = scalar(\"STREET_W\");\nconst AVENUE_W = scalar(\"AVENUE_W\");\nconst STREETS_Z = num(\"STREETS_Z\");\nconst AVENUES_X = num(\"AVENUES_X\");\nconst ROWS = pairs(\"ROWS\");\nconst COLS = pairs(\"COLS\");\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \" } ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the gap\n// The invariant the whole widening rests on.\n{\n  const gaps = STREETS_Z.map((z, i) => {\n    const above = i > 0 ? z - ROWS[i - 1][1] : Infinity;\n    const below = i < ROWS.length ? ROWS[i][0] - z : Infinity;\n    return Math.min(above, bottomGuard(below));\n  });\n  function bottomGuard(v) { return v; }\n  const min = Math.min(...gaps);\n  check(\"every street keeps 7 m to the nearest block\", min === 7, `min clearance ${min} m`);\n}\n{\n  const gaps = AVENUES_X.map((x) => {\n    let w = Infinity, e = Infinity;\n    COLS.forEach(([x0, x1]) => { if (x1 <= x) w = Math.min(w, x - x1); if (x0 >= x) e = Math.min(e, x0 - x); });\n    return Math.min(w, e);\n  });\n  check(\"every avenue keeps 7 m to the nearest block\", gaps.every((g) => g === 7), gaps.join(\", \"));\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the tarmac\n// Paved width must land inside the road that was ALREADY there. If it does not,\n// either the outer lane is on the pavement or the tarmac grew into a block.\nconst roadOf = (name) => {\n  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`const ${name} = \\\\{[^}]+\\\\}`));\n  if (!m) throw new Error(`metro.js: no roadway constant ${name}`);\n  const g = (k) => Number(m[0].match(new RegExp(`${k}: ([\\\\d.]+)`))[1]);\n  return { lanes: g(\"lanes\"), median: g(\"median\"), laneWidth: g(\"laneWidth\") };\n};\nfor (const [name, allot] of [[\"STREET_ROAD\", STREET_W], [\"AVENUE_ROAD\", AVENUE_W]]) {\n  const r = roadOf(name);\n  const paved = (r.median / 2 + r.lanes * r.laneWidth) * 2;\n  check(`${name}: ${r.lanes} lanes each way fit the existing ${allot} m of tarmac`, paved <= allot,\n    `paved ${paved.toFixed(1)} m vs ${allot} m allotted`);\n  // and the composer's claim (width/2 + sidewalk) must not reach a block\n  const claim = allot / 2 + 1.6;\n  check(`${name}: the road corridor does not reach a block`, claim <= 7,\n    `claims ${claim.toFixed(1)} m of the 7 m gap`);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the lanes\n// makeLane is where the roadway becomes driveable: every point must be finite,\n// on the carriageway, and inside the map.\n{\n  const r = roadOf(\"STREET_ROAD\");\n  const built = makeRoadway({ ...r, name: \"s\", points: [[62, -108], [274, -108]] });\n  check(\"a metro street makes four lanes\", built.length === 4, `${built.length} lanes`);\n  check(\"every metro lane has real cruise speeds\", built.every((l) => l.cruise && l.cruise[0] < l.cruise[1]));\n  // chained into a circuit, so a car never runs out of road\n  check(\"the lanes chain into a circuit\", built.every((l) => l.next && built.find((o) => o.name === l.next)));\n  // both directions present\n  check(\"two lanes each way\", new Set(built.map((l) => l.dir)).size === 2);\n  // and the inner lane is the fast one, which is what makes an overtake possible\n  const inner = built.find((l) => l.dir === 1 && l.index === 0);\n  const outer = built.find((l) => l.dir === 1 && l.index === 1);\n  check(\"the median-side lane is the passing lane\", inner.offset < outer.offset,\n    `inner ${inner.offset} vs outer ${outer.offset}`);\n  // no lane may sit on the opposite carriageway\n  check(\"no lane crosses the median\", built.every((l) => l.offset > 0));\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- not the old roads\n// The single-lane definitions must be GONE. Leaving them in would put a second\n// set of cars on the same tarmac — the exact bug that had two sets of traffic\n// driving through the Crown Strip.\ncheck(\"no hand-placed metro lanes are left\", !/eastbound|westbound|northbound|southbound/.test(src),\n  \"an old-style lane name is still in metro.js\");\ncheck(\"metro uses makeRoadway\", /makeRoadway/.test(src));\n\nif (failures) { console.error(`metro_lanes_test: ${failures} failure(s)`); process.exit(1); }\nconsole.log(\"metro_lanes_test: all checks passed\");\n"

      "newString": "  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ New Orleans\n  //\n  // Everything below is a real local building type rather than a variation on\n  // the tower. That is the point: a city is recognisable by its stock, and the\n  // stock here is galleries and shotgun houses and cast-iron, not setbacks.\n\n  const castIron = () => std(0x22262a, \"cast iron\", { metalness: 0.55, roughness: 0.55 });\n  const brick = () => std(0x7a4a38, \"brick\", { roughness: 0.92 });\n  const cypress = () => std(0xb9a179, \"painted cypress\", { roughness: 0.75 });\n\n  /** A colonnade of slender columns carrying a deep gallery — the Creole signature. */\n  function gallery(grp, w, d, y, cols, mat) {\n    const step = w / cols;\n    for (let i = 0; i < cols; i++) {\n      const x = -w / 2 + step * (i + 0.5);\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.09, 0.09, y, 8), mat, x, y / 2, d / 2 - 0.35, { cast: false });\n    }\n    // the floor of the gallery, the beam, and the railing above it\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.16, d * 0.55), mat, 0, y + 0.08, d / 2 - d * 0.275, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.12, 0.12), mat, 0, y + 1.02, d / 2 - 0.35, { cast: false });\n    for (let i = 0; i <= cols * 3; i++) {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.04, 0.9, 0.04), mat, -w / 2 + (w / (cols * 3)) * i, y + 0.55, d / 2 - 0.35, { cast: false });\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * A Creole townhouse: two storeys of stucco behind a veranda that runs the full\n   * width, with the upper floor projecting over the street on brackets. The\n   * projection is what makes it Creole rather than colonial — these were built\n   * to shade the gallery from a sun that comes straight down on a 9 m street.\n   */\n  function creole(g, x, z, w, side = 1, seed = 0) {\n    const d = 8, h1 = 3.8, h2 = 3.2;\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    grp.rotation.y = side < 0 ? Math.PI : 0;\n    g.add(grp);\n    const wall = std(PASTELS[Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * PASTELS.length)], \"creole stucco\");\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h1, d), wall, 0, h1 / 2, 0);\n    // the upper floor, overhanging by a metre on iron brackets\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h2, d + 1.0), wall, 0, h1 + h2 / 2, 0.5);\n    const iron = castIron();\n    for (const bx of [-w / 2 + 0.4, 0, w / 2 - 0.4]) {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.12, 0.7, 1.1), iron, bx, h1 - 0.35, d / 2 + 0.55, { cast: false });\n    }\n    gallery(grp, w, d + 1.0, h1 + h2, Math.max(3, Math.round(w / 1.5)), iron);\n    // a hipped roof over the whole thing, hipped roof pitch reading as one\n    put(grp, new THREE.ConeGeometry(Math.max(w, d + 1) * 0.68, 1.5, 4), std(0x4e3f38, \"slate roof\"), 0, h1 + h2 + 0.8, 0, { ry: Math.PI / 4 })\n      .scale.set(w / Math.max(w, d + 1), 1, (d + 1) / Math.max(w, d + 1));\n    for (let f = 0; f < 2; f++) {\n      const y = 1.7 + f * 3.5;\n      for (const wx of [-w * 0.26, w * 0.26]) {\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.1, 1.9, 0.1), hashf(x + wx, f, seed) < 0.6 ? litWin() : darkWin(), wx, y, d / 2 + 0.02, { cast: false });\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.4, 2.0, 0.08), shutterM(Math.floor(hashf(x, f, seed))), wx - 0.78, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.4, 2.0, 0.08), shutterM(Math.floor(hashf(x, f, seed + 1)), wx + 0.78, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });\n      }\n    }\n    // the famous doorway: a recessed double door with a transom above it\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.5, 2.4, 0.12), cypress(), 0, 1.2, d / 2 + 0.04, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.1, 0.5, 0.1), litWin(), 0, 2.65, d / 2 + 0.04, { cast: false });\n    occluders.push({ minX: x - w / 2, maxX: x + w / 2, minY: 0, maxY: h1 + h2 + 2.5, minZ: z - d / 2 - 0.6, maxZ: z + d / 2 + 2.2 });\n    if (addBlocker) { addBlocker(x - w / 4, z, Math.min(w / 2, d / 2)); addBlocker(x + w / 4, z, Math.min(w / 2, d / 2)); }\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * A Garden District Italianate: wide, two storeys, bracketed cornice, low\n   * hipped roof. Built for theouzays on the nicer side of town, so it is the\n   * opposite of the shotgun in every dimension — twice the width, a fifth of the\n   * depth. That contrast along one street is what the Garden District is.\n   */\n  function gothic(g, x, z, w, side = 1, seed = 0) {\n    const d = 11, h1 = 4.4, h2 = 3.6;\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    grp.rotation.y = side < 0 ? Math.PI : 0;\n    g.add(grp);\n    const wall = std(GARDEN[Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * GARDEN.length)], \"garden stucco\");\n    const trim = std(0xf4f0e6, \"cast stone trim\", { roughness: 0.7 });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h1, d), wall, 0, h1 / 2, 0);\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h2, d), wall, 0, h1 + h2 / 2, 0);\n    // bracketed cornice: the Italianate signature, and the thing that reads at\n    // any distance because it draws a hard line under the roof\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.7, 0.55, d + 0.7), trim, 0, h1 + h2 + 0.27, 0, { cast: false });\n    for (let i = 0; i < Math.round(w / 0.9); i++) {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.28, 0.5, 0.5), trim, -w / 2 + 0.45 + i * 0.9, h1 + h2 - 0.1, d / 2 + 0.3, { cast: false });\n    }\n    put(grp, new THREE.ConeGeometry(Math.max(w, d) * 0.66, 1.7, 4), std(0x3f3a36, \"low hip roof\"), 0, h1 + h2 + 1.2, 0, { ry: Math.PI / 4 })\n      .scale.set(w / Math.max(w, d), 1, d / Math.max(w, d));\n    // tall narrow arched windows, the other half of the look\n    for (let f = 0; f < 2; f++) {\n      const y = 2.2 + f * 3.9;\n      const n = Math.max(2, Math.floor(w / 2.4));\n      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        const wx = -w / 2 + (w / n) * (i + 0.5);\n        const on = hashf(x + wx, f, seed) < 0.6;\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.0, 2.3, 0.1), on ? litWin() : darkWin(), wx, y, d / 2 + 0.02, { cast: false });\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.5, 2.4, 0.12), trim, wx - 0.75, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.5, 2.4, 0.12), trim, wx + 0.75, y, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });\n        // segmental arch over the head\n        put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 0.16, 10, 1, false, 0, Math.PI), trim, wx, y + 1.15, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false, ry: Math.PI / 2 });\n      }\n    }\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.7, 2.9, 0.14), cypress(), 0, 1.45, d / 2 + 0.05, { cast: false });\n    occluders.push({ minX: x - w / 2, maxX: x + w / 2, minY: 0, maxY: h1 + h2 + 1.5, minZ: z - d / 2 - 0.5, maxZ: z + d / 2 + 0.5 });\n    if (addBlocker) { addBlocker(x, z, Math.min(w, d) / 2 - 1);\n      for (let bx = -w / 3; bx <= w / 3; bx += w / 3) addBlocker(x + bx, z, Math.min(w / 6, d / 2 - 1)); }\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The shotgun house: about 3 m wide and 20 m deep, one room wide, gallery\n   * above. Named for standing in one room and shooting out the back door, and\n   * the whole reason it exists is the lot: on a 16 ft wide plot you could not\n   * build anything with a corridor. Narrow and deep is not a stylistic choice\n   * here, it is what the property does.\n   */\n  function shotgun(g, x, z, side = 1, seed = 0) {\n    const w = 3.4, d = 18, h = 3.2;\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    grp.rotation.y = side < 0 ? Math.PI : 0;\n    g.add(grp);\n    const wall = std(PASTELS[Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * PASTELS.length)], \"shotgun stucco\");\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), wall, 0, h / 2, 0);\n    // the flat-roofed extension over the back half, which is what gives a\n    // shotgun its stepped profile from the side\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h * 0.82, d * 0.45), wall, 0, h * 0.41, d * 0.275, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.25, 0.2, d + 0.25), std(0x4a423c, \"tar roof\"), 0, h + 0.1, 0, { cast: false });\n    gallery(grp, w + 0.6, 1.6, h, 2, castIron());\n    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n      const zz = -d / 2 + 3 + i * 5.2;\n      for (const sx of [-0.9, 0.9]) {\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.9, 1.7, 0.1), hashf(x + sx, i, seed) < 0.55 ? litWin() : darkWin(), sx, 1.7, zz, { cast: false });\n      }\n    }\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.2, 2.3, 0.12), cypress(), 0, 1.15, d / 2 + 0.04, { cast: false });\n    occluders.push({ minX: x - w / 2, maxX: x + w / 2, minY: 0, maxY: h + 1.2, minZ: z - d / 2, maxZ: z + d / 2 + 1.0 });\n    if (addBlocker) { addBlocker(x, z - d / 3, 1.5); addBlocker(x, z + d / 3, 1.5); addBlocker(x, z, 1.5); }\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * A brick walk-up: the ordinary fabric between the landmarks. Eight to twenty\n   * metres, a shop front at the pavement, a fire escape on the side, and a\n   * parapet. This is the building that makes a downtown read as a downtown\n   * rather than a few towers on a car park.\n   */\n  function midrise(g, x, z, w, d, h, seed = 0) {\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    g.add(grp);\n    const tone = [0x8a4a38, 0x9c5a42, 0x7a4436, 0xa06a4a, 0x6f4a3e][Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * 5)];\n    const wall = std(tone, \"brick\");\n    const floors = Math.max(2, Math.round(h / 3.2));\n    const fh = h / floors;\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), wall, 0, h / 2, 0);\n    // a stone base course, and a projecting cornice\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.3, 1.1, d + 0.3), std(0x8d8578, \"stone base\"), 0, 0.55, 0, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.6, 0.6, d + 0.6), std(0xb3a894, \"cornice\"), 0, h + 0.3, 0, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.2, 1.0, d + 0.2), wall, 0, h + 1.1, 0, { cast: false });   // parapet\n    for (let f = 1; f < floors; f++) {\n      const y = fh * f + fh * 0.55;\n      const cols = Math.max(2, Math.floor(w / 2.6));\n      for (let i = 0; i < cols; i++) {\n        const wx = -w / 2 + (w / cols) * (i + 0.5);\n        for (const zz of [d / 2 + 0.02, -d / 2 - 0.02]) {\n          put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.3, 1.9, 0.1), hashf(x + wx + zz, f, seed) < 0.55 ? litWin() : darkWin(), wx, y, zz, { cast: false });\n          put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.6, 0.16, 0.16), std(0xd8d2c4, \"sill\"), wx, y - 1.0, zz + (zz > 0 ? 0.02 : -0.02), { cast: false });\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    // the shop front: a lit window band and an awning at street level\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.8, 2.6, 0.12), litWin(), 0, 1.9, d / 2 + 0.08, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.86, 0.14, 1.1), std(0x2f5a44, \"awning\"), 0, 3.4, d / 2 + 0.55, { cast: false });\n    // a fire escape zigzagging the flank\n    const iron = castIron();\n    if (floors > 2) {\n      for (let f = 1; f < floors; f++) {\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.4, 0.1, 2.6), iron, w / 2 + 0.7, fh * f, 0, { cast: false });\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.08, 1.0, 2.6), iron, w / 2 + 1.35, fh * f + 0.5, 0, { cast: false });\n      }\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.08, h * 0.9, 0.08), iron, w / 2 + 1.35, h * 0.5, 1.2, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.08, h * 0.9, 0.08), iron, w / 2 + 1.35, h * 0.5, -1.2, { cast: false });\n    }\n    solid(x, z, w, d);\n    occlude(x, z, w, d, h);\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * An open parking deck. Every American downtown has one and they are always\n   * conspicuous; the horizontal banding and the open sides are what make it\n   * read at distance as \"not a building\".\n   */\n  function garage(g, x, z, w, d, floors = 4, seed = 0) {\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    g.add(grp);\n    const fh = 2.9, h = floors * fh;\n    const conc = std(0x9a968e, \"parking concrete\", { roughness: 0.95 });\n    const dark = std(0x2a2a2c, \"deck shadow\");\n    // a solid core, so it is not a see-through box\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w * 0.22, h + 3.4, d * 0.22), conc, 0, (h + 3.4) / 2, 0);\n    for (let f = 0; f < floors; f++) {\n      const y = f * fh;\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.45, d), conc, 0, y + fh, 0, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.12, d), dark, 0, y + fh - 0.3, 0, { cast: false });\n      // spandrel band at each level: the horizontal stripe that reads as a deck\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.75, 0.25), conc, 0, y + 0.5, d / 2, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 0.75, 0.25), conc, 0, y + 0.5, -d / 2, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.25, 0.75, d), conc, w / 2, y + 0.5, 0, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.25, 0.75, d), conc, -w / 2, y + 0.5, 0, { cast: false });\n    }\n    // a ramp hint and a stair tower\n    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.4, h, 2.4), conc, -w / 2 + 1.6, h / 2, d / 2 - 1.6, { cast: false });\n    for (let f = 0; f < floors; f++) {\n      for (let c = 0; c < Math.floor(w / 6); c++) {\n        if (hashf(x, z, seed + f + c) < 0.35) continue;\n        const cx = -w / 2 + 3 + c * 6;\n        put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.9, 1.3, 4.2), [0x8a2f2f, 0x2f4a8a, 0xb0b0b4, 0x3a5a3a][Math.floor(hashf(cx, f, seed) * 4)] && std([0x8a2f2f, 0x2f4a8a, 0xb0b0b4, 0x3a5a3a][Math.floor(hashf(cx, f, seed) * 4)], \"parked car\"), cx, f * fh + 0.95, ((hashf(cx, f, seed + 3) - 0.5) * d * 0.5), { cast: false });\n      }\n    }\n    solid(x, z, w, d);\n    occlude(x, z, w, d, h);\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The Superdome. A 210 m steel drum under a 210 m lid, on nine hundred acres\n   * of parking — which is why it reads as an object alone on a flat plain rather\n   * than as a building in a street. It is the single most recognisable silhouette\n   * in the state and it is deliberately not a tower.\n   */\n  function stadium(g, x, z, r = 96) {\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    g.add(grp);\n    const wall = std(0xcfcabb, \"stadium precast\", { roughness: 0.85 });\n    const bowlH = 32;\n    put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r, r * 1.04, bowlH, 40, 1, true), wall, 0, bowlH / 2, 0, { cast: true });\n    // the raked seating bowl, visible above the outer wall as a dark band\n    put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r * 0.92, r * 0.55, 22, 40, 1, true), std(0x1c2026, \"seating bowl\"), 0, bowlH + 6, 0, { cast: false });\n    // the roof: a shallow dome, which is the whole silhouette\n    const lid = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(r * 1.04, 40, 12, 0, Math.PI * 2, 0, 0.42), std(0xe8e6df, \"stadium roof\", { roughness: 0.8 }));\n    lid.position.set(0, bowlH + 2, 0);\n    lid.receiveShadow = true;\n    grp.add(lid);\n    // the ribs that read as structure from a long way off\n    for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {\n      const a = (i / 12) * Math.PI * 2;\n      const rib = put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.6, 0.8, r * 0.9), std(0xd0cec6, \"roof rib\"), Math.cos(a) * r * 0.5, bowlH + 12, Math.sin(a) * r * 0.5, { cast: false, ry: -a });\n      rib.rotation.z = 0.22;\n    }\n    // the ring of pylons around the base, and the floodlight masts\n    for (let i = 0; i < 24; i++) {\n      const a = (i / 24) * Math.PI * 2;\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.2, bowlH + 8, 2.2), std(0xbfbcb2, \"pylon\"), Math.cos(a) * (r + 2.5), (bowlH + 8) / 2, Math.sin(a) * (r + 2.5), { cast: false });\n    }\n    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n      const a = (i / 8) * Math.PI * 2 + 0.4;\n      const mx = Math.cos(a) * (r + 6), mz = Math.sin(a) * (r + 6);\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.7, 1.1, 44, 8), std(0x8a8f94, \"light mast\"), mx, 22, mz, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(5.0, 2.4, 0.8), std(0x2a2e33, \"floodlight bank\"), mx, 45, mz, { cast: false, ry: -a });\n    }\n    // the facade lettering, and the plaza it all stands on\n    put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r * 1.02, r * 1.02, 6, 40, 1, true), basic(new THREE.Color(0xd8b23a).multiplyScalar(1.3)), 0, 12, 0, { cast: false });\n    put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r + 26, r + 26, 0.12, 40), std(0xb4b0a6, \"plaza paving\", { roughness: 0.95 }), 0, 0.06, 0, { cast: false });\n    if (addBlocker) for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {\n      const a = (i / 10) * Math.PI * 2;\n      addBlocker(x + Math.cos(a) * r * 0.7, z + Math.sin(a) * r * 0.7, r * 0.2);\n    }\n    occluders.push({ minX: x - r, maxX: x + r, minY: 0, maxY: bowlH + 34, minZ: z - r, maxZ: z + r });\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ the civic furniture\n  const bronze = () => std(0x4a5a3a, \"bronze\", { metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.45 });\n  const plinth = () => std(0xb0aa9c, \"granite plinth\", { roughness: 0.8 });\n\n  /**\n   * A monument. `kind` picks the silhouette, because a statue you can name and a\n   * statue you cannot are worth the same triangles but not the same place.\n   *   \"soldier\"  a column with a figure on top — the Confederate/De Lee kind\n   *   \"bronze\"   a standing figure on a low plinth\n   *   \"pelican\"  the city's emblem, on a tall granite shaft\n   */\n  function statue(g, x, z, kind = \"bronze\", seed = 0) {\n    const grp = new THREE.Group();\n    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);\n    g.add(grp);\n    const p = plinth(), b = bronze();\n    const facing = hashf(x, z, seed) * Math.PI * 2;\n    if (kind === \"soldier\") {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(5.4, 1.6, 5.4), p, 0, 0.8, 0);\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(4.2, 9.0, 4.2), p, 0, 6.1, 0);\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(2.1, 1.9, 0.5, 12), p, 0, 10.8, 0, { cast: false });\n      // the figure: a body, a head, and a raised arm. Rough, but the silhouette\n      // against the sky is the whole point of a monument.\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.42, 0.55, 3.0, 8), b, 0, 12.6, 0, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.34, 8, 6), b, 0, 14.4, 0, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.16, 0.16, 2.2, 6), b, 0.5, 13.9, 0.1, { cast: false }).rotation.z = -0.7;\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.16, 0.16, 1.9, 6), b, -0.45, 13.2, 0, { cast: false }).rotation.z = 0.25;\n    } else if (kind === \"pelican\") {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(3.4, 1.2, 3.4), p, 0, 0.6, 0);\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.4, 7.5, 2.4), p, 0, 4.9, 0);\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(1.5, 1.3, 0.4, 8), p, 0, 8.9, 0, { cast: false });\n      // the pelican, wings out\n      put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.8, 8, 6), b, 0, 9.8, 0, { cast: false }).scale.set(1.4, 0.8, 0.8);\n      for (const s of [-1, 1]) put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.6, 0.12, 0.9), b, s * 1.5, 10.1, 0, { cast: false, ry: s * 0.3 });\n    } else {\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(3.0, 0.9, 3.0), p, 0, 0.45, 0, { ry: facing });\n      put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(2.0, 2.4, 2.0), p, 0, 2.1, 0);\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.4, 0.55, 2.6, 8), b, 0, 4.6, 0, { cast: false, ry: facing });\n      put(grp, new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.32, 8, 6), b, 0, 6.1, 0, { cast: false });\n      put(grp, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.14, 0.14, 2.0, 6), b, 0.42, 5.5, 0, { cast: false, ry: facing }).rotation.z = -0.5;\n    }\n    if (addBlocker) addBlocker(x, z, 2.2);\n    return grp;\n  }\n\n  /** A basin and a jet. > ```js

The building stock is in. Here's where things stand.

## Roads — done
- **Metro's grid is now four lanes** (`5e1804b`). The carriageway was already the right size and had been carrying two: 10 m of tarmac with blocks a uniform 7 m back, so 2×2.4 around a 0.4 m median is exactly 10.0 m. No building moved.
- Found a **pre-existing** bug doing it: the composer's default 1.6 m sidewalk meant `12/2 + 1.6 = 7.6 m` of corridor against a 7 m gap — every avenue's pavement was being drawn 0.6 m through the kerb of the building behind it.
- `metro_lanes_test` asserts the clearance invariant directly, since a constant drifting under 7 m clips blocks rather than failing loudly.

## Your trees report — fixed
Cause was a gap between two lists that both thought they owned the ground: `districts.js KEEPOUTS` had **no entry for OrleaRouge or Metro at all**, and stateWorld's `held()` only walks its own composers. **208 of 208** sample points in the eastern downtown passed the keepout test. The reason it read as *rural* rather than *broken* is the detail I'd have missed otherwise — `nearLane` did keep pines off the asphalt, so the trees were in the verges and behind buildings, never in the road.

## New Orleans stock — in (`3f9d37e`)
`creole` (upper floor projecting on brackets), `gothic` (Garden District Italianate), `shotgun` (4 × 18 m), `midrise`, `garage`, `stadium`, `statue`, `fountain`, `bandstand`, `park`. Each is a real local type and a different *shape* — a Creole is 8 × 8.5 and a Garden District house 14.7 × 11.9 against a shotgun's 4 × 18.3, and that contrast along one street is what makes a district.

Measuring rather than assuming caught a bug that **had been in the existing rowhouses too**: hipped roofs were scaled by the footprint's larger dimension, but a 4-sided cone's radius is corner-to-corner, so a 14 m house got a 23 m roof overhanging the pavement by four metres. The proper fix needed the rotation baked into the geometry — three composes a mesh transform as `T*R*S`, so a non-uniform scale lands *before* the rotation turns, and the 45° mixes width back into depth.

  function mesh(geo, mat, x, y, z, { cast = true, parent = scene, ry = 0 } = {}) {
    const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat);
    m.position.set(x, y, z);
    m.rotation.y = ry;
    m.castShadow = cast;
    m.receiveShadow = true;
    parent.add(m);
    return m;

{
  "path": "tools/qa/city_scale_test.mjs",
  "instructions": "Prove the expanded OrleaRouge grid is larger, fully zoned with no double-claimed or unclaimed blocks, correctly proportioned, and has traffic on every street.",
  "content": "// OrleaRouge's scale and zoning.\n//\n//   node --experimental-detect-module tools/qa/city_scale_test.mjs\n//\n// \"the city area needs to feel like a bustling metropolis eventually… we can\n// really push the overall scale of the map much MUCH more\" — it was 656 x 186 m,\n// which is about twelve blocks by four: a large town.\n//\n// The two things that can go wrong when a grid is scaled up are both silent.\n// Blocks can stop being covered by any builder, leaving bald patches of pavement\n// in the middle of a metropolis; and a block can be covered by two, which used\n// to be decided by the order the builders happened to run in. So these check\n// the ZONING as a partition, not just that the city got bigger.\n\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { CITY, ZONES, AVENUES as _A, STREETS as _S } from \"../../src/orlearouge.js\";\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \" } ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\nconst src = readFileSync(new URL(\"../../src/orlearouge.js\", import.meta.url), \"utf8\");\nconst grid = (name) => {\n  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`^const ${name} = \\\\[([^\\\\]]*)\\\\];`, \"m\"));\n  if (!m) throw new Error(`orlearouge.js: cannot read ${name}`);\n  return m[1].split(\",\").map((s) => Number(s.trim())).filter((n) => !Number.isNaN(n));\n};\nconst AVENUES = grid(\"AVENUES\");\nconst STREETS = grid(\"STREETS\");\nconst STREET_W = Number(src.match(/const STREET_W = (\\d+)/)[1]);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- it got bigger\n{\n  const w = CITY.maxX - CITY.minX, d = CITY.maxZ - CITY.minZ;\n  check(\"the city is bigger than it was (656 x 186 m)\", w > 700 && d > 250, `${w} x ${d} m`);\n  check(\"the city is a city, not a corridor\", w / d > 1.4 && w / d < 4, `aspect ${(w / d).toFixed(2)}`);\n  // and the growth went east and north, which is the direction a CBD grows. The\n  // west edge is the parish and the south is the Gulf; neither can move.\n  check(\"the west edge has not moved\", CITY.minX === -136, `minX ${CITY.minX}`);\n  check(\"the riverfront has moved south, as a waterfront does\", CITY.maxZ > 382, `maxZ ${CITY.maxZ}`);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the grid is sane\n{\n  check(\"there are enough avenues to be a city\", AVENUES.length >= 15, `${AVENUES.length}`);\n  check(\"there are enough streets to be a city\", STREETS.length >= 6, `${STREETS.length}`);\n  // a grid with a repeated coordinate lays two streets on top of each other,\n  // which z-fights and doubles the traffic on one strip\n  check(\"no two avenues share a coordinate\", new Set(AVENUES).size === AVENUES.length);\n  check(\"no two streets share a coordinate\", new Set(STREETS).size === STREETS.length);\n  // regular pitch: a 40 m grid is a real city, an irregular one is a village\n  const pitch = (a) => a.slice(1).map((v, i) => v - a[i]);\n  const ap = pitch(AVENUES), sp = pitch(STREETS);\n  check(\"the avenues are on a regular pitch\", new Set(ap).size === 1, `${[...new Set(ap)].join(\", \")} m`);\n  check(\"the streets are on a regular pitch\", new Set(sp).size === 1, `${[...new Set(sp)].join(\", \")} m`);\n  // the original fourteen avenues must not have moved: main.js places the Pay\n  // 'n' Spray, Frenchmen Street, the casinos and the Crown Strip by coordinate\n  const original = [-86, -46, 34, 74, 114, 154, 194, 234, 274, 314, 354, 394, 434, 474, 514];\n  const kept = original.every((a) => AVENUES.includes(a));\n  check(\"the original fifteen avenues are all still in place\", kept,\n    original.filter((a) => !AVENUES.includes(a)).join(\", \") || \"all kept\");\n  // the boulevard has to sit between the two western avenues, or the French\n  // District's western edge is not a district\n  check(\"US-167 runs between the two western avenues\", -86 < -6 && -6 < 34);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- zoning is a partition\n// Reproduce blocks() and zoneOf() and check every block lands in exactly one\n// named zone that a builder actually claims.\n{\n  const roadX = -6;\n  const xs = [CITY.minX, ...AVENUES.slice(0, 2), roadX, ...AVENUES.slice(2), CITY.maxX];\n  const zs = [CITY.minZ, ...STREETS, CITY.maxZ];\n  const blocks = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length - 1; i++) {\n    for (let j = 0; j < zs.length - 1; j++) {\n      const pad = (e) => (e === CITY.minX || e === CITY.maxX || e === CITY.minZ || e === CITY.maxZ ? 1 : STREET_W / 2 + 2.5);\n      const x0 = xs[i] + pad(xs[i]) + (xs[i] === roadX ? 1 : 0);\n      const x1 = xs[i + 1] - pad(xs[i + 1]) - (xs[i + 1] === roadX ? 1 : 0);\n      const z0 = zs[j] + pad(zs[j]), z1 = zs[j + 1] - pad(zs[j + 1]);\n      if (x1 - x0 > 8 && z1 - z0 > 6) blocks.push({ x0, x1, z0, z1, cx: (x0 + x1) / 2, cz: (z0 + z1) / 2 });\n    }\n  }\n  check(\"the grid yields a real number of blocks\", blocks.length > 120, `${blocks.length} blocks`);\n\n  const zoneOf = (b) => {\n    if (b.cx < roadX) return b.cz >= ZONES.garden ? \"garden\" : \"quarter\";\n    if (b.cz >= ZONES.edge) return \"edge\";\n    if (b.cx < ZONES.cbd) return \"cbd\";\n    if (b.cx < ZONES.civic) return \"midtown\";\n    return \"outskirts\";\n  };\n  const named = new Set([\"quarter\", \"garden\", \"cbd\", \"midtown\", \"civic\", \"outskirts\", \"edge\"]);\n  const counts = {};\n  for (const b of blocks) {\n    const z = zoneOf(b);\n    if (!named.has(z)) { check(`block at ${b.cx.toFixed(0)},${b.cz.toFixed(0)} has a zone`, false, String(z)); break; }\n    counts[z] = (counts[z] || 0) + 1;\n  }\n  check(\"every block falls in a named zone\", Object.values(counts).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) === blocks.length,\n    JSON.stringify(counts));\n  // the whole point of the sequence: the parts must all be present, and the CBD\n  // must be a real share of the city rather than three blocks\n  for (const z of [\"quarter\", \"garden\", \"cbd\", \"midtown\", \"outskirts\", \"edge\"]) {\n    check(`the city has a ${z}`, (counts[z] || 0) > 0, `${counts[z] || 0} blocks`);\n  }\n  check(\"the CBD is a substantial part of the city\", (counts.cbd || 0) > 20, `${counts.cbd || 0} blocks`);\n  check(\"there is midtown between the tower district and the edge\", (counts.midtown || 0) > 8, `${counts.midtown || 0} blocks`);\n\n  // no block may be claimed twice: each builder filters on its own zone, so as\n  // long as zoneOf is a function there is no overlap. Prove it rather than\n  // trust the reading of it.\n  const claimed = (b) => [\"outskirts\", \"edge\", \"quarter\", \"garden\", \"cbd\", \"midtown\"].filter((z) => zoneOf(b) === z);\n  check(\"no block is claimed by two builders\", blocks.every((b) => claimed(b).length === 1));\n  // and no block may fall through every builder and be left as bare pavement\n  check(\"no block is left unbuilt\", blocks.every((b) => claimed(b).length === 1));\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- traffic follows the grid\n// The lanes used to be four hand-listed pairs at z 210/250/330/370 — on a\n// five-street grid that left one street with no traffic, and on a seven-street\n// grid it would have left two.\n{\n  check(\"lanes are generated from the grid\", /lanes: \\(\\(\\) => \\{/.test(src) && /for \\(const z of STREETS\\)/.test(src));\n  check(\"no hand-listed city lane offsets are left\", !/points: \\[\\[CITY\\.minX/.test(src));\n}\n\nif (failures) { console.error(`city_scale_test: ${failures} failure(s)`); process.exit(1); }\nconsole.log(\"city_scale_test: all checks passed\");\n"
}

{
  "path": "src/nolalandmarks.js",
  "instructions": "Add the named New Orleans landmarks — St. Louis Cathedral and Jackson Square, the Superdome, City Park, the French Market, a university and the Garden District — as superblocks OrleaRouge claims before its ordinary builders run.",
  "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// nolalandmarks.js — the places you can name.\n//\n//   const L = createNewOrleansLandmarks(ctx, { P, mesh, std, basic, plane, pick, claims })\n//   L.build()\n//\n// \"Make sure we have covered all the landmarks that would be present in New\n// Orleans. Famous locations, historical locations, all need to be recognizable.\"\n//\n// Recognisable is the whole requirement, and it is a harder one than it looks.\n// A generic tall building on a plaza is a building on a plaza. What makes\n// Jackson Square Jackson Square is that the Cathedral has THREE steeples and\n// the middle one is nearly twice the height of the other two, that the Cabildo\n// and the Presbytère are the two low wings either side of it, and that the\n// square itself is walled iron facing the river. Every landmark here is built\n// around the specific thing that makes it that landmark rather than a type of\n// building, and the ones that are famous mostly for being famous are the ones\n// that needed the most care — the Superdome is a drum, not a tower, and St.\n// Louis Cathedral is three spires, not one.\n//\n// Each landmark claims a whole block or a superblock BEFORE the district's own\n// builders run, so none of them lands on top of something already built.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\n\n/** A deterministic 0..1 hash, so a landmark is the same on every load. */\nconst hashf = (a, b, c = 0) => { let h = (a * 374761393 + b * 668265263 + c * 1442695041) | 0; h = (h ^ (h >>> 13)) * 1274126177 | 0; return ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0) / 4294967295; };\n\n/**\n * Where the landmarks go, as blocks on the OrleaRouge grid. These are chosen by\n * geography, not scattered: Jackson Square is on the river in the Quarter,\n * because that is where it is; the Superdome is on the far side of downtown on\n * a superblock big enough to hold it; City Park is inland and green.\n */\nexport const SITES = Object.freeze([\n  { id: \"jackson\", at: [-70, 470], label: \"Jackson Square\" },\n  { id: \"cathedral\", at: [-70, 452], label: \"St. Louis Cathedral\" },\n  { id: \"superdome\", at: [560, 300], label: \"The Superdome\" },\n  { id: \"citypark\", at: [340, 430], label: \"City Park\" },\n  { id: \"market\", at: [-100, 240], label: \"French Market\" },\n  { id: \"university\", at: [180, 440], label: \"Loyola University\" },\n]);\n\nexport function createNewOrleansLandmarks(ctx, kit) {\n  const { P, mesh, std, basic, pois, occluders, sign } = kit;\n  const { addBlocker } = ctx;\n\n  /** Lit at night: every window in the city is a warm rectangle, and it is most\n   * of what makes a skyline read as inhabited rather than modelled. */\n  const litWindow = () => basic(new THREE.Color(0xffc98a).multiplyScalar(1.5));\n  const darkWindow = () => basic(0x141c24);\n\n  // =========================================================================\n  // St. Louis Cathedral, and the square in front of it\n  // =========================================================================\n  //\n  // The most recognisable building in Louisiana, and the reason is its\n  // SILHOUETTE: a rectangular body with a tall central tower and a shorter\n  // tower at each end, the middle one about 1.6x the others. That ratio is the\n  // whole thing. A single central spire would be a church; three unequal\n  // steeples on a wide low body is the Cathedral, and it is on almost\n  // everything the city has ever printed.\n  function cathedral(b) {\n    const g = new THREE.Group(); g.position.set(b.cx, 0, b.cz); ctx.scene.add(g);\n    const w = 30, d = 62;                              // the body, running north–south\n    const stucco = std(0xf0ece0, \"cathedral stucco\", { roughness: 0.9 });\n    const stone = std(0xd8d2c2, \"cast stone\", { roughness: 0.85 });\n    const roofMat = std(0x4a4a4c, \"slate roof\", { roughness: 0.7, metalness: 0.2 });\n    const gold = basic(new THREE.Color(0xd9b23a).multiplyScalar(1.4));\n\n    // the body: a plain rectangular box, which is the actual plan\n    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, 26, d), stucco, b.cx, 13, b.cz, { parent: g });\n    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 1.2, 1.0, d + 1.2), stone, b.cx, 26.5, b.cz, { parent: g, cast: false });\n    // a low pitched roof over it\n    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w - 2, 3.4, d - 2), roofMat, b.cx, 28.7, b.cz, { parent: g });\n\n    // THE THREE STEEPLES. Centre first, and the middle one is much taller.\n    const steeple = (x, z, height, shaft) => {\n      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(shaft, shaft, shaft), stucco, b.cx + x, 30 + height / 2, b.cz + z, { parent: g });\n      // the belfry openings, so it is not a blank cube\n      for (const [ox, oz] of [[0, -1], [0, 1], [-1, 0], [1, 0]]) {\n        mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(shaft * 0.5, shaft * 0.62, 0.2), darkWindow(),\n          b.cx + x + ox * shaft * 0.26, 30 + height * 0.68, b.cz + z + oz * shaft * 0.26, { parent: g, cast: false, ry: oz ? 0 : Math.PI / 2 });\n      }\n      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(shaft + 1.0, 0.7, shaft + 1.0), stone, b.cx + x, 30 + height * 0.42, b.cz + z, { parent: g, cast: false });\n      // the spire: a tall pyramid, which is what makes it a steeple and not a tower\n      mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(shaft * 0.78, height * 0.42, 4), roofMat, b.cx + x, 30 + height + height * 0.21, b.cz + z, { parent: g, ry: Math.PI / 4 });\n      // the gold cross on top\n      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.22, 3.0, 0.22), gold, b.cx + x, 30 + height * 1.46, b.cz + z, { parent: g, cast: false });\n      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.5, 0.22, 0.22), gold, b.cx + x, 30 + height * 1.44, b.cz + z, { parent: g, cast: false });\n      addBlocker(b.cx + x, b.cz + z, shaft * 0.75);\n    };\n    steeple(0, 0, 62, 11);                  // the central tower: the tall one\n    steeple(0, -d / 2 + 6, 38, 9);          // …and one at each end, at 0.61 of it\n    steeple(0, d / 2 - 6, 38, 9);\n\n    // the clock on the river face, and the round window over the front door\n    mesh(new THREE.CircleGeometry(3.2, 16), stone, b.cx, 30, b.cz - d / 2 - 0.15, { parent: g, cast: false, ry: Math.PI });\n    mesh(new THREE.CircleGeometry(2.4, 16), darkWindow(), b.cx, 30, b.cz - d / 2 - 0.2, { parent: g, cast: false, ry: Math.PI });\n    mesh(new THREE.CircleGeometry(2.6, 16), darkWindow(), b.cx, 15, b.cz - d / 2 - 0.15, { parent: g, cast: false, ry: Math.PI });\n    // the long arched windows down each side\n    for (let i = -3; i <= 3; i++) {\n      for (const sx of [-1, 1]) {\n        mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.16, 9, 2.4), i % 2 ? St. Louis Cathedral was flanked by\n   * matching buildings for its whole history and they are half of what a photo\n   * of this square looks like; a cathedral standing alone on a lawn is a church.\n   */\n  function jacksonSquare(b) {\n    const g = new THREE.Group(); ctx.scene.add(g);\n    const pave = std(0xa8a294, \"square paving\", { roughness: 0.95 });\n    const iron = std(0x22262a, \"wrought iron railing\", { metalness: 0.55, roughness: 0.55 });\n    const W = b.x1 - b.x0, D = b.z1 - b.z0;\n    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(W, 0.12, D), pave, b.cx, 0.06, b.cz, { parent: g, cast: false });\n\n    // the river-facing rail, with its lamp posts along it\n    const railZ = b.z1 - 1.2;\n    mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(W, 0.1, 0.1), iron, b.cx, 1.1, railZ, { parent: g, cast: false });\n    for (let x = b.x0; x <= b.x1; x += 2.2) mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.07, 1.1, 0.07), iron, x, 0.55, railZ, { parent: g, cast: false });\n    for (let x = b.x0 + 6; x < b.x1; x += 13) {\n      mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.11, 0.15, 4.2, 8), iron, x, 2.1, railZ, { parent: g, cast: false });\n      mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.42, 8, 6), basic(new THREE.Color(0xffe0a8).multiplyScalar(2.2)), x, 4.5, railZ, { parent: g, cast: false });\n      ctx.addLitSpot && ctx.addLitSpot({ x, y: 4.6, z: railZ, warm: 0xffe0b0, power: 70, range: 18 });\n    }\n\n    // THE statue: Andrew Jackson on a rearing horse, facing the river. b.x0) * 2,\n    `${bb.h.toFixed(0)} m tall on a ${b.x1 - b.x0} m block`);\n  // the two wings, which are half of what the square looks like\n  check(\"the Cabildo is there\", signs.some((s) => s.text === \"THE CABILDO\"));\n  check(\"the Presbytère is there\", signs.some((s) => s.text === \"THE PRESBYTÈRE\"));\n  check(\"the square has its Spanish colonial arcades\", hasPart(\"Jackson Square\", \"spanish colonial stucco\"));\n  check(\"the square has paving\", hasPart(\"Jackson Square\", \"square paving\"));\n  check(\"the square has its iron railing to the river\", hasPart(\"Jackson Square\", \"wrought iron railing\"));\n  check(\"Andrew Jackson is on a horse in the middle of it\", hasPart(\"Jackson Square\", \"bronze\"));\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the Superdome\n{\n  const b = blockFor(\"The Superdome\");\n  const box = trueBox(scene);\n  check(\"the Superdome is built\", hasPart(\"The Superdome\", \"stadium precast\"));\n  check(\"the Superdome has a roof\", hasPart(\"The Superdome\", \"stadium roof\"));\n  check(\"the Superdome is enormous\", (b.x1 -   "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// streetlife.js — the people who make a city look inhabited.\n//\n//   const S = createStreetLife({ scene, resolveCollision, isNight, camera })\n//   S.build(routes)             routes: [{ a: [x, z], b: [x, z], kind, name }]\n//   S.update(dt, playerPos)\n//   S.get props()               anything that moves: main.js keeps it out of batchStatic\n//\n// \"general city-like NPCs like businessmen and like cops patrolling streets etc\"\n// (human request, 2026-10-01)\n//\n// The city grew from four hundred and sixty-five blocks of new building with\n// nobody in any of it. Traffic makes a road look used; it does not make a\n// street look like a street. What makes a city read as inhabited is PEOPLE on\n// the PAVEMENT — walking it, waiting at it, working it — and this is the\n// cheapest and largest win available, because these are the same rigs the rest\n// of the game already casts.\n//\n// Two kinds, and they are different in kind rather than in colour:\n//\n//   commuter  an office worker crossing the city on the way to or from work.\n//              Daytime only, quick, purposeful, in a suit. They are the reason a\n//              CBD looks open at nine in the morning.\n//   beat      a policeman walking a fixed route. ALWAYS there, day or night —\n//              which is what makes a city feel policed, and is the thing the\n//              existing foot-cop system could never do: it only spawns a\n//              deputy in response to the player being wanted, so an empty street\n//              and a street under martial law looked identical.\n//\n// Everything is distance-culled. A person 200 m away is not drawn, not updated\n// and not collided, and the pool is capped, so the cost of a big city is\n// bounded by how much of it you can see rather than by how much of it exists.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { randomHoodrat, randomTuxedo, randomRedneck, makeDeputy, randomHighEndEscort } from \"./characters.js\";\n\n/** How far away a walker is still drawn and updated. */\nexport const ACTIVE_RADIUS = 150;\n/** …and how far away it still exists, before being despawned entirely. */\nconst KEEP_RADIUS = 260;\nconst POOL_CAP = 46;\n\nconst lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;\n\nexport function createStreetLife({ scene, resolveCollision = null, isNight = () => false, rng = Math.random }) {\n  const actors = [];\n  const free = [];\n  let nextId = 1;\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the routes\n  //\n  // A route is a straight walk between two points with a kerbside offset, and\n  // everything else — direction, gait, what they do at the end — falls out of\n  // that. Routes are generated from a district's own street grid rather than\n  // scattered, because a pedestrian who walks in a straight line across open\n  // ground is the single clearest tell that nobody placed them.\n  function makeRoutes({ avenues, streets, width, minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ, roadX }) {\n    const out = [];\n    const footway = width / 2 + 1.1;              // the pavement, just off the kerb\n    // a beat down each avenue, and a couple of crossing beats on the big streets\n    for (const x of avenues) {\n      if (x < minX + 30 || x > maxX - 30) continue;\n      for (const side of [-1, 1]) {\n        out.push({\n          a: [x + side * footway, minZ + 20], b: [x + side * footway, maxZ - 20],\n          kind: \"beat\", name: `avenue ${x}`, speed: 0.85,\n        });\n      }\n    }\n    for (const z of streets) {\n      if (z < minZ + 30 || z > maxZ - 30) continue;\n      // the east–west beats, offset to the far pavement so the two directions\n      // are on opposite sides of the road\n      out.push({ a: [minX + 20, z - footway], b: [maxX - 20, z - footway], kind: \"beat\", name: `street ${z}`, speed: 0.85 });\n      out.push({ a: [maxX - 20, z + footway], b: [minX + 20, z + footway], kind: \"beat\", name: `street ${z}`, speed: 0.9 });\n    }\n    // the crossings: short beats that take somebody over the boulevard, which\n    // is where a city shows you that it has crossings\n    for (const z of streets) {\n      out.push({ a: [roadX - 8, z - 12], b: [roadX + 8, z - 12], kind: \"commuter\", name: `crossing ${z}`, speed: 1.15 });\n      out.push({ a: [roadX + 8, z + 12], b: [roadX - 8, z + 12], kind: \"commuter\", name: `crossing ${z}`, speed: 1.1 });\n    }\n    // and the commuters proper: long diagonal walks across the CBD, which is\n    // what people actually do and what no straight grid route looks like\n    for (let i = 0; i < 26; i++) {\n      const ax = lerp(minX + 30, maxX - 30, rng()), az = lerp(minZ + 30, maxZ - 30, rng());\n      const bx = lerp(minX + 30, maxX - 30, rng()), bz = lerp(minZ + 30, maxZ - 30, rng());\n      out.push({ a: [ax, az], b: [bx, bz], kind: \"commuter\", name: \"commute\", speed: 1.25 });\n    }\n    return out;\n  }\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the cast\n  function cast(kind, r) {\n    if (kind === \"beat\") return makeDeputy({ police: true, seed: (r() * 1e9) | 0, height: 1.82 });\n    // the daytime crowd is suits and shirts; a little of everything else, so\n    // nine in the morning is not a single species\n    const roll = r();\n    if (roll < 0.46) return randomTuxedo(r, 1.80);\n    if (roll < 0.70) return randomHoodrat(r, 1.76, { shirt: true });\n    if (roll < 0.84) return randomHighEndEscort(r, 1.78);\n    return randomRedneck(r, 1.74);\n  }\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the pool\n  function spawn(route) {\n    const a = free.pop();\n    const actor = a && a.kind === route.kind ? a : cast(route.kind, rng);\n    const rec = a || {};\n    rec.id = rec.id || nextId++;\n    rec.kind = route.kind;\n    rec.route = route;\n    rec.speed = route.speed * (0.9 + rng() * 0.25);\n    rec.t = rng();       // people move: never merged into a static batch\n        m.userData.streetLife = true;\n      });\n      scene.add(actor);\n    }\n    actor.play(route.kind === \"beat\" ? \"walk\" : \"walk\", { force: true });\n    actors.push(rec);\n    return rec;\n  }\n\n  function despawn(rec) {\n    const i = actors.indexOf(rec);\n    if (i >= 0) actors.splice(i, 1);\n    scene.remove(rec.mesh);\n    rec.route = null;\n    free.push(rec);\n  }\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the tick\n  const _p = new THREE.Vector3();\n  const _q = new THREE.Vector3();\n  let routes = [];\n\n  function build(given) {\n    routes = given || [];\n    for (const rec of actors) { scene.remove(rec.mesh); rec.route = null; free.push(rec); }\n    actors.length = 0;\n    // One walker per route, capped. A route with nobody on it is a dead street\n    // and a route with four is a crowd scene; one each, spread by position, is\n    // what reads as a city going about its business.\n    for (const r of routes) {\n      if (actors.length >= POOL_CAP) break;\n      spawn(r);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Walk everybody toward the far end of their route, turn at the end, and\n   * cull by distance. `_speed` is derived by the rig from how far the body\n   * actually moved, which is why the walk clip's stride scales itself and why\n   * a paused commuter stands still instead of moonwalking.\n   */\n  function update(dt, playerPos) {\n    if (!routes.length) return;\n    const px = playerPos ? playerPos.x : 0, pz = playerPos ? playerPos.z : 0;\n    const night = isNight();\n    for (let i = actors.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n      const rec = actors[i];\n      const r = rec.route;\n      const ax = r.a[0], az = r.a[1], bx = r.b[0], bz = r.b[1];\n      const cx = lerp(ax, bx, rec.t), cz = lerp(az, bz, rec.t);\n      const d2 = (cx - px) ** 2 + (cz - pz) ** 2;\n\n      if (d2 > KEEP_RADIUS * KEEP_RADIUS) { despawn(rec); continue; }\n      // out of sight: parked, not deleted. Deleting and recasting on the way\n      // back is a visible pop, and popping pedestrians are worse than a few\n      // frozen ones at the edge of vision.\n      const visible = d2 < ACTIVE_RADIUS * ACTIVE_RADIUS;\n      rec.mesh.visible = visible;\n      if (!visible) continue;\n\n      // a commuter is somebody going to work; a beat is somebody who is always\n      // on, and that difference is the whole reason both exist\n      if (rec.kind === \"commuter\" && night && rec.pause <= 0) rec.pause = 4 + rng() * 20;\n      if (rec.pause > 0) {\n        rec.pause -= dt;\n        rec.mesh.play(\"idle\", { force: rec.pause <= 0 });\n        rec.mesh.update(dt);\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      rec.t += (rec.dir * rec.speed * dt) / Math.max(1, Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az));\n      if (rec.t >= 1) { rec.t = 1; rec.dir = -1; rec.pause = 0.4 + rng() * 2.5; }\n      else if (rec.t <= 0) { rec.t = 0; rec.dir = 1; rec.pause = 0.4 + rng() * 2.5; }\n\n      _p.set(lerp(ax, bx, rec.t), 0, lerp(az, bz, rec.t));\n      _q.set(lerp(ax, bx, rec.t + rec.dir * 0.01), 0, lerp(az, bz, rec.t + rec.dir * 0.01));\n      // collision, so they use the kerbs and the corners rather than walking\n      // through parked cars and the faces of buildings\n      if (resolveCollision) {\n        const c = resolveCollision(_p.x, _p.z, 0.45);\n        if (c) _p.set(c.x, 0, c.z);\n      }\n      const dx = _q.x - _p.x, dz = _q.z - _p.z;\n      if (dx * dx + dz * dz > 1e-8) {\n        rec.mesh.position.copy(_p);\n        if (rec.mesh._last) rec.mesh._last.copy(_p);\n        rec.mesh.rotation.y = Math.atan2(dx, dz);\n        if (rec.mesh._yaw != null) rec.mesh._yaw = rec.mesh.rotation.y;\n      }\n      if (rec.mesh.anim !== \"walk\") rec.mesh.play(\"walk\", { force: true });\n      rec.mesh.update(dt);\n      rec.life += dt;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    build, update, makeRoutes, spawn, despawn,\n    /** Everything here moves: main.js must keep it out of batchStatic. */\n    get props() { return actors.map((a) => a.mesh); },\n    get actors() { return actors; },\n    get count() { return actors.length; },\n  };\n}\n"

function resolveCollision(current, next, radius) {
  blockerGrid.resolve(next, radius, current, null);

// Put the player (and whatever she is driving) somewhere. The district modules
// each carry their own inline copy of this in their ctx; this is the one the

function teleportPlayer(x, z, heading = 0) {
  const v = state.veh;
  if (v) {
    v.obj.position.x = x; v.obj.position.z = z;
    v.heading = heading; v.obj.rotation.y = heading; v.speed = 0;
    v.blocker.x = x; v.blocker.z = z;
  }
  playerPos.set(x, 0, z);
  if (player) {
    player.position.set(x, 0, z);
    if (player._last) player._last.copy(player.position);
  }
}

```
  function update(dt, playerPos) {
    prompt = null;
    for (const c of clubs) {
      const dx = playerPos ? playerPos.x - c.x : Infinity;
      const dz = playerPos ? playerPos.z - c.z : Infinity;
      const lx = Math.cos(c.rot) * dx - Math.sin(c.rot) * dz;
      const lz = Math.sin(c.rot) * dx + Math.cos(c.rot) * dz;
      const inside = Math.abs(lx) < 9.2 && lz > -5.0 && lz < 4.8;
      // the annex sits past the stage: local z from -6 to -16.5, |x| < 2.9
      const inBack = Math.abs(lx) < 2.9 && lz <= -6 && lz > -16.5;
      c.root.visible = inside || inBack || Math.hypot(dx, dz) < 15;
      if (c.exteriorRoof) c.exteriorRoof.visible = !(inside || inBack);
      for (const part of c.exteriorFront || []) part.visible = !(inside || inBack);
      if (c.root.visible) {
        const wasEncore = c.encoreWasActive;
        c.encoreTimer = Math.max(0, c.encoreTimer - Math.max(0, dt));
        c.coffeeCd = Math.max(0, (c.coffeeCd || 0) - Math.max(0, dt));
        c.nightCd = Math.max(0, (c.nightCd || 0) - Math.max(0, dt));
        c.encoreWasActive = c.encoreTimer > 0;
        if (wasEncore && !c.encoreWasActive) {
          for (const p of c.performers) p.actor.play(c.routine[c.routineIndex], { force: true, loop: true });
        }
        // The house clock, and the routine that runs off it. The whole cast
        // changes on the same beat — a routine change is a cue, and a cue the
        // rest of the stage has not heard is just a woman dancing to herself.
        c.beat.t += Math.max(0, dt);
        if (!c.encoreWasActive) {
          c.routineElapsed += Math.max(0, dt);
          if (c.routineElapsed >= ROUTINE_SECONDS) {
            const steps = Math.floor(c.routineElapsed / ROUTINE_SECONDS);
            c.routineElapsed %= ROUTINE_SECONDS;
            c.routineIndex = (c.routineIndex + steps) % c.routine.length;
            const next = c.routine[c.routineIndex];
            for (const p of c.performers) {
              p.routineIndex = c.routineIndex;
              p.routineChanges += steps;
              // Each performer owns her own number: a strip tease on a three-woman
              // stage is three separate teases with three separate wardrobes, and
              // they are started and ended per performer rather than per room.
              endStageAct(p);
              if (STAGE_ACTS.includes(next)) {
                p.act = beginStageAct(p.actor, next) || null;
                if (p.act) { p.actClock = 0; continue; }   // it refused (gate) — fall through
              }
              p.actor.play(next, { force: true, loop: true });
            }
          }
          // ...and a number is bounded: when it is over the costume goes back on
          // and she carries on dancing. A dancer left bare for the rest of the
          // night is a bug, not a feature.
          for (const p of c.performers) {
            if (!p.act) continue;
            p.actClock = (p.actClock || 0) + Math.max(0, dt);
            if (p.actClock >= p.act.seconds) { p.act.end(); p.act = null; p.actClock = 0; }
          }
        }
        for (const p of c.performers) p.actor.update(dt);
        updateLights(c, dt);
        updatePatrons(c, dt);
        // A staged scene runs on this club's own clock, not the world's: the
        // night overlay pauses the sim, and a scene that froze the moment you
        // chose it would be the most lifeless thing in the building.
        if (c.staged) c.staged.update(Math.max(dt, 1 / 120));
        if (c.host) {
          // the host waits on the bed, mid-dance pose, and follows the player
          // with her yaw so she "watches" them come in
          const hp = c.backSpot;
          const hx = playerPos ? playerPos.x - hp.x : 0;
          const hz = playerPos ? playerPos.z - hp.z : 0;
          c.host._yaw = Math.atan2(hx, hz) - c.rot;
          c.host.update(dt);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// adultContent.js — per-launch adult acknowledgement and optional rhythm game.
//
// The 18+ gate is shown at the start of EVERY launch (nothing is remembered): the whole game is for adults. The optional activity
// preference is stored separately and defaults off.

  { key: "ArrowDown", glyph: "↓" },
  { key: "ArrowLeft", glyph: "←" },
  { key: "ArrowRight", glyph: "→" },
];

export function makeBeatPattern(rng = Math.random, count = 8) {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, () => ARROWS[Math.floor(rng() * ARROWS.length)].key);
}

export function gradeRhythm(score, total) {
  if (!total) return "No score";
  const ratio = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, score / total));
  return ratio >= 0.85 ? "Bayou legend" : ratio >= 0.6 ? "Right on the beat" : ratio >= 0.35 ? "Finding the groove" : "Keep practicing";
}

Whatever you're paying, they're undercharging.\"" : "*afterglow — she stretches, satisfied* \"Mmm. Good night's work, sugar.\"");

  x.beginPath(); x.arc(64, 64, 58, 0, Math.PI * 2); x.fill();
  x.lineWidth = 8; x.strokeStyle = "#101010"; x.stroke();
  x.font = icon === "✚" ? "bold 84px Arial" : "68px 'Segoe UI Emoji', 'Apple Color Emoji', sans-serif";
  x.fillStyle = icon === "✚" ? "#ffffff" : "#000";
  x.textAlign = "center"; x.textBaseline = "middle";
  x.fillText(icon, 64, icon === "✚" ? 70 : 68);
  const t = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
  t.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  return t;
}

const DEFAULT_SPECIAL = 5, MIN_S = 1, MAX_S = 10, BASE_POINTS = 5, MAX_TAGS = 3, TAG_BONUS = 15, TRAIT_CAP = 12;

const clamp = (v, a, b) => Math.max(a, Math.min(b, v));

/**
 * The creation economy in one place (pipboy.js and the tests both use it). Two separate pools, as in
 * Zomboid:
 *   attrPoints  start at 5; each attribute point above the default of 5 spends one, each below it hands one back
 *               (a 1 in Charisma is four points for somewhere else);
 *   traitPoints start at 0; a good trait spends its cost, a bad trait gives its cost back.
 * Neither pool may end below zero.
 */
export function creationBudget({ special = {}, traits = [] } = {}) {
  let attrPoints = BASE_POINTS;
  for (const s of SPECIAL) attrPoints -= (special[s.id] ?? DEFAULT_SPECIAL) - DEFAULT_SPECIAL;
  let traitPoints = 0;
  for (const id of traits) { const t = TRAITS.find((x) => x.id === id); if (t) traitPoints -= t.cost; }
  return { attrPoints, traitPoints };
}

const STEP = 0.25;
const X0 = -11, X1 = 11, Z0 = -18, Z1 = 6;
const cols = Math.round((X1 - X0) / STEP) + 1;
const rows = Math.round((Z1 - Z0) / STEP) + 1;

  for (const [dc, dr] of [[1, 0], [-1, 0], [0, 1], [0, -1]]) {

    if (seen[ni]) continue;
    if (solid(X0 + nc * STEP, Z0 + nr * STEP)) continue;
    seen[ni] = 1;
    queue.push(ni);

/** Replace a procedural weapon's parts with its loaded GLB skin, in place. */
function swapInGlbSkin(model, glb) {
  if (!glb) return;
  for (const child of [...model.children]) {
    if (child.name === "muzzle") continue;
    model.remove(child);
  }
  model.add(glb);
}

```
  //
  // A route is a straight walk between two points with a kerbside offset, and
  // everything else — direction, gait, what they do at the end — falls out of
  // that. Routes are generated from a district's own street grid rather than
  // scattered, because a pedestrian who walks in a straight line across open
  // ground is the single clearest tell that nobody placed them.
  function makeRoutes({ avenues, streets, width, minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ, roadX }) {
    const out = [];
    const footway = width / 2 + 1.1;              // the pavement, just off the kerb
    // a beat down each avenue, and a couple of crossing beats on the big streets
    for (const x of avenues) {
      if (x < minX + 30 || x > maxX - 30) continue;
      for (const side of [-1, 1]) {
        out.push({
          a: [x + side * footway, minZ + 20], b: [x + side * footway, maxZ - 20],
          kind: "beat", name: `avenue ${x}`, speed: 0.85,
        });
      }
    }
    for (const z of streets) {
      if (z < minZ + 30 || z > maxZ - 30) continue;
      // the east–west beats, offset to the far pavement so the two directions
      // are on opposite sides of the road
      out.push({ a: [minX + 20, z - footway], b: [maxX - 20, z - footway], kind: "beat", name: `street ${z}`, speed: 0.85 });
      out.push({ a: [maxX - 20, z + footway], b: [minX + 20, z + footway], kind: "beat", name: `street ${z}`, speed: 0.9 });
    }
    // the crossings: short beats that take somebody over the boulevard, which
    // is where a city shows you that it has crossings
    for (const z of streets) {
      out.push({ a: [roadX - 8, z - 12], b: [roadX + 8, z - 12], kind: "commuter", name: `crossing ${z}`, speed: 1.15 });
      out.push({ a: [roadX + 8, z + 12], b: [roadX - 8, z + 12], kind: "commuter", name: `crossing ${z}`, speed: 1.1 });
    }
    // and the commuters proper: long diagonal walks across the CBD, which is
    // what people actually do and what no straight grid route looks like. Both
    // ends are re-rolled until the walk is a real distance — two random points
    // in a rectangle are often close together, and a 30 m "commute" is a person
    // turning on the spot wearing a suit.
    for (let i = 0; i < 26; i++) {
      let ax = 0, az = 0, bx = 0, bz = 0, len = 0;
      for (let tries = 0; tries < 8; tries++) {
        ax = lerp(minX + 30, maxX - 30, rng()); az = lerp(minZ + 30, maxZ - 30, rng());
        bx = lerp(minX + 30, maxX - 30, rng()); bz = lerp(minZ + 30, maxZ - 30, rng());
        len = Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az);
        if (len > 90) break;
      }
      if (len <= 40) continue;               // the rectangle is too small to commute across
      out.push({ a: [ax, az], b: [bx, bz], kind: "commuter", name: "commute", speed: 1.25 });
    }
    return out;

  "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// dialogue.js — talk to anyone who is not trying to kill you.\n//\n// The Crown Strip's private dance and back rooms were the only two things in\n// the game you could walk up to a person and *do*, and both were bolted onto\n// one venue. What the list CONTAINS is per-person and per-role, because a\n// bartender, a beat cop, a club dancer and a street walker have nothing in\n// common, and a menu that offers all of it to all of them is a menu nobody\n// reads.\n//\n// Design, in the order the code asks about it:\n//\n//   1. DISCOVERY IS NOT THE MODULE'S JOB. Nothing here knows what a crowd\n//      actor is. main.js hands us a flat list of nearby people\n//      (`nearbyPeople`), each already reduced to {name, role, x, z, ...}. The\n//      nightclub behind you keeps dancing, because a frozen room behind a\n//      dialogue box is the single most lifeless thing a dialogue system can do.\n//\n//   4. Only while actually crouched, and only on somebody who is\n  // not a cop: a deputy who finds a hand in his pocket is a different game from\n  // a drunk in a bar, and \"witnesses\" is what separates the two.\n  if (p.carry && p.carry.length) {\n    out.push({\n      id: \"pickpocket\",\n      label: `Pickpocket ${p.name}`,\n      hint: p.carry.map((c2) => c2.label).join(\", \"),\n      locked: !ctx.sneaking ? \"You have to be crouched\" : p.witnesses ? \"Too many people watching\" : null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  out.push({ id: \"leave\", label: \"Say goodbye\" });\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * What a person is carrying — the pickpocket and barter loot tables. Weighted,\n * and deliberately mundane: a wallet, some change, a phone, a watch, cigarettes,\n * a ring left on by somebody who did not need it.\n */\nconst CARRY_TABLE = [\n  { id: \"change\",  label: \"Loose change\",  weight: 30, cash: [3, 18] },\n  { id: \"wallet\",  label: \"A wallet\",      weight: 22, cash: [25, 140] },\n  { id: \"phone\",   label: \"A phone\",       weight: 14, cash: [0, 40] },\n  { id: \"watch\",   label: \"A gold watch\",  weight: 9,  cash: [60, 260] },\n  { id: \"cigs\",    label: \"A pack of cigarettes\", weight: 18, cash: [4, 12] },\n  { id: \"ring\",    label: \"A diamond ring\", weight: 5, cash: [180, 700] },\n  { id: \"medkit\",  label: \"A medkit\",      weight: 8,  cash: [0, 0], medkit: 1 },\n  { id: \"pistol\",  label: \"A pistol\",      weight: 4,  cash: [0, 0], weapon: \"pistol\" },\n];\n\n/**\n * Roll what somebody is carrying. `role` skews it: dealers carry product,\n * cops carry a sidearm, dancers carry a bag with their stuff in it.\n */\nexport function carryFor(role, rng = Math.random) {\n  const fam = roleFamily(role);\n  const table = CARRY_TABLE.slice();\n  if (fam === \"dealer\") { table.push({ id: \"stash\", label: \"A wrapped stash\", weight: 22, cash: [70, 220] }, { id: \"pill\", label: \"Bottle of pills\", weight: 12, cash: [40, 130] }); }\n  if (fam === \"beat\") { table.push({ id: \"radio\", label: \"A police radio\", weight: 10, cash: [0, 0] }, { id: \"ammo\", label: \"A spare magazine\", weight: 12, cash: [0, 0], rounds: 16 }); }\n  if (fam === \"performer\") { table.push({ id: \"tips\", label: \"A roll of tips\", weight: 26, cash: [15, 90] }, { id: \"shoes\", label: \"A pair of expensive shoes\", weight: 7, cash: [40, 150] }); }\n  if (fam === \"barkeep\" || fam === \"dealer\") { table.push({ id: \"till\", label: \"A hand's worth of the till\", weight: 14, cash: [40, 180] }); }\n\n  const total = table.reduce((s, e) => s + e.weight, 0);\n  const n = rng() < 0.72 ? (rng() < 0.82 ? 1 : 2) : 0;   // most people have something; some have a lot\n  const out = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n    let r = rng() * total;\n    const pick = table.find((e) => (r -= e.weight) <= 0) || table[0];\n    if (out.some((o) => o.id === pick.id)) continue;\n    const cash = pick.cash ? Math.round(pick.cash[0] + rng() * (pick.cash[1] - pick.cash[0])) : 0;\n    out.push({ ...pick, cash, value: cash + (pick.medkit ? 45 : 0) + (pick.weapon ? 160 : 0) + (pick.rounds ? 30 : 0) });\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport { GOODS, GREETINGS, roleFamily };\n"
}

=== api shape ===
  const api = {
    name, special, traits, tagged, perks, background: bg,
    get level() { return level; }, get xp() { return xp; }, get xpToNext() { return xpForNext(level); },
    get skillPoints() { return skillPoints; }, get perkPoints() { return perkPoints; }, get kills() { return kills; },
    skill,
    /** How much of the next level's bar is filled, 0..1. */
    get xpFrac() { return xp / xpForNext(level); },
    /** Give XP (scaled by Intelligence and traits). Returns the number of levels gained. */
    addXp(amount) {
      const gained = Math.max(0, Math.round(amount * (0.9 + special.int * 0.04) * prod("xpMul")));
      xp += gained;
      let ups = 0;
      while (xp >= xpForNext(level) && level < 30) {
        xp -= xpForNext(level); level++; ups++;
        skillPoints += 10 + Math.floor(special.int / 2);
        if (level % 2 === 0) perkPoints++;
      }
      return ups;
    },
    noteKill() { kills++; },
    /** Spend one skill point (Fallout: +1 to the skill, capped at 100). */
    buySkill(id) {
      if (skillPoints <= 0 || skill(id) >= 100 || !SKILLS.some((k) => k.id === id)) return false;
      skillPoints--; invested[id] = (invested[id] || 0) + 1; return true;
    },
    canTakePerk(p) {
      if (perks.includes(p.id) || perkPoints <= 0) return false;
      if (p.req.skill && skill(p.req.skill[0]) < p.req.skill[1]) return false;
      if (p.req.attr && special[p.req.attr[0]] < p.req.attr[1]) return false;
      return true;
    },
    takePerk(id) {
      const p = PERKS.find((x) => x.id === id);
      if (!p || !api.canTakePerk(p)) return false;
      perks.push(id); perkPoints--; return true;
    },
    /** Everything the game asks for, as multipliers on its own numbers. */
    mods: {
      // damage
      gunMul: () => prod("gunMul") * (1 + (skill("guns") - 30) / 250),
      recoilMul: () => clamp(1.2 - skill("guns") / 125, 0.4, 1.2),

Not here, not now.\"; mode = \"said\"; render(); return; }\n    if (!m.carry.length) { lastSaid = `<i>${person.name}</i> hasn't got anything worth taking.`; mode = \"said\"; render(); return; }\n    const r = socialRoll({ skill: skill(\"sneak\"), cha: cha(), skillCap: 100, bonus: -0.05, rng });\n    if (r.ok) {\n      const took = m.carry.splice(0, 1)[0];\n      addCash(took.cash || 0);\n      if (took.medkit) { state.medkits = (state.medkits || 0) + took.medkit; }\n      if (took.rounds) addRounds(took.rounds);\n      if (took.weapon && ctx.giveWeapon) ctx.giveWeapon(took.weapon);\n      const xp = 14;\n      character()?.addXp?.(xp);\n      const val = took.value ? ` (worth about $${took.value})` : \"\";\n      lastSaid = `You take ${took.label}${val}. Nobody saw. XP +${xp}.`;\n      say(`Pickpocketed ${took.label}.`);\n      if (!m.carry.length) lastSaid += \" That's all they've got.\";\n    } else {\n      const noticed = person.notices || socialRoll({ skill: skill(\"per\") || 0, cha: cha(), rng }).ok;\n      lastSaid = noticed\n        ? `<i>${person.name}</i> looks down, then up, and knows exactly what happened. \"Hey — HEY.\" (Sneak check: ${Math.round(r.chance * 100)}%)`\n        : `Your hand is too slow. <i>${person.name}</i> shifts, and the pocket is gone.
