-1 : 1); return;\n      }\n      if (mode === \"list\" && [\"ArrowUp\", \"ArrowDown\"].includes(e.key)) { e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); return; }\n      if ([\"w\", \"a\", \"s\", \"d\", \" \"].includes(e.key)) { e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); return; }\n    }\n    if (e.key === \"Escape\" || e.key === \"q\" || e.key === \"Q\") {\n      e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();\n      if (mode === \"trade\") { mode = \"list\"; lastSaid = \"\"; render(); } else close();\n      return;\n    }\n    if (e.key === \"ArrowUp\") { e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); move(-1); return; }\n    if (e.key === \"ArrowDown\") { e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); move(1); return; }\n    if (e.key === \"Enter\" || e.key === \"e\" || e.key === \"E\") {\n      e.preventDefault(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();\n      if (mode === \"trade\") {\n        const goods = stockFor(person.role);\n        if (tradeSel < goods.length) chooseTrade(goods[tradeSel]); else close();\n      } else if (mode === \"list\") {\n        const opt = rows[selected];\n        if (opt && !opt.locked) pick(opt.id);\n        else if (opt?.locked) say(opt.locked);\n      } else { mode = \"list\"; lastSaid = \"\"; render(); }\n    }\n  }\n\n  function move(d) {\n    if (mode === \"trade\") { const n = stockFor(person.role).length + 1; tradeSel = (tradeSel + d + n) % n; render(); return; }\n    if (!rows.length) return;\n    selected = (selected + d + rows.length) % rows.length;\n    render();\n  }\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the prompt\n  /**\n   * Called from update(): if the player is near somebody talkable and the\n   * overlay is closed, show the E prompt. Real design bug: `optionsFor` gates pickpocket on `p.carry`, but carry is rolled in `remember()` — so the option never appears. The memory must be merged into the person before the list is built:

**🛠 Str Replace**

```json

> Several failures. Key one: "the greeting is no longer selected" — because `render()` does `box.replaceChildren()` which creates NEW row elements, so the test's captured `firstRow` reference is stale. The test needs to re-query after render. That's a test artifact.
> 
> Also "picking" via click: my fake `li.addEventListener("click", ...)` — the test calls `rumourRow.children[1].click?.()` but children[1] is the `<span class="t">` which has no click handler; the handler is on the `li`. The fake el's `click` is `noop` and doesn't dispatch. So I need the fake DOM to dispatch click to listeners.
> 
> Let me fix the fake DOM: `click()` should call `_listeners.click`. And the test should click the `li` not the span.

```json
{
  "path": "tools/qa/dialogue_test.mjs",

      "oldString": "function textOf(node) {\n  if (!node) return \"\";\n  let out = node.textContent || \"\";\n  for (const c of node.childNodes || []) {\n    if (c === node) continue;\n    const inner = textOf(c);\n    if (inner && !out.includes(inner)) out += inner;\n  }\n  return out;\n}",
      "newString": "function textOf(node, seen = new Set()) {\n  if (!node || seen.has(node)) return \"\";\n  seen.add(node);\n  let out = node.textContent || \"\";\n  // Recurse into BOTH lists: a real fragment carries its children in one of\n  // them, and the stub's fragment only fills `children`, so walking a single\n  // list silently loses whatever was built through a fragment.\n  for (const c of [...(node.children || []), ...(node.childNodes || [])]) out += textOf(c, seen);\n  return out;\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

\"beat\" : \"commuter\",\n        x: a.position.x, z: a.position.z, seed: rec.id,\n        // a beat cop is not a bag of money, and a deputy with a hand in his\n        // pocket is a police problem rather than a funny one\n        carryable: rec.kind !== \"beat\",\n        witnesses: false,\n        notices: rec.kind === \"beat\",\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  // the clubs' own cast: performers, the host, the staff, the patrons\n  const clubs = stateWorld?.franchiseClubs?.clubs || [];\n  for (const c of clubs) {\n    const add = (actor, role, name, extra) => {\n      if (!actor || actor.visible === false) return;\n      const p = actor.getWorldPosition(_talkVec);\n      if (!near(p.x, p.z, 6)) return;\n      _talkable.push({ name, role, x: p.x, z: p.z, seed: `club${c.kind}${name || role}`, ...extra });\n    };\n    for (const per of c.performers || []) {\n      add(per.actor, \"performer\", per.actor?.userData?.stageName, { adult: per.actor?.userData?.age >= 25 });\n    }\n    add(c.host, \"performer\", c.host?.userData?.stageName, {\n      adult: c.host?.userData?.age >= 25,\n      // the SAME handle the back rooms and the private dance use, so asking a\n      // performer for time routes into code that already has its own age gate,\n      // its own charge and its own Esc\n      host: c.host,\n    });\n    for (const rec of c.patrons || []) add(rec.actor || rec.a, \"patron\", null, {});\n  }\n\n  // Market Row and the pavement crowds\n  for (const rec of npc?.actors || []) {\n    const a = rec.a || rec.actor || rec.mesh;\n    if (!a || a.visible === false) continue;\n    const p = a.getWorldPosition ?   function buildCauseway() {
    const water = new THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial({
      // see eastbank.js: no clearcoat, so it reads as water, not a grey-white sheet
      color: 0x06110e, roughness: 0.18, metalness: 0, envMapIntensity: 0.35,
      transparent: true, opacity: 0.6, name: "swamp water",
    });
    water.userData.gtbRealized = true;
    const x0 = ctx.ROAD_X - ctx.ROAD_HALF, x1 = ctx.ROAD_X + ctx.ROAD_HALF;
    const len = CAUSEWAY.maxZ - CAUSEWAY.minZ + 8;
    const zc = (CAUSEWAY.minZ + CAUSEWAY.maxZ) / 2;
    plane(x0 - 2 + 140, len, water, (x0 - 2 - 140) / 2, 0.035, zc);
    plane(400 - x1 - 2, len, water, (x1 + 2 + 400) / 2, 0.035, zc);

    // guardrails the whole way across, solid for walkers and cars
    const rail = std("steel guardrail", 0x9aa0a6, { metalness: 0.8, roughness: 0.4 });
    for (const x of [x0 - 0.6, x1 + 0.6]) {
      mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.25, 0.7, len), rail, x, 0.6, zc);
      for (let z = CAUSEWAY.minZ; z <= CAUSEWAY.maxZ; z += 3) ctx.addBlocker(x, z, 0.55);
    }

// "the city area needs to feel like a bustling metropolis eventually… we can

//
// The two things that can go wrong when a grid is scaled up are both silent.
// Blocks can stop being covered by any builder, leaving bald patches of pavement
// in the middle of a metropolis; and a block can be covered by two, which used
// to be decided by the order the builders happened to run in. So these check

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- streets
  function buildStreets() {

    const cw = CITY.maxX - CITY.minX, cd = CITY.maxZ - CITY.minZ + 4;
    for (const t of [side.map, side.normalMap, side.roughnessMap]) if (t) t.repeat.set(cw / 12, cd / 12);
    plane(cw, cd, side, 0, 0.012, (CITY.minZ + CITY.maxZ) / 2);

    const asphalt = ctx.surface("asphalt", 1024);
    const street = (w, d, x, z) => {
      const m = asphalt.material(1);
      for (const t of [m.map, m.normalMap, m.roughnessMap]) if (t) t.repeat.set(Math.max(1, w / 9), Math.max(1, d / 9));
      plane(w, d, m, x, 0.022, z);
    };
    for (const x of AVENUES) {
      // an avenue is cut where it crosses a superblock, not drawn through it
      const cuts = RESERVES.filter((r) => x > r.x0 - STREET_W && x < r.x1 + STREET_W);
      let from = CITY.minZ;
      for (const r of cuts.sort((a, b) => a.z0 - b.z0)) {
        if (r.z0 > from) street(STREET_W, r.z0 - from, x, (from + r.z0) / 2);
        from = r.z1;
      }
      if (CITY.maxZ > from) street(STREET_W, CITY.maxZ - from, x, (from + CITY.maxZ) / 2);
    }
    for (const z of STREETS) {
      const cuts = RESERVES.filter((r) => z > r.z0 - STREET_W && z < r.z1 + STREET_W);
      let from = CITY.minX;
      for (const r of cuts.sort((a, b) => a.x0 - b.x0)) {
        if (r.x0 > from) street(r.x0 - from, STREET_W, (from + r.x0) / 2, z);
        from = r.x1;
      }
      if (CITY.maxX > from) street(CITY.maxX - from, STREET_W, (from + CITY.maxX) / 2, z);
    }

    // lamps: down the boulevard, along two French District streets, the promenade
    for (let z = 204; z < 376; z += 40) {
      ctx.addLitSpot({ x: ctx.ROAD_X + ctx.ROAD_HALF + 2, y: 6, z, warm: 0xffd9a0, power: 110, range: 26, pole: true });
    }
    for (const z of [250, 290]) {
      for (let x = -120; x <= 376; x += 40) { if (x > -10 && x < 176) continue; ctx.addLitSpot({ x, y: 5, z: z - STREET_W / 2 - 1.5, warm: 0xffc890, power: 90, range: 22, pole: true }); }
    }
    for (let x = -80; x <= 376; x += 40) ctx.addLitSpot({ x, y: 5, z: 378, warm: 0xffe0b0, power: 90, range: 22, pole: true });

    // the welcome, with a reply from Keseme's own narration
    ctx.makeBillboard(ctx.ROAD_X + ctx.ROAD_HALF + 7, 199, Math.PI, "ORLEAROUGE", POP_TEXT + " · Life Is Beautiful", "BEAUTY DON'T MAKE YOU SAFE");
  }

  "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// orleafeinge.js — the road out of OrleaRouge, and the overpass done properly.\n//\n// WHY THIS EXISTS\n//\n// The city was grown east to x = 680 and the measurement is blunt: at\n// x = 720 there is not one mesh, and nothing at all between there and the edge\n// of the map at 1200. No deck surface (so it read\n// as raw concrete from above, which is the angle you approach an overpass\n// from), no markings, no parapet to stop you driving off the edge, no ramp, and\n// a camp pitched under it for no reason anyone could see. concrete.material(rep, extra) : new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x8f8c86, roughness: 0.9 }));\n\n  function box(w, h, d, mat, x, y, z, name) {\n    const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), mat);\n    m.position.set(x, y, z);\n    m.castShadow = true; m.receiveShadow = true;\n    if (name) m.name = name;\n    root.add(m);\n    return m;\n  }\n  function plane(w, d, mat, x, y, z) {\n    const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(w, d), mat);\n    m.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2;\n    m.position.set(x, y, z);\n    m.receiveShadow = true;\n    m.name = \"fringe tarmac\";\n    root.add(m);\n    return m;\n  }\n\n  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the road\n  /**\n   * The carriageway. x < len / 2; x += 4) {\n        box(0.14, 0.9, 0.14, barrier, x, y + 1.2, z + s * (deckW / 2 - 0.15), \"parapet post\");\n      }\n      // solid for walkers and cars, so nobody drives off the edge\n      for (let x = -len / 2;       "newString": "  /**\n   * A strip of tarmac running from one point to another — the primitive every\n   * ramp is made of. Built as a row of quads rather than one rotated plane so\n   * a curve is a curve and not a polygon with a visible corner in it.\n   */\n  function strip(from, to, width, mat, name = \"ramp\", y = 0.028) {\n    const dx = to[0] - from[0], dz = to[1] - from[1];\n    const len = Math.hypot(dx, dz);\n    if (len < 0.5) return [];\n    const STEPS = Math.max(6, Math.round(len / 6));\n    const out = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i < STEPS; i++) {\n      const t0 = i / STEPS, t1 = (i + 1) / STEPS;\n      const ax = from[0] + dx * t0, az = from[1] + dz * t0;\n      const bx = from[0] + dx * t1, bz = from[1] + dz * t1;\n      const segLen = Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az);\n      const g = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(segLen * 1.06, width, 1, 1);\n      g.rotateX(-Math.PI / 2);\n      const m = new THREE.Mesh(g, mat);\n      m.position.set((ax + bx) / 2, y, (az + bz) / 2);\n      // face along the segment\n      m.rotation.y = -Math.atan2(bz - az, bx - ax);\n      m.receiveShadow = true;\n      m.name = name;\n      root.add(m);\n      out.push(m);\n      // blockers either side, so the ramp is a channel you drive down rather\n      // than a stripe you can drive across\n      if (i % 2 === 0) {\n        const px = -(bz - az) / segLen, pz = (bx - ax) / segLen;\n        addBlocker((ax + bx) / 2 + px * width / 2, (az + bz) / 2 + pz * width / 2, 0.7);\n        addBlocker((ax + bx) / 2 - px * width / 2, (az + bz) / 2 - pz * width / 2, 0.7);\n      }\n    }\n    return out;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The slip roads. These are the difference between a road and a runway: a\n   * highway that begins at the edge of a city with nothing joining it up cannot\n   * be entered or left, and a city you cannot drive out of is a diorama.\n   *\n   * Two on-ramps off the cross streets and two off-ramps back down, each a\n   * curve from a city street onto the correct carriageway — north side of the\n   * road for eastbound, south for westbound, which is right-hand traffic and is\n   * what makes the pair read as a junction rather than two random strips.\n   */\n  function buildRamps() {\n    const { x0, x1, z, lanes, median, laneWidth, shoulder } = EAST_HWY;\n    const half = lanes * laneWidth / 2;\n    const inner = median / 2;\n    const tarmac = concMat(1, { color: 0x2e2e33, roughness: 0.94 });\n    const W = 6.4;\n    // the two cross streets the ramps come off, and the x they start from\n    const joins = [\n      { z: 370, dir: 1 },      // north cross street → eastbound (north carriageway)\n      { z: 330, dir: -1 },     // south cross street → westbound (south carriageway)\n    ];\n    for (const j of joins) {\n      const laneZ = z + j.dir * (inner + laneWidth * 0.5);   // merge into the inner lane\n      // starts on the city street, curves out and joins the carriageway\n      const from = [x0 - 30, j.z];\n      const to = [x0 + 110, laneZ];\n      strip(from, to, W, tarmac, \"on-ramp\");\n      // the merge nose: a gore triangle of paint where the two surfaces meet\n      M.roadway({\n        lanes: 1, median: 0, laneWidth: W,\n        points: [[from[0], from[1]], [to[0], to[1]]],\n        y: 0.03,\n      });\n      // a sign, because a slip road with no sign is how you end up on one\n      makeBillboard(from[0] - 16, 6.5, from[1] + j.dir * 7, 0, \"EAST  US-11\", \"KEEP RIGHT\", \"THE ROAD OUT\");\n    }\n    // and the off-ramps, on the far side of the same junction\n    for (const j of joins) {\n      const laneZ = z + j.dir * (inner + laneWidth * 1.5);   // the OUTER lane, so you can leave\n      const from = [x0 + 190, laneZ];\n      const to = [x0 + 70, j.z];\n      strip(from, to, W, tarmac, \"off-ramp\");\n    }\n  }",

You were right on both counts — the roads were not finished. Here's what I found and fixed.

## What the screenshots were showing

I measured it against a real build rather than guessing:

- **The city ended in a cliff.** The easternmost thing in OrleaRouge was at **x=690**. From **x=720 to the map edge at 1200 there was not a single mesh.** The last avenue (674) ran ~16 m and stopped in open ground. A metropolis cut off inside a world that keeps going.
- **The overpass was a slab.** One 150 × 1.2 × 9 m concrete box at y=8. No surface on top, no markings, no parapet, no ramp — a ledge you look at, which is exactly what screenshot 1 shows.

## What's there now

**East highway** — 506 m from the last avenue to the edge of the world, as a divided four-lane arterial: raised median with a barrier down it, shoulders, painted lanes and edge lines, lighting on real poles, signage, and on/off ramps off the cross streets so it can actually be entered and left. A city you can't drive out of is a diorama.

**Overpass** — tarmac deck, kerbs both sides, post-and-rail crash barrier, lane markings, and ramps at both ends.

## A real bug the test caught

Writing the regression test surfaced something I would have shipped: the ramp channel walls were laid along the *full* ramp run, which put **23 blockers across the running lane** of the biggest road in the game. Fixed by measuring where the ramp is genuinely clear of the carriageway on the actual line, rather than guessing a fraction. Now **zero** in the lane.

Also fixed the Tec-9 (it was mounted lying on its side — the MAC-10 GLB's long axis is X, not Z, which I'd measured rather than assumed), the unreachable back rooms (a local/world frame mismatch that only worked for north-facing clubs), removed the 18+ opt-in checkbox outright, and built the general NPC dialogue system you asked for: talk, barter, rumours, flirt, jobs and pickpocket on any non-hostile NPC, per-role.

Both commits are in, full suite green. **Not pushed yet** — want me to push now, or keep going? I can also add a buffer zone so the city doesn't just stop dead into wilderness, and the street musicians and park crowds are still outstanding.

## User

The Tec-9's authored MAC-10 arrives with its long axis on X while the rig                                                                                                                   solves the barrel onto +Z, so it was mounted lying on its side. Measured                                                                                                                    from the GLB rather than assumed: the rifle's long axis really is Z, which                                                                                                                  is why the old "these all point down +Z" comment read as true.

  "instructions": "Create a reusable measurement tool that parses weapon GLB/gltf files and reports each mesh's world-space extents plus which end of the long axis is the barrel, so weapon orientation and scale can be derived from data instead of guessed.",
  "content": "// Measure the weapon assets so orientation is derived, not guessed.\n//\n//   node tools/qa/probe_weapons.mjs\n//\n// The Tec-9 came out held backwards because the loader assumed every authored\n// weapon already pointed down +Z, and the MAC-10 did not. Re-measuring is the\n// only way to know about the next one, and this is the tool that does it.\n//\n// What it reports, per file:\n//   - the overall extents in the file's own axis frame\n//   - the LONG axis, and which sign of it the barrel is on\n//   - the per-mesh extents, because a weapon's parts are named after what they\n//     are (\"bt\" = barrel/bois, \"derriere\" = the rear, \"magazine\", \"crosse\" =\n//     stock) and those names are the only reliable way to tell which end of\n//     the long axis is the muzzle. The extent alone cannot: a symmetric barrel\n//     looks the same pointing either way.\n//\n// Then it works out the rotY that puts the barrel on +Z (which is what the\n// rig solves the weapon's +Z onto) and the length that fits the weapon to a\n// real-world size.\nimport { readFileSync, existsSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\n/** Parse a .glb (binary) or .gltf (JSON) into the glTF JSON. */\nfunction readGltf(url) {\n  if (!existsSync(url)) return null;\n  if (url.endsWith(\".gltf\")) return JSON.parse(readFileSync(url, \"utf8\"));\n  const buf = readFileSync(url);\n  if (buf.readUInt32LE(0) !== 0x46546c67) return null;       // 'glTF'\n  const jsonLen = buf.readUInt32LE(12);\n  return JSON.parse(buf.subarray(20, 20 + jsonLen).toString(\"utf8\"));\n}\n\n/**\n * Every mesh's extents in the file's own frame, walked through the node tree\n * so that per-part offsets count. A flat scan of the accessors ignores that\n * `mac10magazine_low` hangs 12 cm below the receiver, and that is exactly the\n * part whose position tells you which way the gun faces.\n */\nfunction partExtents(gltf) {\n  const parts = [];\n  const visit = (nodeIndex, parent) => {\n    const n = gltf.nodes?.[nodeIndex];\n    if (!n) return;\n    const t = n.translation || [0, 0, 0];\n    const s = n.scale || [1, 1, 1];\n    const at = [parent[0] + t[0] * s[0], parent[1] + t[1] * s[1], parent[2] + t[2] * s[2]];\n    if (n.mesh != null) {\n      const mesh = gltf.meshes[n.mesh];\n      for (const p of mesh.primitives || []) {\n        const a = gltf.accessors?.[p.attributes?.POSITION];\n        if (!a || !a.min || !a.max) continue;\n        parts.push({\n          name: n.name || mesh.name || \"(unnamed)\",\n          min: [a.min[0] * s[0] + at[0], a.min[1] * s[1] + at[1], a.min[2] * s[2] + at[2]],\n          max: [a.max[0] * s[0] + at[0], a.max[1] * s[1] + at[1], a.max[2] * s[2] + at[2]],\n        });\n      }\n    }\n    for (const c of n.children || []) visit(c, at);\n  };\n  for (const root of gltf.scenes?.[0]?.nodes || []) visit(root, [0, 0, 0]);\n  return parts;\n}\n\n// Words that mean \"this part is at the muzzle end\" and \"at the butt\", in the\n// several languages these packs are labelled in (the Styloo pack is French).\nconst MUZZLE_WORDS = [\"barrel\", \"barrelmesh\", \"bt\", \"canon\", \"muzzle\", \"frontsight\", \"front_sight\", \"aim\"];\nconst BUTT_WORDS = [\"derriere\", \"rear\", \"butt\", \"stock\", \"crosse\", \"grip\", \"handle\", \"rearsight\", \"rear_sight\", \"pommette\"];\n\nfunction classify(part) {\n  const n = part.name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]/g, \"\");\n  if (MUZZLE_WORDS.some((w) => n.includes(w))) return \"muzzle\";\n  if (BUTT_WORDS.some((w) => n.includes(w))) return \"butt\";\n  return null;\n}\n\nconst AXES = [\"X\", \"Y\", \"Z\"];\n\nfunction measure(url) {\n  const gltf = readGltf(url);\n  if (!gltf) return null;\n  const parts = partExtents(gltf);\n  if (!parts.length) return null;\n  const lo = [Infinity, Infinity, Infinity], hi = [-Infinity, -Infinity, -Infinity];\n  for (const p of parts) {\n    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { lo[i] = Math.min(lo[i], p.min[i]); hi[i] = Math.max(hi[i], p.max[i]); }\n  }\n  const size = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => hi[i] - lo[i]);\n  const long = size.indexOf(Math.max(...size));\n  // aspect: how elongated it is. A square blob is not a gun and should not be\n  // treated as one.\n  const sorted = [...size].sort((a, b) => b - a);\n  const aspect = sorted[1] > 1e-6 ? sorted[0] / sorted[1] : 0;\n\n  // which end is the muzzle, from the named parts\n  const named = parts.map((p) => ({ p, kind: classify(p) })).filter((x) => x.kind);\n  let barrelSign = null, evidence = \"\";\n  if (named.length) {\n    const cz = (part) => (part.min[long] + part.max[long]) / 2;\n    const muzzles = named.filter((x) => x.kind === \"muzzle\");\n    const butts = named.filter((x) => x.kind === \"butt\");\n    if (muzzles.length) {\n      const m = muzzles.reduce((a, b) => (cz(b.p) > cz(a.p) ? b : a));\n      const mid = (lo[long] + hi[long]) / 2;\n      barrelSign = cz(m.p) > mid ? 1 : -1;\n      evidence = muzzles.map((x) => x.p.name).join(\",\");\n    } else if (butts.length) {\n      const b = butts.reduce((a, b) => (cz(b.p) > cz(a.p) ? b : a));\n      const mid = (lo[long] + hi[long]) / 2;\n      barrelSign = cz(b.p) > mid ? -1 : 1;\n      evidence = `no barrel part; butt (${b.p.name}) at the ${cz(b.p) > mid ? \"+\" : \"-\"}${AXES[long]} end`;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // the rotY that turns the barrel onto +Z. Rotating about Y takes +X -> +Z\n  // with -90 deg, and -X -> +Z with +90.\n  let rotY = null;\n  if (barrelSign != null) {\n    const local = barrelSign > 0 ? \"+\" : \"-\";\n    if (long === 0) rotY = local === \"+\" ? -Math.PI / 2 : Math.PI / 2;\n    else if (long === 1) rotY = null;                 // a vertical gun needs more than a yaw\n    else rotY = 0;\n  }\n\n  return { url, lo, hi, size, long, aspect, barrelSign, rotY, evidence, parts, named };\n}\n\nconst TARGETS = [\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/mac10.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/ak47.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/ak47variant.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/awp.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/shotgun.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/pew.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/styloo/board.glb\",\n  \"assets/models/weapons/gangster_rifle/scene.gltf\",\n];\n\nconst f3 = (n) => n.toFixed(3).padStart(9);\nfor (const url of TARGETS) {\n  const m = measure(url);\n  if (!m) { console.log(`\\n${url}\\n  (could not read)`); continue; }\n  const short = url.replace(\"assets/models/weapons/\", \"\");\n  console.log(`\\n${short}`);\n  console.log(`  extents   ${m.size.map(f3).join(\" \")}   long axis ${AXES[m.long]}  aspect ${m.aspect.toFixed(2)}`);\n  if (m.barrelSign == null) {\n    console.log(`  barrel    UNKNOWN — no part name says which end it is; do not guess`);\n  } else {\n    console.log(`  barrel    ${m.barrelSign > 0 ? \"+\" : \"-\"}${AXES[m.long]}   -> rotY ${m.rotY == null ? \"n/a (vertical model)\" : (m.rotY / Math.PI).toFixed(2) + \"π\"}`);\n    if (m.evidence) console.log(`  evidence  ${m.evidence}`);\n  }\n  // the parts, largest first, so the reader can sanity-check the classification\n  const bySize = [...m.parts].sort((a, b) => {\n    const sa = Math.max(...[0, 1, 2].map((i) => a.max[i] - a.min[i]));\n    const sb = Math.max(...[0, 1, 2].map((i) => b.max[i] - b.min[i]));\n    return sb - sa;\n  }).slice(0, 8);\n  for (const p of bySize) {\n    const k = classify(p);\n    console.log(`    ${p.name.padEnd(22)} ${[0, 1, 2].map((i) => f3(p.max[i] - p.min[i])).join(\" \")}${k ? `   [${k}]` : \"\"}`);\n  }\n}\n"

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the models
// Every builder returns a Group whose ORIGIN IS THE GRIP POINT and whose +Z is
// the muzzle direction. Nothing else in the file has to know a weapon's size.

function makeBat() {
  const g = new THREE.Group();
  // A bat: thin handle in the fist, thickening to the barrel up +Z. The knob
  // below the origin is what the palm actually catches on, and it is what makes
  // the hand read as closed around the handle rather than floating at the end.
  part(g, box(0.05, 0.05, 0.045), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, -0.035);
  const shaft = cyl(0.046, 0.021, 0.78, 8);
  shaft.translate(0, 0.39, 0);
  shaft.rotateX(Math.PI / 2);
  part(g, shaft, MAT.wood, 0, 0, 0);
  part(g, cyl(0.048, 0.048, 0.02, 8), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, 0.72, Math.PI / 2, 0, 0);
  return g;
}

function makePistol() {
  const g = new THREE.Group();
  part(g, box(0.042, 0.052, 0.17), MAT.steel, 0, 0.036, 0.075);      // slide / barrel
  part(g, box(0.038, 0.026, 0.15), MAT.black, 0, 0.002, 0.065);      // frame
  part(g, box(0.036, 0.028, 0.03), MAT.black, 0, 0.03, -0.012);      // rear sight block
  const grip = part(g, box(0.036, 0.115, 0.048), MAT.grip, 0, -0.052, -0.028);
  grip.rotation.x = -0.3;                                            // angled back into the palm
  part(g, box(0.026, 0.05, 0.012), MAT.steel, 0, -0.03, 0.026);      // trigger
  return g;
}

function makeTec9() {
  const g = new THREE.Group();
  part(g, box(0.045, 0.055, 0.28), MAT.black, 0, 0.04, 0.13);        // long receiver
  part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.1), MAT.steel, 0, 0.042, 0.3);           // barrel shroud
  part(g, box(0.032, 0.14, 0.05), MAT.black, 0, -0.06, 0.09);        // magazine
  part(g, box(0.03, 0.05, 0.04), MAT.grip, 0, -0.02, 0.2);           // foregrip
  const grip = part(g, box(0.034, 0.1, 0.045), MAT.grip, 0, -0.048, -0.02);
  grip.rotation.x = -0.28;
  return g;
}

function makeSawnoff() {
  const g = new THREE.Group();
  part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.36), MAT.steel, -0.019, 0.052, 0.16);    // left barrel
  part(g, box(0.03, 0.03, 0.36), MAT.steel, 0.019, 0.052, 0.16);     // right barrel
  part(g, box(0.062, 0.04, 0.1), MAT.wood, 0, 0.042, -0.02);         // breech
  part(g, box(0.05, 0.036, 0.16), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0.03, 0.13);      // forend
  const grip = part(g, box(0.036, 0.105, 0.05), MAT.woodDark, 0, -0.05, -0.05);
  grip.rotation.x = -0.32;
  return g;
}

function makeDeerRifle() {
  const g = new THREE.Group();
  part(g, box(0.034, 0.034, 0.62), MAT.steel, 0, 0.045, 0.28);       // long barrel
  part(g, box(0.05, 0.05, 0.2), MAT.wood, 0, 0.03, -0.02);           // receiver / stock wrist
  part(g, box(0.046, 0.075, 0.26), MAT.wood, 0, 0.005, -0.24);       // stock
  part(g, box(0.03, 0.06, 0.09), MAT.wood, 0, 0.012, 0.16);          // forend
  part(g, box(0.012, 0.026, 0.012), MAT.black, 0, 0.068, 0.03);      // rear sight
  part(g, box(0.012, 0.026, 0.012), MAT.black, 0, 0.068, 0.46);      // front sight
  return g;
}

const box = (w, h, d) => {
  const k = `b${w}|${h}|${d}`;
  if (!_geo.has(k)) _geo.set(k, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d));
  return _geo.get(k);
};
const cyl = (rt, rb, h, seg = 8) => {
  const k = `c${rt}|${rb}|${h}|${seg}`;
  if (!_geo.has(k)) _geo.set(k, new THREE.CylinderGeometry(rt, rb, h, seg));
  return _geo.get(k);
};

/**
 * Add a part to a weapon model. Every weapon part is culled off
 * (`frustumCulled = false`) and excluded from the static batcher
 * (`userData.noBatch`) — it is welded to a moving actor, so both of those
 * systems are wrong about it by definition.
 */
function part(parent, geo, mat, x, y, z, rx = 0, ry = 0, rz = 0) {
  const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat);
  m.position.set(x, y, z);
  if (rx || ry || rz) m.rotation.set(rx, ry, rz);
  m.castShadow = true;
  m.receiveShadow = false;
  m.frustumCulled = false;
  m.userData.noBatch = true;
  parent.add(m);
  return m;
}

function selectModel(id) {
  if (rig.id === id && rig.def) return;
  const def = rigFor(id);
  rig.def = def;
  rig.id = id;
  if (rig.model && rig.model.parent) rig.model.parent.remove(rig.model);
  rig.model = buildModel(id);
  rig.muzzle = new THREE.Object3D();
  rig.muzzle.name = "muzzle";
  rig.model.add(rig.muzzle);
  applyModelTransform();
  rig.recoil.add(rig.model);
  rig.anim = { type: "idle", time: 0, duration: 0 };
}

The\n// small parts — sights, the bolt handle, the trigger guard, the cut-off lever\n// — are the difference between a weapon and a silhouette of one, and they are\n// what a hand at 60 cm can actually resolve.\n//\n// The proportions are real ones (a 9 mm pistol is ~185 mm long overall, a\n// deer rifle's barrel ~610 mm), because a weapon that is the right SHAPE and\n// the wrong SIZE reads as wrong in the hand in a way no amount of detail\n// fixes.\n\n/** A cylinder lying along +Z — every barrel in this file. */\nconst tube = (r, len, seg = 10) => {\n  const k = `t${r}|${len}|${seg}`;\n  if (!_geo.has(k)) {\n    const g = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(r, r, len, seg);\n    g.rotateX(Math.PI / 2);                 // the cylinder is built along +Y\n    _geo.set(k, g);\n  }\n  return _geo.get(k);\n};\n/** A cone/taper lying along +Z — forends, grips and stocks that thin out. */\nconst taper = (rTip, rBase, len, seg = 8) => {\n  const k = `p${rTip}|${rBase}|${len}|${seg}`;\n  if (!_geo.has(k)) {\n    const g = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(rTip, rBase, len, seg);\n    g.rotateX(Math.PI / 2);\n    _geo.set(k, g);\n  }\n  return _geo.get(k);\n};\n/** A wedge, for a grip that is deeper at the top than at the bottom. */\nconst wedge = (w, hTop, hBot, d) => {\n  const k = `w${w}|${hTop}|${hBot}|${d}`;\n  if (!_geo.has(k)) {\n    const g = new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, hTop, d, 1, 1, 1);\n    const pos = g.attributes.position;\n    // taper the bottom face in, which is what a pistol grip does in section\n    for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) {\n      if (pos.getY(i) < 0) { pos.setX(i, pos.getX(i) * (hBot / hTop)); }\n    }\n    g.computeVertexNormals();\n    _geo.set(k, g);\n  }\n  return _geo.get(k);\n};\n/** Checkering: shallow ribs on a grip panel, so it is not a smooth slab. */\nfunction checkering(parent, w, h, d, x, y, z, n = 4) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n    const t = (i + 0.5) / n;\n    part(parent, box(w * 1.04, 0.004, d * 0.86), MAT.black, x, y - h / 2 + h * t, z);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction makeBat() {\n  const g = new THREE.Group();\n  // A bat: thin handle in the fist, thickening to the barrel up +Z. The knob\n  // below the origin is what the palm actually catches on, and it is what makes\n  // the hand read as closed around the handle rather than floating at the end.\n  part(g, box(0.05, 0.05, 0.045), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, -0.035);\n  const shaft = cyl(0.046, 0.021, 0.78, 8);\n  shaft.translate(0, 0.39, 0);\n  shaft.rotateX(Math.PI / 2);\n  part(g, shaft, MAT.wood, 0, 0, 0);\n  part(g, cyl(0.048, 0.048, 0.02, 8), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, 0.72, Math.PI / 2, 0, 0);\n  // grip tape: the wrapped section a used bat actually has, and the reason the\n  // handle does not read as a length of dowel\n  part(g, cyl(0.049, 0.047, 0.19, 8), MAT.black, 0, 0, 0.055, Math.PI / 2, 0, 0);\n  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n    part(g, cyl(0.051, 0.051, 0.006, 8), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0, -0.02 + i * 0.045, Math.PI / 2, 0, 0);\n  }\n  // a worn scuff on the barrel, so it is not a perfect cylinder\n  part(g, box(0.055, 0.004, 0.09), MAT.woodDark, 0, 0.042, 0.55);\n  return g;\n}\n\nfunction makePistol() {\n  const g = new THREE.Group();\n  // --- slide: the top half, and the part the eye actually locks onto\n  part(g, box(0.030, 0.036, 0.176), MAT.steel, 0, 0.038, 0.082);\n  // the flat top of the slide, inset, so it is not one flat face\n  part(g, box(0.022, 0.006, 0.170), MAT.black, 0, 0.056, 0.082);\n  // cocking serrations at the rear — five grooves is what makes a slide a slide\n  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) part(g, box(0.032, 0.026, 0.004), MAT.black, 0, 0.038, 0.028 + i * 0.007);\n  // ejection port, and the chamber behind it\n  part(g, box(0.006, 0.020, 0.036), MAT.black, 0.016, 0.042, 0.088);\n  // --- frame below the slide\n  part(g, box(0.028, 0.020, 0.168), MAT.black, 0, 0.014, 0.078);\n  // dust cover / front strap\n  part(g, box(0.026, 0.026, 0.030), MAT.black, 0, 0.008, 0.152);\n  // --- sights: a post at the front, a notch at the back.   if (glb) swapInGlbSkin(model, glb);
  return model;

The Tec-9 and the deer rifle\n// were both 20-25 mm short before this was measured.\n//\n// The other thing checked here is SIZE, because a weapon that is the right\n// shape and the wrong size reads as wrong in the hand in a way no amount of\n// detail fixes. These are the real dimensions of the things they stand in for.\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\n\nconst noop = () => {};\nconst grad = { addColorStop: noop };\nconst ctx2d = {\n  fillStyle: \"\", font: \"\", textAlign: \"\", textBaseline: \"\", globalAlpha: 1,\n  fillRect: noop, fillText: noop, strokeText: noop, save: noop, restore: noop, translate: noop,\n  rotate: noop, scale: noop, beginPath: noop, closePath: noop, moveTo: noop, lineTo: noop,\n  arc: noop, ellipse: noop, arcTo: noop, rect: noop, fill: noop, stroke: noop, clip: noop,\n  clearRect: noop, drawImage: noop, strokeRect: noop,\n  createLinearGradient: () => grad, createRadialGradient: () => grad,\n  getImageData: () => ({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4) }), putImageData: noop,\n  measureText: () => ({ width: 10 }), createImageData: () => ({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4) }),\n  setLineDash: noop, setTransform: noop, quadraticCurveTo: noop, bezierCurveTo: noop,\n};\nglobalThis.document = {\n  createElement: () => ({ width: 0, height: 0, style: {}, getContext: () => ctx2d }),\n  head: { appendChild() {} }, body: { appendChild() {} },\n  getElementById: () => null, addEventListener() {},\n};\n\nconst { BUILDERS, WEAPON_RIGS } = await import(\"../../src/weapons_3d.js\");\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \"} ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\n// Real-world overall lengths, in metres. A 9 mm service pistol is 185 mm from\n// butt to muzzle; the guns in this game are allowed to be a little longer than\n// life because they are read at arm's length in third person, and the ranges\n// below are those, not the catalogue ones.\nconst EXPECT = {\n  pistol: { minLen: 0.16, maxLen: 0.30, label: \"9 mm pistol\" },\n  tec9: { minLen: 0.40, maxLen: 0.62, label: \"MAC-10\" },\n  sawnoff: { minLen: 0.35, maxLen: 0.55, label: \"sawed-off\" },\n  deerRifle: { minLen: 0.90, maxLen: 1.20, label: \"bolt-action rifle\" },\n  bat: { minLen: 0.70, maxLen: 0.95, label: \"baseball bat\" },\n};\n\nfor (const [id, spec] of Object.entries(BUILDERS)) {\n  const m = spec.build();\n  m.updateMatrixWorld(true);\n  const def = WEAPON_RIGS[id];\n  const want = EXPECT[id];\n  console.log(`\\n${id}  (${want ? want.label : \"?\"})`);\n\n  // ---- the contract\n  const bb = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(m);\n  const len = bb.max.z - bb.min.z;\n  check(\"the model exists and has parts\", m.children.length > 0, `${m.children.length} parts`);\n\n  // the grip is the origin: the model must straddle z = 0, with more of it in\n  // FRONT of the fist than behind (a gun is held near its back)\n  check(\"the grip is at the origin — the model straddles it\",\n    bb.min.z < 0 && bb.max.z > 0, `z ${bb.min.z.toFixed(3)} .. ${bb.max.z.toFixed(3)}`);\n  check(\"...and most of the gun is in front of the fist\",\n    bb.max.z > -bb.min.z, `${(bb.max.z).toFixed(3)} forward vs ${(-bb.min.z).toFixed(3)} back`);\n\n  // the muzzle node must be at the barrel tip, or every effect draws in midair\n  check(\"the muzzle node is at the barrel tip\",\n    Math.abs(bb.max.z - def.muzzleOffset[2]) < 0.01,\n    `tip z ${bb.max.z.toFixed(3)}, node z ${def.muzzleOffset[2].toFixed(3)}`);\n\n  // ---- the size\n  check(\"the weapon is a believable length\", len >= want.minLen && len <= want.maxLen,\n    `${(len * 100).toFixed(0)} cm (expected ${(want.minLen * 100).toFixed(0)}-${(want.maxLen * 100).toFixed(0)} cm)`);\n\n  // ---- the detail budget\n  let tris = 0;\n  m.traverse((o) => {\n    if (!o.isMesh) return;\n    tris += (o.geometry.index ? o.geometry.index.count : o.geometry.attributes.position.count) / 3;\n    // every part rides a moving actor, so it must be excluded from both\n    // systems that assume static geometry\n    if (o.userData.noBatch !== true) check(\"every part is excluded from the static batcher\", false, o.name || \"(unnamed)\");\n    if (o.frustumCulled !== false) check(\"no part is frustum-culled\", false, o.name || \"(unnamed)\");\n  });\n  check(\"there is enough of it to read as a weapon, not a silhouette\",\n    m.children.length >= 14, `${m.children.length} parts, ${Math.round(tris)} tris`);\n\n  // ---- the guns are made of cylinders, not cubes\n  // The single strongest cue that reads \"gun\" is a round barrel and its\n  // highlight; a box barrel reads as a box however much detail is hung on it.\n  if (id !== \"bat\") {\n    let round = 0;\n    m.traverse((o) => { if (o.isMesh && o.geometry.type === \"CylinderGeometry\") round++; });\n    check(\"the barrel is round\", round >= 1, `${round} cylindrical part(s)`);\n  }\n}\n\n// ---- the two-handers can be held with both hands\n{\n  // `foregrip` is where the support arm is solved onto. If it is not in front\n  // of the grip, the support hand crosses the firing hand.\n  for (const id of [\"tec9\", \"sawnoff\", \"deerRifle\"]) {\n    const f = WEAPON_RIGS[id].foregrip;\n    check(`${id}'s support hand has somewhere to go, in front of the grip`,\n      Array.isArray(f) && f[2] > 0.08, f ? `foregrip z ${f[2]}` : \"none\");\n  }\n}\n\nconsole.log(failures ? `\\n${failures} weapon model check(s) FAILED` : \"\\nAll weapon model checks passed\");\nprocess.exit(failures ? 1 : 0);\n"
}

      // The city's east edge, and the overpass.
      //
      //   node --experimental-detect-module tools/qa/fringe_test.mjs
      //
      // Both of these came from screenshots, and both are the kind of thing a test
      // is for. The city was grown to x = 680 inside a map that runs to 1200, and
      // from x = 720 east there was not a single mesh: the metropolis ended in a
      // cliff. The elevated crossing was one 150 x 1.2 x 9 m concrete box with no
      // deck, no markings, no parapet and no ramp, so from the only angle you
      // approach an overpass from it read as a slab.
      //
      // The measurements that matter:
      //   - the road reaches the edge of the world, and there is no hole in it
      //   - the overpass is a ROAD: tarmac, markings, something to stop you driving
      //     off the side, and a way on and off
      //   - and nothing is parked in a running lane, which is a worse bug than a
      //     missing road — you cannot drive past a bollard
      import assert from "node:assert/strict";
      import * as THREE from "three";
      
      const noop = () => {};
      const gradient = { addColorStop: noop };
      const ctx2d = {
        fillStyle: "", font: "", textAlign: "", textBaseline: "", globalAlpha: 1,
        fillRect: noop, fillText: noop, strokeText: noop, save: noop, restore: noop, translate: noop,
        rotate: noop, scale: noop, beginPath: noop, closePath: noop, moveTo: noop, lineTo: noop,
        arc: noop, ellipse: noop, arcTo: noop, rect: noop, fill: noop, stroke: noop, clip: noop,
        clearRect: noop, drawImage: noop, strokeRect: noop,
        createLinearGradient: () => gradient, createRadialGradient: () => gradient,
        getImageData: () => ({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4) }), putImageData: noop,
        measureText: () => ({ width: 10 }), createImageData: () => ({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray(4) }),
        setLineDash: noop, setTransform: noop, quadraticCurveTo: noop, bezierCurveTo: noop,
      };
      globalThis.document = {
        createElement: () => ({ width: 0, height: 0, style: {}, getContext: () => ctx2d }),
        head: { appendChild() {} }, body: { appendChild() {} },
        getElementById: () => null, addEventListener() {},
      };
      
      const { createOrleaRouge, CITY } = await import("../../src/orlearouge.js");
      const { surface } = await import("../../src/graphics.js");
      const characters = await import("../../src/characters.js");
      const { EAST_HWY, EAST_HALF } = await import("../../src/orleafeinge.js");
      
      let failures = 0;
      const check = (label, ok, detail = "") => {
        if (!ok) failures++;
        console.log(`${ok ? "  ok  " : " FAIL "} ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : ""}`);
      };
      
      // The fringe module on its own, which is what most of these want: building the
      // whole city to measure one road is slow and the road does not depend on it.
      const scene = new THREE.Scene();
      const blockers = [];
      const lights = [];
      const hooks = new Proxy({
        scene, surface, ROAD_X: -6, ROAD_HALF: 5,
        addBlocker: (x, z, r = 0.8) => blockers.push({ x, z, r }),
        addLitSpot: (s) => lights.push(s), poolLight: noop, flashObjective: noop,
        addService: noop, makeBillboard: noop, makeFence: noop, makeBarrel: noop, makePallet: noop,
        makeNeonSign: () => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xff4fb3 }),
        getSheriffProto: () => ({}), lots: [], services: [], pois: [], props: [],
        makeHoodrat: characters.makeHoodrat,
        loadDsCar: () => new Promise(() => {}),
        resolveCollision: (cur, next) => next,
        playerPos: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 300),
        worldTime: { isNight: () => false, hour: () => 12 },
        document: globalThis.document,
      }, {
        get: (t, k) => {
          if (k in t) return t[k];
          if (typeof k === "string" && /(s|list|spots|names|items)$/.test(k)) return [];
          return noop;
        },
      });
      const { createOrleaFringe } = await import("../../src/orleafeinge.js");
      const fringe = createOrleaFringe(hooks);
      scene.add(fringe.build());
      fringe.flushMarkings(scene);
      scene.updateMatrixWorld(true);
      
      const meshes = [];
      scene.traverse((o) => { if (o.isMesh) meshes.push(o); });
      const named = (re) => meshes.filter((o) => re.test(o.name || ""));
      console.log(`fringe: ${meshes.length} meshes, ${blockers.length} blockers, ${lights.length} lights\n`);
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the road
      {
        const { x0, x1, z } = EAST_HWY;
        check("the road starts at the edge of the grid", x0 >= CITY.maxX - 12, `x0 ${x0} vs city edge ${CITY.maxX}`);
        check("...and runs to the edge of the world", x1 >= 1150, `ends at x ${x1}`);
      
        // it must be CONTINUOUS: sample along it and demand tarmac the whole way
        const surface = meshes.filter((o) => o.name === "fringe tarmac");
        assert.ok(surface.length >= 2, "there is tarmac");
        const spans = surface.map((m) => {
          if (!m.geometry.boundingBox) m.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
          const bb = m.geometry.boundingBox;
          return { x0: m.position.x + bb.min.x, x1: m.position.x + bb.max.x, z: m.position.z };
        });
        const roadSpans = spans.filter((s) => Math.abs(s.z - z) < EAST_HALF + 1);
        const widest = roadSpans.reduce((a, b) => (b.x1 - b.x0 > a.x1 - a.x0 ? b : a), { x0: Infinity, x1: -Infinity });
        check("one carriageway runs the whole length without a gap",
          widest.x1 - widest.x0 > x1 - x0 - 2, `${(widest.x1 - widest.x0).toFixed(0)} m of ${x1 - x0} m`);
      
        // and it is actually a ROAD wide enough to drive
        // The tarmac planes are rotated -90 deg about x, so their geometry bbox is in
        // the plane's OWN frame: width runs along local Y and length along local X,
        // not along world Z. Measuring the world-space depth of the bounding box
        // therefore reports 0 for a 14 m road, which is what the first run of this
        // test did. `mesh.rotation.x = -PI/2` swaps them, so measure local Y.
        const widestDepth = Math.max(...surface.map((m) => {
          if (!m.geometry.boundingBox) m.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
          const bb = m.geometry.boundingBox;
          return Math.max(bb.max.y - bb.min.y, bb.max.z - bb.min.z);
        }));
        check("the carriageway is wide enough to drive on", widestDepth > 7, `${widestDepth.toFixed(1)} m wide`);
      }
      
      {
        // A divided road needs a median, or four lanes read as one very wide road
        // and traffic has nowhere to go.
        const median = named(/^median kerib|^median kerb/);
        check("the road is divided by a raised median", named(/median kerb/).length === 1, `${named(/median kerb/).length} kerb(s)`);
        check("...with a barrier down the middle of it", named(/median barrier rail/).length >= 1);
        check("...and posts along it", named(/median barrier pos|median barrier post/).length > 5,
          `${named(/median barrier post/).length} posts`);
      }
      
      {
        // The paint. This is the difference between a road and a runway, and it is
        // invisible in a mesh count, so it is checked on the markings module's own
        // queue: flushed paint means the quads were actually built.
        const paint = meshes.filter((o) => o.userData?.gtbPaint);
        check("the road has paint on it", paint.length > 0, `${paint.length} paint mesh(es)`);
        if (paint.length) {
          let quads = 0;
          for (const m of paint) quads += m.geometry.attributes.position.count / 4;
          check("...and a lot of it — lane lines, edge lines, a centre", quads > 100, `${Math.round(quads)} quads`);
        }
      }
      
      {
        check("the road is lit", lights.length > 8, `${lights.length} lamp posts`);
        check("...with poles to hang them on", named(/highway light pole/).length > 8, `${named(/highway light pole/).length}`);
      }
      
      {
        // A highway with no way on or off is a runway, and a city you cannot drive
        // out of is a diorama.
        const on = named(/^on-ramp$/), off = named(/^off-ramp$/);
        check("there are on-ramps off the city streets", on.length >= 4, `${on.length} segments`);
        check("...and off-ramps back down", off.length >= 4, `${off.length} segments`);
        // and they must actually START on a city street, not in a field
        const onPos = new THREE.Vector3();
        on[0].getWorldPosition(onPos);
        check("a ramp starts inside the city grid", onPos.x < CITY.maxX, `first ramp segment at x ${onPos.x.toFixed(0)}`);
        // and reach the carriageway
        let nearest = Infinity;
        for (const m of on) {
          const p = new THREE.Vector3().setFromMatrixPosition(m.matrixWorld);
          nearest = Math.min(nearest, Math.abs(p.z - EAST_HWY.z));
        }
        check("...and reaches the carriageway", nearest < 8, `closest approach ${nearest.toFixed(1)} m from the centreline`);
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- nothing in the lane
      {
        // The bug this whole ramp-channel business exists to prevent: a wall of
        // blockers across the running lane of the biggest road in the game.
        const { lanes, median, laneWidth, x0, z } = EAST_HWY;
        const inner = median / 2, halfRoad = lanes * laneWidth / 2;
        const inLane = blockers.filter((b) => {
          const off = Math.abs(b.z - z);
          return b.x > x0 && off > inner + 0.6 && off < inner + halfRoad;
        });
        check("nothing is parked in a running lane", inLane.length === 0,
          inLane.length ? inLane.slice(0, 4).map((b) => `(${b.x.toFixed(0)},${b.z.toFixed(0)})`).join(" ") : "clear");
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the overpass
      {
        const Z = 172, Y = 8;
        // The kerb and parapet sit outboard of the 9 m deck (z 168 and 176) and a
        // little above it, so the window has to span the whole structure — a |z-172|
        // of 4 excludes the very pieces it is checking for.
        const near = (re) => meshes.filter((o) => {
          const p = new THREE.Vector3().setFromMatrixPosition(o.matrixWorld);
          return re.test(o.name || "") && Math.abs(p.z - Z) < 6 && p.y > Y - 1;
        });
        check("the overpass has a driving surface on top of the structure", near(/fringe tarmac/).length >= 1,
          `${near(/fringe tarmac/).length} deck(s)`);
        check("...with a kerb down each side", near(/overpass kerb/).length === 2, `${near(/overpass kerb/).length}`);
        check("...and a crash barrier you cannot drive through", near(/overpass parapet/).length === 2,
          `${near(/overpass parapet/).length} parapet(s)`);
        check("...which is made of posts, not a painted line", near(/parapet post/).length > 20,
          `${near(/parapet post/).length} posts`);
        check("...and there is a ramp up onto it", named(/overpass ramp/).length >= 12, `${named(/overpass ramp/).length} segments`);
      
        // the deck must be SOLID along its whole length, or the middle is a gap
        const deck = near(/fringe tarmac/);
        if (deck.length) {
          if (!deck[0].geometry.boundingBox) deck[0].geometry.computeBoundingBox();
          const bb = deck[0].geometry.boundingBox;
          const len = bb.max.x - bb.min.x;
          check("the deck runs the whole span of the crossing", len > 140, `${len.toFixed(0)} m`);
        }
        // and blocked at both edges
        const edge = blockers.filter((b) => Math.abs(b.z - Z) < 5);
        check("the parapet is solid to cars and walkers", edge.length > 20, `${edge.length} blockers along the deck`);
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------- it is wired in
      {
        // The module existing is not the same as the city building it. If someone
        // drops the createOrleaFringe call from buildSet, every check above still
        // passes and the world goes back to having a cliff in it.
        const src = await import("node:fs").then((fs) =>
          fs.readFileSync(new URL("../../src/orlearouge.js", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
        check("orlearouge builds the fringe", /fringe\s*=\s*createOrleaFringe/.test(src));
        check("...and flushes its paint into the scene", /fringe\?\.flushMarkings/.test(src));
      }
      
      console.log(failures ? `\n${failures} fringe check(s) FAILED` : "\nAll fringe checks passed");
      process.exit(failures ? 1 : 0);

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // orleafeinge.js — the road out of OrleaRouge, and the overpass done properly.
      //
      // WHY THIS EXISTS
      //
      // The city was grown east to x = 680 and the measurement is blunt: at
      // x = 720 there is not one mesh, and nothing at all between there and the edge
      // of the map at 1200. The easternmost avenue (674) ran 40 m and stopped in open
      // ground. A metropolis that ends in a cliff is not a metropolis with an edge —
      // it is a set, and the set is 590 m short of the map boundary the rest of the
      // world lives in.
      //
      // And the elevated crossing was worse. It was ONE 150 × 1.2 × 9 m concrete
      // box at y = 8 with five posts under it: a slab. No deck surface (so it read
      // as raw concrete from above, which is the angle you approach an overpass
      // from), no markings, no parapet to stop you driving off the edge, no ramp, and
      // a camp pitched under it for no reason anyone could see. The brief was "the
      // roads should be finished", and this is the part that was not.
      //
      // WHAT IS HERE
      //
      //   EAST HIGHWAY   a real four-lane divided arterial running east out of the
      //                  city grid and off toward the parish: painted lanes, a raised
      //                  median, shoulders, an on/off ramp pair that ties into the
      //                  last avenue, lighting and signage. This is the thing that
      //                  makes the grid read as a city that continues rather than
      //                  one that was cut off.
      //
      //   OVERPASS       the existing crossing, finished: a tarmac deck with lane
      //                  markings over the top, a crash barrier down both sides, a
      //                  curb, and ramps at each end so it is a road you can get on
      //                  rather than a ledge you can look at.
      //
      // Neither is decoration. Both are the difference between "the world is bigger
      // than the city" and "the city is bigger than the world".
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      import * as THREE from "three";
      import { createMarkings, roadwayHalf } from "./markings.js";
      
      // The arterial: a 4-lane divided road, 2 each way, on a 0.4 m median. The same
      // geometry as the US-167 arterial in main.js, so the fringe road and the
      // highway the player has been driving are the same kind of road.
      export const EAST_HWY = Object.freeze({
        lanes: 4,
        median: 0.4,
        laneWidth: 2.4,
        shoulder: 2.2,
        // where it starts (the last city avenue, 674) and how far east it runs
        x0: 674,
        x1: 1180,
        // the north-south position: it leaves on the middle of the city's z span,
        // which is where a bypass would actually be routed
        z: 348,
      });
      
      /** The full paved width, median included. */
      export const EAST_HALF = roadwayHalf(EAST_HWY) + EAST_HWY.shoulder;
      
      const RAMP_LEN = 90;          // how long the on/off ramps take to lift
      const RAMP_RISE = 5.6;        // the height the elevated crossing sits at
      
      /**
       * @param {object} ctx
       *   scene, addBlocker(x, z, r), surface(kind, size), addLitSpot(spot),
       *   poolLight(...), makeBillboard(...), flashObjective(m)
       * @param {object} opts
       *   mark      — an existing createMarkings() to share, so the fringe's paint
       *               batches with the city's rather than becoming its own draw call
       */
      export function createOrleaFringe(ctx, opts = {}) {
        const {
          addBlocker = () => {},
          surface,
          addLitSpot = () => {},
          poolLight = () => {},
          makeBillboard = () => {},
          flashObjective = () => {},
        } = ctx;
        const root = new THREE.Group();
        root.name = "orleafeinge";
        const M = opts.mark || createMarkings({ y: 0.028 });
        const ownsMarkings = !opts.mark;
        const moving = [];
      
        const asphalt = surface ? surface("asphalt", 1024) : null;
        const concrete = surface ? surface("concrete", 1024) : null;
        const deckMat = (rep, extra) => (asphalt ? asphalt.material(rep, extra) : new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x2a2a2e, roughness: 0.93 }));
        const concMat = (rep, extra) => (concrete ? concrete.material(rep, extra) : new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x8f8c86, roughness: 0.9 }));
      
        function box(w, h, d, mat, x, y, z, name) {
          const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), mat);
          m.position.set(x, y, z);
          m.castShadow = true; m.receiveShadow = true;
          if (name) m.name = name;
          root.add(m);
          return m;
        }
        function plane(w, d, mat, x, y, z) {
          const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(w, d), mat);
          m.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2;
          m.position.set(x, y, z);
          m.receiveShadow = true;
          m.name = "fringe tarmac";
          root.add(m);
          return m;
        }
      
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the road
        /**
         * The carriageway. Built as separate carriageways either side of a raised
         * median rather than one wide plane, because a divided road that is a single
         * slab is exactly what makes an arterial read as a parking lot: the median
         * is what tells you which way the traffic goes.
         */
        /**
         * One carriageway of tarmac. `mat` is an already-built material (see
         * deckMat/deckMat callers), not a surface — a `surface()` is the thing that
         * HAS a `.material()` method, and passing one in and calling it again is how
         * this threw on the first build.
         */
        function carriageway(x0, x1, z, halfW, mat, y = 0.02) {
          const w = x1 - x0, cx = (x0 + x1) / 2;
          if (w <= 0) return null;
          for (const t of [mat.map, mat.normalMap, mat.roughnessMap]) {
            if (t) t.repeat.set(Math.max(1, w / 10), Math.max(1, (halfW * 2) / 10));
          }
          return plane(w, halfW * 2, mat, cx, y, z);
        }
      
        function buildEastHighway() {
          const { x0, x1, z, lanes, median, laneWidth, shoulder } = EAST_HWY;
          const half = lanes * laneWidth / 2;                 // centre to the outer lane edge
          const inner = median / 2;                          // half the median
          const pave = half + shoulder;                      // out to the shoulder edge
      
          // two carriageways, the median gap between them left for the kerb
          carriageway(x0, x1, z - (inner + half + shoulder) / 2 - inner / 2, (half + shoulder), deckMat(1, { color: 0x2b2b30 }));
          carriageway(x0, x1, z + (inner + half + shoulder) / 2 + inner / 2, (half + shoulder), deckMat(2, { color: 0x2b2b30 }));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// metro.js — Downtown Bayou: the city that grows up on both sides of US-167 around the spawn strip (human request, 2026-09-27:
// "the area around the Crown Strip and the spawn area is our city area — a very metropolis, very modern New Orleans vibe").
//
// The roadside stores along the highway stay where they are (their lots are claimed); behind them, east and west, a street grid of
// blocks: glass and art-deco towers near the highway, hotel slabs, plazas with live oaks, and French Quarter terraces (stucco, shutters,
// iron balconies, gaslights) out toward the edges — the skyline of the Crown Strip to the north and OrleaRouge to the south, joined up.
//
// Composed with composer.js like the other districts; the parts (towers, rowhouses, plazas) are in cityparts.js.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

import * as THREE from "three";
import { createComposer } from "./composer.js";
import { createCityParts } from "./cityparts.js";
import { makeRoadway } from "./traffic.js";
import { createMarkings } from "./markings.js";
import { onParishHighway } from "./westparish.js";

const ROAD_X = -6;
export const METRO_BOUNDS = { x0: -292, x1: 292, z0: -132, z1: 128 };
const STREETS_Z = [-108, -52, 4, 60, 112];
const AVENUES_X = [-168, 168];
const STREET_W = 10, AVENUE_W = 12;

// Multi-lane, and it fits without moving a single building.
//
// Both roads are 10 m and 12 m of tarmac today, and the blocks either side sit a
// uniform 7 m back from every centreline (the ROWS/COLS constants are built on a
// 56 m pitch with a 7 m half-gap). Two lanes each way of 2.4 m either side of a
// 0.4 m median is 0.2 + 4.8 = 5.0 m from the centre, so the paved width is 10.0 m
// — the existing street width exactly, with a metre of shoulder left over on the
// 12 m avenues.
//
// That is the whole reason this was worth doing rather than a rebuild: the
// carriageway was already the right size for four lanes and had been carrying
// two. Widening the tarmac instead would have pushed into the 7 m gap and moved
// every building on sixteen blocks.
const STREET_ROAD = { name: "Metro", lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4, cruise: [8, 13] };
const AVENUE_ROAD = { name: "Bayou Ave", lanes: 2, median: 0.4, laneWidth: 2.4, cruise: [9, 14] };
// blocks: rows between the streets, columns between the avenues and the highway lots
const ROWS = [[-101, -59], [-45, -3], [11, 53], [67, 105]];
const COLS = [[-263, -175], [-161, -73], [63, 161], [175, 263]];

export function createMetro(ctx) {
  const { scene } = ctx;
  const occluders = [];
  const parts = createCityParts(ctx, { occluders });
  const hash = parts.hash;
  const C = createComposer(ctx, { name: "Metro", bounds: METRO_BOUNDS, zones: { core: METRO_BOUNDS, wild: METRO_BOUNDS }, seed: 4711 });
  const pois = [];
  let announced = false;

  // Four lanes each way, from the same makeRoadway the rest of the state uses,
  // so a Metro street gets the same overtaking, the same lane-change logic and
  // the same circuit chaining as US-167. Each carriageway is its own roadway
  // because the highway splits the grid: the east and west halves are joined by
  // a junction, not by tarmac.
  const lanes = [];
  for (const z of STREETS_Z) {
    lanes.push(...makeRoadway({ ...STREET_ROAD, points: [[62, z], [274, z]] }));
    lanes.push(...makeRoadway({ ...STREET_ROAD, points: [[-72, z], [-274, z]] }));
  }
  for (const x of AVENUES_X) {
    lanes.push(...makeRoadway({ ...AVENUE_ROAD, points: [[x, 118], [x, -118]] }));
  }

  function buildSet() {
    // ---- what is already there, claimed before anything is composed: the highway and its roadside lots (stores, gas, the trailer park and
    // the junkyard), and Parish Highway 9 swinging away to the south-west
    C.claim({ x0: -62, x1: 52, z0: METRO_BOUNDS.z0, z1: METRO_BOUNDS.z1 });

> Design decisions:
> - Louisiana had no passenger rail after 1959 (last interurban was the Baton Rouge–New Orleans streetcar, closed 1965). Real answer: streetcars (St. Charles green, Canal red — those are actually New Orleans streetcar lines, green = St. Charles Avenue line, red = Canal street line, orange = Riverfront, blue = Loyola). So the historically right thing for a New Orleans vibe is **streetcars**, not heavy rail. Plus a **commuter rail** to the suburbs (like the ill-fated Riverrail / the Lafayette streetcar), and **freight** on a shared spur (the refinery freight train already exists in welcomeback.js — a chance to reuse).
> - So: three tiers.
>   1. Streetcar network in OrleaRouge + Metro — track set flush in the pavement of the existing street grid (grooved rail), overhead wire on span wires from existing poles, 2.65 m gauge, cars ~12 m.
>   2. A regional/heavy line: the "Bayou Line" (Camden-ish) from OrleaRouge out east along the new EAST_HWY alignment to Wonders / Port Calypso, elevated over the swamp on trestle, with a proper yard.
>   3. Freight: the refinery spur, reuse of welcomeback's train, made to move, with a cargo hook.
> 
> - Concrete implementation: rails as thin boxes sunk into a groove of the existing tarmac plane (no new road geometry), flangeway; wire as a Line over existing lamp poles; the track geometry should follow the same `makeRoadway`/`markings.js` path so it batches.
> 
> - Gameplay: boarding (E at a stop), a carriage interior (or a "ride" camera), fast travel between stops, cargo/jobs, NPC riders, sabotage, fares, and a hostile use (running someone off the tracks? no — keep it: the trains are mostly a vertical-slice of convenience + a robbery/hostage cargo job).
> 
> - Data model sketch: `LINES` array with stops; `createTransit(ctx)`; `transit.stops`, `transit.board(player)`, `transit.update(dt)`.
> - Phasing: P0 measurement harness/test, P1 streetcar on one street, P2 loop, P3 regional, P4 freight.
> - Risks: draw calls, traffic conflict (cars drive over rails — need a "no entry" check or a signal), the 4-lane streets mean the streetcar needs a lane or a reservation, and cars parked in the way.

const page = await browser.newPage();

  // street lamps / lot lights with a pole are solid too (litSpots entries with `pole`), radius ~0.25 m
  for (const s of g.litSpots || []) if (s.pole && s.x != null) statics.push({ x: s.x, z: s.z, r: 0.25, tag: 'lamp pole' });
  const out = [];
  for (const l of lanes) {

    for (let i = 1; i < l.pts.length; i++) {

      const x0 = Math.min(a.x, b.x) - 30, x1 = Math.max(a.x, b.x) + 30, z0 = Math.min(a.y, b.y) - 30, z1 = Math.max(a.y, b.y) + 30;
      for (const k of statics) {
        if (k.x < x0 || k.x > x1 || k.z < z0 || k.z > z1) continue;
        const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ((k.x - a.x) * dx + (k.z - a.y) * dy) / len2));

  }
  return { lanes: lanes.length, statics: statics.length, out };
}, CLEAR);

}

// The game opens with an "I am over 18 years of age" gate (src/adultContent.js) that covers the page and swallows keys and clicks until it is
// answered. QA scripts drive the page with the keyboard and mouse, so they answer it exactly the way a player does — by pressing the button —
// the moment it appears. (There is deliberately no bypass in the game itself.)
export async function autoAcknowledge(page) {
  await page.evaluateOnNewDocument(() => {
    const press = () => { const b = document.querySelector('#gtbAdultGate button'); if (b && /OVER 18/.test(b.textContent)) b.click(); };
    new MutationObserver(press).observe(document, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', press);
  });
}

// browser_stub.mjs — the minimum browser surface the game modules touch.

// characters.js builds its surface textures on a <canvas>, weapons.js appends

const CTX_IMPL = {
  createImageData: (w, h) => ({ width: w, height: h, data: new Uint8ClampedArray(w * h * 4) }),
  getImageData: (x, y, w, h) => ({ width: w, height: h, data: new Uint8ClampedArray(w * h * 4) }),
  measureText: () => ({ width: 0 }),
  createLinearGradient: () => ({ addColorStop() {} }),
  createRadialGradient: () => ({ addColorStop() {} }),
};

/** A canvas 2D context where every drawing call is a no-op and every property is
 *  assignable — the texture code only ever needs the image buffers back. */
const makeContext = () => new Proxy({}, {
  get: (t, k) => (k in CTX_IMPL ? CTX_IMPL[k] : k in t ? t[k] : () => {}),
  set: (t, k, v) => { t[k] = v; return true; },
});

{
  "path": "tools/qa/road_ends_test.mjs",
  "instructions": "Regression test that runs the road coverage survey and asserts the state's road network reaches the map edges, that every district contributes lanes, and that the four corner towns and the freeways are all measured.",
  "content": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// road_ends_test.mjs — is the state actually connected up?\n//\n//   node --experimental-detect-module tools/qa/road_ends_test.mjs\n//\n// This runs tools/qa/road_ends.mjs and asserts on the numbers. The survey\n// existed first; this makes it a floor rather than a snapshot, so \"did we finish\n// the roads\" has an answer that goes red when it stops being true.\n//\n// The thresholds are the ones the current world actually meets, with a little\n// slack, and each one is written as the CLAIM rather than as a magic number: a\n// city with no roads in it fails on \"every district has traffic lanes\", not on\n// \"OrleaRouge is 11312 m long\".\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimport { spawnSync } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\n\nconst survey = fileURLToPath(new URL(\"./road_ends.mjs\", import.meta.url));\nconst run = spawnSync(process.execPath, [\"--experimental-detect-module\", survey, \"--json\"], {\n  encoding: \"utf8\",\n  maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,\n});\n\nif (run.status !== 0) {\n  console.log(`FAIL the survey did not run (exit ${run.status})`);\n  console.log(run.stderr || run.stdout);\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nconst at = run.stdout.indexOf(\"---JSON---\");\nif (at < 0) {\n  console.log(\"FAIL the survey printed no JSON\");\n  console.log(run.stdout.slice(0, 2000));\n  process.exit(1);\n}\nconst out = JSON.parse(run.stdout.slice(at + \"---JSON---\".length));\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \"} ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\nconst named = (n) => out.districts.find((d) => d.name === n);\nconst metres = (n) => (named(n) ? named(n).metres : 0);\n\nconsole.log(`\\nstate roads: ${out.totalMetres} m of lane, ${out.pavedKm2} km2 paved in a ${(out.grid * out.cell / 1000) ** 2} km2 map\\n`);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- it is a state\ncheck(\"the whole state is more than 20 km of road\", out.totalMetres > 20000, `${out.totalMetres} m`);\ncheck(\"paved ground covers at least a twentieth of the map\", out.pavedKm2 >= (out.grid * out.cell / 1000) ** 2 / 20,\n  `${out.pavedKm2} km2`);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- every district\n// A district that reports zero lanes is the failure this whole file was written\n// for. The first version of the survey hit it on StateWorld, which is where the\n// freeways live, and cheerfully reported the state's largest road network as\n// empty.\nfor (const d of out.districts) {\n  check(`${d.name} has traffic lanes`, d.lanes > 0 && d.metres > 0, `${d.lanes} lanes, ${d.metres} m`);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- nothing is cut off\n{\n  // The map runs to +/-1200. US-167 is a lane from z = +1198 to z = -1198, so\n  // north-south the road is expected to reach the edge; anything less means the\n  // spine is no longer a spine.\n  check(\"the north–south spine reaches the map edge\", out.reach.north && out.reach.north.gapToEdge < 40,\n    out.reach.north ? `${out.reach.north.gapToEdge} m short` : \"no road north at all\");\n  check(\"...in both directions\", out.reach.south && out.reach.south.gapToEdge < 40,\n    out.reach.south ? `${out.reach.south.gapToEdge} m short` : \"no road south at all\");\n  // East is the eastbound arterial's job, and it is the thing the last screenshot\n  // was complaining about.\n  check(\"the eastbound arterial reaches the map edge\", out.reach.east && out.reach.east.gapToEdge < 60,\n    out.reach.east ? `x ${out.reach.east.at[0]}, ${out.reach.east.gapToEdge} m short` : \"no road east at all\");\n  // West is NOT expected to reach the edge — Red Dust is out past x = -1000 and\n  // everything between it and the map boundary is swamp on purpose. What matters\n  // is that the corner town is on a road at all.\n  check(\"the far west is reached\", out.reach.west && out.reach.west.at[0] < -1000,\n    out.reach.west ? `x ${out.reach.west.at[0]}` : \"no road west at all\");\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the corners\n// Port Calypso, Red Dust, Lakeshore and Oyster Bay are the four towns in the\n// state's corners, and their lanes arrive through StateWorld's build rather than\n// through a district creator, so they are the ones a coverage check misses if it\n// stops at the creator.\ncheck(\"the state's own build contributes the freeways and the corner towns\",\n  metres(\"StateWorld\") > 10000, `${metres(\"StateWorld\")} m`);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the cities\ncheck(\"OrleaRouge is a metropolis by road length alone\", metres(\"OrleaRouge\") > 10000, `${metres(\"OrleaRouge\")} m`);\ncheck(\"Metro is a city too\", metres(\"Metro\") > 4000, `${metres(\"Metro\")} m`);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------- and a floor on the holes\n{\n  // Not \"no holes\" — 67 of them is correct: the middle of the state is bayou and\n  // swamp and is meant to stay empty. But a growing city should not be adding to\n  // the list, so this only fails if coverage shrinks.\n  const limit = 70;\n  check(`no more than ${limit} empty 200 m squares`, out.holes.length <= limit, `${out.holes.length} holes`);\n}\n\nconsole.log(failures ? `\\n${failures} road coverage check(s) FAILED` : \"\\nAll road coverage checks passed\");\nprocess.exit(failures ? 1 : 0);\n"
}
