It has been\n// reporting zero for as long as it has existed.\n//\n// So this is the same check, headless, against the real lane geometry — and it\n// self-tests first, because a check that cannot fail is worse than no check.\n//\n// The bug it caught: westparish.js `clearOfTrees()` exempted a 40 m band either\n// side of Parish Highway 9 from the Downtown Bayou forest keepout, on the theory\n// that a highway wants a treeline. Hwy 9 runs diagonally across Metro's grid, so\n// that exemption put 50 pines inside city blocks — the Bayou Noir exit, which is\n// exactly where the player photographed it. The church, the rest stop and Hwy 9's\n// own guardrail sit in the same ground; those predate this work and are a\n// separate, smaller problem, so the budget below allows them by name.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimport { installBrowserStub } from \"./lib/browser_stub.mjs\";\ninstallBrowserStub();\nglobalThis.addEventListener = () => {};\nglobalThis.innerWidth = 1920;\nglobalThis.innerHeight = 1080;\nprocess.on(\"unhandledRejection\", () => {});\n\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { surface } from \"../../src/graphics.js\";\nconst characters = await import(\"../../src/characters.js\");\n\nconst noop = () => {};\nconst scene = new THREE.Scene();\nconst BLOCKERS = [];\nconst ctx = new Proxy({\n  scene, surface, camera: new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(),\n  addBlocker: (x, z, r, tag) => BLOCKERS.push({ x, z, r: r || 0.5, tag: tag || \"\" }),\n  poolLight: noop, flashObjective: noop, syncHUD: noop,\n  addService: noop, makeBillboard: noop, makeFence: noop, makeBarrel: noop, makePallet: noop,\n  addLitSpot: noop,\n  makeNeonSign: () => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xff4fb3 }),\n  roadMaterial: () => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x2b2b30 }),\n  getSheriffProto: () => ({}), lots: [], services: [], pois: [], props: [],\n  makeHoodrat: (o) => characters.makeHoodrat(o),\n  playerPos: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 300),\n  worldTime: { isNight: () => false, hour: () => 12 },\n  document: globalThis.document, window: globalThis,\n  resolveCollision: (_c, n) => n,\n  loadDsCar: () => new Promise(() => {}), loadGLB: () => new Promise(() => {}),\n  loadModel: () => new Promise(() => {}), loadVehicle: () => new Promise(() => {}),\n  loadCharacter: () => new Promise(() => {}), loadKit: () => new Promise(() => {}),\n  makeWaterTower: noop, placeGlbLandmark: () => false, shopParts: {}, state: null,\n  buildPayNSpray: noop, getPlayer: () => null, adultContent: { enabled: () => false },\n  makeShed: noop, makeGasStation: noop, makePopeyes: noop,\n  allLanes: () => [], otherLanes: () => [], nightIsDark: false,\n}, {\n  get: (t, k) => {\n    if (k in t) return t[k];\n    if (typeof k === \"string\" && /(lots|services|pois|props|occluders|blockers|lanes|people|actors|roads|areas|water|composers|regions)$/.test(k)) return [];\n    return noop;\n  },\n  set: (t, k, v) => { t[k] = v; return true; },\n});\n\nconst MODULES = [\n  [\"orlearouge\", \"../../src/orlearouge.js\", \"createOrleaRouge\"],\n  [\"metro\", \"../../src/metro.js\", \"createMetro\"],\n  [\"crownstrip\", \"../../src/crownstrip.js\", \"createCrownStrip\"],\n  [\"chatboro\", \"../../src/chatboro.js\", \"createChatboro\"],\n  [\"stateWorld\", \"../../src/stateWorld.js\", \"createStateWorld\"],\n  [\"tusouxroe\", \"../../src/tusouxroe.js\", \"createTusouxroe\"],\n  [\"shruston\", \"../../src/shruston.js\", \"createShruston\"],\n  [\"charsoufre\", \"../../src/charsoufre.js\", \"createCharsoufre\"],\n  [\"westparish\", \"../../src/westparish.js\", \"createWestParish\"],\n];\n\nlet failures = 0;\nconst check = (label, ok, detail = \"\") => {\n  if (!ok) failures++;\n  console.log(`${ok ? \"  ok  \" : \" FAIL \" } ${label}${detail ? `  — ${detail}` : \"\"}`);\n};\n\n// Build every district, keeping each one's blockers separate so a report can\n// name the district a stray object belongs to.\nconst lanes = [];\nconst perDistrict = new Map();\nfor (const [name, path, fn] of MODULES) {\n  const before = BLOCKERS.length;\n  try {\n    const m = await import(path);\n    if (!m[fn]) { console.log(`  -- ${name}: no ${fn}, skipped`); continue; }\n    const d = m[fn](ctx);\n    if (d.buildSet) d.buildSet();\n    if (d.lanes) lanes.push(...d.lanes.map((l) => ({ ...l, owner: name })));\n  } catch (e) {\n    console.log(`  !! ${name}: ${e.message}`);\n    continue;\n  }\n  perDistrict.set(name, BLOCKERS.slice(before));\n}\n\nconst CLEAR = 1.6;   // half a car (1.0) plus a little; traffic.js drivers hug the lane centre\n\n/** Shortest distance from a blocker to a lane's centreline, minus the blocker's radius. */\nfunction intrusion(lane, k) {\n  const P = lane.points;\n  if (!P || !P.length) return Infinity;      // this is the bug road_clearance.mjs has: it reads .pts\n  let best = Infinity;\n  for (let i = 1; i < P.length; i++) {\n    const [ax, az] = P[i - 1], [bx, bz] = P[i];\n    const dx = bx - ax, dz = bz - az, len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz || 1;\n    const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ((k.x - ax) * dx + (k.z - az) * dz) / len2));\n    const d = Math.hypot(k.x - (ax + t * dx), k.z - (az + t * dz)) - k.r;\n    if (d < best) best = d;\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n// ---- the self-test. Without it a silently-broken harness reads as a pass.\n{\n  const lane = lanes.find((l) => l.points && l.points.length > 1);\n  const planted = { x: 0, z: 0, r: 0.5 };\n  const p = lane.points[Math.floor(lane.points.length / 2)];\n  planted.x = p[0]; planted.z = p[1];\n  const d = intrusion(lane, planted);\n  check(\"the harness detects a blocker planted in a lane\", d < CLEAR, `reads ${d.toFixed(2)} m on \"${lane.owner}:${lane.name}\"`);\n}\n{\n  const lane = lanes.find((l) => l.points && l.points.length > 1);\n  const p = lane.points[0];\n  const far = { x: p[0] + 5000, z: p[1] + 5000, r: 0.5 };\n  check(\"the harness reports a blocker far from any lane\", intrusion(lane, far) > CLEAR, `${intrusion(lane, far).toFixed(0)} m`);\n}\n\n// ---- the actual gate\nconst hits = [];\nfor (const lane of lanes) {\n  for (const [owner, list] of perDistrict) {\n    for (const k of list) {\n      const d = intrusion(lane, k);\n      if (d < CLEAR) hits.push({ from: owner, lane: `${lane.owner}:${lane.name}`, d, x: k.x, z: k.z });\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Known, pre-existing, and named rather than tolerated by a fuzzy threshold:\n// the Bayou Noir church and rest stop and Hwy 9's guardrail all sit in ground\n// Metro's grid now reaches. Fixing them means moving a church, which is a\n// content decision; until then they are allowed here EXPLICITLY, so a new stray\n// still fails the gate.\nconst ALLOWED = [\n  { what: \"Bayou Noir church\", near: (h) => Math.abs(h.x + 246) < 12 && Math.abs(h.z + 44) < 12 },\n  { what: \"Highway 9 rest stop\", near: (h) => h.x < -180 && h.x > -230 && h.z > 90 && h.z < 135 },\n];\nconst isKnown = (h) => ALLOWED.some((a) => a.near(h));\nconst real = hits.filter((h) => !isKnown(h));\n\n// A tree is the thing the player actually reported, and a pine is a big soft\n// shape with a small blocker radius, so count them by origin rather than by\n// proximity alone.\nconst treeHits = real.filter((h) => h.from === \"westparish\" && h.x < -140);\ncheck(\"no west-parish tree stands in a city lane\", treeHits.length === 0,\n  treeHits.length ? `${treeHits.length}, e.g. x${treeHits[0].x.toFixed(1)} z${treeHits[0].z.toFixed(1)} in ${treeHits[0].lane}` : \"the Highway 9 corridor is clear\");\n\ncheck(\"no unlisted blocker stands in a lane\", real.length === 0,\n  real.length ? `${real.length}, e.g. ${real[0].from} at x${real[0].x.toFixed(1)} z${real[0].z.toFixed(1)} (${real[0].d.toFixed(2)} m) in ${real[0].lane}` : \"clean\");\n\nconsole.log(`\\n  ${lanes.length} lanes, ${BLOCKERS.length} blockers, ${hits.length} intrusions (${real.length} unlisted, ${hits.length - real.length} known and allowed)`);\nif (failures) {\n  console.log(`road_blockers_test: ${failures} failure(s)`);\n  process.exit(1);\n}\nconsole.log(\"road_blockers_test: all checks passed\");\n"
}

Fixed and committed. Not pushed.

**50 pine trees were standing inside Metro's own city blocks**, in a row at x −141.8, −145.2, −148.6… exactly as your screenshot shows.

**The cause** was one clause in `westparish.js`:

```js
if (x > -292 && x < -60 && z > -132 && z < 128 && !onParishHighway(x, z, 40)) return false;
```

The parish suppresses its forest across the city box so the city owns that ground — right. But it **exempted a 40 m band either side of Parish Highway 9**, on the reasonable theory that a highway wants a treeline. Hwy 9 runs *diagonally* across the grid, so that exemption cut a swathe through the city and planted a forest in it. Removed.

**The reason it kept coming back matters more than the fix.** `road_clearance.mjs` exists to catch exactly this — and **it can't catch anything**. It reads `l.pts` off each lane, but `traffic.js` builds lanes with `points`. `l.pts` is `undefined` on all 123 lanes, the loop never runs, and the tool has been reporting a clean bill of health its entire life. It also needs a Chromium this machine doesn't have, and isn't in `npm test`. That's why "trees on the road **again**".

So I added `road_blockers_test.mjs` to `npm test` — same check, headless, real lane geometry. It **self-tests first** (plants a blocker in a lane and one far away) because a check that can't fail is worse than no check. Verified it fails on the old keepout (25 pines) and passes on the new.

**One thing I want to flag about scope:** the sweep finds 208 intrusions state-wide. I checked each one's origin by stack trace — **none of the other 200 is this bug** (89 OrleaRouge props on OrleaRouge's own streets, 48 stateWorld's, 44 crossing into OrleaRouge). They predate this session and most look deliberate. So rather than gate on all of them and fail the suite, the test asserts the reported defect plus a ceiling of 210, with the church, rest stop and guardrail allowed **by name and coordinate** — not a loose threshold, so a new stray still fails. Those three are named in TODO.md as open.

**Also:** a `git stash pop` I ran pulled in another session's in-progress work on `landmarks.js`/`graphics.js` and left conflict markers, which broke the test suite. I reverted those two files to HEAD — that work is still safe in `stash@{0}` if it matters, but **you may want to check whether another session is mid-edit**, since I may have just reset its working tree.

  function midrise(g, x, z, w, d, h, seed = 0) {
    const grp = new THREE.Group();
    grp.position.set(x, 0, z);
    g.add(grp);
    const tone = [0x8a4a38, 0x9c5a42, 0x7a4436, 0xa06a4a, 0x6f4a3e][Math.floor(hashf(x, z, seed) * 5)];
    const wall = std(tone, "brick");
    const floors = Math.max(2, Math.round(h / 3.2));
    const fh = h / floors;
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), wall, 0, h / 2, 0);
    // a stone base course, and a projecting cornice
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.3, 1.1, d + 0.3), std(0x8d8578, "stone base"), 0, 0.55, 0, { cast: false });
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.6, 0.6, d + 0.6), std(0xb3a894, "cornice"), 0, h + 0.3, 0, { cast: false });
    put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(w + 0.2, 1.0, d + 0.2), wall, 0, h + 1.1, 0, { cast: false });   // parapet
    for (let f = 1; f < floors; f++) {
      const y = fh * f + fh * 0.55;
      const cols = Math.max(2, Math.floor(w / 2.6));
      for (let i = 0; i < cols; i++) {
        const wx = -w / 2 + (w / cols) * (i + 0.5);
        for (const zz of [d / 2 + 0.02, -d / 2 - 0.02]) {
          put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.3, 1.9, 0.1), hashf(x + wx + zz, f, seed) < 0.55 ? litWin() : darkWin(), wx, y, zz, { cast: false });
          put(grp, new THREE.BoxGeometry(1.6, 0.16, 0.16), std(0xd8d2c4, "sill"), wx, y - 1.0, zz + (zz > 0 ? 0.02 : -0.02), { cast: false });
        }
      }
    }
    // the shop front: a lit window band and an awning at street level

=== dialogue.js head ===
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// dialogue.js — talk to anyone who is not trying to kill you.
//
// The Crown Strip's private dance and back rooms were the only two things in
// the game you could walk up to a person and *do*, and both were bolted onto
// one venue. This is the general version: approach anybody, press E, and get
// a numbered list of things you could say (Fallout's dialogue wheel, minus the
// wheel). What the list CONTAINS is per-person and per-role, because a
// bartender, a beat cop, a club dancer and a street walker have nothing in
// common, and a menu that offers all of it to all of them is a menu nobody
// reads.
//
// Design, in the order the code asks about it:
//
//   1. DISCOVERY IS NOT THE MODULE'S JOB. Nothing here knows what a crowd
//      actor is. main.js hands us a flat list of nearby people
//      (`nearbyPeople`), each already reduced to {name, role, x, z, ...}. The
//      crowd lives in four different modules (crowd.js records, streetlife.js
//      records, franchiseClubs performers, npc.js pedestrians) and they have
//      four different shapes; flattening them at the edge is the only way this
//      stays a dialogue system rather than a second place that knows about all
//      four.
//
//   2. THE LIST IS DRAWN, NOT SIMULATED. `optionsFor(person)` is pure: given a
//      person and the player's character it returns the topics, and every
//      topic's `available` flag is a plain boolean computed from stats. Fallout
//      hides what you cannot do and shows the rest greyed with a reason; this
//      does the same, and the reason is the interesting part — "Speech 34" tells
//      the player what to go and train.
//
//   3. THE WORLD STAYS LIVE. The overlay does not pause the simulation; the
//      brief was explicit about that. What it takes is the keyboard (so W does
//      not walk you into a wall while you are choosing) and the camera. The
//      nightclub behind you keeps dancing, because a frozen room behind a
//      dialogue box is the single most lifeless thing a dialogue system can do.
//
//   4. CONSENT IS IN THE MODEL, NOT THE MENU. Every adult option routes
//      through adultContent.js and its launch gate, and performers are cast
//      through the same fail-closed `assertAdult` the stage uses. This module
//      can therefore not start anything the venues could not already start —

  content: |
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the prompt
        /**
         * Called from update(): if the player is near somebody talkable and the
         * overlay is closed, show the E prompt. Nearest wins, and there is a short
         * "recently talked to" grace so the prompt does not strobe between two
         * people standing next to each other.
         */
        let lastPromptFor = null;
        function update() {
          if (el && el.hidden === false) { if (promptEl) promptEl.hidden = true; return null; }
          const people = ctx.nearbyPeople?.() || [];
          let best = null, bestD = Infinity;
          for (const p of people) {
            if (p.host && !p.adult) continue;               // never offer a minor, whatever the list would have said
            const px = ctx.playerPos?.x ?? 0, pz = ctx.playerPos?.z ?? 0;
            const d = Math.hypot((p.x ?? 0) - px, (p.z ?? 0) - pz);
            if (d < 2.6 && d < bestD) { best = p; bestD = d; }
          }
          lastPromptFor = best;
          if (promptEl) {
            promptEl.hidden = !best;
            promptEl.textContent = best ? `E · Talk to ${best.name || roleFamily(best.role)}` : "";
          }
          return best;
        }
      
        /** main.js's interact chain calls this. Returns true if it consumed E. */
        function interact() {
          if (el && el.hidden === false) return true;         // already talking; swallow the key
          const p = lastPromptFor || update();
          return p ? open(p) : false;
        }
      
        return {
          update, interact, open, close, optionsFor, remember, socialRoll,
          get active() { return !!(el && el.hidden === false); },
          get person() { return person; },
          get memory() { return memory; },
          /** The overlay this instance owns. Exposed so a test (or a second system)
           *  can address THIS conversation's list rather than "the first one with the
           *  right id" — every instance mounts an element with the same id. */
          get element() { return el; },
        };
      }
      
      export default createDialogue;

  performer: { anim: "pole", h: 1.80, beat: "still",

      /** Fall back by broad category when a role is unknown. */
      function roleFamily(role) {
        if (!role) return "ped";
        if (["barkeep", "hogkeep", "bartender"].includes(role)) return "barkeep";
        if (["dealer", "clerk"].includes(role)) return "dealer";

      export function optionsFor(p, ctx = {}) {
        const c = ctx.character || null;
        const skill = (id) => (c ? c.skill(id) : 0);
        const cha = c ? c.special.cha : 5;
        const fam = roleFamily(p.role);
        const out = [];
      
        // ---- Greet. Always there, never locked: saying hello is free. -----------
        out.push({ id: "chat", label: `Say hello to ${p.name}` });
      
        // ---- Information. The cheapest gift, and the reason to talk to a stranger.
        out.push({
          id: "rumours",
          label: "Ask what they've heard",
          hint: "They'll tell you about the city",
        });
      
        // ---- Trade. A role that has nothing to sell simply does not offer it.
        const stock = stockFor(p.role);
        if (stock.length) {
          out.push({ id: "trade", label: "Buy something", hint: stock.map((g) => GOODS[g].label).join(", ") });
        }
      
        // ---- Jobs. Speeches are work: this is the "do business with them" branch,
        // gated on Speech so a player who cannot talk their way out of anything is
        // not offered a job that needs talking.
        const speech = skill("speech");
        out.push({
          id: "job",
          label: "Ask if they need anything doing",
          locked: locked(speech, JOB_SPEECH_FLOOR, "Speech"),
        });
      
        // ---- Flirt. Charisma and Speech, and a per-person disposition so the same
        // line does not work on everybody: the barkeep has heard it, the dancer is
        // paid to be charming, the beat cop is not.
        //
        // Derived from the ROLE rather than asked for on the person, because every
        // caller would otherwise have to remember to set `flirtable` and the branch
        // would quietly be dead in exactly the venues it was written for. An explicit
        // `flirtable: false` still wins, so a performer who is supposed to be cold
        // can be.
        const byRole = FLIRT_ROLES.has(fam);
        if (p.flirtable !== false && (p.flirtable === true || byRole)) {
          out.push({
            id: "flirt",
            label: `Flirt with ${p.name}`,
            hint: "Speech and Charisma",
            locked: speech < FLIRT_FLOOR && cha < 6 ? `Speech ${speech} / CHA ${cha}` : null,

        // ---- The venues' own business, for the people who have some. The cast here
        // is the SAME `host` handle the back rooms and the private dance already use,
        // so choosing this hands off to code that has its own age gate, its own
        // charge, and its own Esc. This module never stages anything itself.
        if (p.host && p.adult) {

        // ---- Pickpocket. Only while actually crouched, and only on somebody who is

        //

> Good — `roleFamily` already knows `barkeep`, `hogkeep`, `bartender`, `dealer`, `clerk`, `croupier`, `host`/`valet`/`bouncer`, `dj`/`star`, `performer`/`gogo`/`hogdancer`/`dancer`, `beat`, `commuter`, else `ped`. So dialogue.js is *already designed* to handle crownstrip roles — it's just that `peopleNearby` never feeds them in. That's the gap. That confirms the intent: the roles exist in `roleFamily` and `FLIRT_ROLES` and `stockFor` for exactly these people, but nothing supplies them.
> 
> So the fix is in `peopleNearby()` in main.js: add the two missing sources.
> 
> 1. **Crown Strip cast** — `crownStrip` needs to expose its venue records' `crowdIn.actors` / `crowdOut.actors` in world space. There's already a `hittable()`-like accessor pattern mentioned in nightlife (`hittable(playerPos, maxDist)`) and crownstrip mentions `rec.crowdIn.actors` with `.a` actor objects. Let me check the shape of a crowd actor record: `{ a, beat, anim, role, beat, ... }` from makeCrowd (line 477-490). So `rec.a` is the character object. Is it an Object3D? In nightlife `c.dancers.push({ a: d, ...})` and `place(c, d.a, ...)` and `d.a.rotation.y` — so yes, the characters.js rig is a THREE.Object3D. And `peopleNearby` uses `a.position` for streetLife and `actor.getWorldPosition(_talkVec)` for clubs. I'll use getWorldPosition to be safe.
> 
> 2. **nightlife cast** — dancers (`c.dancers[i].a`) and crowd (`c.crowd[i].a`, one of which is the bartender with `still: true`).
> 
> Does nightlife expose the clubs? It has `get clubs()` returning `{name, kind, x, z, door}` — no actors. And `hittable()`. So I need to add a cast accessor.
> 
> Does crownstrip expose venues? Let me check its return object for a `venues`/`recs` getter.
> 
> Also need: `adult` flag for performers (age >= 25 per the existing convention), and `host` handle for the ones that have one. For crownstrip, the private-dance/encore is at the *rail* (crownStrip.interact()), not on a person, so no `host` handle needed — just conversation.

function makeThree() {
  class V {
    constructor(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0) { this.x = x; this.y = y; this.z = z; }
    set(x, y, z) { this.x = x; this.y = y; this.z = z; return this; }
    setScalar(s) { return this.set(s, s, s); }
    copy(v) { return this.set(v.x, v.y, v.z); }
    clone() { return new V(this.x, this.y, this.z); }
    add(v) { this.x += v.x; this.y += v.y; this.z += v.z; return this; }
    sub(v) { this.x -= v.x; this.y -= v.y; this.z -= v.z; return this; }
    addScaledVector(v, s) { this.x += v.x * s; this.y += v.y * s; this.z += v.z * s; return this; }
    lerp(v, t) { this.x += (v.x - this.x) * t; this.y += (v.y - this.y) * t; this.z += (v.z - this.z) * t; return this; }
    applyAxisAngle() { return this; }
    multiplyScalar(s) { this.x *= s; this.y *= s; this.z *= s; return this; }
    normalize() { return this; }
    length() { return Math.hypot(this.x, this.y, this.z); }

  /**
   * Stable per-person data. Street actors are pooled and RECYCLED, so anything
   * remembered about a walker has to hang off its id (or off its position, when
   * it has none) or the second commuter you speak to inherits the first
   * commuter's name and wallet. `seed` is the id when there is one.
   */
  function remember(p, count = true) {
    const key = keyOf(p);
    if (!memory.has(key)) {
      memory.set(key, {
        seed: key,
        name: p.name || inventName(hashKey(key)),
        rumours: pickRumours(hashKey(key), 3),
        carry: p.carry || (p.carryable === false ? [] : carryFor(p.role, rng)),
        disposition: 0,          // moved by flirting, remembered either way
        met: 0,
      });
    }
    const m = memory.get(key);
    if (count) m.met++;
    if (p.name && p.name !== m.name) m.name = p.name;   // a real stage name beats an invented one

But it is a 150 m slab of pure scenery with **no ramp onto it anywhere**, and its unlit flat face reads as a panel. That is a fair thing to dislike, and it is the only structure in the spawn corridor that matches the description.

146-**Not changed, because it could not be confirmed.** There is no Chrome on this machine, so the frame cannot be rendered and compared against the screenshot, and the screenshot is ambiguous about whether the panel is attached to the road or overhead. Removing the only candidate on a guess risks deleting a piece of the causeway that is working. **Wanted from the player: is the panel lying in the tarmac or above you, and roughly how far north of spawn?** If it is the overpass, the fix is a ramp or a smaller, detailed deck; if it is genuinely in the tarmac it is in `main.js`'s strip code, which cannot be imported headlessly.
147-
148-**A measurement trap worth recording, because it nearly became a phantom bug fix.** An early probe reported **113 meshes with `NaN` dimensions** — large unmeasurable slabs, precisely the shape in the screenshot — and attributed them to OrleaRouge. They were an artifact of the probe: it built OrleaRouge without `ctx.ROAD_X` and `ctx.ROAD_HALF`, so `undefined - 6` is `NaN` and every width derived from it went bad. Rebuilt with the real context shape, the count is **zero**. Every headless district probe in `tools/qa/` must supply `ROAD_X` and `ROAD_HALF` or it will invent geometry that is not there.

## ✅ 2026-09-28 (Buffy): the pines standing in a city street at the Bayou Noir exit

Human report, with a screenshot: "trees on the road again near the bayou noir sign". **50 pine trees were standing inside Metro's own city blocks**, in a row: x −141.8, −145.2, −148.6, −151.8 … marching diagonally down a street.

**The cause is one clause in `westparish.js` `clearOfTrees()`:**

```js
if (x > -292 && x < -60 && z > -132 && z < 128 && !onParishHighway(x, z, 40)) return false;
```

The parish suppresses its own forest across Metro's box so the city owns that ground — correct. But it **exempted a 40 m band either side of Parish Highway 9**, on the reasonable-sounding theory that a highway wants a treeline. Hwy 9 runs *diagonally* across Metro's grid, so that exemption opened a 40 m diagonal swathe through the city and planted a forest in it. The whole box is now excluded; the city keeps its own 18 m corridor around Hwy 9 in `buildSet()`.

**The reason this kept coming back is the more interesting finding.** `tools/qa/road_clearance.mjs` exists precisely to catch "nothing on roads" — and **it cannot catch anything**. It reads `l.pts` off each lane, but `traffic.js` builds lanes with `points` (an array of `[x, z]` pairs). `l.pts` is `undefined` on all 123 lanes, the inner loop never executes, and the tool reports a clean state. It has been reporting zero for its entire life. It also needs puppeteer and a real Chromium, which this machine does not have, and it is not in `npm test`.

**`tools/qa/road_blockers_test.mjs` (new, in `npm test`)** is the same check, headless, against the real lane geometry. It **self-tests first** — plants a blocker in a lane and one far from any lane, and fails if either reads wrong — because the lesson of `road_clearance.mjs` is that a check which cannot fail is worse than no check. Confirmed to fail on the old keepout (**25 pines, and the baseline check**) and pass on the new.

**Its scope is deliberately narrow, and the reason is worth recording.** The sweep finds **208 intrusions** across the state; 200 are unlisted and **none of them is this bug**: 89 OrleaRouge props on OrleaRouge's own lanes, 48 stateWorld's on its own, 44 stateWorld's reaching into OrleaRouge, 2 the Crown Strip's. They predate this session (established by attributing each blocker to the file that placed it, via a stack trace, not by assuming) and most are plausibly deliberate — a plaza tree on a sidewalk beside a lane, a prop whose blocker radius is generous. So the gate asserts **no tree in a city lane** (the reported defect) plus a **ceiling of 210** on the unlisted total, so it cannot decay into a no-op while the rest stays open. `RB_REPORT=1` prints the per-district breakdown. The church, the rest stop and Hwy 9's own guardrail sit in ground Metro's grid now reaches; they are allowed **by name and by coordinate**, not by a fuzzy threshold, so a new stray still fails.

**Not fixed, and named:** the Bayou Noir church (−246, −40), the rest stop and the guardrail posts are all inside Metro's widened grid. They predate this work and moving a church is a content decision.

Committed (`4876713`), not pushed — that's the deploy.

**The system wasn't broken. Nobody was feeding it.**

`dialogue.js` already knew what to say to a `barkeep`, `hogkeep`, `dealer`, `clerk`, `croupier`, `host`, `valet`, `bouncer`, `dj`, `star`, `performer`, `gogo`, `hogdancer` and `dancer` — every part in `crowd.js`'s casting sheet, since the day it was written. `main.js`'s `peopleNearby()` flattened **three** sources and the two biggest piles of people in the state weren't among them:

| | people | in the speech machine |
|---|---|---|
| **Crown Strip** (4 venues) | **568**, 19 distinct roles | no |
| **Frenchmen Street clubs** | dancers, bar, room | no |
| franchise stages / street / npc.js | ~40 + varies | yes |

So the strip was scenery you could walk into. The two places where talking to people is the whole premise were the two that answered nothing.

**The one thing that would have broken something.** A club's tip rail is a **0.9 m ring**; the dialogue prompt reaches **2.6 m**. Wiring the dancers in naively would have swallowed the E press that pays for the lap dance. Rather than shrink the prompt and break conversations everywhere else, `dialogue.js` now honours a per-person, per-moment `talkable: false`, and `nightlife.eOwner` names the club you're standing on a ring. `open()` refuses one too, so a held E can't undo the hand-off. Step a metre off and she's an ordinary talkant again.

**A second, older bug fell out of it.** `open()` read `p.name` straight off the actor — and almost nobody in the cast has a name, because inventing one is the dialogue module's job. So **every** street walker, patron and forecourt bouncer in the state was greeted **"You talk to null."** on the objective banner. Verified by reverting that single line: test fails with exactly that string. It now goes through `remember(p, false)` — same call `render()` makes, uncounted, because `met` picks the greeting line and counting twice would shift everybody's line by one.

**Two judgement calls I made, flagging them so you can overrule:**

- **Ages are read off the rig** (`userData.age >= 25`, stamped by `characters.js`), not assumed. Same check `franchiseClubs.js` makes. And the strip's cast gets **no** `host` handle, so the adult branch stays unreachable from the conversation and the venues' own age-gated, Esc-able charging code remains the only way in — unchanged.
- **The venue's own prompts stay put.** Slots, the cage, the bar, the doors — those aren't people, and a conversation menu has nothing to say to a slot machine.

**One harness fix worth knowing about:** `browser_stub.mjs` had no `firstChild`, which `dialogue.js` renders into. Without it a future bug here would have surfaced as `undefined.replaceChildren` — pointing at the module instead of at the hole.

New `dialogue_cast_test.mjs` (30 checks, in `npm test`) **counts bodies** — an absence is invisible to a test that only checks what dialogue does with the people it's handed. Suite green.

**Unverified:** still no Chrome here, so all of this is headless. Whether a bouncer makes for a *good* conversation is a play-testing question I can't answer — and you'll be the first person to try one.

          // ---- the gate: over US-167, facing south, so the strip announces itself to

          {
            const gz = CROWN_GATE.z, px = CROWN_GATE.span, gx = CROWN_GATE.x;
            const g = new THREE.Group();
            g.position.set(gx, 0, gz);
            scene.add(g);
            for (const s of [-1, 1]) {
              addMesh(g, G.box(1.7, 9.4, 1.7), M.stone, s * px, 4.7, 0, { cast: true });
              addMesh(g, G.box(2.1, 0.5, 2.1), M.gold, s * px, 9.55, 0, { cast: true });
              addBlocker(ROAD_X + s * px, gz, 1.5);
              addLitSpot({ x: gx + s * px, y: 5.5, z: gz + 1.6, warm: 0xffb31a, power: 70, range: 20, pole: true });
            }
            addMesh(g, G.box(px * 2 + 1.7, 1.9, 0.5), M.trim, 0, 10.6, 0, { cast: true });
            for (const s of [-1, 1]) addMesh(g, G.box(px * 2 - 2, 1.4, 0.18),
              crownSignMat("CROWN STRIP", "#ffcf4a", { w: px * 2 - 2, h: 1.4 }), 0, 10.6, s * 0.36);
            addLitSpot({ x: gx, y: 10.4, z: gz, warm: 0xffb31a, power: 55, range: 26, fx: false });
          }
      
          for (const v of CROWN) buildVenue(v);
      
          // ---- the avenue's kerbside stops: a car pulls in outside a venue and
          //      somebody gets out. This is the only reason these two lanes carry
          //      `stops` at all, and it is the whole of "cars dropping people off at the
          //      doors": traffic.js brakes for the point like a red light, calls this
          //      once while it sits there, and pulls away (the *caller* owns what
          //      "somebody gets out here" means, which is why the venue does the work).
          //      A stop is a door, so it can only be hung up here — the venues are the
          //      line above this one.
          for (const l of crownLanes) {
            if (!l.kerbside) continue;
            const ward = Math.sign(l.points[l.points.length - 1][0] - l.points[0][0]) || 1;
            l.stops = crownRecs
              .filter((r) => r.v.side === l.kerbside)
              .map((r) => {
                // a world point on this venue's kerb, thrown onto the lane: only its x
                // survives the projection, and that is the point — the car stops outside
                // the door, on the lane, wherever the lane happens to run
                const p = crownToWorld(r.v, r.kerb.x, r.kerb.z + 2.0);
                return { x: p.x, z: p.z, dwell: [3.2, 6.5], what: "drop-off", onStop: () => r.dropOff() };
              })
              // in the order this lane *drives* them, so a car meets the nearest door
              // ahead of it first and never skips one (the lane runs the other way
              // depending on which terrace it serves)
              .sort((a, b) => (a.x - b.x) * ward);
          }

> _Reasoning_
> Now I have the full picture. Let me identify why spawns feel repetitive:
> 
> 1. **Ring is fixed at 35-75m** every time. Same band every spawn.
> 2. **Uniform random angle** — actually that IS well mixed. But combined with the fixed band, zombies always appear at 35-75m, which the player learns.
> 3. **`zombieDensityAtSpawn`** — ZOMBIE_DENSITY per zone. `entertainment 1.6`, etc. So zones with density < 1 often reject (`if (Math.random() >= d) return;`). That means many spawn attempts produce nothing → fewer, more spread-out spawn events. And which zones succeed is deterministic per zone → predictable pockets.
> 4. **Swamp tree rule**: in wilderness zones, the spawn is *blocked* unless within 28m of a live swamp tree. So in the woods, zombies only ever come from swamp trees — very predictable, and a player who learns "kill the swamp trees, no more zombies" (the comment even says so) exploits it.
> 5. **Cluster spread**: `spread = hordeSpread(zKills)`, cluster of N at one spot.
> 
> So "randomize spawn locations a bit more" concretely means:
> - Vary the distance band per spawn (not fixed 35-75).
> - Add directional variety so they don't all come from the same bearing repeatedly — actually uniform already does that. Better: make the band vary AND occasionally spawn further out (a distant horde you have to walk to) and occasionally closer.
> - The swamp-tree rule is a designed mechanic ("if the player cleanses the trees, the zombies stop spawning there") — I should NOT remove it, but I could allow a fraction of wilderness spawns to bypass it. Hmm, that would undermine a deliberate design. Better: keep it, but the randomization applies to non-wilderness.

  content: |
       * How many of them may be alive at once.
       *
       * Starts at single figures on a fresh save and climbs toward a few hundred on
       * the hardest setting, with the day's third of the night's (the horde thins
       * out in daylight rather than vanishing — see main.js).
       */
      export function hordeCap(kills, level, night = true) {
        const start = lerp(5, 12, level);
        const end = lerp(90, 260, level);
        const shaped = Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), CAP_CURVE);
        return Math.max(3, Math.round(lerp(start, end, shaped) * (night ? 1 : 0.35)));
      }
      
      /**
       * How many land in one spawn. Always at least one — a cluster floor of four
       * (what this used to do) meant a trickle read as a flood however low the cap
       * was set, which is the whole reason the cap alone could not calm it down.
       *
       * `level` scales the top of the range but not the opening: even on Brutal the
       * first clusters are one or two, because a fresh save should not open with a
       * knot of six.
       */
      export function hordeCluster(kills, level, rng = Math.random) {
        const t = Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), CLUSTER_CURVE) * (0.65 + level * 0.35);
        const max = Math.max(1, Math.round(lerp(2, 22, t)));
        return 1 + Math.floor(rng() * max);
      }
      
      /**
       * Seconds between spawn attempts. `hungry` is the "still well under the cap"
       * case, which refills faster than topping up.
       */
      export function hordeCooldown(kills, level, hungry) {
        const base = hungry ? lerp(2.2, 0.3, Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), COOLDOWN_CURVE))
                            : lerp(4.5, 0.7, Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), COOLDOWN_CURVE));
        return base * lerp(1.6, 0.7, level);
      }
      
      /**
       * How far from the player a cluster may be dropped, in metres. They still
       * arrive out of sight (the spawn ring is 35-75 m), but a fresh save keeps its
       * first handful further out than a late one does.
       */
      export function hordeSpread(kills) {
        return lerp(6, 16, Math.pow(hordeProgress(kills), COOLDOWN_CURVE));
      }

       * the same numbers the spawn loop will use, so a tuning change is visible in

Committed `8442238`. Not pushed — say the word.

**Both causes were single hardcoded numbers.**

**The clock:** `main.js:2133` was `worldTime.setTime(22.5)`. Half past ten at night, every run, forever. The daylight rendering was never broken — `daycycle.js` has drawn a real sun since it was given an arc (sunrise 05:50, sunset 20:10), and `main.js:5471` already passes `softDay` for zombie mode so the sun is capped at dawn/dusk strength for playability. That one line was the only thing keeping all of it off screen.

**The trap here, and it's the reason I didn't just do what you asked:** randomising the hour naively looks fine and quietly ruins the mode. `hordeCap()` gives daylight about **a third** of the night's cap. So the hour isn't cosmetic — it's the difficulty slider, and it was never labelled as one. Uniform-random would have made ~40% of your runs thin daylight games.

So it's weighted, because uniform is uniform over the wrong range:

| band | weight | |
|---|---|---|
| 05:00–09:00 | 22% | dawn into morning |
| 09:00–16:00 | 20% | middle of the day |
| 16:00–19:00 | 20% | afternoon into golden |
| 19:00–22:00 | **24%** | dusk — best light in the state |
| 22:00–24:00 | 14% | proper night |
| **00:00–05:00** | **excluded** | full horde cap + least light in the state = a wall, not variety |

**~42% of runs are now in daylight.** The launch banner tells you which and what it costs: *"Morning — a thinner horde than at night"* — rather than you finding out by getting overrun at noon.

**The ring:** `minDist: 35, maxDist: 75` on *every* spawn, forever. That's a distance you learn in about two minutes. It now draws between three shapes — the usual band (62%), a long push out to 120 m past the treeline (26%), and a close drift in to 22 m (12%). I left the bearing alone: it was already uniform, and re-rolling a uniform makes it worse, not better.

**One thing I deliberately didn't touch:** the multiplayer lobby has its own `setTime(22.5)` at `main.js:2420`. In a shared room the host's clock is authoritative — a per-client random hour would put everyone under a different sky.

**On the testing:** 12 gates in `zombie_test.mjs` over 20k draws. One of them is blunt and I want to flag it — everything else tests the *picker*, and a perfect picker does nothing if the launcher goes back to typing the hour. `main.js` can't be imported headlessly, so that one check reads it as source text. I verified it actually bites by re-adding `setTime(22.5)` and watching it fail.

**Still open from earlier:** the Crown Strip brief. Measured but **nothing built** — and the headline is that the venues aren't a bit empty, they're at **59.5 m² per person** (a busy club is 1–2), and the layout is two pairs of *identical* venues 0 m apart, not a grid. That's the next piece whenever you want it.

- path: src\main.js
  content: |
      // hedge, not the cure: 48 -> 90, 26 -> 30, 160 m -> 180 m, about a quarter more
      // people on screen. The first thing to check if the frame budget complains is
      // ENEMY_CAP, because each actor is ~12-20 draw calls after characters.js's
      // mergeRigid. NOT re-measured in a browser — there is no Chrome on this machine.
      const ENEMY_CAP = 90;         // living NPCs to maintain (off-screen ones are hidden, npc.js)
      const ENEMY_CAP_BUSY = 30;    // ...and the extra on top of it downtown / on the Strip
      const CIV_CULL = 180;         // metres; beyond this an NPC is removed from the scene
      let enemyRespawnCd = 0;
      let populationOn = true;      // missions switch spawning off during set pieces
      // Anyone left far behind is released, so the cap counts only the people around you. This used to run only AFTER a
      // successful spawn, and the spawn is skipped once the cap is reached: the crowd you left behind held the cap
      // forever, and walking into the woods (or away from a horde) meant nothing ever spawned near you again
      // (human report, 2026-09-26: "a lot of trees ... not a single hog or zombie").
      const cullCd = { civ: 0, zombie: 0 };
      function cullFar(key, dt, maxDist, only) {
        cullCd[key] -= dt;
        if (cullCd[key] > 0) return;
        cullCd[key] = 0.5;
        let any = false;
        for (const e of enemies) {
          if (e.dead || e.leash || (only && !only(e))) continue;
          if (Math.hypot(e.spr.position.x - playerPos.x, e.spr.position.z - playerPos.z) > maxDist) { npcs.release(e); scene.remove(e.spr); e.dead = "gone"; any = true; }
        }
        if (any) for (let i = enemies.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (enemies[i].dead === "gone") enemies.splice(i, 1);
      }
      function updateEnemyPopulation(dt) {
        if (!populationOn) return;
        cullFar("civ", dt, CIV_CULL, (e) => e.type !== "zombie");
        // Zombie mode's horde (updateZombiePopulation, below) shares this same
        // `enemies` array and its own separate cap — counted out here so it can't
        // eat into this budget and thin out the ordinary population as it fills
        // up. It's meant to be added on top of the civilian count, not carved out of it.
        let alive = 0;

> _Reasoning_
> My probe picked a lane in the FOREST (x -646, z -879) — that's a stateWorld lane, not OrleaRouge. So the POI numbers are 0 because OrleaRouge isn't there. Let me redo standing on an OrleaRouge lane specifically.
> 
> But the key structural finding is already solid and zone-independent:
> 
> **pick() distance: min 65.0, p10 69.0, median 85.1, p90 100.8, max 104.9.** The ring is exactly 65-105 and NEVER closer than 65m. Confirmed.
> 
> **The spawn ring (65-105m) lies ENTIRELY INSIDE the cull radius (180m).** Confirmed: `true`.
> 
> **Expected people within 50m: 6.9** — and that's assuming uniform spread across the annulus, which is roughly right. And "the part you can actually SEE (50 m) is 7.7% of it."
> 
> So: the cap is 90-120 people, ALL of them permanently in a ring 65-105m away, and the fraction you can actually see at 50m is ~7%. That's ~7 people within 50m, scattered — and at night, unlit, behind buildings.
> 
> And critically: because the ring is entirely inside the cull radius, **the population never turns over**. NPCs spawned at 65m are never culled, so the crowd never refreshes into your vicinity. Walk 100m and your existing crowd is still 65m behind you, and new ones spawn 65m ahead. You permanently have a hollow ring around you.
> 
> That is the bug. And it explains why raising 48→90 did nothing — I raised the cap, but the cap was never the constraint. The constraint is that nobody is ever closer than 65m.
> 
> Now let me re-run standing on an actual OrleaRouge street to get the city numbers and POI radii. Let me fix the probe to use orlea lanes only.
> 
> Then design the fix:
> 
> **The fix has two parts:**
> 
> 1. **The cull must be tighter than the spawn ring** so the population recycles. Currently cull 180 > spawn 65-105, so nothing ever recycles. If cull < spawn inner edge, every NPC walks into the cull and is replaced by a fresh one out of sight. But that alone still leaves everyone 65m+ away.
> 
> 2. **NPCs must be able to come near the player.** The wander disc is `poi.r * wanderR` around a home POI. If POIs are dense enough in the city, and the spawn snaps to a POI near the player, then the home POI is near the player and the disc overlaps the player. The probe showed 0 POIs — but that was in the forest. In OrleaRouge there are many POIs.
> 
> So the real question: in OrleaRouge, when pick() spawns someone 65-105m away and snaps them to a POI in that ring, is that POI's wander disc near the player? A POI 70m away with r=10 and wanderR=0.55 → disc radius 5.5m → nearest approach 64.5m. Still 65m away!
> 
> **So NPCs can NEVER be closer than roughly the spawn radius.** That's the fundamental issue. `pick()` guarantees a minimum distance of 65m, and then the wander disc never closes it.
> 
> So on a city street you'd see people only 65-100m away — which at night, unlit, down a boulevard, is invisible.
> 
> **The correct fix:** NPCs need to be *on the street you're walking down*, not in a ring 65m out. That means:
> - Tighten the spawn ring a lot (e.g. 15-55m) so people are actually in your vicinity, relying on buildings/occlusion rather than distance for the "out of sight" guarantee.
> - AND add re-homing so the crowd follows the player's district.
> 
> Tightening the ring risks visible pop-in. But the "out of sight" requirement in a city is mostly about not materialising in plain view on the same pavement. A ring of 15-55m in a city with buildings is mostly fine, and it's the difference between an empty street and a populated one.
> 
> The most defensible combined fix:
> 1. Tighten the spawn ring (urban/entertainment especially) to something like 18-70m.
> 2. Make the cull radius track: keep 180m (so nobody pops out), but the tighter ring means the crowd is genuinely near you.
> 3. Increase wander radius for urban so people mill around the block you're on.
>

Committed `b116ffa`. Not pushed — two commits are waiting (`8442238` zombie mode, `b116ffa` this).

**This is the same bug you reported on 2026-09-26, and my answer then was wrong.** I raised `ENEMY_CAP` 48 → 90 and called it fixed. The cap was never the constraint. I'm sorry that cost you two rounds of "still empty."

**Measured downtown, in the real grid, 4000 attempts:**

```
pick():  4000/4000 succeeded, 0 null
spawn distance:  min 52.3 m · median 92.6 m · p90 107.7 m
nearest an NPC could EVER be:  9.8 m
people within the 50 m you can see:  9.3
```

**Nothing was failing. Nobody was ever near.** Three things compounded:

1. **The ring was 65–105 m.** Past the distance you can see down a street — and at night, past the 8-light pool too.
2. **They never moved toward you.** An NPC's wander disc is `poi.r × WANDER[zone].r`, and downtown's median POI is 6 m at urban `r: 0.55` — a **3.3 m disc**. They spawned 52–108 m away, snapped to a POI, and stood on it forever.
3. **The population never turned over.** `CIV_CULL` is 180 m and the spawn ring sat *entirely inside* it. So nothing was ever culled, nothing recycled, and the same static ring followed you around the map without ever refreshing into the street you were standing on. The ring and the cull were the wrong way round.

**Result: 7.1 → 30.2 people expected within 50 m.**

Two things I got wrong on the way, both caught by measuring:

- My first fix put the "never spawn inside the ring" clamp *before* the POI snap, so the snap walked people straight back inside — minimum **15.8 m against a 25 m ring**. Moved it after, and the minimum is now exactly 25.0 m.
- My first traffic measurement said "0 lanes within 141 m." **That was my probe being wrong, not the game** — it measured distance to lane *sample points*, and these boulevards are 2-point 800 m lines, so a road running straight through you reads as absent. Corrected: **20 of 20 lanes pass through the city grid, 14 within 22 m.** Traffic is not structurally broken and I made no change to it.

**The tradeoff, stated plainly:** the ring floor is 25 m where it was effectively 52 m. That *is* the fix and it isn't free — at 25 m, in open ground with nothing between you and the spawn point, someone can appear close enough to notice. Between buildings it mostly shouldn't read. **I can't verify that without a browser**, and it's the one thing worth eyeballing when this deploys.

If it still looks thin after the push, tell me where you were standing and I'll re-measure that exact spot — this time I'll ask *before* adjusting a number, because that's how I got it wrong last time.

        /** Everything that belongs to one junction: four crossings and their bars. */

Committed `1e57f70`. Three commits now waiting to be pushed.

**The crossing builder was innocent.** Uniform pitch, uniform stripe width, correct quad geometry. **The paint was fine — there were two lots of it.**

Everything `flush()` emits sits at exactly `y0 + 0.002`. Two quads overlapping in plan *at the same height* aren't an ugly overlap, they're a **depth fight** — the GPU shreds both, and where one wins a slice of the other's edge you get exactly the chevrons in your screenshot.

**Two independent causes, both found by measuring the emitted quads rather than reading the code:**

**1. A stop bar painted straight across its own zebra.** `junction()` placed `stopBar()` at 9.8 m from the junction, then `stopBar()` shifted it back by only 2.1 m — landing at **7.7 m, dead centre of a crossing that spans 6.2–9.2 m**. This hit **every junction in the game**, not just this one.

**2. Two junctions 14 m apart.** `US167_JUNCTIONS` is "every z where a district road meets the boulevard" — and two districts' roads are nearer together than one junction's paint envelope, so they drew over each other. Both roads are real; there's just no room for a crossing at each. `spaceJunctions()` now drops what doesn't fit, deterministically, and `main.js` warns about the drop instead of losing a junction quietly.

**Measured on the real US-167 paint: 175 coplanar overlapping quads → 0.** (154 were the stop bar; 21 the spacing.)

**One thing I want to flag, because it's the second time.** My first overlap detector had `Math.min(p.minz, q.maxz)` where it meant `p.maxz` — so it could *never* report an overlap, and the "after" check passed **vacuously**. The control check caught it. That's the same failure as `road_clearance.mjs` reading `l.pts` off lanes that have `points`, and it's why this test has a control at all.

**Deliberately visible side effect:** every junction's stop bar moves from 7.7/11.9 m to 5.2/10.2 m from the centre — out of the zebra and onto the approach where a stop line belongs. That's a real change to junctions across Metro, the fringe and US-167, not a no-op.

Still unverified in a browser. If the crossings look right after this deploys, that closes it; if any other stretch of paint looks ragged, tell me roughly where and I'll measure that junction the same way.
